context.description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.

latestRelease.title: v0.5.17
latestRelease.notes:
# Highlights

*582 PRs from 194 contributors.*

**Kimi K3 day-0 support**: A 2.8T-parameter multimodal LatentMoE (896 experts, top-16, routed in a 3584-dim latent space) with a 1M-token context, 69 KDA linear-attention layers interleaved with 24 MLA layers, and a MoonViT3d vision tower, shipping as a native MXFP4 checkpoint. SGLang serves it from day 0 with DCP, DSpark speculative decoding, chunked-prefill PP with TP decode, KDA-aware prefix caching, HiCache L2 over DCP, LoRA on the quantized weights, and reasoning, tool-call and OpenAI-compatible serving, verified on NVIDIA GB300 and AMD MI35x ([#32541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32541), [#32828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32828), [#32890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32890), [#33025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33025), [#33112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33112), [blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K3), [roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607)).

**MiniMax-H3 day-0 support**: MiniMax's video generation model that produces a video and a synchronized stereo audio track in one request, served natively on SGLang-Diffusion across all three public task profiles: text-to-video-and-audio (`t2va`), first/last-frame conditioning (`fl2va`), and image/video/audio reference conditioning (`ref2va`, which also covers video-to-video). Verified on B200 (TP2 + Ulysses4), H100 (TP2 + Ulysses2), AMD MI300X and MI355X (Ulysses1/2/4/8), and 2x RTX 5090 with layerwise offload ([#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3)).

**Other new models added**: [EmbeddingGemma](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Google/EmbeddingGemma) and [LFM2.5](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/LiquidAI/LFM2.5) embedding models, nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4, plus cookbook recipes for Poolside's [Laguna-S-2.1](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Poolside/Laguna-S-2.1) family and [Inkling-Small](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/ThinkingMachines/Inkling-Small).

**Initial support for the Rust frontend**: Migrates the front half of the server, everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler, from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation ([#29799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799)).

**DCP communication backends and q-replicate (Helix)**: The DeepSeek-MLA decode context-parallel path gains pluggable comm backends. `a2a` exchanges packed attention output plus fp32 LSE in a single NCCL collective per layer, with fp8 KV carried as uint8 byte transport; `fi_a2a` delegates the cross-rank exchange to the FlashInfer MNNVL kernel on GB200. `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` projects full-head Q locally and skips the per-layer Q head-dim all-gather. Select with `--dcp-comm-backend {ag_rs, a2a, fi_a2a}` ([#21637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21637)).

**DWDP for MoE prefill**: A new prefill parallelism strategy that prefetches peer expert weights over NVLink P2P and computes all experts locally, removing EP all-to-all token dispatch. On 4x B200 with gpt-oss-120b, prefill-only, DWDP4 reaches **1.92x over DEP4** at MNT 32K / ISL 32K, and **506K vs 329K tok/s (1.54x)** at saturation (CONC=128, ISL=8K). Enable with `--dwdp-size`; the authors mark it early-development ([#29778](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29778)).

**Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache**: For agentic and RL-rollout workloads, requests can carry a stable `session_id` so eviction knows which prefixes an active session still references, instead of evicting purely by cache policy. Release the references with `/close_session`. Opt in with `--enable-session-radix-cache` ([#29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173)).

**SM90 FP8 MegaMoE for DeepSeek-V4**: Adds the DeepGEMM MegaMoE A2A path on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro FP8, including the pre-dispatch JIT kernel and FP8 expert weight preparation. Guarded behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1` ([#29016](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29016)).

**Faster large-MoE model loading**: Oversized or non-contiguous CPU weight views were driving pathological H2D transfers, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 spending 27 to 32 minutes in H2D on some ranks. Copying those views into contiguous storage before H2D cuts full model loading from about **35 minutes to 6m20s (5.6x)**, and GPT-OSS-20B BF16 from **545s to 70s (7.8x)**, with Qwen3.5-397B measured at 1.93x to 2.3x. Opt in with `SGLANG_MOE_COPY_WEIGHT_VIEWS_BEFORE_H2D`, off by default ([#32315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32315)).

**Lower DeepSeek-V4 memory on AMD**: Removing unnecessary expert padding drops MI355X FP4 MoE model weights from **159.07 GB to 112.36 GB**, and bringing the HIP compress-state pool into the memory_saver KV_CACHE region lets colocated RL reclaim it, cutting the measured training-phase footprint from about **143 GiB to 87 GiB per GPU** ([#31450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31450), [#31747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31747)).

**Faster engine recovery**: Large-model restarts cost 3 to 6+ minutes today, about 6.5 minutes for Qwen3-235B FP8 on 4 GPUs, because weights reload from storage and CUDA graphs recapture. A weight-cache daemon holds weights per GPU so a restarting engine can recover from cache instead ([#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139)).

**Lower host overhead in hybrid-linear MTP decode**: Under spec-v2 overlap scheduling each decode step runs draft, verify and extend CUDA graphs, and the eager seams between them become GPU idle time at low concurrency. This trims that host work so the host stays off the critical path ([#32219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32219)).

**Dependencies**: flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 ([#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927)), sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1 ([#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345), [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)), helion 1.4 ([#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)), mooncake 0.3.12.post1 ([#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)), dynamo-tokenizers 1.7.0 ([#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)). PyTorch stays at 2.11.0 and the CUDA base image at 13.0.1.

*Full release notes by category below; breaking changes and known issues are at the end.*

* [SM120] Only split touched SWA pages in FlashMLA page-split kernel: [#32320](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32320)

* [Fix][AMD] Qwen3.5 MoE: disable global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends (MoRI + dp-attention init crash): [#31793](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31793)

* [AMD] Fix JIT compile failure in sgl_kernel/warp.cuh: [#33195](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33195)

## NPU / Ascend

* [NPU] Optimize DeepSeek-V4 performance: [#31931](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31931)
* :sparkles: [llm][npu][quant] Add W8A8 MXFP8 quantization for Qwen3 MoE on Ascend NPU: [#30768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30768)
* [NPU] adapt dflash v2 on npu: [#31739](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31739)
* [NPU] Adapt MiMo-V2.5-W8A8: [#29131](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29131)

* [Intel GPU] Add XPU Platform support: [#31949](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31949)
* [XPU] Enable breakable prefill CUDA graph on XPU: [#30273](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30273)

* [Bugfix] Fix CUDA import on non-CUDA platforms: [#31919](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31919)

## Dependencies

* Bump FlashInfer to 0.6.15.post1: [#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927) ⭐
* Bump sgl-deep-gemm to 0.1.5: [#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345)
* Replace Kimi K3 DeepGEMM patch with 0.1.5.post1: [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)
* Bump helion version to 1.4: [#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)
* chore: bump mooncake version to 0.3.12.post1: [#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)
* bump dynamo-tokenizers to 1.7.0: [#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)
* [AMD] ROCm AITER pin reverted to 9127c94, then updated to d9e5ef7: [#32879](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32879), [#32939](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32939)
* Fix PyPI release: drop the git-only sgl-eval dep from packaged metadata: [#32354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32354)

## Breaking Changes & Upgrade Notes

* **`helion` jumps 0.2.6 to 1.4**, a major-version move for anyone depending on helion-backed kernels: [#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)
* **`sglang.jit_kernel` is retired into `sglang.kernels`**, completing RFC [#29630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630). Imports from the old module path must move: [#32072](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32072), [#31666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31666), [#32015](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32015), [#32045](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32045)
* **Breakable prefill CUDA graph is now on by default for DP attention**: [#31682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31682)
* **CuteDSL BF16 GEMM on SM100 is on by default** when the heuristic allows it: [#30567](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30567)
* **sgl-kernel AOT `bmm_fp8` is deleted in favor of `flashinfer.bmm_fp8`; the AOT router GEMM and fused A GEMM are also removed**: [#31202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31202), [#30280](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30280)
* **The FP8 per-tensor GEMM backend on SM120 switches to cuBLAS**: [#31961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31961)
* **Unfetchable or unparseable multimodal inputs now return HTTP 400 instead of 500**, and text-only models reject media input outright: [#31417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31417), [#32914](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32914)
* **Diffusion request-level quality is restricted to two validated tiers**, lossless (default) and high: [#33453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33453)
* **`ServerArgs` is being made read-only** behind namespace config bags. Code that mutated `ServerArgs` at runtime must route through the new accessors: [#31809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31809), [#31811](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31811), [#33334](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33334), [#33338](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33338)

## Known Issues

* **The FlashInfer rmsnorm + quant fusion for SM90/SM100/SM120 was landed and reverted** this cycle ([#32994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32994), [#33455](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33455)). It is not in this release.
* **Breakable CUDA graph is disabled for NemotronH** pending a fix: [#33130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33130)
* **`test_update_weights_from_disk` is skipped on ROCm** pending a reload fix ([#31924](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31924)): [#31925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31925)
* **The SM120 DeepGEMM release-pipeline test is temporarily skipped**: [#32193](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32193)

**Full Changelog**: [`v0.5.16...v0.5.17`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/compare/v0.5.16...v0.5.17)

signals.title: [Roadmap] Unified Hybrid Radix Cache Refactor
signals.text: Blog: https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-11-unified-radix-cache/ ## Motivation The current radix cache implementations (RadixCache, MambaRadixCache, SWARadixCache, etc.) share a large amount of logic but are maintained as separate, diverged copies. This leads to code duplication, inconsistent behavior, and high maintenance burden when extending cache functionality to new model types (e.g., hybrid linear models, sliding window attention models). The goal of this refactor is to unify the hybrid radix cache hierarchy around a common base interface, making it easier to: - Add new cache variants without duplicating logic - Ensure consistency across all cache implementations - Enable future extensions (e.g., HiCache, PD disaggregation, new model architectures) @hzh0425 @yizhang2077 @pansicheng @ispobock ## Progress ### Stage 0: Unify Radix Tree Interface - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17142 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17397 @yizhang2077 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17401 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17852 @pansicheng - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18147 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19427 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19429 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20330 @pansicheng - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20590 @hzh0425 ### Stage 1: Support Unified HybridRadixTree V2 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21206 @hzh0425 @ispobock @yizhang2077 @pansicheng - [x] Move UnifiedRadixTree into the main mem_cache directory and place reusable components under a separate dedicated directory. - [x] provide detailed Markdown documentation, including each api's purpose, inputs and outputs, mutation behavior, and time complexity. - [x] Review all tree APIs carefully, ensure that core tree operations remain linear time cost - [x] Add HiCache support, including offloading support for mamba, swa, and full components. @hzh0425 @ispobock @pansicheng - [x] L2 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23316 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23391 - signals.title: [Bug] Router circuit breaker treats 4xx client errors as worker failures
signals.text: ### What happened We hit a production failure mode where client/request-validation errors from a healthy SGLang worker opened the router circuit breaker and then caused follow-up requests to fail with `no_available_workers`. The concrete case was an oversized generation request: the client sent a request whose prompt tokens plus requested completion exceeded the model context. The backend correctly returned HTTP 400. After several such requests, the router treated those 400 responses as worker failures, opened the worker circuit(s), and subsequent requests failed as if the workers were unhealthy. ### Why this looks like a router bug A 4xx response, especially a deterministic validation error like context length exceeded, does not indicate that the worker is unhealthy. It is a property of the request. Counting it toward the worker circuit breaker can turn a bad client request into a fleet-level outage until the circuit breaker timeout expires. On current `main` (`897587b03`), the HTTP router records every non-2xx response as a circuit-breaker failure: - `route_typed_request_once` calls `worker.record_outcome(status.is_success())`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/897587b03/sgl-model-gateway/src/routers/http/router.rs#L322-L323 - `record_outcome(false)` forwards directly to the circuit breaker: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/897587b03/sgl-model-gateway/src/core/worker.rs#L203-L205 - once open, worker selection filters the worker out via `is_available()` / `can_execute()`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/897587b03/sgl-model-gateway/src/core/worker.rs#L198-L200 - if all workers are filtered out, the router returns `no_available_workers`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/897587b03/sgl-model-gateway/src/routers/http/router.rs#L281-L290 The OpenAI router appears to have the same issue: it records a circuit-breaker failure for any non-success status, not just transport/server-side failures: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/897587b03/sgl-model-gateway/src/routers/openai/router.rs#L596-L602 ### Expected behavior Client/request errors should be returned to the caller, but they should not poison the worker's circuit breaker. In particular, HTTP 400 context-length/request-validation errors should not make a healthy worker unavailable for unrelated future requests. I would expect the circuit breaker to count only statuses that imply worker/backend health or availability problems, for example transport errors, read failures, retryable/server-side statuses, and maybe explicit overload/backpressure statuses depending on intended semantics. Non-retryable 4xx request errors should not increment worker failure counts. ### Reproduction sketch 1. Start an SGLang deployment behind the router with circuit breaker enabled. 2. Send several requests to a healthy worker that deterministically return HTTP 400, e.g. requests where `input_tokens + max_new_tokens` exceeds the model context length. 3. Observe the router recording worker circuit-breaker failures for those responses. 4. After the failure threshold, the worker is filtered by `can_execute()` and subsequent routing can return `no_available_workers` even though the worker is healthy. ### Impact A single bad caller or a misconfigured integration can trip the circuit breaker for healthy workers and temporarily take the router out of service for valid requests. This is particularly surprising because the original error is a 4xx client error, but the blast radius becomes a router/availability failure.

signals.title: [Bug] Server stops responding after 2-3 requests — Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, TP=4 across 4x DGX Spark (GB10/SM121)
signals.text: ## Summary Reproducible scheduler/server hang: after 2–3 successful chat completions, all subsequent requests (including `/health`) time out indefinitely. Reproduced 3/3 attempts across 2 host boots. Generation quality and speed are normal until the hang. ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` @ `sha256:ceaf8b16e02d165143633ac228bbb994a05fe77d7e0526cf035ae4bbf4eacc36` (sglang 0.5.12.post1, torch 2.11.0+cu130) - Hardware: 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 128GB unified each), dual-rail 200G RoCE, NET/IB transport verified in NCCL logs (zero socket fallback) - Model: nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4, `--quantization modelopt_fp4` ## Launch ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --tp 4 --nnodes 4 --node-rank N --dist-init-addr <rank0>:29500 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8890 --attention-backend triton \ --context-length 4096 --max-running-requests 1 ``` (GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME/TP_SOCKET_IFNAME/NCCL_* set for the RoCE fabric; happy to paste full env) ## Repro 1. Serve; wait for "fired up and ready". 2. Send 2-3 sequential streaming chat completions (200 max_tokens, temp 0, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`). First 1-2 complete normally (observed 12.9-25.4 tok/s decode). 3. Next request hangs past 600s; `/health` also stops answering. No crash, no error in rank-0 log; container stays up. Run-to-run details vary slightly (sometimes 2 succeed, sometimes 3; one run wedged with thinking-mode requests that exceeded max_tokens via reasoning). The hang itself is 3/3. ## Observations (NOT a diagnosis — flagging for maintainers, unverified hypotheses) - At one hang we observed on rank 0: `resource_tracker: There appear to be 1 leaked semaphore objects to clean up at shutdown`. We have NOT established this as cause — could be shutdown noise. A shared-memory/IPC angle is our only (unverified) hypothesis; we'd value maintainer guidance on what to instrument. - Possibly relevant config quirks on our side: stock MoE kernel configs (no tuned configs for GB10), startup warning `DeepGemm is enabled but the scale_fmt of checkpoint is not ue8m0`, `--max-running-requests 1`. - Config deltas vs the known-good community run (ht12, sglang 0.5.10, same checkpoint, same 4x Spark shape, forum thread 366325): they ran `disable_deep_gemm=true` (we did not — and our build warns about DeepGemm scale_fmt), `max_running_requests=32` (ours 1 — maybe the single-slot admission path is implicated), raised `watchdog_timeout=3600`/`dist_timeout=1800`, fp8_e4m3 KV, explicit `fp4_gemm_backend=flashinfer_cutlass` with an SM121 cute/mma.py patch, sglang 0.5.10 vs our 0.5.12.post1. Happy to bisect any of these on request. - Community reports (ht12, NVIDIA forum) show this checkpoint serving fast and concurrent on Spark-class hardware via SGLang — so this may well be config-specific. We can run any diagnostic build/flags on the 4-node rig on request; full rank logs, env dumps, and probe streams preserved. - Related blocker we hit attempting to bisect on 0.5.10: this model cannot load at all on sglang ≤0.5.13 + transformers 5.x without out-of-tree patches (vision_config/text_config sub-config dicts not promoted; PR #22839 addresses it but has been unmerged since April 15) — which limits how much of the community-vs-stock delta anyone can bisect on stock builds. ## Evidence available rank-0 log tails at each hang (3 runs), full launch env, raw probe streams (timestamps per token), NCCL transport logs.

signals.title: [Bug] Prometheus /metrics scrape can starve prefill bootstrap health checks
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] This issue is written in English. ### Describe the bug I observed the following failure pattern in a PD deployment: - `/metrics` latency on the prefill leader suddenly increased to seconds. - The bootstrap `/health` endpoint started returning read timeouts, even though the handler itself only returns `OK`. - Decode workers reported `Losing connection with prefill instance` for the same prefill bootstrap address. - After `/metrics` pressure stopped, `/health` became fast again. This makes the prefill instance look disconnected even when the process is still alive. The symptom is a false prefill connection loss caused by health-check starvation. After reading the code, I think the problem is in the current `/metrics` serving path: - In single-tokenizer prefill mode, `TokenizerManager` owns both the HTTP server that exposes `/metrics` and the bootstrap health server used by decode heartbeats. - `add_prometheus_middleware()` mounts the Prometheus ASGI app directly on the main app with `CollectorRegistry`, `MultiProcessCollector`, and `make_asgi_app`. - Each scrape can read and aggregate Prometheus multiprocess files and generate the full text response in the request path. - Concurrent scrapes can enter this path at the same time. - When this collection path becomes slow, it shares the same Python process failure domain as bootstrap health handling, so `/health` can be starved. I tested a small experimental patch to compare behavior. Patch approach: - Run metrics collection in a subprocess so it is isolated from the main event loop. - Apply singleflight: at most one scrape generates metrics at a time; concurrent scrapes are rejected immediately. - Enforce a bounded timeout on generation so a slow collection cannot block the server indefinitely. Prototype diff (single commit, hash-pinned): - https://github.com/junliu-mde/sglang/commit/c31b7ca2283b557cf4b5d9e9c979f52e58954c70 The comparison result was straightforward: - Before the patch, local `/metrics` scrape pressure caused bootstrap health misses and decode-side `Losing connection with prefill instance` logs. - After the patch, a stronger `/metrics` scrape test produced no health misses. Extra concurrent scrapes failed fast instead of piling up behind metrics generation. This patch is not intended as the final design. It only validates that isolating, bounding, and limiting `/metrics` generation protects the critical health path. In principle, returning `503` immediately for concurrent scrapes is already enough to mitigate the starvation: each rejected scrape exits quickly instead of blocking, so `/health` is no longer crowded out. For a production design, however, the preferred fix should still be code-path isolation: metrics exposition should not share the same Python failure domain as critical health or heartbeat handling. Prometheus exporter guidance also points in this direction. It says exporters should normally pull metrics synchronously when Prometheus scrapes them, and that caching is acceptable only for particularly expensive metrics and should be called out in the metric `HELP` string. The same guidance notes that the default Prometheus scrape timeout is 10 seconds, so any bounded generation timeout should stay below the configured scrape timeout. See: https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/writing_exporters/#scheduling A bounded cache of the last successful Prometheus metrics snapshot can still be useful, but it should be treated as a secondary protection rather than the primary fix. Serving cached bytes to concurrent scrapes can keep the `/metrics` HTTP path constant-time under scrape pressure and preserve Prometheus data continuity, but stale data must be bounded, documented, and observable. `503`/`504` should still surface when there is genuinely no usable snapshot, when the snapshot is too stale, or when generation repeatedly fails. ### Reproduction Run a PD deployment where the prefill leader uses the single-tokenizer topology and metrics are enabled. From the affected prefill pod, apply local scrape pressure to `/metrics` while probing bootstrap health. Example procedure: 1. Start multiple local clients scraping `http://127.0.0.1:30000/metrics`. 2. In parallel, probe `http://127.0.0.1:8998/health` with a short read timeout. 3. Watch decode logs for `Losing connection with prefill instance`. 4. Stop the `/metrics` pressure and verify that `/health` becomes fast again. ### Environment `python3 -m sglang.check_env` on the affected prefill pod: ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 590.48.01 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.12 sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post2 flashinfer_python: 0.6.11.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.11.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.11.post1+cu130 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.6.0 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.13.5 fastapi: 0.136.1 huggingface_hub: 1.15.0 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 pydantic: 2.13.4 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.47.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 xgrammar: 0.2.0 ulimit soft: 1048576 ```

signals.title: [AMD][multimodal-gen] HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED in torch._scaled_mm FP8 GEMM on MI325 — all diffusion tests failing on main
signals.text: ## Summary All `multimodal-gen-test-*-gpu-amd` diffusion tests (`flux2_modelopt_fp8_tp2_t2i`, `wan2_*`, `mova_360p_tp2`) have been failing on `main` since at least 2026-06-20 (10+ days) with `RuntimeError: CUDA error: HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` inside `torch._scaled_mm` FP8 GEMM. ## Error ``` [denoising_step_0] Error during execution after 8104.9789 ms: CUDA error: HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED when calling `HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` Traceback (most recent call last): File "python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py", line 1042, in _run_denoising_step noise_pred = self._predict_noise_with_cfg( File "python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py", line 1550, in predict_fn raw = self._predict_noise( File "python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py", line 1221, in forward encoder_hidden_states, hidden_states = block( File "python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py", line 179, in _get_qkv_projections query, _ = attn.to_q(hidden_states) File "python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/linear.py", line 427, in forward output_parallel = self.quant_method.apply(self, input_, bias) File "python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py", line 425, in apply return apply_fp8_linear( File "python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py", line 1733, in apply_fp8_linear output = torch._scaled_mm( RuntimeError: CUDA error: HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED when calling `HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` ``` ## Environment - **Runner:** `linux-mi325-2gpu-sglang` (MI325, gfx942) - **Workflow:** `PR Test (AMD)` → `multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu-amd` (and 1-gpu variant) - **Model:** `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev` (FP8, modelopt quantized) - **Code path:** `apply_fp8_linear` → `torch._scaled_mm` (per_tensor_weights + per_tensor_activations branch, `fp8_utils.py:1733`) ## Reproducibility **Deterministic** — 10 of 10 recent `main` scheduled runs fail the same way (checked runs 28239034418 through 28331834544). Not runner-variance. ## Impact - Blocks all PRs whose diff triggers `multimodal-gen-test-amd` (diffusion/video gen changes) - Does NOT block PRs that only touch serving/CI/test code (the `check-changes` gate skips multimodal-gen for those diffs — e.g. PR #29584 is unaffected) ## Likely root cause `torch._scaled_mm` with per-tensor FP8 scales calls into hipBLASLt, which returns `HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` for this GEMM shape/dtype combination on MI325 (gfx942). The comment at `fp8_utils.py:1712` notes this path is "For now validated on ROCm platform" with ROCm 6.3+/torch 2.7+, but the specific shape from FLUX.2's attention QKV projection appears unsupported. ## Possible fixes 1. **ROCm/hipBLAS side:** add support for this FP8 GEMM shape on gfx942 (out of sglang's control) 2. **sglang side:** catch `HIPBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` in `apply_fp8_linear` and fall back to `_apply_fallback_scaled_mm` (the channelwise fallback path at `fp8_utils.py:1757`) on MI325 3. **Test side:** skip `flux2_modelopt_fp8_*` parametrizations on MI325 until hipBLAS supports the shape ## CI run references - Latest failure: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28331834544/job/83931200386 - Failing since at least: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27864213328 (2026-06-20) /cc @sgl-project/amd

signals.title: [Feature] RFC: SGLang KV Indexer for Distributed KV Cache Placement Metadata
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation cc: @isytwu @TianDi101 ## Summary This RFC proposes a SGLang KV Indexer for collecting and querying distributed KV cache location metadata. The indexer does not store KV cache bytes. It tracks which worker holds which KV block hash and at which storage tier, so schedulers and routing components can make cross-worker KV reuse decisions. SGLang workers already emit KV cache lifecycle events such as `BlockStored`, `BlockRemoved`, and `AllBlocksCleared`. A bridge component converts these events into indexer metadata updates. Query clients can then ask the indexer which workers may hold a given set of KV block hashes. The initial project will be implemented out of tree as an independent Rust service. It integrates with SGLang through the existing KV event stream and gRPC APIs, without requiring the indexer code to live inside the SGLang source tree. ## Goals 1. Collect KV location metadata from SGLang workers. The bridge subscribes to SGLang KV events and converts them into metadata operations such as `report`, `revoke`, and `revoke-all`. The indexer maintains a location index in the form of `hash -> worker -> tier`. 2. Provide cross-worker KV location lookup. Schedulers or query clients can ask the indexer where a list of KV block hashes may be found. The response includes worker IDs and storage tiers, and can optionally update hit-count statistics for scheduling policies. ## Architecture ```text +------------------+ +----------------------------+ | SGLang | | Bridge | |------------------| |----------------------------| | KV Cache | ZMQ | - subscribe KVEventBatch | | Event Publisher +------->| - decode KV events | | BlockStored | events | - map hash / medium / tier | | BlockRemoved | | - batch report / revoke | | AllBlocksCleared | | | +------------------+ +-------------+--------------+ | | gRPC metadata API v +------------------------+ +-------------+--------------+ | Metadata Store |<-| KV Indexer | |------------------------| |----------------------------| | hash -> worker | | location index | | worker -> tier | | hit-count index | | hit counts | | query API | |------------------------| | | | possible backends: | | | | - in-memory | | | | - Redis | | | | - MySQL / PostgreSQL | | | | - RocksDB | | | +------------------------+ +----------------------------+ ``` The data flow is metadata-only. The bridge sends KV block location updates to the indexer. The indexer stores and serves location metadata. KV bytes remain owned by SGLang workers and are not transferred through the indexer. ## KV Indexer The indexer is a standalone metadata service. Its core responsibility is to maintain KV block location state and expose query APIs. | Function | Description | | --- | --- | | Location update | Record that a worker holds a set of KV block hashes at a specific tier. | | Location revoke | Remove specific hashes, or remove all hashes from a worker at a specific tier. | | Location lookup | Return workers and tiers that may hold requested KV block hashes. | | Hit counting | Optionally count real lookup hits for scheduling or monitoring. | | Store abstraction | Persist metadata in memory, Redis, SQL, RocksDB, or another backend. | The primary data model is: ```text hash -> worker_id -> set<tier> ``` This allows a KV block hash to exist on multiple workers and on multiple tiers of the same worker. ## Bridge The bridge adapts SGLang KV events into indexer metadata operations. The initial implementation will run out of tree, most likely as a sidecar near each SGLang worker. This avoids changes to the SGLang worker process and keeps the indexer deployable independently while the API stabilizes. | Function | Description | | --- | --- | | Event subscription | Subscribe to SGLang ZMQ `KVEventBatch`. | | Event decoding | Decode `BlockStored`, `BlockRemoved`, and `AllBlocksCleared`. | | Tier mapping | Map SGLang storage medium to indexer tier, for example GPU -> HBM, CPU pinned memory -> DRAM, disk -> SSD. | | Hash normalization | Convert SGLang block hashes into the indexer hash format. | | Batching | Group updates by action and tier before sending gRPC requests. | | Observability | Track decode errors, sequence gaps, and report / revoke failures. | Event mapping: | SGLang event | Indexer operation | | --- | --- | | `BlockStored(block_hashes, medium)` | `ReportExternalKvBlocks(hashes, tier)` | | `BlockRemoved(block_hashes, medium)` | `RevokeExternalKvBlocks(hashes, tier)` | | `AllBlocksCleared()` | `RevokeAllExternalKvBlocksAtTier(tier)` for configured tiers | For multi-worker or DP-rank deployments, the bridge can manage multiple event sources. Each source has its own worker ID, endpoint, topic, and sequence tracking. ## Metadata Store The metadata store is the persistence layer behind the indexer. It stores location metadata and optional hit-count data. The indexer should keep the store behind an interface so deployments can choose a backend based on latency, durability, and operational requirements. | Store backend | Suitable use case | | --- | --- | | in-memory | Prototype, single indexer, fastest lookup, no persistence. | | Redis | Shared low-latency metadata service. | | MySQL / PostgreSQL | Durable state, operational visibility, SQL queries. | | RocksDB | Embedded persistent KV store for a single indexer node. | The initial implementation can use an in-memory store and keep the backend abstraction stable. Redis, SQL, or RocksDB can be added later without changing the gRPC API. ## gRPC API The indexer exposes a small set of metadata update and query APIs. The API operates on hashes, worker IDs, and tiers. It does not expose KV bytes. ### API Overview | RPC | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `ReportExternalKvBlocks` | Report that a worker holds hashes at a tier. | | `RevokeExternalKvBlocks` | Remove hashes from a worker at a tier. | | `RevokeAllExternalKvBlocksAtTier` | Remove all hashes for a worker at a tier. | | `MatchExternalKv` | Query which workers and tiers hold requested hashes. | | `GetExternalKvHitCounts` | Query accumulated hit counts for hashes. | ### Proto Sketch ```proto enum TierType { TIER_UNKNOWN = 0; TIER_HBM = 1; TIER_DRAM = 2; TIER_SSD = 3; } service KVIndexer { rpc ReportExternalKvBlocks(worker_id, hashes, tier) returns (Empty); rpc RevokeExternalKvBlocks(worker_id, hashes, tier) returns (Empty); rpc RevokeAllExternalKvBlocksAtTier(worker_id, tier) returns (Empty); rpc MatchExternalKv(hashes, count_as_hit) returns (matches); rpc GetExternalKvHitCounts(hashes) returns (hit_counts); } ``` `MatchExternalKv` returns matches grouped by worker and tier, for example `worker_id -> tier -> hashes`. `GetExternalKvHitCounts` returns `hash -> hit_count_total`. `count_as_hit` is used to distinguish real scheduling lookups from diagnostic queries. When it is true, only matched hashes should increase hit-count statistics. ## Implementation Approach The indexer service will be implemented in Rust. Rust provides near-C++ performance, strong memory and thread-safety guarantees, and a mature async / gRPC ecosystem. This is a good fit for a high-QPS metadata service with concurrent location updates and lookups. The first implementation can use `tonic` for gRPC, `tokio` for async runtime, and an in-memory metadata store. The project should remain out of tree from SGLang and keep the store interface stable so Redis, SQL, or RocksDB backends can be added later without changing the gRPC API. ## Open Questions - Should the out-of-tree bridge remain a sidecar long term, or should parts of it be upstreamed into SGLang after the API stabilizes? - Should the indexer store only block-level hashes initially, or also accept prefix-chain information for future prefix-aware routing? - What consistency guarantees are required between SGLang KV events and indexer metadata? - Which metadata store backend should be recommended for production deployment? ### Related resources _No response_

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool (SWA/HiSparse) has no get_cpu_copy() → decode-mode retract crashes with NotImplementedError (offload is unconditional, not gated on --disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On a **disaggregated (PD) decode** node serving **DeepSeek-V4** (which uses the SWA / HiSparse KV pool `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool`), whenever the KV pool fills up and the scheduler has to **retract** a running request, the process crashes with `NotImplementedError` from `KVCache.get_cpu_copy()`. Root cause: on the decode server, `release_req()` **unconditionally** offloads the retracted request's KV cache to CPU. This offload path is gated only on `disaggregation_mode == "decode"` — it is **not** gated on `--disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache` (which defaults to `False`). The offload calls `token_to_kv_pool_allocator.get_cpu_copy(...)`, but `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool` (a `BaseSWAKVPool` subclass) does **not** implement `get_cpu_copy()`, so it inherits the base `KVCache.get_cpu_copy()` that raises `NotImplementedError`. `MHATokenToKVPool`, `MLATokenToKVPool` and `DSATokenToKVPool` all implement it; the SWA pool does not. Net effect: for DeepSeek-V4 in PD decode mode, **any** KV-full retract crashes the scheduler, even though the user never enabled KV offloading. The only known workaround is to keep KV utilization below the retract threshold (e.g. raise `--mem-fraction-static` to ~0.95 to leave headroom), which merely *avoids* the crash path rather than fixing it. ### Crash chain (file:line on v0.5.14, commit 49e384c) ``` retract_decode() → release_req(req, ..., server_args, ...) python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1606 if server_args.disaggregation_mode == "decode": python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1619 # UNCONDITIONAL: not gated on offload flag req.offload_kv_cache(req_to_token_pool, token_to_kv_pool_allocator) :1620 → Req.offload_kv_cache() python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1485 self.kv_cache_cpu = token_to_kv_pool_allocator.get_cpu_copy(...) :1490 → SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.get_cpu_copy() python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:381 return self._kvcache.get_cpu_copy(indices, mamba_indices=...) :382 → DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool (class BaseSWAKVPool) python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:438 # NO get_cpu_copy override → BaseSWAKVPool(KVCache) python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_swa_memory_pool.py # NO get_cpu_copy override → KVCache.get_cpu_copy() python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:1058 raise NotImplementedError() :1059 ``` Traceback (representative): ``` File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", ... in event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", ... in update_running_batch File ".../sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", ... in retract_decode File ".../sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 1620, in release_req req.offload_kv_cache(req_to_token_pool, token_to_kv_pool_allocator) File ".../sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 1490, in offload_kv_cache self.kv_cache_cpu = token_to_kv_pool_allocator.get_cpu_copy(...) File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py", line 382, in get_cpu_copy return self._kvcache.get_cpu_copy(indices, mamba_indices=mamba_indices) File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 1059, in get_cpu_copy raise NotImplementedError() NotImplementedError ``` ### Reproduction Environment: - Model: DeepSeek-V4 (SWA / HiSparse KV pool), tp8 / dp8, `--enable-dp-attention`. - PD disaggregation, decode server: `--disaggregation-mode decode`. - Natural MTP4 speculative decoding (EAGLE, `--speculative-num-steps 3`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`). - `--disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache` **left at its default `False`** (never set). Trigger: 1. Drive the decode server with a long-input / long-output closed-loop load (e.g. input ~60000, output 1000, `ignore_eos`, high concurrency) so that the KV pool reaches ~100% utilization. 2. When the running decode batch pushes KV usage to the full line, the scheduler calls `retract_decode()` to free space. 3. `retract_decode → release_req → req.offload_kv_cache → allocator.get_cpu_copy → NotImplementedError` → scheduler process dies. Observed: `#running-req` at the CUDA-graph max (e.g. 144), `full token usage == 1.00`, then the crash. It is a race near the KV-full line, not deterministic per seed; higher concurrency / higher accept-length loads hit it sooner. ### Environment - SGLang: v0.5.14 (commit `49e384c`). - Model: DeepSeek-V4 (SWA / HiSparse KV pool, `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool`). - Parallelism: tp8, dp8, `--enable-dp-attention`. - Mode: PD disaggregation, decode server (`--disaggregation-mode decode`), `--disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache` = default `False`. - Speculative decoding: EAGLE / MTP, `--speculative-num-steps 3`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`.

signals.title: [Bug] DSpark speculative decoding cannot start on SM120: decode-dsv4 has no topk=192 instantiation, so verify falls through to the prefill kernel's num_tokens > 64 assert
signals.text: ## Summary On SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), DSpark speculative decoding for DeepSeek-V4-Flash can never start. Every launch dies during CUDA graph capture with: ``` tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: num_tokens > 64 (50 vs. 64) : Decode (num_tokens <= 64) must go through sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv3_2 or sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4; got num_tokens=50 ``` The assertion can never be satisfied, because speculative verify submits `batch x (gamma + 1)` tokens, which is below 64 by construction. ## Root cause FlashInfer instantiates `sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4` only for a fixed `(num_heads, topk)` table (`_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH`). For 64 heads that is `{128, 512, 1024}`. I instrumented `_flash_mla_flashinfer` in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_mla_sm120.py` and logged every call over a full startup. The split is clean: | topk | `_decode_dsv4_dispatchable` | calls | |-----:|---|------:| | 128 | True | 4644 | | **192** | **False** | **4** | Normal decode always arrives with `topk=128` and dispatches to the decode kernel. DSpark's draft attention arrives with `topk=192`, which has no instantiation, so `_decode_dsv4_dispatchable` returns False and the call falls through to `module.sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention`, the prefill orchestrator, whose first check is `num_tokens > 64`. Every other dispatch input is fine: `model_type=_MODEL_TYPE_DSV4`, `d_qk=512`, `kv_pbs=64` after the existing page-split, `num_heads=64`. ## What is *not* the cause - **Not the CUDA graph ladder.** `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` of 1, 2 and 10 all fail identically, only with different token counts (6, 12, 50). - **Not gamma.** `--speculative-dspark-block-size 5` matches the checkpoint's own `dspark_block_size: 5` in `config.json`. - **Not the attention backend.** `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton` clears capture but aborts on the first real prefill. ## Reproduction ``` sglang serve --model-path <DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731> \ --tp-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --max-running-requests 10 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 10 \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 ``` Hardware: 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), PCIe-only, driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.3. SGLang `0.0.0.dev1+ga358374ae`. The same code path is present on `main` today (`flash_mla_sm120.py`, the `_sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention` call after the `B <= _FI_DECODE_MAX_TOKENS` block). ## Fix Two options: 1. Instantiate `decode-dsv4` for `topk=192` in FlashInfer. 2. Have the SGLang shim pad the sparse index up to the next instantiated width and bound the real length with `topk_length`, which the kernel already accepts. I implemented (2) and will open a PR. Measured on the hardware above: | Metric | before | after | |---|---:|---:| | single-stream decode, natural text | 80.8 tok/s | **223.7 tok/s** | | aggregate decode, 10 concurrent | 429.2 tok/s | 465.2 tok/s | | acceptance rate | n/a | 0.62 (accept len 4.10) | Correctness check: padding with two different values (first index vs last index of the row) produces byte-identical output across five deterministic fixtures, which confirms `topk_length` bounds the read and the padding is never consumed.

signals.title: [Bug] sglang 0.5.17 + hierarchical cache + chunked prefill 16K: scheduler hang in DSV4 sparse prefill (watchdog abort) on DeepSeek-V4 FP8 / H20 — plus sampling device-side assert on 0.5.16+PR
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Key launch arguments ``` --tp-size 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 --max-running-requests 64 --page-size 256 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 3.0 --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-mem-layout page_first --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ (speculative_num_steps=1, speculative_eagle_topk=1, speculative_num_draft_tokens=6) ``` Scheduler init line: ``` max_total_num_tokens=9027840, chunked_prefill_size=16384, max_prefill_tokens=32768, max_running_requests=64, context_len=1048576, available_gpu_mem=17.10 GB DSV4 memory calculation: bytes_per_full_token=9259.90, available_bytes=79.15 GB, full_token=9027840 ``` ## Crash A (0.5.17, primary): scheduler hang -> watchdog abort in DSV4 sparse prefill Timeline on 2026-08-08 (hicache ON, chunked_prefill_size=16384): - 12:28:02 server starts on 0.5.17 - 15:02:37 last batch log (decode batches, ~89.9K full tokens, SWA window active) - 15:08:34 all 8 TP ranks: `Scheduler watchdog timeout (self.watchdog_timeout=300, self.soft=False)` - 15:08:53 CUDA coredump attempt (`CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP` was not set), 60s wait - 15:09:53 `kill_process_tree` py-spy dump (`--native`) of the scheduler MainThread — identical shape on all ranks: ``` cuStreamSynchronize (libcuda.so.580.95.05) cudaStreamSynchronize (libcudart.so.13) at::native::_local_scalar_dense_cuda (libtorch_cuda.so) at::native::item / at::_ops::item::call torch::autograd::THPVariable_item (libtorch_python.so) build_swa_token_ids (dsv4/sparse_prefill_utils.py:241) build (dsv4/sparse_prefill_utils.py:333) _forward_prefill_sparse (deepseek_v4_backend.py:1794) forward (deepseek_v4_backend.py:1710) forward (deepseek_v4.py:1287 / 1698 / 2423 / 2615) _execute_extend (runner/eager_runner.py:331) _forward_prefill (dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:412) run_batch (scheduler.py:3594) -> event_loop_overlap -> run_scheduler_process ``` The main thread is blocked in `.item()` inside `build_swa_token_ids`, i.e. `cudaStreamSynchronize` never returns: a kernel enqueued during sparse prefill apparently never completes (device-side hang). The watchdog then aborts all 8 scheduler processes. There is no Python-level exception; the server simply freezes and stops serving. ## Crash B (0.5.16 + PR patches): device-side assert in sampling (NaN/Inf in probs) Observed twice with the same chunked-prefill-16K config: - 2026-08-05 14:15:50, hicache **ON** — preceded by a large prefix-cache hit (`#cached-token: 178176`), matching the signature of issue #33656 (hicache restores target-side KV/SWA but not the DSpark draft-side SWA state -> SWA KV written at wrong positions -> NaN logits). dmesg shows all 8 GPUs raised Xid 43 in cascade. - 2026-08-06 18:02:24, hicache **OFF** — same assert, so the plain radix-cache large-prefix path seems able to trigger it too (or a related SWA/prefix-reuse bug remains). All 8 TP ranks die with: ``` Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed. (_assert_async_cuda_kernel, /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109) ... File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 448, in _forward_prefill ctx_lens = torch.tensor(batch.extend_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered ``` (reported asynchronously at the H2D copy; the asserting kernel is multinomial sampling, i.e. the model produced NaN/Inf logits/probs.) Note: the Aug 5 occurrence looks like issue #33656, whose fix (PR #30393) only landed in 0.5.17. The Aug 6 occurrence had hicache disabled, which #33656 does not explain. ## Previously observed, resolved (for completeness, logs omitted) On 0.5.16 + PR patches we also hit a plain CUDA OOM inside deep_gemm `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (~7 GiB transient workspace). It disappeared after lowering `--mem-fraction-static` and has not recurred; we believe it is unrelated to the two failures above. ## Reproduction notes - Long-context serving workload (tens to hundreds of K tokens per request), high prefix reuse (hicache hits of 100K+ tokens). - Crash A: once on 0.5.17. Crash B: twice on 0.5.16+PR (hicache on and off); not yet seen on 0.5.17, but only one day of traffic so far. - No minimal repro yet. For the next occurrence we will set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP=1`; happy to add extra logging if advised. ## Questions 1. Any known issue in the DSV4 sparse prefill path (`sparse_prefill_utils.build` / `build_swa_token_ids`) that can deadlock/hang the CUDA stream with chunked prefill 16K + hierarchical cache on 0.5.17 (i.e. *with* PR #30393 included)? The `.item()` sync in the hot path also looks fragile — should this be pre-computed on CPU? 2. Crash B on Aug 6 reproduced with hicache OFF, which issue #33656 / PR #30393 does not cover. Is there another known NaN source in the DSV4 / DSPARK prefix-reuse path (0.5.16 era), and is a fix included in 0.5.17? 3. We are also aware of issue #31023 (compact-verify TP8 + overlap IMA instability); we run the default static ragged-verify mode, so it should not apply — but mentioning it in case it is related to Crash A. Full (sanitized) log excerpts attached: `sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt` [sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30889446/sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt) ### Reproduction - Long-context serving workload (tens to hundreds of K tokens per request), high prefix reuse (hicache hits of 100K+ tokens). - Crash A: once on 0.5.17. Crash B: twice on 0.5.16+PR (hicache on and off); not yet seen on 0.5.17, but only one day of traffic so far. - No minimal repro yet. For the next occurrence we will set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP=1`; happy to add extra logging if advised. ### Environment - sglang: **0.5.17** (released 2026-08-08; installed 12:16 and crashed the same day). 0.5.17 includes PR #30393 (HiCache packed/sidecar draft caches, the fix for issue #33656), yet the hang below still occurred with hicache ON. - The two earlier crashes (Aug 5-6) below were on **0.5.16 + local PR patches** (local patches only touch the decode-stage grammar vocab mask; they predate the upstream fix PR #30393). - torch 2.11.0, triton 3.6.0, flashinfer-python 0.6.15.post1, sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11, sglang-kernel 0.4.5, transformers 5.12.1 - GPU: 8x NVIDIA H20-3e (139.80 GiB each), driver 580.95.05 - Model: DeepseekV4ForCausalLM, FP8 weights, KV cache fp8_e4m3, context_len = 1048576 - OS: Linux, Python 3.12

signals.title: [Bug] Prefill FLOPs estimate ignores `prefix_lens`, so `est. prefill TFLOPS/s` degenerates into 1/latency across chunked-prefill chunks
signals.text: ## Checklist - [x] I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help. - [x] The bug has not been fixed in the latest version (checked `main` @ `77c90e7e54`). - [x] Please use English, otherwise it will be closed. ## Describe the bug `SchedulerMetricsReporter._estimate_prefill_perf()` ignores the per-request prefix lengths and collapses all extend tokens in the batch into one fictitious sequence. It only reads `extend_lens` and never consults `batch.prefix_lens`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py#L456-L480 ```python tokens = max(0, int(sum(batch.extend_lens))) if tokens == 0: return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 # Causal prefill token-context product. context_product = tokens * (tokens + 1) / 2.0 flops = ( tokens * self._linear_flops_per_token + self._attn_dot_flops_coeff * context_product ) read_bytes = ( tokens * self._weight_read_bytes_per_token + tokens * self._qkv_act_bytes_per_token + tokens * self._prefill_attn_act_read_per_token ) ``` `extend_lens` is the length of the **current chunk only** — not the cumulative sequence length. See `prepare_for_extend`, where `prefix_lens` and `extend_lens` are built as two separate lists and the invariant is asserted explicitly: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L2364-L2365 ```python prefix_lens = [len(r.prefix_indices) for r in reqs] extend_lens = [r.extend_range.length for r in reqs] ... assert seq_len - pre_len == req.extend_range.length # line 2414 ``` So `batch.prefix_lens` is available on the same object and is simply not used by the estimator. There is a second error in the same formula: for a multi-request batch, applying one triangular number to `sum(extend_lens)` invents attention pairs between different requests. For example, two independent 100-token prefills have `2 × 100 × 101 / 2 = 10,100` causal pairs, while the current code estimates `200 × 201 / 2 = 20,100`. ### Consequence 1: with a fixed chunk size the numerator is a constant The reported value is `flops / gap_latency`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py#L592-L604 ```python flops, _, _ = self._estimate_prefill_perf(batch) tflops_per_s = flops / gap_latency / 1e12 msg += f", est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU): {tflops_per_s:.2f}" ``` Because `flops` depends only on `sum(extend_lens)`, every chunk of a long request under a fixed `--chunked-prefill-size` produces the **exact same numerator**. The log line therefore reduces to ``` est. prefill TFLOPS/s (chunk k) = C / gap_latency_k (C constant) ``` i.e. an inverse-latency plot wearing a TFLOPS label. Later chunks generally take longer as their prefix grows, so the number tends to decay even though the GPU is doing more useful work per chunk. Scheduler jitter, concurrency, and the use of an inter-log wall-clock interval mean strict monotonicity is not guaranteed; the deterministic problem is that the numerator remains constant and the metric is proportional only to `1 / gap_latency`. This is the opposite of the intended signal, and it breaks precisely the "trend analysis" use case the docs recommend the metric for: > These metrics are estimates intended for observability and trend analysis. > — `docs/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx` ### Consequence 2: the dense-attention undercount grows linearly with prefix length For a chunk of `c` tokens at prefix `P`, the true causal pair count is `c·P + c(c+1)/2`, while the code computes `c(c+1)/2`. The undercount factor is ``` 1 + 2P/(c+1) ``` With `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, the attention term is undercounted by ~33x at `P` = 128K, ~65x at 256K, and ~129x at 512K. These factors apply to the attention component, not necessarily to the estimator's total FLOPs, which also includes a prefix-independent linear term. The same defect applies to any prefill served from a prefix-cache hit, not just chunked prefill — a request with a 100K-token cache hit and a 200-token extend is scored as a 200-token prefill from scratch. ### Consequence 3: `read_bytes` omits the prefix KV cache read entirely Every term in the prefill `read_bytes` is `tokens * <per-token constant>`. There is no prefix-dependent KV-cache read term, so prefill contributes no KV-cache read traffic for the cached prefix at all. `sglang:estimated_read_bytes_per_gpu_total` and any MBU derived from it are therefore underestimated for chunked prefill and prefix-cache hits. The size of the error depends on the kernel's tiling and cache reuse, KV layout, cache dtype, and whether the intended metric represents logical traffic or actual HBM traffic. ### Consequence 4: the decode path already does this correctly `_estimate_decode_perf()` right below it uses the full context for both FLOPs and KV read bytes, which suggests the prefill path is an oversight rather than a deliberate simplification: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py#L482-L506 ```python total_context = float(_decode_total_seq_lens(batch)) flops = ( tokens * self._linear_flops_per_token + self._attn_dot_flops_coeff * total_context ) read_bytes = ( ... + total_context * self._kv_cache_bytes_per_token ) ``` Note also that this fallback branch is what essentially every deployment hits: `_prefill_sol_suffix()` is an unconditional `return ""` in the base class (line 507) and no subclass overrides it anywhere in the tree, so the `sol_suffix` short-circuit never fires. ## Observed impact Setup: GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), 8×B300 SXM, TP8, FP8 KV cache, `index_topk=2048`, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--enable-mfu-metrics`. Observed behaviour in this run: `est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU)` fell monotonically across the chunks of a single long request, which initially read as "prefill is becoming memory bound at long context". That interpretation is invalid: with a fixed chunk size the estimated numerator is frozen, so changes in the reported value reflect only changes in the inter-log interval. Other runs need not be strictly monotonic because that interval also contains scheduler and concurrency noise. Analytical/model-based decomposition of one 8192-token chunk (not measured per-kernel timings; absolute times depend on the model configuration and efficiency assumptions): | prefix `P` | chunk time | MoE+linear | sparse MLA attn | DSA indexer GEMM | logits + top-k | KV dequant | reported TFLOPS (rel.) | achieved TFLOPS (rel.) | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 0 | 56 ms | 15.6 ms | 36.6 ms | 2.3 ms | 0.9 ms | 0.0 ms | 1.00 | 1.00 | | 32K | 88 ms | 15.6 ms | 41.9 ms | 20.8 ms | 8.5 ms | 1.0 ms | 0.63 | 0.92 | | 128K | 168 ms | 15.6 ms | 41.9 ms | 76.2 ms | 31.0 ms | 3.3 ms | 0.33 | 0.91 | | 512K | 489 ms | 15.6 ms | 41.9 ms | 297.9 ms | 121.2 ms | 12.5 ms | 0.11 | 0.90 | In this model, the reported metric drops ~9x while the modeled achieved FLOP/s remains within 10%. The modeled growth is dominated by the DSA indexer, which the estimator does not account for. This table illustrates the mechanism; the source-level reproduction above does not depend on these modeled timings. ## Additional gaps in `_init_estimated_perf_constants` (same metric, separate root causes) These are independent of the `prefix_lens` bug but make the absolute magnitude unusable for MLA / MoE / sparse-attention models: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py#L372-L455 1. **MLA is charged using dense MHA/GQA shapes.** `attn_linear_flops` uses `2·hidden·head_dim·(n_q + 2·n_kv) + 2·hidden·head_dim·n_q`. For GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3-class MLA configs, `ModelConfig._derive_model_shapes` sets `head_dim = 256`, while `num_key_value_heads` defaults to `num_attention_heads` when the config does not provide it. This does not represent the actual MLA projection path through fields such as `kv_lora_rank`, `q_lora_rank`, and `qk_rope_head_dim`. For the configuration above it substantially misestimates the projection cost; the magnitude and even the net direction of the full linear-layer error are architecture- and implementation-dependent. 2. **MoE is charged as a dense FFN.** `mlp_flops = 6 · hidden · intermediate_size` uses `hf_text_config.intermediate_size` (the dense width) for all `num_hidden_layers`. The per-token MoE cost is `moe_intermediate_size × num_experts_per_tok` plus shared experts, and `first_k_dense_replace` layers differ from MoE layers. Neither is modeled, so the constant is off by a large factor in an unpredictable direction. 3. **Sparse attention is not modeled.** For DSA/NSA models the main attention is capped at `index_topk` keys per query, so `context_product` should saturate rather than grow — see `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.forward_extend`, which builds a `page_table` of `index_topk` entries per query token, and `SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` (default 2048) which gates the dense path. Conversely, the indexer's `fp8_mqa_logits` scan over the *whole* context is unaccounted for, and because the indexer submodules are `ReplicatedLinear`, that cost is not divided by TP size. At long context this term dominates per-chunk time. ## Reproduction ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <any model> \ --tp-size 8 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --enable-metrics --enable-mfu-metrics \ --context-length 262144 ``` Send one long request (e.g. 128K input tokens) and watch the `Prefill batch` log lines for that request: ``` Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 8192, ..., est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU): <A> Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 8192, ..., est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU): <B> Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 8192, ..., est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU): <C> ... ``` In an otherwise idle single-request run, the values will typically trend downward while `#new-token` stays at 8192 on every line. Strict `A > B > C > ...` ordering is not required to reproduce the estimator bug because `gap_latency` is an asynchronous scheduler interval. Two checks that isolate the bug from any real hardware effect: 1. Multiplying each line's reported TFLOPS by that line's inter-log interval yields the same product, up to log rounding — confirming the numerator is constant across equal-sized chunks. 2. Send a request with a ~100% prefix-cache hit plus a short extend. The reported TFLOPS is computed purely from the extend length and ignores the cached prefix the attention kernels actually read. ## Suggested fix Minimal correctness fix — use the `prefix_lens` that is already on the batch, and add the missing KV read term: ```python def _estimate_prefill_perf(self, batch) -> Tuple[float, float, float]: if batch is None or batch.extend_lens is None: return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 extend_lens = batch.extend_lens prefix_lens = batch.prefix_lens or [0] * len(extend_lens) tokens = 0 context_product = 0.0 context_kv_tokens = 0.0 for c, p in zip(extend_lens, prefix_lens): if c <= 0: continue tokens += c # Causal pairs for this request: chunk-vs-prefix plus chunk-vs-chunk. context_product += c * p + c * (c + 1) / 2.0 # One possible logical-traffic convention: count one stream of the KV # context per chunk. This is not a measurement of actual HBM traffic. context_kv_tokens += p + c / 2.0 if tokens == 0: return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 flops = ( tokens * self._linear_flops_per_token + self._attn_dot_flops_coeff * context_product ) read_bytes = ( tokens * self._weight_read_bytes_per_token + tokens * self._qkv_act_bytes_per_token + tokens * self._prefill_attn_act_read_per_token + context_kv_tokens * self._kv_cache_bytes_per_token ) ... ``` `prefix_lens` is safe to zip against `extend_lens`: both are assigned together in `prepare_for_extend` and both are appended in parallel by `mix_with_running`, which pushes the running request's full context into `prefix_lens` alongside its `[1] * running_bs` extend entry. So the same patch also fixes mixed prefill+decode batches, where today the appended decode tokens contribute `1` to `context_product` and nothing to the KV read. The per-request attention pair-count above is exact for standard dense causal self-attention; it is not an exact whole-model FLOPs estimate and does not apply unchanged to sparse attention. The KV `read_bytes` term is only one possible logical-traffic convention, and maintainers should first define what the metric is intended to represent. `p + c/2` approximates one stream of the logical KV context per chunk, while using `context_product` models one KV-vector read per query/key pair, similar to the convention used by `_estimate_decode_perf`. Neither necessarily equals actual HBM traffic: real traffic depends on query tiling, on-chip and L2 reuse, fused paths, the model-specific KV layout, and cache dtype. Either convention at least accounts for the currently omitted prefix, but it should be documented explicitly. Two follow-ups worth considering, either here or as separate work: - Cap the per-query context at `index_topk` for sparse-attention models and add the indexer scan term, so DSA/NSA numbers stop being dominated by unmodeled work. `ModelConfig` already exposes `index_head_dim` / the DSA fields needed for this. - Make `_linear_flops_per_token` MoE- and MLA-aware (`moe_intermediate_size`, `num_experts_per_tok`, `n_shared_experts`, `first_k_dense_replace`, `kv_lora_rank`, `q_lora_rank`), or otherwise document that the absolute value is not meaningful for these architectures. Separately, dividing by `gap_latency` is documented in-code as a known mismatch (the comment at lines 592-597 notes it is "decoupled from this forward's execution"). Since `_prefill_sol_suffix` never returns content in-tree, that caveat applies to every deployment. Using the device-timer span when `ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER` is set would make the wall-clock branch meaningful too. ## Environment - SGLang: `main` @ `77c90e7e54` (also present in v0.5.17, v0.5.16, v0.5.15; introduced in #19395 "MFU metrics in Prometheus" and carried through the `SchedulerMetricsReporter` refactor) - Model: GLM-5.2 NVFP4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), 78 layers, 64 heads, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, `index_topk=2048` - Hardware: 8× B300 SXM, TP8 - The defect is architecture-independent and reviewable from the source alone; the GLM-5.2/DSA details only affect how large the discrepancy gets.

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention indexer (`fp8_paged_mqa_logits`) illegal memory access with long-context requests
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Summary Serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on sglang 0.5.17 (8x H100, TP=8), the server reliably crashes with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` inside the sparse attention indexer's `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` DeepGEMM kernel when a long-context request (roughly 80K–130K input tokens) reaches its first decode step. It looks related to #26427 and #21532, but those are filed under HiSparse specifically; this reproduces without it. All 8 TP ranks crash simultaneously with the identical traceback, and the bug is 100% reproducible by sending a single long-context request to a freshly started server — no concurrency needed. ## Investigation notes (ruling out other causes) We went through several false leads before isolating this, noting them here in case they're useful: - **Not speculative decoding**: reproduces with `--speculative-algorithm` entirely unset (no DSpark/EAGLE). - **Not CUDA graphs, structurally**: with CUDA graphs enabled (default), the crash is instead first detected inside `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py` → `full_cuda_graph_backend.py:129` (`self._graphs[shape_key].replay()`), and in other runs at essentially random subsequent CUDA API calls (`torch.cat`, `TensorImpl::~TensorImpl()` during a stream-capture-status check, `result.copy_done.synchronize()`), consistent with CUDA's async error reporting ("CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call"). This made it look like a CUDA-graph-replay or radix-cache bug. Only after combining `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` with `--disable-cuda-graph` did the traceback resolve to the true origin below — and the crash still occurs with `--disable-cuda-graph`, ruling out CUDA graphs as the root cause. ## Traceback (with `--disable-cuda-graph`) ``` File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3594, in run_batch batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation( File ".../sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 593, in forward_batch_generation out = self.model_runner.forward( File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1614, in _forward_raw ret = self.eager_runner.execute( File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py", line 244, in _execute_decode return model_runner.model.forward( File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 2423, in forward hidden_states, prev_residual, prev_post, prev_comb = layer( File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1698, in forward hidden_states = self.self_attn( File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1241, in forward q, kv = self._forward_prepare( File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1157, in _forward_prepare self.indexer( File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 961, in forward return attn_backend.forward_c4_indexer( File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 774, in forward_c4_indexer logits = fn( File ".../deep_gemm/__init__.py", line 207, in fp8_paged_mqa_logits return _C.fp8_paged_mqa_logits(q, kv_cache, weights, context_lens, block_table, schedule_meta, max_context_len, clean_logits, indices) File "python/tvm_ffi/cython/function.pxi", line 968, in tvm_ffi.core.Function.__call__ tvm.error.InternalError: CUDA driver error (/deepgemm/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/runtime_utils.hpp:144): 700 (CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS, an illegal memory access was encountered) ``` One of the 8 ranks instead surfaced a secondary/cascading symptom (the CUDA context on that rank was likely already poisoned by the same root fault before its next CUDA call): ``` File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 679, in forward_c4_indexer q_indexer, weights = self._forward_prepare_normal( File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 468, in _forward_prepare_normal weights = c4_indexer.compute_weights(x, skip_scale=True) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 946, in compute_weights out, _ = self.weights_proj(x) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 282, in forward output = self.quant_method.apply(self, x, bias) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py", line 255, in apply return F.linear(x, layer.weight, bias) RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED when calling `cublasGemmEx(...)` ``` ## Expected behavior Long-context single requests (well within the configured `--context-length 262144`) should not crash the server via illegal memory access in the sparse attention indexer. ## Related issues - #26427 — DeepSeek-V4 HiSparse crashes/wedges with multiple long-context requests (same `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` / C4 indexer path, but filed with `--enable-hisparse` on; this report reproduces without it) - #21532 — CUDA illegal memory access when enabling HiSparse on disaggregated decode node with long prompts ### Reproduction ## Launch command ```bash sglang serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp-size 8 --max-running-requests 256 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.82 --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 16}' \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --context-length 262144 --allow-auto-truncate \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash-0731 --trust-remote-code --log-level debug --enable-metrics ``` ### Environment - sglang: 0.5.17 - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 - Hardware: 8x H100, single node - `flashinfer` version: 0.6.15.post1 1. Start the server fresh (cold start). 2. Send a single request (concurrency = 1) with ~80K+ input tokens. 3. The server crashes on all 8 TP ranks as soon as the request transitions from prefill to its first decode step. Observed with real production traffic (a single ~130K-token request, first request after server startup).

signals.title: [Feature] Bit-exact correctness coverage for Unified Radix Cache
signals.text: ## Motivation Cache correctness is difficult to verify from model output alone. A corrupted KV block or recurrent-state checkpoint can still produce fluent text, and the resulting numerical drift can remain far below the tolerance used by accuracy and KL tests. These failures have shipped because the existing signals are approximate. Bit-exact logprob consistency turns one of these approximate signals into a correctness oracle. `kl_test_utils` evaluates the same token through prefill and decode. If both paths are batch-invariant and compute the same function, they must produce identical logprobs. Once that baseline is established, the contract for every cache-reuse path becomes: > **Any nonzero KL is a KV/state reuse bug.** This is stronger than threshold-based testing. It does not ask whether the error is large enough to matter to a benchmark. It asks whether restoring cached state is exactly equivalent to recomputing it. Bugs that previously sat below a model-specific noise floor become unambiguous regressions. Examples: - Incorrect reused state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29792 ## Foundation Bit-exactness depends on the model and execution path. Deterministic inference can remove batch-dependent kernel and communication behavior, but it cannot make two mathematically different algorithms identical. For example, Qwen3-Next uses different GDN kernels for prefill and decode, and retains a nonzero numerical floor. Inkling provides the combination needed for continuous gating. Its prefill and decode paths compute the same function, so under deterministic inference its prefill-versus-decode KL is exactly `0`. A shrunken checkpoint runs on one GPU. The model also contains `FULL`, `SWA`, and `MAMBA` cache components, so one test process exercises full KV, sliding-window, and recurrent-state reuse together. The resulting foundation has four layers: 1. deterministic execution makes repeated computation batch-invariant; 2. logprob consistency establishes an exact prefill/decode baseline; 3. cache tests apply that baseline to each state restoration path; 4. revert-then-red validation proves that each regression guard can detect the defect it claims to cover. Supporting work: - Inkling deterministic execution: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33417, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34159 - Workflow tools: [KL consistency test skill](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/.claude/skills/kl-consistency-test), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34169 - Real-weight consistency coverage: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34168, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34356 - Per-commit guards: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34607 - Calibration and follow-up validation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653 ## Roadmap The remaining work is coverage, not a new testing method. Every feature that can save, move, or restore model state introduces a distinct correctness boundary and needs its own exact-KL test class. - [x] Base cache path - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer` - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer_lazy` - [x] HiCache multi-turn - [ ] Speculative decoding - [x] MTP - [ ] DSpark / DFlash @alphabetc1 - Support return_logprob https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35058 - [ ] Unified memory
