signals.title: [Bug] Kimi K3 decode crash: DSPARK target_verify + DCP → cumsum(extend_prefix_lens=None) in layers/dcp/planner.py
signals.text: ## Summary On Kimi K3, the **decode** side crashes deterministically when running **PD disaggregation + DCP (`--dcp-size 8`) + DSPARK speculative decoding** together. The first target-verify batch hits `dcp/planner.py` with `extend_prefix_lens=None` and all TP ranks die with `TypeError: cumsum(): argument 'input' (position 1) must be Tensor, not NoneType`. Each pair works on its own (DCP without DSPARK; DSPARK without DCP). Only the combination fails. ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260814-c4271c3f` (commit `c4271c3f`) - Model: Kimi K3 (hybrid: 69 KDA linear-attention layers + 24 MLA layers) - Topology: 1P1D PD disaggregation (Mooncake transfer backend), single node per side, 8 GPUs (B300) - Decode-side launch args (relevant): `--tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 --enable-linear-replayssm-spec --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake` - Prefill side runs the same image with `--tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 --disaggregation-mode prefill` and stays alive; only the decode side crashes. ## Reproduction 1. Start prefill and decode with the args above. 2. Send any chat completion request through the router. 3. As soon as the decode side runs its first DSPARK target-verify batch, all ranks crash (in our case 26 minutes after process start, on first real traffic). ## Stack trace (all 8 TP ranks, identical) ``` Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5058, in run_scheduler_process scheduler.run_event_loop() File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4920, in dispatch_event_loop scheduler.event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode() File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py", line 2217, in event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode batch_result = self.run_batch(batch) File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3691, in run_batch batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation( File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 424, in forward_batch_generation return self._forward_decode(batch, on_publish, grammar_barrier) File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 673, in _forward_decode target_verify = self._verify_executor.run_non_compact( File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py", line 258, in run_non_compact result = self._forward_prepared_verify( File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py", line 288, in _forward_prepared_verify target_out = self.target_worker.forward_batch_generation( File ".../sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 609, in forward_batch_generation out = self.model_runner.forward( File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1742, in _forward_raw ret = self.eager_runner.execute( File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py", line 282, in _execute_extend model_runner.model.prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp( File ".../sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py", line 3383, in prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp return self.language_model.prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp( File ".../sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py", line 2826, in prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp return prepare_decode_context_parallel_metadata( File ".../sglang/srt/layers/dcp/planner.py", line 63, in prepare_decode_context_parallel_metadata extend_cu_prefix_lens[1:] = torch.cumsum(extend_prefix_lens, dim=0) TypeError: cumsum(): argument 'input' (position 1) must be Tensor, not NoneType ``` ## Root cause analysis - `eager_runner._execute_extend` calls `prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp` unconditionally whenever `dcp_size > 1` and the batch needs forward-metadata init, passing `forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens` straight through. - The DSPARK **target-verify** batch built by `dspark_verify.run_non_compact` never populates `extend_prefix_lens` (verify tokens are not an "extend with prefix" in the usual sense), so the planner receives `None` and crashes on `torch.cumsum`. - The DCP+DSpark support merged in #32828/#33149 covered the tokenspeed MLA backend and draft-KV pool layout, but the non-compact verify path through the DCP planner has no `None` guard. Possible fixes: guard `extend_prefix_lens is None` in `prepare_decode_context_parallel_metadata` (e.g. treat verify batches as zero-prefix), or populate the field when the verify batch is constructed in `dspark_verify.run_non_compact`. ## Related work - #34343 (WIP) tracks **PD disaggregation + DCP + DSPARK**, but fixes a *different* failure point in that combination (draft KV geometry in `send_kvcache_dcp`). This issue is a second, independent bug in the same combination. - #33863 tracks PP + PD + DSpark.

signals.title: [Bug] DSPARK silently corrupts identifiers on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, making speculative decoding unsafe
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug

Summary

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, SGLang’s DSPARK speculative decoding silently introduces single-character corruptions into identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt:

kimi-k3 → kimi-kw nova-x7 → nova-7 apollo-n9 → apollo-n11

The same server, weights, prompts, and launch configuration—with only speculative decoding disabled—produces zero such corruptions across thousands of grounded identifier tokens.

The corruption rate increases with the DSPARK verify-window width:

--speculative-dspark-block-size | speculative_num_draft_tokens | Temp 0 | Temp 1 -- | -- | -- | -- 6 | 7 | 1.03% | 0.82% 5 | 6 | 0.32% | 0.77% 1 | 2 | 0.00% | 0.00% Speculation disabled | — | 0.00% | 0.00%

Aggregated across both block_size=1 runs:

  • Temperature 0: 0 / 4561
  • Temperature 1: 0 / 3701

Using the rule of three, the corresponding approximate 95% upper bounds are:

  • Temperature 0: <0.066%
  • Temperature 1: <0.081%

This contrasts with the 1.03% observed rate at block_size=6, temperature 0.

Examples of corrupted identifiers

Malformed forms observed at block_size=6, temperature 0:

kimi-kw -> kimi-k3 (x5) kimi-k2 -> kimi-k3 (x3) kimi-k7 -> kimi-k3 (x2) apollo-n11 -> apollo-n9 (x2) nova-12 -> nova-x7 (x2) wq-7f2e -> wq-7f2b (x2) kimi-kw2 -> kimi-k3 kimi-v2 -> kimi-k3 kimi-k11 -> kimi-k3 apollo-n12 -> apollo-n9 nova-7 -> nova-x7 nova-v7 -> nova-x7 wq-7f2e2 -> wq-7f2b

These are not malformed responses or obvious decoding failures. They are plausible-looking, single-character-wrong identifiers embedded in otherwise normal output.

Expected behavior

At temperature 0, DSPARK should emit the same greedy token sequence as the target model without speculative decoding.

A draft token should only be committed if it matches the corresponding target prediction. On mismatch, DSPARK should emit the target prediction instead.

Therefore, enabling DSPARK should not change grounded identifiers from:

kimi-k3

to:

kimi-kw

when the non-speculative target forward selects the correct token.

Actual behavior

With multi-position DSPARK verification enabled:

  • Grounded identifiers are silently corrupted.
  • The issue reproduces at temperature 0.
  • The issue requires or is strongly amplified by heterogeneous concurrent batching.
  • The rate increases with verify-window width.
  • No request error or warning is produced.
  • The finish reason remains normal.
  • Disabling speculation eliminates the corruption.
  • Reducing DSPARK to block_size=1 eliminates the corruption.

Hypotheses investigated and ruled out

1. Lossy accept/verify rule

This does not appear to be the cause.

Both accept_greedy and accept_greedy_triton in:

sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/dspark/dspark_accept.py

delegate to compute_dflash_correct_drafts_and_bonus in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py

The relevant logic is:

matches = candidates[:, 1:] == target_predict[:, :-1] correct_len = matches.to(torch.int32).cumprod(dim=1).sum(dim=1) bonus = target_predict[torch.arange(bs, ...), correct_len]

Every committed token should therefore be either:

  1. An accepted draft token that compared equal to target_predict; or
  2. The bonus token, which is taken directly from target_predict.

A mismatching draft token should not be able to leak into the output.

This implies that the corrupted emitted tokens are likely themselves present in target_predict. In other words, the target verify forward appears to be producing incorrect logits or incorrect token alignment.

2. Ragged verify-window misalignment

accept_greedy performs:

torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( bs, verify_num_draft_tokens )

A dense reshape could misalign tokens if requests had different verify lengths.

However, SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE defaults to static. In static mode, resolve_ragged_verify_layout returns None, and verify lengths are uniform.

Therefore, the rectangular reshape is expected to be valid for this reproduction.

3. Numerical noise or batch-shape-dependent reductions

We tested three separate interventions. Each was verified to engage, and none removed the corruption.

FP32 LM head

Enabled:

--enable-fp32-lm-head

Engagement was confirmed empirically:

  • Before the change, 65.5% of recorded margins fell on the 0.25 BF16 grid.
  • After the change, 0% did.
  • There were zero exact ties across 34,420 records.

The typo rate did not improve.

Deterministic FP32 MoE reduction

We forced:

use_atomic_add = False

so the already-passed:

use_fp32_reduce = True

would engage.

In:

sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_wna16_marlin.py

the FP32 temporary buffer is allocated only under:

if use_fp32_reduce and not use_atomic_add:

This provides a structural confirmation that the path was active.

The observed rates remained approximately:

  • Temperature 0: 1.03%
  • Temperature 1: 0.82%

Tie epsilon on sampled accept path

Adding a tie epsilon to the sampled acceptance path had no effect.

More generally, an identifier repeated verbatim several times in the prompt should usually be a high-margin prediction. Low-order numerical noise would not be expected to repeatedly transform such identifiers into plausible alternatives.

The non-speculative control also varies in free-form prose between temperature-0 runs—likely due to prefix-cache or chunked-prefill effects—but it never corrupts a grounded identifier.

4. Draft/target gamma mismatch

The CLI can override the draft checkpoint’s declared gamma with only a warning:

DSpark gamma mismatch: using gamma=6 (from speculative_num_draft_tokens=7) but draft config block_size=5.

This occurs in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_config.py

The draft module itself obtains gamma from the checkpoint:

self.gamma = int(dspark_config.resolve_gamma(...))

in:

sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py

This means the draft module and worker may disagree about the verify-window width.

However, running with block_size=5:

  • Makes the configured values agree
  • Removes the warning
  • Still reproduces the bug

Observed rates at block_size=5 were:

  • Temperature 0: 0.32%
  • Temperature 1: 0.77%

Therefore, the gamma mismatch is not the root cause of this corruption, although the silent override may be worth hardening as a separate issue.

5. Draft-side kernels

SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL only gates the draft forward.

Under a correct speculative verification rule, draft quality may affect acceptance and performance, but it should not affect temperature-0 correctness. Incorrect draft tokens should be rejected in favor of the target prediction.

Therefore, a draft-only kernel failure does not explain committed token corruption unless there is also a target-verification or alignment bug.

Suspected fault area

The following is a hypothesis, not yet a verified root cause.

Given that:

  1. The accept rule appears to emit only target_predict;
  2. The corruption reproduces at temperature 0;
  3. The corruption disappears at a two-position verify window;
  4. The rate generally increases with verify-window width;
  5. Multiple numerical-determinism interventions had no effect; and
  6. The issue depends on concurrent heterogeneous batching,

the likely fault is in the target verify forward for multi-position DSPARK verification, especially for in-block positions t >= 1.

Potential areas include:

  • Intra-block causal masking
  • Position-ID construction or indexing
  • KV-cache placement for draft positions
  • Request-to-token mapping under heterogeneous batching
  • CUDA graph replay metadata for TARGET_VERIFY
  • Batch-slot reuse or stale per-request metadata
  • dsv4 attention behavior during multi-token verification

The current evidence suggests the target verification pass is computing incorrect logits or associating correct logits with the wrong request/position.

We have not yet isolated the specific kernel or metadata transition.

Suggested next diagnostics

A useful first datapoint would be:

--speculative-dspark-block-size 2

This would help distinguish between:

  • Failure beginning at the first genuinely multi-position verify step; and
  • Error probability accumulating with larger verify windows.

Other useful comparisons may include:

  1. DSPARK with CUDA graphs disabled.
  2. DSPARK with the hierarchical cache disabled.
  3. DSPARK with radix cache and chunked prefill disabled.
  4. An alternate attention backend, if DeepSeek-V4-Flash supports one.
  5. Capturing target_predict before acceptance and comparing it against independent one-token target forwards.
  6. Logging request IDs, verify positions, position IDs, and KV locations for the first divergent token.

Workaround

Both of the following avoid the observed corruption:

Option 1: Disable speculative decoding

This is the safest workaround.

Option 2: Use block_size=1

--speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1

This produced zero true typos across:

  • 4,561 grounded identifiers at temperature 0
  • 3,701 grounded identifiers at temperature 1

However, this sacrifices most of the speculative speedup, so it is a mitigation rather than a practical fix.

Until the multi-position verification issue is resolved, DSPARK should not be used with DeepSeek-V4-Flash for workloads where exact token reproduction matters.

Reproduction notes

DeepGEMM JIT warmup

Changing:

--speculative-dspark-block-size

changes num_tokens_per_req and invalidates the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache.

The first launch after changing this value may compile approximately 16,000 shapes and exceed a 3,600-second readiness budget. If the process is killed during warmup, it may look like an unrelated startup failure.

Please allow additional warmup time when changing the block size.

Log probabilities unavailable

DSPARK currently rejects:

"return_logprob": true

with:

DFLASH speculative decoding does not support return_logprob yet

Therefore, per-token target margins cannot currently be collected over HTTP on the affected speculative arm.

Severity

This is a silent data-corruption issue, not only a quality or performance regression.

The generated response is well-formed, and the corrupted identifier often looks plausible. Downstream systems therefore have no reliable way to distinguish the incorrect value from an intended value.

For DeepSeek-V4-Flash, this makes multi-position DSPARK speculative decoding unsafe for exact-identifier and tool-use workloads.

### Reproduction

Reproduction

The corruption usually requires concurrent, heterogeneous batching. A single request in isolation may not reproduce it. The script below sends four byte-identical target requests and four variable-length distractor requests per round.

1. Launch the affected DSPARK configuration

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \ --tp 4 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 6 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

2. Save the reproduction script

Save the following code as dspark_typo_repro.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Concurrency typo probe for one model and temperature.""" import collections import concurrent.futures import json import os import re import time import urllib.error import urllib.request MODEL = os.environ["TEST_MODEL"] TEMP = float(os.environ.get("TEST_TEMP", "0")) ROUNDS = int(os.environ.get("TEST_ROUNDS", "30")) BASE = os.environ.get("TEST_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:30000") URL = f"{BASE}/v1/chat/completions" IDS = [ "kimi-k3", "nova-x7", "atlas-j9", "wq-7f2b", "zeta-r1", "apollo-n9", ] CTX = " ".join( f"event{i}=ok latency={i % 37}ms owner=team{i % 9}" for i in range(350) ) PROMPT = ( f"Analyze this deployment history and write a 6-section operational report. " f"{CTX}\n" f"Canonical identifiers: {', '.join(IDS)}. " "Include a table and prose recap. " "Use every identifier at least four times, always verbatim; " "do not invent or normalize identifiers." ) RX = re.compile(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*-[a-z0-9]+", re.I) def lev(a, b): prev = list(range(len(b) + 1)) for i, x in enumerate(a, 1): cur = [i] for j, y in enumerate(b, 1): cur.append( min( cur[-1] + 1, prev[j] + 1, prev[j - 1] + (x != y), ) ) prev = cur return prev[-1] def ask(prompt=PROMPT, max_tokens=700, retries=5): body = json.dumps( { "model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": TEMP, "top_p": 1.0, } ).encode() for n in range(retries): request = urllib.request.Request( URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=300) as response: result = json.load(response) return result["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or "" except urllib.error.HTTPError as error: if error.code not in (429, 503) or n + 1 == retries: raise time.sleep(0.3 * (n + 1)) raise RuntimeError("retries exhausted") wrong = collections.Counter() truncations = collections.Counter() error_types = collections.Counter() exact = 0 grounded = 0 responses = 0 errors = 0 typo_responses = 0 started = time.time() with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool: for rnd in range(ROUNDS): futures = [pool.submit(ask) for _ in range(4)] # Variable-length distractors perturb server-side batch composition. for j in range(4): length = 50 + ((rnd * 67 + j * 97) % 500) distractor = "Summarize: " + " ".join( f"word{k}" for k in range(length) ) futures.append(pool.submit(ask, distractor, 128)) for future in futures[:4]: try: text = future.result() responses += 1 except Exception as error: errors += 1 error_types[type(error).__name__] += 1 continue response_has_typo = False for token in ( match.lower().rstrip(".,;:") for match in RX.findall(text) ): if token in IDS: exact += 1 grounded += 1 continue distance, target = min( (lev(token, identifier), identifier) for identifier in IDS ) if distance <= 2: grounded += 1 if any(identifier.startswith(token) for identifier in IDS): # Prefixes are output-limit truncations, not typos. truncations[(token, target, distance)] += 1 else: wrong[(token, target, distance)] += 1 response_has_typo = True typo_responses += response_has_typo for future in futures[4:]: try: future.result() except Exception: pass print( f"MODEL={MODEL} TEMP={TEMP} rounds={ROUNDS} " f"responses={responses} errors={errors} " f"errtypes={dict(error_types)} " f"elapsed={time.time() - started:.1f}s" ) print( f"grounded_ids={grounded} exact={exact} " f"true_typos={sum(wrong.values())} " f"typo_responses={typo_responses} " f"rate={(sum(wrong.values()) / grounded if grounded else 0):.4%} " f"truncations={sum(truncations.values())}" ) print("typo_forms:", dict(wrong.most_common(20)) or "NONE")

A true typo is a token with Levenshtein distance 1–2 from a canonical identifier that is not a prefix of one. Prefixes are counted separately as output-limit truncations.

3. Run the reproduction at temperature 0

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \ TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ TEST_TEMP=0 \ TEST_ROUNDS=30 \ python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

4. Repeat at temperature 1

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \ TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ TEST_TEMP=1 \ TEST_ROUNDS=30 \ python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

5. Run the non-speculative control

Relaunch the server with all --speculative-* flags removed while leaving every other launch argument unchanged. Repeat both commands above. This control produced zero true typos.

6. Test the block-size workaround

Relaunch DSPARK with a block size of 1: 

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \ --tp 4 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

Repeat the temperature-0 and temperature-1 tests. This configuration also produced zero true typos.

Expected result

At temperature 0, DSPARK should produce the same greedy token sequence as non-speculative decoding. All identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt should be emitted without modification.

Observed result

With --speculative-dspark-block-size 6, the output silently contains plausible single-character corruptions such as: 

kimi-k3 -> kimi-kw nova-x7 -> nova-7 apollo-n9 -> apollo-n11 wq-7f2b -> wq-7f2e

In one temperature-0 run, 23 of 2,224 grounded identifiers were corrupted (1.0342%), affecting 15 of 120 target responses. The same test produced zero corruptions with speculative decoding disabled and with DSPARK block size 1.

Reproduction note

Changing --speculative-dspark-block-size changes num_tokens_per_req and may invalidate the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache. The first launch after changing the block size can require a long recompilation warmup. Allow enough startup time to prevent the server from being killed before it becomes ready.

### Environment Run this **inside the same Python environment/container used to launch the affected SGLang server**: ```bash python3 -m sglang.check_env 2>&1 | tee sglang_check_env.txt ``` Then paste the **complete command output verbatim** into that field, preferably wrapped as: ```text ``` Do not substitute the manually listed environment details; the maintainers explicitly require the actual `check_env` output.

signals.title: AMD Development Roadmap (2026 Q3)
signals.text: # AMD SGLang Roadmap — 2026 Q3 *Contributions and feedback are welcome*. [Join SGLang Slack channel](https://sgl-fru7574.slack.com/archives/C09TPAM1N68). ## Focus - **New Hardware support & higher performance**: Helios rack scale system, MI45x (gfx1250) GPUs, Ryzen AI Halo (gfx1151/1152) platform. - **Upstream Feature compatibility & reliability**: Full compatibility and production-level reliability across P/D disaggregation, all parallelisms, speculative decoding, HiCache/HiSparse/UMBP, and load balancing on AMD Instinct GPUs (MI30x, MI35x and MI45x). - **Usability**: Easy installation on AMD; simple large-scale deployment (k8s, OME). - **Kernel optimization**: For current and next-gen hardware, pursue better performance and higher feature velocity through Triton, FBTriton, TileLang, FlyDSL, HipKittens. - **Reinforcement learning**: Framework integration and training-inference optimizations with Miles, slime. - **Multimodal**: Enhance diffusion models for video, image and 3D generation, enable more data types for performance with gen quality. SGLang-Omni support. ## New Feature and Performance Improvements - **New Platforms and performance** Goals: Extending SGLang to SOTA hardware, demonstrating unparalleled performance, quality and convenience. - Helios rack system: scale up, scale in and scale out - Instinct flagship GPUs: MI45x (gfx1250) series - Ryzen AI Strix/Gorgon Halo local AI platforms, Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395/495 laptops, gfx1151/1152 series - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33939 - **New SOTA Models and performance** Goals: Demonstrating excellent Day-0 support to frontier models and rapid performance ramp-up. - DeepSeek-V4+ - MiniMax-M3 - Kimi-K3 - Qwen3.8 - GLM-5.2 - **New benchmark and performance** Goals: Empowering Agentic AI with realistic benchmarks to drive system performance. - AgentX - **General features and performance** Goals: Add new models, new AI operators support. Fully distributed inference support to all workloads, on top of full support of new features and enablement with competitive performance defined in general roadmap. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22949 - **MoRI** Goals: Extend distributed inference, hierarchical cache, and disaggregated serving capabilities on AMD platforms. - **UMBP** - Expand UMBP support for frontier reasoning models, including Kimi-K3. - Implement HiCache Indexer for scalable cache management. - Add support for the new SGLang Connector. - **MoRI-EP v2** - Implement next-generation intra-node Expert Parallelism (EP v2). - Integrate MoRI-EP v2 into SGLang distributed inference. - Enable support for major MoE models through the EP v2 runtime. - **MI45x (gfx1250) Enablement** - Enable MoRI-EP on MI45x (gfx1250). - Support DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.x, and future MoE models. - Enable MoRI-IO on MI45x (gfx1250). - Enable SGLang Prefill/Decode Disaggregation on MI45x platforms. - **Distributed Inference** Goal: DI for all major models (DPSKvX, Qwen3.X, GLM-5X, Kimi-K2.X, MiniMax-M2.X, GPT-OSS) on Helios, multi-nodes - **Speculative Decoding** Goal: SD/MTP for all major models (DPSKvX, Qwen3.X, GLM-5X, Kimi-K2.X, MiniMax-M2.X, GPT-OSS) on ROCm - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23388 (@zhentaocc) - **Attention Kernels & MxFP4 KV Cache** Goals: Improve attention performance with bounded accuracy, on FP8/MxFP4 dtype for Matmul and KV cache - Optimize FP8 attention kernels for NSA/DSA models — including improving the existing tilelang implementation, potential rewrites using triton or flyDSL, and subsequent configuration tuning for better performance - Explore MXFP4 KV cache support for NSA/DSA models to reduce memory footprint. - Explore MXFP4 attention kernels for NSA/DSA models to improve inference throughput with minimal accuracy loss. - **Context parallelism** Goal: Context Parallelism (CP) on ROCm - Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) on ROCm. - Support triton backend decode context parallel for Qwen3.5. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25090 (@IzacharyI @At1a8) - Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) for MLA models. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19975 - **Multimodal** - Diffusion Transformer Models - SGLang-Omni - **Upstream CI** Goal: Improve coverage, runner health, passing rate & fix turn-around. - MI45x runners instantiate - Instantiate multi-nodes Distributed Inference CI for PD/D & wide-EP. - Improve end to end image build/release & PR test workflow, CI regression detection and analysis with AI assistance. - Enhance current AMD CI Bot for improved daily report and analysis, from per-job failure triage to a true daily quality dashboard for the AMD CI fleet. Enhance AMD CI Job monitoring for better runner/job status and queue time analysis. - **Kernel, fusion & Optimizations** Goals: Performance boost - Add FBTriton support - Extending Kernels and Kernel Fusions with Triton, FBTriton, TileLang, FlyDSL, etc. - **Quantization and Quark** Goals: Performance Improvement with Assured Accuracy - Enable higher performance for SOTA models with Quark quant introduced to specific layer/ops, dynamic weight quant at loading, NVFP4 to MxFP4 weight conversion (dequant and quant) for models interop. - Quantization for Diffusion models, Sage Attention with MxFP4. - **Post-Training/RL support - Miles** Goals: Drive performance Improvement and optimal integration with post-train RL framework: Miles - Miles AMD Q3 Roadmap: https://github.com/radixark/miles/issues/2025 - Automate integrated build, nightly and PR CIs with Miles. - **Documentation & Recipes** Goals: Maintain clear and up-to-date documentation, recipes, cookbook, utility scripts and READMEs for DI and all features on AMD. ------ TODO: This is still WIP. More sections will be added.

signals.title: [Bug] Inkling MTP crashes during draft-extend CUDA graph capture
signals.text: ### Describe the bug Serving Inkling with MTP (multi-layer EAGLE) crashes at startup while capturing the draft-extend CUDA graph. `forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens` is `None` when the short-conv backend refreshes its track indices: ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape' speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:930 multi_step_fn layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:1007 init_forward_metadata_in_graph layers/attention/linear/inkling_sconv_backend.py:451 _refresh_track_conv_indices ``` The same configuration serves normally with CUDA graphs disabled (`--disable-cuda-graph --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`), reaching an accept length of 2.4-3.0, so it is specific to the capture path. ### Reproduction ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code \ --model-path thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4 --tp 8 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 --attention-backend fa4 --page-size 128 \ --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed \ --enable-torch-symm-mem --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.1 \ --enable-multimodal --reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 8 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 9 --enable-multi-layer-eagle --speculative-use-rejection-sampling ``` All 8 ranks hit the same exception and the server never becomes ready. ### Environment sglang `4a6dc267`.

signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug > An unsolved duplicate of #20709 I noticed that `flashinfer` is gated again in [srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py#L391](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py#L391). I encountered this while running [verl's Delta Weight Sync example](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/verl/experimental/one_step_off_policy/shell/grpo_0.6b_gsm8k_fsdp2_sglang_delta_sharded_2_6.sh) with `sglang==0.5.17` and `torch==2.11.0+cu130` on **`sm_103` Blackwell GPUs (more precisely, B300)**. The server fails during attention backend initialization with: ```bash AssertionError: Only {'trtllm_mha', 'triton', 'fa4'} backends are supported on Blackwell GPUs for hybrid GDN models. Got attention_backend=flashinfer. ``` Is this restriction intentional in the latest distribution, or is there a recommended configuration/workaround for this setup? In particular, I'm wondering whether `flashinfer` is expected to support this workload again. ### Reproduction Script: [verl's Delta Weight Sync signals.title: [Bug] apply_rotary_emb_flat_kernel rotates and overwrites the columns past rope_dim
signals.text: ## Describe the bug `apply_rotary_emb_triton` in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/deepseek_v4_rope.py` picks one of three kernels for the same operation. Two of them mask the column axis against the real rotary width: ```python apply_rotary_emb_triton_kernel mask = offs_pair < (rope_dim // 2) # :102 apply_rotary_emb_triton_kernel_batched pair_mask = pair < (rope_dim // 2) # :154 ``` The third does not. `apply_rotary_emb_flat_kernel` is launched with `RD = max(triton.next_power_of_2(rope_dim), 2)` (:290) and walks `d = tl.arange(0, RD)`, but its load and its store carry only the *row* mask: ```python d = tl.arange(0, RD) xo = base + d[None, :] * sx_d x = tl.load(x_ptr + xo, mask=rmask[:, None], other=0.0).to(tl.float32) # :225 ... tl.store(x_ptr + xo, out.to(x_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=rmask[:, None]) # :254 ``` The `cos` / `sin` loads at :232 and :237 have the same shape. So whenever `rope_dim` is not a power of two, the columns from `rope_dim` to `RD - 1` are read, rotated and written back. The kernel works in place, so those writes land on the next head's data — and on the final row, past the end of the tensor. Both effects are visible: - **Wrong values.** Against the library's own per-token kernel, selected by the same public call, `batch=4 n_heads=8 rope_dim=6` gives `max|flat - per_token| = 3.81` with 48 of 192 elements differing. `rope_dim` 96 and 192 happen to come out equal in that comparison, because each stray write lands inside the *next* head's region, where that head's own program writes the correct value too — but see below, they are still out of bounds. - **Out-of-bounds access.** Under `compute-sanitizer`, `rope_dim=6` reads 5 bytes past the 96-byte `freqs` allocation at `:238`, and `rope_dim=96` reads 1 byte past the 12288-byte `x` allocation at `:225`. Both then die with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`. **This is latent on the shipped configurations**, and the caveat belongs with the report: DeepSeek-V4 uses a power-of-two `rope_dim`, and the flat path is opt-in (`_USE_BATCHED_ROPE` is `False` by default, set by `set_batched_rope(True)` / `SGLANG_ROPE_BATCHED=1`). Nothing in the tree reaches it today. It is filed because the kernel silently disagrees with its two siblings over a parameter it already receives, so the first non-power-of-two rotary width to use this path gets wrong numbers rather than an error. ## Reproduction ```python import torch, triton from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.deepseek_v4_rope import ( apply_rotary_emb_triton, precompute_freqs_cis, set_batched_rope) batch, n_heads, rope_dim = 4, 8, 6 # RD = next_power_of_2(6) = 8 torch.manual_seed(0) x = torch.randn(batch, n_heads, rope_dim, device="cuda") freqs = precompute_freqs_cis(rope_dim, batch, 0, 10000.0, 1.0, 32, 1).to("cuda") set_batched_rope(False) # per-token kernel: masks the columns ref = apply_rotary_emb_triton(x.clone(), freqs) set_batched_rope(True) # flat kernel: does not got = apply_rotary_emb_triton(x.clone(), freqs) print("max|flat - per_token|:", (got - ref).abs().max().item()) print("differing cells:", int((got - ref).abs().gt(1e-4).sum()), "of", got.numel()) ``` ``` max|flat - per_token|: 3.8119478225708008 differing cells: 48 of 192 ``` And under the sanitizer, with `x` allocated last so the overrun reaches unallocated memory: ``` $ PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck python repro_oob.py 96 rope_dim=96 RD=128 stray columns=32; x is 3072 elements = 12288 bytes ========= Invalid __global__ read of size 16 bytes ========= at apply_rotary_emb_flat_kernel+0x2df0 in deepseek_v4_rope.py:225 ========= by thread (24,0,0) in block (1,0,0) ========= Access to 0x7f7faa403600 is out of bounds ========= and is 1 bytes after the nearest allocation at 0x7f7faa400600 of size 12288 bytes ========= ERROR SUMMARY: 12 errors ``` ## Expected behavior The padded columns are neither read past the tensors nor written back, as in the two sibling kernels. `_fused_norm_rope_kernel` in the same file already carries the real width as a `ROPE_DIM: tl.constexpr` (:410) and masks with it (:438). ## Environment - `sgl-project/sglang` at `92b1d382c` - NVIDIA B200 (sm_100), driver 595.71.05 - torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12

signals.title: [Bug] [AMD] SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1 is ignored by AITER FP4 MoE on ROCm
signals.text: ### Describe the bug On ROCm with AITER enabled, `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1` is accepted but does not dequantize routed FP4 expert weights. The server later fails during MoE kernel dispatch instead of serving the model. `Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading_block_quant()` returns through the native AITER FP4 branch before checking `dequant_fp4_to_fp8`. The existing dequant block is also unreachable on ROCm because `_is_fp8_fnuz` takes the preceding branch. ### Reproduction - Hardware: 8x MI308X (gfx942), TP8 - Checkpoint: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (original FP4) - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi30x-20260809` - Environment: `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1`, AITER enabled - MoE runner: `auto` Observed with the stock image: ```text RuntimeError: Unsupported kernel config for moe heuristic dispatch ``` Expected: the flag converts routed FP4 experts to block FP8 and the model starts. A local fix was validated on the same hardware: - stock v0.5.17: does not start; - patched v0.5.17: starts, graph capture is clean on all 8 ranks, no OOM; - GSM8K: **187/200 = 93.5%**, 0 errors; - runner guard: **344/344** MoE-layer/rank probes selected AITER shuffle, with 0 false or ambiguous cases. This is related to [#32333](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32333) but distinct: #32333 changes backend selection in `get_quant_method`, while this issue is the missing ROCm weight-processing path. ### Environment - Hardware: 8x AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942), TP8; all GPU links are XGMI. - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi30x-20260809` - SGLang: `0.5.17.dev20260809+g7120f3ee13` - PyTorch: `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4` - ROCm: `/opt/rocm-7.2.0`, HIPCC `7.2.26015-fc0010cf6a`, driver `6.16.13` - `ulimit -n`: `1024` Full `python3 -m sglang.check_env` output: <details> <summary>Show full environment output</summary> ```text WARNING: AMD GPU device(s) is/are in a low-power state. Check power control/runtime_status Python: 3.10.12 (main, Jan 8 2026, 06:52:19) [GCC 11.4.0] ROCM available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: AMD Instinct MI308X GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.4 ROCM_HOME: /opt/rocm-7.2.0 HIPCC: HIP version: 7.2.26015-fc0010cf6a ROCM Driver Version: 6.16.13 PyTorch: 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4 sglang: 0.5.17.dev20260809+g7120f3ee13 sglang-kernel: 0.4.6.post1 flashinfer_python: Module Not Found flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.6.0+git42270451 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.9.0 numpy: 2.2.6 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.1 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.121.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: Module Not Found AMD Topology: ============================ ROCm System Management Interface ============================ =============================== Link Type between two GPUs =============================== GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 GPU4 GPU5 GPU6 GPU7 GPU0 0 XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI GPU1 XGMI 0 XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI GPU2 XGMI XGMI 0 XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI GPU3 XGMI XGMI XGMI 0 XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI GPU4 XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI 0 XGMI XGMI XGMI GPU5 XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI 0 XGMI XGMI XGMI GPU6 XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI 0 XGMI XGMI GPU7 XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI XGMI 0 ================================== End of ROCm SMI Log =================================== ulimit soft: 1024 ``` </details>

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + dsv4 + DSPARK + HiCache: long agentic sessions get #cached-token: 0 every turn despite stable 50%+ prefix (short requests hit ~98%)
signals.text: # [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (dsv4 + DSPARK + HiCache): long agentic sessions get `#cached-token: 0` on every turn despite stable 50%+ token-level prefix, while short requests hit ~98% ## Summary On a production deployment of DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (8×H20, TP=8, `dsv4` attention backend, DSPARK speculative decoding, HiCache `write_through_selective`), **long multi-turn agent sessions (Claude Code) get zero prefix-cache hits on every turn**, while short requests served in the same window hit ~98%. Token-weighted prefix hit rate over 5 hours of real traffic is **83.8%**, dominated by these large-request misses. We verified on the **client side via packet capture** that the requests themselves are not at fault, so the root cause appears to be in the DSV4 hybrid-pool radix reuse path on the server. ## Environment - sglang **v0.5.17** (image `lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130` built 2026-08-08, torch 2.11.0+cu130) - 8 × NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90, 143.8 GB each), single node - Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, bundled DSpark draft head), TP=8 - Relevant server args: - `attention_backend='dsv4'`, `kv_cache_dtype='fp8_e4m3'`, `page_size=256` (auto-forced) - `swa_full_tokens_ratio=0.1` - `speculative_algorithm='DSPARK'`, `speculative_num_draft_tokens=6` - `enable_hierarchical_cache=True`, `hicache_ratio=1.0`, `hicache_write_policy='write_through_selective'` - `mem_fraction_static=0.69`, `chunked_prefill_size=32768`, `max_running_requests=8` - `schedule_policy='lpm'`, `radix_eviction_policy='lru'` - Pool sizes at startup (per rank): `full=8,460,800, swa=846,080, c4=2,115,200, c128=66,100` (`DSV4 memory calculation: bytes_per_full_token=9259.90, available_bytes=73.17 GB`) - Traffic: Claude Code native Anthropic protocol (`/v1/messages?beta=true` with `claude-code-20250219, interleaved-thinking, context-management, prompt-caching-scope` betas), relayed unchanged by a gateway; 6–13万-token prompts, 15–60 s per turn. ## Observed behavior 1. **Large sessions always miss.** A user session at ~110K prompt tokens issues consecutive turns 10–40 s apart, each turn a strict append of the previous turn (+100–2,000 tokens). Every turn logs chunked prefill as: ``` Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 32768, #cached-token: 0 Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 32768, #cached-token: 0 Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 13568, #cached-token: 0 ``` Even the tail chunk of the same request only picks up leftovers from *other* users' sessions. 2. **Short requests in the same seconds hit fine** (`#new-token: 512, #cached-token: 80640`; `#new-token: 256, #cached-token: 212480`) — so the radix tree itself is functional. 3. **Eviction paradox.** Over ~5 h: `evicted_tokens_total = 9.08e8` (31,512 evictions, 271 s cumulative) vs `uncached_prompt_tokens = 6.37e7` — evicted tokens are **14× the uncached input** — yet peak `full token usage` is only **0.08** and the pool holds 8.46M tokens. Nothing is ever "full"; enormous churn happens anyway. 4. **HiCache load-back is ~dead**: `load_back_tokens_total = 14,336` over 5 hours, although `write_through_selective` writes the C4/C128 sidecars to host (SWA 21.28 GB + C4 25.99 GB + C128 1.14 GB host pools allocated per rank). ## Client-side verification (packet capture) We tcpdump'ed the ingress and reassembled 17 complete consecutive JSON bodies from a single keep-alive connection (one Claude Code session). Findings: - Adjacent turns share a **70–75% byte-level common prefix** (each turn = previous turn + appended messages; the drop from 100% is explained below). - `tools` (23 entries) are **identical in name and order** across turns. - The byte-level divergence point is exactly where Anthropic's `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` breakpoint **moves with the last user message** (positions: turn N → `messages[14]`, turn N+1 → `messages[16]`). The `system` blocks keep their two breakpoints at fixed positions. - After stripping `cache_control` fields, the first 14 messages serialize **byte-identical** across turns (138,156 bytes = **53% of the full body**), i.e. a stable, reusable token prefix of well over 50% exists on every turn. So the client presents a stable 50%+ prefix every 10–40 s, yet the server reports `#cached-token: 0` for the entire request. This rules out prompt drift / unstable tool ordering as the cause. ## Suspected area Given short-prefix hits work and long-prefix (multi-chunk, 32K×n) reuse always fails, this looks like the DSV4 hybrid-group reuse/translation path — possibly the same family as: - #33656 — deterministic SWA KV position corruption on the cached-prefix **restore** path under HiCache + high reuse (same model, same 8×H20 topology, same ~86% radix hit workload). Our deployment shows the same near-zero `load_back` on that path. - #33549 — same model/hardware/software combo (8×H20 + Flash-0731 + dsv4 + DSPARK) hang at ~245K context. - #26427 — HiSparse long-context concurrency issues traced to full-token→compressed-C4 location translation. - vllm-project/vllm#42948 (upstream sibling engine) — DSv4-Flash hybrid groups losing first-block cache keys on every physical-block reassignment, cascading `hit_length` to 0 across all groups **while pool usage stays <10%** — which matches our eviction paradox (usage 8%, churn 14×) and the long-request-only miss pattern (long requests trigger many block allocations via chunked prefill; short requests don't). ## Reproduction Replaying the two captured bodies back-to-back against the same server (turn 1 to warm the cache, turn 2 immediately after) reproduces `#cached-token: 0` for turn 2. Minimal data: any two Anthropic-protocol requests where request 2 = request 1 + 2 appended messages and prompt > ~64K tokens (i.e. ≥ 3 chunked-prefill chunks), sent within seconds of each other. Happy to provide the captured request bodies (sanitized) and full startup logs if useful. ## Questions 1. Is long-prefix (multi-chunk) reuse expected to work with `write_through_selective` on v0.5.17, or is there a known regression fixed after v0.5.17 (we saw SWA-eviction-related fixes like #35809 and UnifiedRadixTree cache-hit-reset PRs #30468/#30636/#30626/#31643 land later)? 2. Could disabling `--enable-hierarchical-cache` restore correct long-prefix reuse as a temporary mitigation, at the cost of losing host-tier offload?

signals.title: [Bug] EAGLE/NEXTN TP=2 hangs at warmup on Intel XPU after #34238 moved the verify-decision TP broadcast out of the sampling branch
signals.text: ## Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. - [x] Please use English. ## Describe the bug On the **Intel XPU backend**, EAGLE/NEXTN speculative decoding with `--tp 2` intermittently hangs on the first decode step after warmup. The scheduler watchdog fires at 300 s and the server never becomes ready, so the test fails at setup after the 600 s launch timeout. We started seeing this after #34238 ("[AMD] Broadcast the EAGLE greedy verify decision across TP ranks on ROCm", merged 2026-08-15). It is intermittent: on the same commit, one run hung at warmup and a later run of the same command passed (GSM8K 0.920, accept len 3.18). ### Why XPU is newly exposed by #34238 #34238 did not add a new code path — it de-indented the existing TP broadcast in `eagle_sample()` out of the `else:` (sampling / rejection-sampling) branch so it now runs after **both** verify branches: ```python # python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu: ... # greedy verify -- XPU ALWAYS lands here else: ... # tree_speculative_sampling_target_only / chain_speculative_sampling_triton # after #34238 this runs for BOTH branches (it used to live inside `else:`) tp_group = get_parallel().attn_tp_group if is_dp_attention_enabled() else get_tp_group() if tp_group.world_size > 1: tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) ``` `_is_xpu` is a term in that branch condition, so **XPU can never reach the `else` branch**. These three broadcasts were unreachable on XPU before #34238 and now execute on every verify step. NVIDIA is effectively unchanged: the non-greedy path already had them, and the newly-covered all-greedy case is a semantic no-op because NCCL's all-reduce yields bitwise-identical logits on every rank. The newly-live set is ROCm (the intended fix), XPU, NPU, CPU, and CUDA-all-greedy — all at TP > 1. ### Stacks at the hang (`--tp 2`, watchdog dump) **TP1 — active, stuck on a Level Zero device event inside the draft extend that follows verify:** ``` Thread 1012034 (active): "MainThread" sched_yield (libc.so.6) 0x7214ac5fa8ed (libze_intel_gpu.so.1.14.36300) 0x7214ac5fb768 (libze_intel_gpu.so.1.14.36300) ur::level_zero::urEventWait (libur_adapter_level_zero_v2.so.0.12.0) compute_spec_mrope_positions (forward_batch_info.py:1131) init_new (forward_batch_info.py:949) prepare_for_draft_extend (eagle_worker_common.py:178) _draft_extend_for_decode (eagle_worker_v2.py:887) forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker_v2.py:1198) run_batch (scheduler.py:3696) event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:1803) ``` **TP0 — idle, already past `run_batch`, waiting on the CPU-group request broadcast of the next iteration:** ``` Thread 1012033 (idle): "MainThread" pthread_cond_wait (libc.so.6) c10d::Work::wait (libtorch_cpu.so) broadcast (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3080) broadcast_pyobj (utils/common.py:2406) _broadcast_reqs_across_ranks (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:210) recv_requests (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:93) event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:1772) ``` Timeline from the log: weights loaded, `max_total_num_tokens=76412`, one warmup `Prefill batch` at 17:33:49, then no further progress; `Scheduler watchdog timeout (self.watchdog_timeout=300, self.soft=False)` on both ranks at 17:41:12-13. So the stall is on the **first decode/draft-extend step after the first verify** — i.e. immediately after the first `eagle_sample()` call. ### Hypothesis (not yet proven — maintainer input welcome) TP0 has drained and is waiting on the **CPU/gloo** group for requests, while TP1's **XPU device queue** never completes an event. That is the signature of an unmatched or stalled collective on the xccl *device* group leaving TP1's queue blocked, with the visible `urEventWait` being downstream work that can never retire. Relevant: `GroupCoordinator.broadcast()` issues a raw `torch.distributed.broadcast` on `self.device_group`. That is exactly the call shape XPU deliberately avoids for all-reduce — `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce()` routes XPU through the `inplace_all_reduce` custom op, with this comment in `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`: > Route through inplace_all_reduce custom op so Dynamo treats this as an opaque call and does not > decompose it into `_c10d_functional` primitives (which invoke `sycl_event.wait()` and break XPU > graph capture). `broadcast()` has no such wrapper, so #34238 introduces three raw eager device-group collectives per verify step on a backend that has an explicit carve-out against them. ### What we have and have not verified - Verified: the hang and the two stacks above, on a commit that contains #34238. - Verified by code reading: the three broadcasts were unreachable on XPU before #34238. - **Not** verified: a hang-rate comparison against the parent of #34238. The failure is intermittent (1 hang, 1 pass observed on the same code), so we are still collecting runs and will post the numbers here. Attribution to #34238 is currently based on when we started seeing it plus the code reading above. ### Side issues found while filing this (happy to send PRs) 1. **`python3 -m sglang.check_env` crashes on Intel XPU**, which blocks the required Environment field of this template. `python/sglang/check_env.py` dispatches on `is_cuda_v2/is_hip/is_npu/is_musa/is_mps` with no XPU branch and no `else`, so `env` is never bound: ``` File ".../python/sglang/check_env.py", line 594, in <module> env.check_env() NameError: name 'env' is not defined ``` The Environment section below was therefore collected manually. 2. **`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` is silently ignored on XPU.** The `_is_xpu` term forces greedy verify, so the rejection-sampling kernel is never reached even when the flag is set — the test below is named for a path it does not exercise on XPU. ### Candidate fix Smallest XPU-scoped change; restores exactly the pre-#34238 XPU behavior and leaves the ROCm fix intact: ```diff - tp_group = ( - get_parallel().attn_tp_group if is_dp_attention_enabled() else get_tp_group() - ) - if tp_group.world_size > 1: - tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) - tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) - tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) + # XPU opts out: a raw `torch.distributed.broadcast` decomposes to `_c10d_functional`, + # whose `sycl_event.wait()` breaks XPU graph capture (why all_reduce takes the + # `inplace_all_reduce` detour). The greedy path never ran this sync on XPU before, + # so skipping it keeps the prior behavior. + if not _is_xpu: + tp_group = ( + get_parallel().attn_tp_group + if is_dp_attention_enabled() + else get_tp_group() + ) + if tp_group.world_size > 1: + tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) + tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) + tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) ``` If XPU does need the rank-0 sync for the same reason ROCm does, the alternative is to route the broadcast through a custom op the way XPU all-reduce already is, rather than skipping it. Happy to send whichever the maintainers prefer. ## Reproduction Model `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, 2x Intel Arc Pro B60, `--device xpu --tp 2`: ```bash pytest -sv test/registered/spec/eagle/test_eagle_reject_sampling.py::TestQwen35EagleRS::test_a_gsm8k ``` Equivalent standalone server command (taken verbatim from the failing run): ```bash sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --trust-remote-code --tp 2 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-use-rejection-sampling \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache \ --device xpu --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21000 ``` Effective server args from the hanging run: `attention_backend='triton'`, `cuda_graph_config` decode=`disabled` prefill=`disabled` (no graph capture involved), `page_size=1`, `disable_radix_cache=True`, `speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True`, `enable_dp_attention=False`, `watchdog_timeout=300`, `disable_overlap_schedule=False`. The hang reproduces before the GSM8K workload starts, during server warmup, so no eval data is needed to trigger it. ## Environment Collected manually because `python3 -m sglang.check_env` raises `NameError` on XPU (see side issue 1 above). ``` sglang: 0.5.18.dev687 (source checkout containing #34238) python: 3.12.13 os: Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 torch: 2.12.0+xpu xccl: available (torch.distributed.is_xccl_available() == True) ipex: not installed oneccl_bindings_for_pytorch: not installed xpu devices: 8x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics, 24 GB each, driver 1.14.36300+8 (this repro uses 2 of them via --tp 2) ``` cc @JessicaJiang-123 @XinyuJiangCMU (authors of #34238), @Ying1123 @merrymercy @hnyls2002 @Qiaolin-Yu (CODEOWNERS for `python/sglang/srt/speculative`)

signals.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 reasoning content does not parse correctly in rust sgl-model-gateway
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug The sgl-model-gateway's `qwen3` reasoning parser does not populate `reasoning_content` for Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 correctly. This occurs when having the sgl-model-gateway in either gRPC mode or HTTP and having the `--reasoning-parser qwen3` set on the model gateway and not setting the reasoning parsing within the model on sglang worker itself. ### Reproduction We have deployed this via docker and can be reproduced as follows: ``` services: worker: image: lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b runtime: nvidia command: > python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --tp-size 1 ports: - "8000:8000" gateway: image: lmsysorg/sgl-model-gateway:v0.3.2 command: > --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --worker-urls http://worker:8000 --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder ports: - "30000:30000" ``` Once containers are up: ``` curl -s http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17 * 23? Think step by step."}], "max_tokens":300}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ``` ... "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "We need answer simple arithmetic. User asks step by step. Need provide final concise. Compute 17*23. Step 17*20=340. Step 17*3=51, sum 391. Or 23*10=230 etc. Final 391.
</think>

We can break it down:

17 × 23 = 17 × (20 + 3) 
= 17 × 20 + 17 × 3 
= 340 + 51 
= **391**", "reasoning_content": null } ... ``` Expected response should return thinking within reasoning_content and clean answer in content... which is what the SGLang Python qwen3 parser produces when run within the worker-side in HTTP mode. Something is distorted when the parser is being run within the sgl-model-gateway. ### Environment `python3 -m sglang.check_env` from sglang docker container: ``` Python: 3.12.3 CUDA available: True GPU: NVIDIA L40S (Compute Capability 8.9) PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 sglang: 0.0.0.dev0+qwen38.27b.g561c8f3 transformers: 5.12.1 ``` Gateway: `sglang_router 0.3.2` Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` (thinking on by default)

signals.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8 DSpark forced-reject is not lossless: accumulated GDN state drift vs Base decode
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Summary With RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark, I can reproduce a deterministic correctness divergence between ordinary Base decode and DSpark TARGET_VERIFY even when every speculative draft token is deliberately rejected and only the target model's own argmax token is committed. The failure is cumulative rather than context-local: Base decode is deterministic across independent processes with a fixed seed. Under gamma=1 forced rejection, DSpark initially matches Base but later diverges. Rebuilding the same prefix through normal prefill restores the correct Base result at the divergence context. Using FP32 Mamba/SSM persistent state delays the divergence substantially, but does not eliminate it. This suggests accumulated GDN recurrent-state drift somewhere in the TARGET_VERIFY / intermediate-state / commit path. Possibly related to the state-correctness work tracked in #34899 and #34297. Environment SGLang: SGLANG_BUILD_COMMIT=c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5 SGLANG_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260814-c4271c3f CUDA 13.0 TP=1 attention backend=triton linear attention backend=triton Target model: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 revision: 52d1adc5f38aa5ebf099c29ed7025ba34cfbb854 Draft model: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark revision: 923ed3a8572615643f0137e424e4ce4edd7f1cda Diagnostic configuration: max_running_requests=1 gamma=1 verify_num_draft_tokens=2 SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static CUDA graph disabled prefill CUDA graph disabled seed=123456789 Triton GDN backend Model weights are not modified. Forced-rejection diagnostic SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 by itself is not a semantically valid forced-rejection test because it changes correct_len without recomputing the naturally selected target bonus token. For gamma=1 I therefore used this local diagnostic patch in dspark_verify.py: if self._simulate_acc_len > 0: - correct_len = self._simulated_correct_len( - bs=bs, dtype=correct_len.dtype, device=correct_len.device + target_predict = torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( + bs, self.verify_num_draft_tokens ) + correct_len = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) + bonus = target_predict[:, 0] + cap_trim_lens = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) The resulting request reports: spec_accept_rate=0.0 spec_num_correct_drafts=0 spec_num_proposed_drafts=95 spec_verify_ct=95 spec_accept_histogram=[95] Thus every first draft is rejected and the committed output token is the target model's own argmax. Exact request The same exact 24 input_ids are used for every run: INPUT_IDS = [ 248045, 846, 198, 623, 799, 61446, 13901, 11, 10033, 3069, 10583, 5802, 4833, 5983, 13, 248046, 198, 248045, 74455, 198, 248068, 271, 248069, 271, ] Input verification: count: 24 SHA256: f3d5baaf2ddb361d0d9fbff4add8071e24718908f76ae350ced01927dd87fcd0 The SHA256 is computed as: hashlib.sha256( ",".join(map(str, INPUT_IDS)).encode() ).hexdigest() Sampling: temperature: 0 top_p: 1 top_k: -1 max_new_tokens: 96 ignore_eos: true Example request: payload = { "input_ids": INPUT_IDS, "sampling_params": { "temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0, "top_k": -1, "max_new_tokens": 96, "ignore_eos": True, }, "stream": False, } Server configuration Relevant arguments: sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend triton \ --context-length 16384 \ --max-total-tokens 16384 \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \ --max-mamba-cache-size 16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --random-seed 123456789 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 Environment: SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 For the FP32-state diagnostic I additionally use: --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 Results 1. Base oracle is deterministic Base-only greedy decode is deterministic across independent server processes with seed 123456789. Original BF16 Base oracle SHA256: a935dafc6111c5acf3280bb9fa1d545f39abf5c9ba92285ba29d39949e971848 2. Original TARGET_VERIFY + forced rejection With gamma=1, static verify, CUDA graph disabled, and the forced-rejection diagnostic: first divergence: output index 13 Base token: 1070 DSpark token: 836 Indices 0..12 match Base. 3. Concrete beta precision mismatch One concrete numerical difference exists between Base packed decode and TARGET_VERIFY. Base rounds beta through the beta tensor's source dtype, while TARGET_VERIFY originally keeps the sigmoid computation in FP32. Diagnostic patch: - b_beta = 1.0 / (1.0 + tl.exp(-b_b)) + b_beta = tl.sigmoid(b_b).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32) With only this change: first divergence: 13 -> 23 Indices 0..22 now match Base. This appears to be a real numerical contributor, but not the complete cause. 4. Fresh-prefix localization Using the beta-aligned path, I rebuilt a fresh request consisting of: original input IDs + exact Base output IDs [0:22] No text was retokenized. The request reported: cached_tokens=0 Expected next Base tokens: [2438, 5306] Generated: [2438, 5306] Exact match. Therefore the long-request divergence at index 23 is not a direct TARGET_VERIFY failure at that context when recurrent state is freshly rebuilt through ordinary prefill. It requires accumulated speculative-state evolution. 5. FP32 persistent SSM state Using the same beta alignment but changing both Base and DSpark to: --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 results are: FP32 Base SHA256: 5557ae475bafcb00ff5ea564e14954f5590cf8e77535edec878a7203225561fc FP32 DSpark SHA256: a982aa8b26b5e7f51d11669da7b42a730d839d721d0d386944c3a964321a2fcb first divergence: index 38 Base token: 6338 DSpark token: 2279 So increasing persistent SSM precision changes: BF16 SSM + beta alignment: index 23 FP32 SSM + beta alignment: index 38 but does not eliminate the divergence. This suggests BF16 persistent-state storage is an error amplifier rather than the sole root cause. 6. KV precision control With FP32 SSM and beta alignment, changing target KV cache from FP8 E4M3 to BF16 moved first divergence only: 38 -> 39 This suggests full-attention KV precision is not the primary cause of the remaining drift. Other isolation work Delta reduction layout Changing only TARGET_VERIFY's delta projection to a literal Base [V,K] / K-axis formulation did not improve correctness: beta + Base-layout delta projection: first divergence = 6 Output reduction layout Changing only TARGET_VERIFY's output projection to a literal Base [V,K] / K-axis formulation also regressed: beta + Base-layout output projection: first divergence = 6 Softplus expression TARGET_VERIFY originally evaluates: beta_x = softplus_beta * x softplus_x = tl.where( beta_x <= softplus_threshold, (1.0 / softplus_beta) * tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp(beta_x)), x, ) Runtime parameters were confirmed as: softplus_beta=1.0 softplus_threshold=20.0 Changing only this expression to Base's literal form: softplus_x = tl.where( x <= 20, tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp(x)), x, ) regressed the FP32 test: first divergence: 38 -> 6 Because the two forms are algebraically equivalent for the actual runtime parameters, this appears to demonstrate sensitivity to Triton floating-point/codegen behavior rather than identify the root cause. Convolution state A source audit found persistent conv state and TARGET_VERIFY intermediate conv windows use the same default BF16 dtype and the expected post-anchor snapshot/scatter semantics for gamma=1. Attempting the independent diagnostic: SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE=float32 cannot currently be used as a clean control because the current implementation hits: RuntimeError: Index put requires the source and destination dtypes match, got Float for the destination and BFloat16 for the source. ReplaySSM The current build exposes: --enable-linear-replayssm-spec but DSPARK/DFLASH explicitly rejects this path for Qwen3.8 GDN: ValueError: --enable-linear-replayssm-spec with DSPARK/DFLASH requires a KDA (kimi_linear) model; got a non-KDA model. So I could not use ReplaySSM as a GDN DSPARK correctness control. Current hypothesis The strongest evidence is: forced reject + repeated TARGET_VERIFY rounds -> divergence fresh prefill of the exact same prefix -> correct again higher persistent SSM precision -> divergence substantially delayed KV precision change -> almost no effect My current hypothesis is that a small difference enters a committed/intermediate GDN recurrent state during repeated TARGET_VERIFY reject/commit rounds and accumulates until it changes the target argmax. For gamma=1, I also audited the reject/commit indexing: candidate row 0 = anchor/current token commit_lens = 1 last_correct_step_indices = 0 and the committed conv window appears to correspond to the post-anchor state as expected. The remaining high-value localization would therefore seem to be the SSM state boundary rather than further source-expression A/B tests. Expected behavior Under this diagnostic every speculative draft token is rejected and only the target model's own greedy token is committed. I would expect DSpark to preserve the same greedy token sequence as ordinary Base decode. If exact Base equivalence is intentionally not guaranteed for GDN TARGET_VERIFY because the recurrent numerical paths differ, clarification on the intended correctness invariant/tolerance would also be useful. Questions Is this accumulated GDN recurrent-state drift a known limitation or bug in the current DSpark TARGET_VERIFY path? Is there an existing GDN state-commit / TARGET_VERIFY correctness patch that should be tested on this Qwen3.8 path? Would the most useful next instrumentation be a per-layer/per-round comparison of: Base persistent SSM state before decode TARGET_VERIFY input persistent SSM state TARGET_VERIFY intermediate step-0 SSM state post-commit/scatter persistent SSM state Is the beta source-dtype rounding difference described above expected, or should TARGET_VERIFY match Base packed decode here? If exact Base equivalence is not expected between packed decode and TARGET_VERIFY, what correctness invariant should speculative decoding enforce for recurrent GDN models? I can provide the exact request script, complete Base/DSpark output token arrays, hashes, and the small diagnostic source patches if useful. ### Reproduction Models: Target: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` revision `52d1adc5f38aa5ebf099c29ed7025ba34cfbb854` Draft: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` revision `923ed3a8572615643f0137e424e4ce4edd7f1cda` Server configuration: ```bash export SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend triton \ --context-length 16384 \ --max-total-tokens 16384 \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \ --max-mamba-cache-size 16 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \ --mm-feature-transport cpu \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --random-seed 123456789 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 For the forced-rejection diagnostic, I locally changed the SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN branch in dspark_verify.py so that gamma=1 always rejects the draft but commits the target model's own argmax: target_predict = torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( bs, self.verify_num_draft_tokens ) correct_len = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) bonus = target_predict[:, 0] cap_trim_lens = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) I also tested the following beta precision alignment in fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py: b_beta = tl.sigmoid(b_b).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32) Exact request: INPUT_IDS = [ 248045, 846, 198, 623, 799, 61446, 13901, 11, 10033, 3069, 10583, 5802, 4833, 5983, 13, 248046, 198, 248045, 74455, 198, 248068, 271, 248069, 271, ] payload = { "input_ids": INPUT_IDS, "sampling_params": { "temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0, "top_k": -1, "max_new_tokens": 96, "ignore_eos": True, }, "stream": False, } Input SHA256: f3d5baaf2ddb361d0d9fbff4add8071e24718908f76ae350ced01927dd87fcd0 With FP32 SSM + beta alignment + forced rejection, Base and DSpark match through output index 37 and first diverge at index 38: Base token: 6338 DSpark token: 2279 Rebuilding the exact same prefix through ordinary prefill restores the correct Base continuation, indicating accumulated recurrent-state drift. ### Environment /sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/environ.py:1402: UserWarning: Environment variable SGLANG_FLASHINFER_PR4266_SOURCE has been deprecated. warnings.warn(f"Environment variable {old_name} has been deprecated.") W0817 11:22:26.937000 441 torch/utils/_pytree.py:630] <enum 'KernelPreference'> is an Enum subclass and is now natively supported by torch.compile as an opaque value type. Calling register_constant() on Enum subclasses is deprecated and will be an error in a future release. W0817 11:22:26.951000 441 torch/utils/_pytree.py:630] <enum 'ScaleCalculationMode'> is an Enum subclass and is now natively supported by torch.compile as an opaque value type. Calling register_constant() on Enum subclasses is deprecated and will be an error in a future release. Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPU 0 Compute Capability: 12.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 610.88 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 sglang: 0.0.0.dev0+qwen38.27b.g561c8f3 sglang-kernel: 0.4.6.post1 flashinfer_python: 0.6.18 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.18.dev20260807 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.18.dev20260807+cu130 triton: 3.7.1 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.3 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.122.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.15.0+cu130 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X N/A Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks Hypervisor vendor:: Microsoft ulimit soft: 1024

signals.title: [Bug] sgl-model-gateway fails Clippy due to needless borrows in cache-aware policy tests
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Running the same Clippy command used by the `sgl-model-gateway` CI fails on the latest `main` branch because two cache-aware policy tests pass a borrowed temporary `String` to `BasicWorkerBuilder::new`. Both occurrences trigger `clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args`, and CI treats Clippy warnings as errors with `-D warnings`: ```text error: the borrowed expression implements the required traits --> src/policies/cache_aware.rs:682:41 | 682 | BasicWorkerBuilder::new(&format!("http://w{}:8000", j)) | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ error: the borrowed expression implements the required traits --> src/policies/cache_aware.rs:741:41 | 741 | BasicWorkerBuilder::new(&format!("http://w{}:8000", j)) | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ``` The expected result is that the gateway's documented CI lint command completes without warnings. The proposed fix is to pass the owned `String` directly at both call sites: ```rust BasicWorkerBuilder::new(format!("http://w{}:8000", j)) ``` This is a mechanical lint fix and should not change behavior. ### Reproduction Starting from commit `a2e88279c` on `origin/main`: ```bash cd sgl-model-gateway cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings ``` Clippy reports `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` at lines 682 and 741 of `src/policies/cache_aware.rs` and exits unsuccessfully. ### Environment ```text OS: Ubuntu Linux x86_64 SGLang commit: a2e88279c (origin/main) rustc 1.90.0 (1159e78c4 2025-09-14) cargo 1.90.0 (840b83a10 2025-07-30) clippy 0.1.90 (1159e78c47 2025-09-14) ``` No model, GPU, or CUDA environment is involved; the issue is reproduced by the Rust lint command alone.
