signals.title: [AMD] Add GLM-5.2-FP8 8-GPU MI35x nightly accuracy CI
signals.text: ## Motivation The [GLM-5.2 cookbook](https://docs.sglang.ai/cookbook/autoregressive/GLM/GLM-5.2#hw=mi355x&variant=default&quant=fp8&strategy=low-latency&nodes=single) publishes the MI355X FP8 cells as `verified: true`, with speed numbers in `glm-5.2-benchmarks.jsx` behind them. Nothing in CI re-checks that claim — there is no GLM-5.2 AMD coverage in tree at all, so the recipe is only as good as the last time someone ran it by hand. gfx950 is the arch that earns a guard here. The block-FP8 `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` miscompile ([#28685](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28685)) was small per layer but compounded across all 78 layers: GSM8K collapsed to ~0 while short factual prompts still looked fine. That failure mode is invisible to smoke tests — only a multi-step reasoning eval catches it. gfx942 (MI300X / MI325X) was never affected, so this stays MI35x-only. ## Modifications - **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_glm52_fp8_eval_mi35x.py`** (new) — GSM8K accuracy for `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`. Server args track the cookbook's MI355X / FP8 / low-latency / single-node cell verbatim (TP8, `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang`, `--dsa-decode-backend tilelang`, `--chunked-prefill-size 131072`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.80`, `--watchdog-timeout 1200`), so a green run is evidence for that specific recipe rather than for some nearby config. The one addition is `enable_multithread_load`, a load-time win on a ~700 GB checkpoint with no effect on numerics. - **`test/run_suite.py`** — registers the `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-glm52-fp8` suite. - **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — one `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` job, wired into the dispatch dropdown and `check-all-jobs`. **Eval and baseline match the CUDA GLM-5.2-FP8 nightly** (`test/registered/8-gpu-models/test_glm52_fp8.py`, gsm8k @ 0.92) rather than the hand-rolled completion harness the GLM-5.1 MI35x sibling uses. Same model, same eval, same bar means a red run points at AMD diverging from CUDA instead of at a harness difference. Accuracy only on purpose: the cookbook already publishes MI355X FP8 speed numbers, and an 8-GPU MI35x runner is scarce enough that a second long job should wait until this one is reliably green. ## Accuracy Tests Ran the new nightly on **both** ROCm lanes against this branch to decide where it should live. Both lanes pulled current same-day images, same sglang version — so this is a real 7.0-vs-7.2 difference, not stale-image rot: | Lane | Image | GSM8K | Result | | ---- | ----- | ----- | ------ | | ROCm 7.2 | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260727` | **0.931** | [PASS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30306627642) | | ROCm 7.0 | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm700-mi35x-20260727` | **0.270** | [FAIL](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30306635632) | **Why 7.0 fails, and why the job is not included.** The 7.0 image ships Triton 3.4.0. The aiter gluon DSA kernels need >= 3.5.0, so that lane logs: ``` ... is unavailable (needs Triton>=3.5.0 or AITER_ENABLE_AOT_GLUON_PA_MQA_LOGITS=1); falling back to legacy page_size=1 / KVBlockSize=1 path. ``` and the legacy DSA fallback is what costs the accuracy. Both lanes selected the same `dsa` attention backend and both reached the eval with all setup steps green, so the delta is that fallback rather than configuration or infra. Note this is a *different* mechanism from the block-FP8 miscompile above, and 0.270 is a partial degradation rather than the ~0 that bug produced — worth its own follow-up. Shipping a 7.0 job would mean shipping a known-red nightly, so it is left out with an in-code note to re-add it once that image carries Triton >= 3.5.0 or the legacy fallback is fixed on gfx950. **One caveat for reviewers:** headroom is thinner than the cookbook's ~0.96 implies. This harness measured 0.931 against the 0.92 baseline, so roughly a 1 point regression trips the test. The cookbook figure comes from a different GSM8K setup so the two are not directly comparable, but a marginal failure here is worth reading rather than retrying away. I kept the baseline at 0.92 to stay aligned with the CUDA nightly rather than tuning it to the observed value. ## Benchmarking and Profiling None — accuracy only, see above. ## Checklist - [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files` (black clean on touched files) - [x] New test registered and discovered by `run_suite.py` (`est_time=5400`, enabled) - [x] Workflow parses; job present in dropdown, body, and `check-all-jobs` needs - [x] All flags validated against `server_args.py` (`tilelang` is a valid `DSA_CHOICES` value) - [x] Green on ROCm 7.2 MI35x (GSM8K 0.931 >= 0.92) - [x] Rebased on current main <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32084452868](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32084452868)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32084514438](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32084514438)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: add aiter fused mHC post+pre with cross-layer boundary dispatch
signals.text: ## Summary Add a HIP/aiter fused `mhc_post` + next-layer `mhc_pre` path for DeepSeek-V4 on gfx95, dispatched across the attention/MoE boundary alongside the existing TileLang and Triton fused paths. On MI355X (gfx950) this is a **+0.8%–1.8% output-throughput win across concurrency 4–64 with accuracy preserved**. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`** - `try_aiter_fused_mhc_post_pre()`: wraps `aiter.ops.mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre`. The aiter kernel self-gates fused-vs-unfused per arch/token-count, so no token threshold is duplicated here; import/runtime failures fall back and warn once. - `try_mhc_fused_post_pre_boundary()`: aiter → Triton dispatch. The two kernels expect opposite fn orientations (Triton transposed, aiter native). - `is_cross_layer_mhc_fusion_enabled()` / `_is_production_mhc_enabled()`: enable cross-layer fusion when either the TileLang path or the aiter gfx95 path is available. `_is_fused_mhc_post_pre_enabled()` is consolidated here (previously duplicated in `deepseek_v4.py`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`**: route the attn-side, FFN-side, and `op_mhc_post_attn_pre_mlp` boundaries through `_apply_mhc_post_pre_boundary()`, falling back to the unfused `hc_post` + `hc_pre` sequence when no fused kernel fires. In the operation/batch-overlap path (DP attention) `state` is a `_StateDict` (attribute access, no `__getitem__`), so read it via `state.<field>`. - **`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py`**: gating/dispatch unit tests plus a gfx95-gated numerical test asserting `next_residual` (bit-exact) and `layer_input`/`post_mix` (bf16 tolerance) vs the unfused reference. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`. Baseline = image tree; Patched = image tree + this patch (only 2 model files differ). Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. ### Unit test ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py -q 8 passed ``` ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 3 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.947 | | 2 | 0.943 | 0.943 | | 3 | 0.937 | 0.944 | | **avg** | **0.941** | **0.945** | Invalid = 0.000 for all runs. signals.title: [Kernel] Enable Helion backend for Kimi Delta-Attention
signals.text: ## Motivation Add an opt-in Helion backend (e.g. used for Inkling [silu_mul fusion](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/inkling_moe.py)) for Kimi Delta Attention packed decode and prefill while preserving the existing default backends, public contracts, state mutations, and fallback behavior. The decode kernel delivers a **1.1x speedup** over Triton default. The prefill kernel delivers a **1.6x speedup** over Triton default. For Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (TP=2, 2xGB200), we observe geomean **5.04%-5.27%** improvement in tok/s with **4.06%-5.22%** reduction in TTFT compared to default kernels. This enables helion==1.4.0 as an optional dependency that is required only for the helion backend, matching what is done for some of the other KDA backends. ## Modifications - Add Helion implementations for packed recurrent decode and fixed/packed-varlen prefill. - Support FP32, BF16, and FP16 recurrent states, padded cache indices, bounded gates, intermediate states, and an opt-in Newton-Schulz research path. - Register helion for KDA decode and prefill selection: ```bash sglang serve MODEL_PATH --linear-attn-backend helion ``` Phases can also be selected independently: ```bash sglang serve MODEL_PATH \ --linear-attn-decode-backend helion \ --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton ``` - Keep generic decode, speculative verification, and ReplaySSM on the existing Triton fallback. - Add registered CUDA kernel tests, CPU dispatcher tests, benchmark coverage, and backend documentation. - Use fixed Helion configurations and static shapes, with no runtime autotuning on the model hot path. ## Accuracy Tests - Decode comparisons against packed Triton: - FP32 state: maximum output difference: 7.63e-6; maximum state difference: 2.24e-8. - BF16 state: maximum output difference: 7.63e-6; maximum state difference: 1.22e-4. - Prefill comparisons against recurrent Triton: - Maximum output difference: 7.32e-4. - Maximum state difference: 4.90e-3. - Covered fixed and packed-varlen prefill, FP32/BF16/FP16 state, padded `-1` cache indices, partial chunks, safe gates with `lower_bound=-5.0`, and stable sub-chunk normalization. - End-to-end Kimi-Linear GSM8K smoke test with Helion decode passed with score 0.915. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on NVIDIA 2xGB200 GPUs. End-to-End benchmarks: - Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct - TP=2 - input length 8192, batches 1/4/16, and output lengths 64/256. - Geomeans cover all six shapes for each state dtype. - We compare against default prefill/decode for KDA. | State dtype | Activation dtype | Overall throughput gain | TTFT reduction | TPOT reduction | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | FP32 | BF16 | 5.04% | 5.22% | 4.83% | | BF16 | BF16 | 5.27% | 4.06% | 5.68% | Microbenchmark summary: | Benchmark | State dtype | Activation dtype | Baseline | Geomean speedup | |---|---|---|---|---:| | Decode | FP32 | FP32 | Packed Triton | 1.134x | | Decode | BF16 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.067x | | Decode | FP32 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.118x | | Decode | BF16 | BF16 | FlashInfer | 1.393x | | Prefill | FP32 | BF16 | Triton | 1.603x | | Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton | 1.595x | H = 12, lower_bound=-5.0 | Benchmark | State dtype | Activation dtype | Baseline | Geomean speedup | |---|---|---|---|---:| | Decode | FP32 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.552x | | Decode | FP32 | BF16 | CUDA decode | 0.721x | | Decode | BF16 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.130x | | Prefill | FP32 | BF16 | Triton | 1.385x | | Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton | 1.390x | | Prefill| FP32 | BF16 | Triton ReplaySSM | 1.707x | | Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton ReplaySSM | 1.225x | Currently Helion decode under performs the custom cuda KDA decode kernel, as the CUDA kernel fuses convolution, recurrence, and RMSNorm. A follow up PR will evaluate Helion under the same fusions. Note that the`bench_kda_prefill_cutedsl.py` script precomputes CuTe metadata and scratch buffers outside the timed region and bypasses the production adapters, so this is not a super faithful representation of performance (helion has a 0.86x speedup compared to cute on this benchmark). If we benchmark the entire KDA wrapper, we observe: | Benchmark | State dtype | Activation dtype | Baseline | Geomean speedup | |---|---|---|---|---:| | Helion | FP32 | BF16 | CuTe DSL | 2.031x | ## signals.title: [HCU] Add Qwen3.5 and GLM-5 support
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Motivation This PR adds initial HCU support to SGLang for `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`, enabling Qwen3.5 and GLM-5 model serving on HCU. The changes address HCU-specific kernel compilation, unsupported runtime fast paths, EAGLE CUDA Graph buffer allocation, and GLM-5 inference accuracy. All platform-specific behavior is isolated behind `is_hcu()` or `USE_HCU` to preserve the existing CUDA and ROCm paths. This PR contains the following commits: - `[HCU] Adapt Qwen3.5-27B` - `[HCU] Fix EAGLE CUDA Graph custom mask buffer allocation` - `[HCU] Fix GLM-5 inference accuracy` - `[HCU] Unify MoE align kernel implementation` ## Modifications ### HCU platform detection and runtime fallbacks - Add `is_hcu()` detection for `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`. - Disable the unsupported multimem symmetric-memory all-gather path on HCU. - Disable the unavailable vLLM RMSNorm fast path on HCU. - Reject Quark W4A4 MXFP4 explicitly on HCU because its required AITER kernels are unavailable. - Keep these fallbacks HCU-only without changing the existing CUDA and ROCm behavior. ### sgl-kernel build support - Add and refine `setup_hcu.py`. - Support `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`. - Add `HCU_TARGET` for explicitly selecting the compilation target. - Use HCU-specific names for target detection and configuration. - Compile with `USE_HCU` and the HCU FP8 configuration. - Reuse the common `csrc/moe/moe_align_kernel.cu`. - Select the HCU Blelloch scan through `USE_HCU`. - Preserve the original CUDA warp scan and ROCm Blelloch scan paths. - Remove the duplicated `moe_align_kernel_hcu.cu`. ### EAGLE CUDA Graph support - Increase the HCU CUDA Graph custom-mask buffer capacity for EAGLE verification. - Account for the per-request draft-token square in addition to the context mask. - Keep the additional allocation isolated to HCU. ### GLM-5 inference accuracy - Bypass the unavailable Hadamard transform on HCU while keeping query and key tensors in the same unrotated space. - Preserve the existing CUDA and standard ROCm indexer paths. - Prevent the routed scaling factor from being applied twice when the HCU Triton MoE runner already applies it. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #30415724324](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30415724324)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #30415724264](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30415724264)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Realtime ASR: bounded long audio with encoder-window caching
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds an experimental, opt-in realtime ASR path for long audio items. It bounds the acoustic work submitted by each update, reuses completed audio encoder windows through SGLang's existing multimodal cache, and publishes decoder progress through the existing append-only transcription delta event. The current realtime path re-submits all audio accumulated for an item every 2 seconds. This preserves full acoustic context, but both prefill and memory grow with the session. On long items, per-update latency eventually dominates realtime playback. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, the opt-in path works as follows: 1. Keep the existing cumulative path through the first 60 seconds. 2. On the first update after 60 seconds, establish a one-way handoff from the cumulative transcript to encoder-window continuation. 3. Keep at most eight complete model-native 8-second audio windows plus the current incomplete tail in each later request. 4. Reuse complete-window embeddings through the existing MM cache; always recompute the mutable tail. 5. Carry older semantic context in a bounded, confirmed transcript prefix and generate only the new suffix. 6. Stream decoder progress through the existing `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta` event. No client schema or new event type is added. The default remains `cumulative`. Encoder windowing is currently enabled only for an explicitly declared English session on a local single-GPU runtime. Unsupported models, languages, and topologies keep the cumulative path and its 60-second safety boundary. ## Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Client appends PCM] --> B[2-second inference boundary] B --> C{Received audio over 60 seconds?} C -- No --> D[Submit audio from 0 to current end] D --> E[Cumulative transcript reconciliation] C -- Yes, first handoff --> F[Submit full audio once] F --> G[Create bounded confirmed-text prefix] C -- Yes, steady state --> H[Choose 8-second-aligned rolling range] G --> H H --> I[Up to 8 complete windows plus mutable tail] I --> J[Complete windows: existing MM embedding cache] I --> K[Mutable tail: encode, do not retain] J --> L[Decoder prefix plus new suffix generation] K --> L E --> M[Reconcile decoder updates] L --> M M --> N[Emit only append-safe delta text] N --> O[Existing transcription.delta event] O --> P[Advance absolute PCM cursors and compact old audio] ``` The first windowed request intentionally includes the full handoff audio. Once the handoff succeeds, steady-state requests retain no more than 64 seconds of complete encoder windows plus an incomplete tail shorter than 8 seconds. For example, a steady-state request near 130 seconds looks like this: ```text Older audio represented by confirmed text | v text: [bounded decoder prefix] audio: [w0][w1] ... [w7][tail] encoder: [cache hits / misses][encode] decoder: [prefix] + [rolling acoustic context] -> new suffix only wire: -> append-only stable deltas ``` ## Encoder-window reuse Qwen3-ASR declares its independent encoder geometry in the multimodal processor. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one complete window is 8 seconds and produces 104 encoder tokens. The generic audio-window builder: - extracts complete windows independently from the mutable tail; - expands one audio placeholder into per-window token ranges; - hashes the exact feature, attention mask, modality, and token geometry; - marks complete windows as cacheable; - marks the mutable tail `use_embedding_cache=False`; and - provides an explicit encoder batch key for variable-width audio features. A cache miss or eviction simply re-encodes the window. Cache reuse is therefore a performance optimization, not persistent session state and not a correctness dependency. The cache is model-owned only through declarative capability data: ```text Transcription adapter -> activation threshold, language gate, text-prefix limits Multimodal processor -> independently encodable window geometry Generic audio-window builder -> feature extraction, MM items, identity, cacheability Existing MM scheduler/cache -> lookup, miss batching, embedding assembly ``` There is no ASR-specific scheduler session, cache service, GPU lease, or model forward API. ## Append-only decoder streaming Each backend ASR request now uses `stream=True` when the realtime endpoint provides a callback. Partial decoder text is stripped of model-specific output markers, reconciled against cumulative or windowed transcript state, and sent only when it extends the text already published for that request. This is decoder-token-driven stable delta streaming, not a guarantee of one WebSocket event per tokenizer token. Local Agreement and suffix holdback may release several tokens together. If a completed decode revises a prefix that was already emitted, the request fails closed rather than sending a conflicting append-only transcript. No client changes are required. The wire protocol remains: ```text conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed ``` ## Enablement ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B \ --asr-long-audio-strategy encoder_window \ --asr-max-buffer-seconds 1800 ``` The client uses the existing realtime transcription session format and must declare a supported language before sending audio: ```json { "type": "session.update", "session": { "audio": { "input": { "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 16000}, "transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr", "language": "en" }, "noise_reduction": null, "turn_detection": null } } } } ``` `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` is the total accepted duration of one client item. Resident PCM is independently compacted after the encoder-window handoff. ## Alternatives evaluated Before selecting this implementation, four approaches were run under the same controlled setup: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one RTX 4090, Triton attention, identical native audio, 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, and 2-second flood-mode appends. Processing time is measured from the first send to the completed event; it measures server work rather than realtime playback. "Word error" is the normalized edit distance from the published reference; lower is better. | Approach | Long-audio behavior | Result | Decision | |---|---|---|---| | Cumulative | Re-submit all received audio every 2 seconds | 178.5 seconds of audio took 153.240 seconds; 291.1 seconds did not finish within 300 seconds | Keep as the unchanged default for normal items | | PCM tail slicing | Submit a bounded PCM tail plus 2-second overlap | 178.5 seconds took 109.735 seconds with 39.81% word error; longer cases did not finish | Rejected: bounded audio alone did not bound decoder-prefix work or preserve quality | | Encoder-aligned rolling context | Reuse complete windows and continue from confirmed text | Completed 291/593/908/1687-second inputs in 16.947/31.721/51.097/90.195 seconds | Selected: fastest completed long-stream approach and no client protocol change | | Independent segment finals | Finalize disjoint segments without a cross-segment prefix | Completed the same inputs in 18.804/35.343/55.127/98.233 seconds | Not selected: slower and requires replaceable snapshot semantics | The long-input comparison was: | Input | Cumulative | PCM slicing | Encoder windows | Independent segments | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | LongLibriHeavy 178.5 s | 153.240 s, 12.04% error | 109.735 s, 39.81% | 9.911 s, 11.30% | 11.586 s, 11.30% | | TED Al Gore 291.1 s | >300 s, incomplete | >300 s, incomplete | 16.947 s, 3.87% | 18.804 s, 4.66% | | LongLibriHeavy 592.6 s | >405 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 31.721 s, 7.95% | 35.343 s, 7.74% | | TED Craig Venter 907.8 s | >405 s, incomplete | >405 s, incomplete | 51.097 s, 4.50% | 55.127 s, 4.75% | | Earnings22 EXCOF 1686.7 s | >397 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 90.195 s, 12.80% | 98.233 s, 10.55% | ## Current-head GPU validation Environment: - Commit: `135eb6cf66` - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24,564 MiB - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B`, snapshot `5eb144179a02acc5e5ba31e748d22b0cf3e303b0` - Attention backend: Triton - Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, Transformers 5.8.1 - 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, 2-second appends - `--mem-fraction-static 0.75`, 100 MiB MM cache, 1800-second item cap All reported accuracy and performance cases below are complete, unmodified published source rows or source files. No reported audio was concatenated, cropped, padded, or silence-extended. For every successful WebSocket case: ```text concatenate(all transcription.delta text) == completed transcript snapshot events == 0 ``` Selected native-audio results on the current head: | Input | Duration | Server processing time | Reference word error | Result vs pre-streaming encoder-window path | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | Qwen English demo | 15.1 s | 0.814 s | no published reference | Byte-identical | | LongLibriHeavy | 75.0 s | 4.245 s | 11.02% | Same normalized output and error rate | | LongLibriHeavy | 93.4 s | 4.899 s; fresh rerun 5.222 s | 7.98%; rerun 7.45% | One-word first-run variation; rerun matched baseline | | TED Al Gore | 291.1 s | 16.837 s | 3.87% | Normalized-exact | | TED Barry Schwartz | 1104.6 s | 58.373 s; rerun 58.485 s | 2.39% both runs | Normalized-exact, full opening and ending | | Earnings22 EXCOF | 1686.7 s | 88.901 s; rerun 88.367 s | 12.80% both runs | Full opening and ending; 0.20-0.22% run-to-run text variation | The 28-minute Earnings22 run issued 844 backend requests. Of 888,608 prompt tokens, 511,624 were cache hits (57.6%); uncached prompt work was 376,984 tokens. The server remained healthy after every request. ### Paced streaming receipt The 15.05-second Qwen demo was also sent at realtime pace instead of flood mode: - 8 backend ASR requests; - 37 existing `transcription.delta` events; - 0 snapshot events; - the joined deltas were byte-identical to the completed transcript; and - the first six deltas arrived between 2.171 and 2.208 seconds after the run began, while 4 seconds of audio had been sent. This confirms that output is emitted while one backend decode is still running, while preserving the endpoint's append-only transcript contract. ## Public audio sources - Qwen English demo: <https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen3-ASR-Repo/asr_en.wav> - LongLibriHeavy: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/inesc-id/longlibriheavy> - TED-LIUM long form: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/tedlium-long-form> - Earnings22: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/earnings22> The benchmark manifest records dataset revisions, row ids, decoded-audio SHA256, wire-PCM SHA256, duration, sample rate, and reference text. Every result reported above uses one native source row or source file without local audio construction. ## Implementation | Area | Responsibility | |---|---| | `realtime/asr_processor.py` | Selects cumulative/windowed requests, reconciles decoder updates, advances absolute cursors, and compacts PCM | | `realtime/audio_buffer.py` | Maintains the per-item absolute PCM timeline | | `realtime/decoder_suffix.py` | Reconciles bounded decoder-prefix continuations without fuzzy deletion | | `realtime/session.py` | Owns WebSocket lifecycle and emits existing append-only events | | `streaming_asr.py` | Runs backend streaming generation and model-specific partial-output processing | | Transcription adapter | Declares activation, supported languages, decoder-prefix limits, and streaming postprocessing | | `audio_encoder_windowing.py` | Builds complete-window and mutable-tail multimodal items | | Base/Qwen multimodal processors | Provide generic construction plus model-config-derived window geometry | | `MultimodalDataItem` / `mm_schedule.py` | Support opt-in cacheability and producer-declared compatible miss batching | | `server_args.py` | Adds the off-by-default `encoder_window` strategy | ## Validation ```text 37 focused CPU tests passed 20 parameterized subtests passed py_compile passed git diff --check passed Ruff format check passed PR-file pre-commit hooks passed (black-jupyter skipped; no notebooks changed) GPU: 15-1687-second unmodified native-audio regression complete TED-LIUM and Earnings22 long-form recordings 1105- and 1687-second long-form reruns realtime-paced decoder-streaming trace ``` ## Limits - Encoder windowing is experimental, off by default, English-only for Qwen3-ASR, and currently limited to a local single-GPU runtime. - Operators must raise `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` above 60 seconds for the strategy to activate. - Stable deltas are driven by backend token streaming, but Local Agreement may group tokens. This is not raw one-event-per-token passthrough. - `finish_reason=length`, irreconcilable streamed-prefix revisions, and unsafe no-word-boundary continuation fail closed. - No timestamps, forced aligner, model-native streaming state, distributed encoder cache, or scheduler-owned ASR session is introduced. - Validation is bounded to Qwen3-ASR-0.6B on one RTX 4090 and does not establish universal multilingual quality or production capacity. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32087695151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32087695151)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32087694930](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32087694930)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [RFC] Rust Tree Core Full Component
signals.text: ## Motivation UnifiedTreeCoreInterface support in Rust (focus on FULL component-only in this PR for early review feedbacks) ## Motivation The Unified Radix Cache was split so the tree state machine lives behind `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface`, selected by `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` (default `python`). This PR adds a Rust implementation of that interface as an in-tree backend registered under `rust`, covering the Full attention component. The tree core does the per-request radix walks, lock bookkeeping, and eviction scans on the scheduler's critical path; moving it to Rust takes that work off the GIL and smooths tail latency, while cache orchestration (pools, controller, action application) stays in Python. **Review guide**: the PR is two commits. The first seeds the three main Rust files with their python counterparts commented out; the second replaces them with the Rust implementation, so its diff reads as the python-to-rust translation side by side. Files without a direct python counterpart arrive as new files in the second commit. ## Modifications ### `rust/mem-cache/` — the tree core crate **Tree state machine** - `src/unified_tree_core.rs` — match/insert walks (resumable inserts with action barriers), lock APIs, device/host eviction walks, tombstone-chain deletion, HiCache backup/load-back/prefetch specs, and the sanity checker. - `src/node.rs` — the tree node: per-(component × tier) value slots and child edges keyed `(namespace, page key)`, mirroring `RadixKey.child_key`. - `src/node_arena.rs` — node storage: freelist-recycled slots behind monotonic never-recycled `NodeId` handles, with a single root serving every namespace. - `src/value.rs` — the `NodeId`/`NodeIdx_` handle types and per-slot value state. **Keys and hashing** - `src/key.rs` — the child-key trait over unigram (`Vec<i64>`) and bigram/EAGLE (`(i64, i64)`) page keys. - `src/hash.rs` — per-page SHA-256 hash chains, bit-identical to the python/native hasher. **Eviction machinery** - `src/unified_lru_list.rs` — intrusive per-slot LRU lists with lock-aware walkers. - `src/evictable_node_set.rs` — O(1) evictable-leaf sets (swap-remove vector plus a slot lookup table). - `src/eviction_strategy.rs` — LRU/FIFO/FILO priority keys for the eviction heap. **Components** - `src/components/mod.rs` — the `TreeComponent` trait the per-attention components implement, plus shared dispatch helpers. - `src/components/full.rs` — the Full attention component: lock walks, eviction, and transfer commits. Only the `[Full]` set is enabled; SWA and Mamba follow later. - `src/component_type.rs` — the `ComponentType` boundary enum (`FULL`/`SWA`/`MAMBA` values shared with python). **Boundary** - `src/python_bindings.rs` — the PyO3 binding exposing unigram and bigram tree cores; component sets other than `[Full]` are rejected with a clear error. - `src/events.rs` — KV cache events (`BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved`/`AllBlocksCleared`) for cache-aware routing. - `src/error.rs` — typed tree-core errors. **Crate scaffolding** - `Cargo.toml` / `README.md` / `src/lib.rs` — standalone crate (links libtorch via `tch`; PyO3 behind a default feature, so `cargo test` runs `--no-default-features`), docs, and module wiring. - `src/tests/` — the unit suite mirroring `src/` one file per module (566 tests, including a randomized multi-namespace op-sequence fuzz with per-step sanity checks). ### `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/` — the backend package - `__init__.py` — registers the `rust` backend factory; the extension import stays inside the factory so unselected installs pay nothing. - `adapter.py` — `RustUnifiedTreeCore`, satisfying `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` over the binding (tagged-tuple action/transfer marshaling at the boundary). - `extension.py` — build-and-load shim: compiles the crate with cargo on first use, deriving libtorch and the Python headers from the running interpreter's torch install, and rpaths torch/lib into the cdylib. ### Wiring and tests - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/tree_core_registry.py` — `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust` lazy-registers the in-tree backend on first lookup (no import-order dependence). - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core.py` — end-to-end smoke through the compiled extension: registry resolution, insert/match round trip, lock accounting, and namespace isolation; module-skips when cargo is absent. ## Verification - `cargo test --no-default-features`: 566 passed. - Smoke suite: 4 passed end-to-end, including the first-use cargo build path. ## Perf Measurement & Accuracy TBD ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31288650474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31288650474)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31288650392](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31288650392)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Convert OE vocab size to Python int in NgramEmbedding to avoid Triton constexpr TypeError
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> When constructing `NgramEmbedding.oe_embeder` (the over-embedding layer used by LongCat-Flash's n-gram composite encoding), `num_embeddings` was passed as `self.exclusive_oe_embedder_size_sums[-1]`, which is a 0-d CUDA `torch.Tensor`, instead of the plain Python `int` required by `VocabParallelEmbedding.__init__`'s type contract. This tensor silently propagates through `VocabParallelEmbedding` (e.g. `pad_vocab_size`, `org_vocab_size`) because `torch.Tensor` overloads Python arithmetic operators, so no error surfaces at construction time. It later reaches `VocabParallelEmbeddingShardIndices._get_indices`, where Python's built-in `min()` does not unify types: ```python org_vocab_start_index = min(padded_org_vocab_start_index, org_vocab_size) ``` This tensor is then passed as a `tl.constexpr` argument into the fused Triton kernel `_vocab_parallel_embedding_kernel`, which only accepts Triton `tl.tensor`/`tl.constexpr`/Python scalars — not `torch.Tensor` — causing a hard compile-time failure: ``` sglang/kernels/ops/embeddings/vocab_parallel_embedding.py: _vocab_parallel_embedding_kernel triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 25:22: org_vocab_mask = (token >= org_vocab_start_index) & (token < org_vocab_end_index) TypeError("cannot convert 76677240 of type <class 'torch.Tensor'> to tensor") ``` **Why this surfaced only recently:** this line has passed a `torch.Tensor` instead of an `int` ever since `NgramEmbedding` was introduced, but it stayed harmless because `VocabParallelEmbedding.forward` used to compute the vocab mask via a `torch.compile(dynamic=True, ...)` function, which happily traces through tensor inputs without type checking. That changed in `dc0b3eb68` (#30948, "Fuse TP vocab-parallel embedding"), which replaced it with a native `@triton.jit` kernel and marked the vocab boundary arguments as `tl.constexpr` — a compile-time-only mechanism that requires plain Python scalars. Once that optimization landed, the same tensor value found no more tolerant type coercion path and instead an existing, previously-latent bug become a compile-time `TypeError`. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - In `python/sglang/srt/layers/n_gram_embedding.py`, convert `self.exclusive_oe_embedder_size_sums[-1]` to a Python `int` via `.item()` before passing it as `num_embeddings` to `VocabParallelEmbedding`, matching the type used by `word_embeder`. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> This is a type-only fix (converts a 0-d CUDA tensor to the equivalent Python int) and does not change any numerical computation. Verified end-to-end on a model (n-gram architecture, TP=8/EP=8): the server starts successfully, the previously-failing `oe_embeder` construction and Triton `_vocab_parallel_embedding_kernel` compilation now succeed, and both prefill and decode complete correctly (including with CUDA Graph enabled) for real inference requests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> Not applicable — this change does not affect the inference hot path or kernel computation, only a one-time scalar conversion during model initialization. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. signals.title: [Fix] DSA Indexer: pad heads for DeepGEMM paged MQA logits on decode/target-verify
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> `deep_gemm.fp8_paged_mqa_logits` hard-asserts the DSA indexer's head count against a fixed per-architecture allow-list (e.g. `{8, 16, 32, 64}` on sm90/100/120). Models whose `index_n_heads` falls outside this allow-list crash on the very first paged decode step: ``` sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py: _get_topk_paged -> deepgemm_paged_mqa_logits_split RuntimeError: Assertion error (/deepgemm/csrc/apis/attention.hpp:317): (arch_major == 10 and (num_heads in {8,16,32,64})) or (arch_major == 12 and (num_heads in {8,16,32,64})) or (arch_major == 9 and (num_heads in {32,64})) ``` The indexer already handles this on the prefill path: `_pad_heads_for_deep_gemm()` zero-pads `q_fp8`/`weights` up to 32 heads before calling the ragged kernels (`_get_topk_ragged` / `_get_topk_ragged_with_cp`), which does not affect topk correctness since the padded heads carry zero weight. However, this padding was never wired up on the paged path (`_get_topk_paged`) used for decode, target-verify, and draft-extend, so any model with `index_n_heads < 32` fails as soon as it reaches decode. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> In `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py`, apply the existing `_pad_heads_for_deep_gemm()` helper before both `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` call sites inside `_get_topk_paged`: - `use_dg_native` branch (`deepgemm_paged_mqa_logits_native`) - fallback branch (`deepgemm_paged_mqa_logits_split`) Both call sites now pass the padded `q_fp8_padded` / `weights_padded` instead of the raw `q_fp8` / `weights`, mirroring the padding already done on the ragged (prefill) path. No new parameters or behavior changes are introduced for models whose head count already satisfies the DeepGEMM allow-list (`_pad_heads_for_deep_gemm` is a no-op when `num_heads >= 32`). ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> Verified end-to-end with a model (MoE + MLA + DSA, `index_n_heads=16`) on 8 × H20-3e with `--tp 8 --ep 8`. Before the fix, decode crashed with the assertion above; after the fix, prefill and decode (including CUDA Graph capture/replay for bs=1~64) complete successfully and return correct completions via the OpenAI-compatible API. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> Not applicable — this change only adds zero-weighted head padding on a path that previously crashed (no valid baseline to compare against for affected models), and is a no-op for models whose indexer head count already meets the DeepGEMM allow-list. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support
signals.text: ## Motivation AMD gfx1250 is a new GPU architecture that differs substantially from the existing gfx95x and gfx942 targets SGLang already supports. Several components require gfx1250-specific paths due to architectural differences: - **No MFMA/WMMA FP4 scale instructions** (`V_WMMA_SCALE_F32_32X16X128_F4`): the existing CK/ASM `fused_moe` and fp4 dense GEMM paths produce garbage or crash. - **Triton `tl.dot(fp8, fp8)` miscompiles** for contraction dim ≥ 128 on gfx1250 (verified correct at K=64, broken at K≥128), requiring bf16 upcasting in the MLA attention Triton kernels. - **`llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.*` buffer instructions are absent** on RDNA4 (gfx12): the `quick_all_reduce` kernel would fail to compile. - **aiter CK-backed kernels (rope, QK RMSNorm, etc.) do not build** against the gfx1250 ROCm 7.15 image's composable_kernel. - **TileLang CK-backed buffer addressing does not compile** on gfx1250, blocking the Sinkhorn/MHC path. - **`num_stages > 1` Triton pipelines miscompile** on gfx1250, causing NaN in block-FP8 matmuls. - **ROCm SDK is pip-installed** (not at `/opt/rocm`) on this new image, requiring build and runtime path fixups for AITER, TileLang, MORI, and SGLang itself. This PR brings up gfx1250 support for DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B models with MXFP4/FP8 quantization. ## Modifications ### Infrastructure & Docker (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, `python/pyproject_other.toml`) - Added a new `gfx1250-rocm7_15` Docker build stage starting from `ubuntu:24.04` with pip-installed ROCm 7.15 SDK, PyTorch 2.11, and Triton 3.7. Includes path and symlink workarounds for a pip-based (non-`/opt/rocm`) ROCm SDK. - Added `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` build-arg and made `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` configurable; per-arch `TRITON_COMMIT_DEFAULT` env vars. - Added gfx1250-specific AITER build path (`ENABLE_CK=0`, pip `--no-build-isolation`) and MORI build path using `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` for the ROCm SDK. - Added gfx1250-aware TileLang `ROCM_PATH` override during CMake build. - Updated Triton rebuild logic to preserve the installed version string (workaround for ROCm 7.15 / [rocm-systems#7643](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/issues/7643)). - Renamed `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` → `SGLANG_VERSION` to avoid leaking SGLang's nightly version into AITER's version. - Added `compressed-tensors==0.16.0` pin to `runtime_common` (supports torch ≥ 2.10) and dropped the old per-`srt_hip` `==0.15.0` pin. - CI install script: ROCm-version-aware AITER rebuild (`pip --no-build-isolation` for ROCm ≥ 7.15), MORI `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` fix, and MORI commit extraction validation. ### Core utility (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`) - Added `is_gfx1250_supported()` (cached) to detect AMD RDNA4 by `gcnArchName`. - Extended `mxfp_supported()` to include `"gfx1250"`. ### sgl-kernel (`sgl-kernel/setup_rocm.py`, `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/quick_all_reduce_base.h`) - Added `gfx1250` to the allowed arch list in `setup_rocm.py`; gfx1250 shares the `E4M3` FP8 type and the 128KB dynamic smem budget with gfx950. - Guarded `llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.load/store.v4i32` declarations behind `#if !defined(__gfx1250__)`, providing stub no-ops for RDNA4 where those intrinsics don't exist. ### Attention kernels (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/`) - **`decode_attention.py`**: Do not downcast `q` to `fp8` before the QK dot; instead upcast K to `q`'s dtype (`bf16`) for the dot product, avoiding the gfx1250 fp8 dot bug at K≥128. Also keep softmax weights `p` in fp32 for the P·V accumulation (recovers GSM8K accuracy ~0.82 → ~0.92 on gfx1250 R1). - **`extend_attention.py`**: Same fp8 upcast fix and fp32 P·V fix for the prefill extend/unified kernels. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_decode.py`**: On gfx1250, dispatch DSv4 sparse decode attention to `aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_decode_sparse.pa_decode_sparse` (the triton path) instead of the custom Triton implementation. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_prefill.py`**: Disable the OPUS (gfx950 ASM) prefill path on gfx1250. ### MoE gate JIT kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/moe_fused_gate.cuh`) - Widened `__shfl_down_sync` mask from `0xFFFFFFFF` to a 64-bit `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFULL` on gfx1250 (which requires a 64-bit sync mask), while staying 32-bit on all other arches. ### Layernorm (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`) - On gfx1250, use aiter's Triton RMSNorm and `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add` instead of the CK-backed aiter equivalents (which do not build). - Added pure-torch (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_torch`) and Triton (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_triton`) implementations of the Sinkhorn MHC kernel, dispatched on gfx1250 since TileLang's CK-backed addressing does not compile there. ### Quantization – FP8 (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`) - **`fp8_kernel.py`**: Added `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_gfx1250`, a gfx1250-specific block-FP8 matmul that: (1) upcasts fp8 operands to bf16 before `tl.dot`, (2) uses only `num_stages=1` (no SW pipelining), and (3) avoids modulo-wrap index tricks that miscompile on gfx1250. Selected automatically when `_is_gfx1250` is set. - **`fp8_utils.py`**: Force `_use_aiter = False` on gfx1250 (CK/MFMA-dependent aiter quant/GEMM kernels cannot run), directing gfx1250 to the pure-Triton block-FP8 path. Extended `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` to accept pre-quantized `(input, input_scale)` from gfx1250's fused quant ops (skipping re-quantization). - **`fp8.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) instead of the gfx950 `shuffle_scale` (e8m0 layout) for FP8 MoE weight scales. Respect the `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` flag to select the triton a8w4 kernel shuffle layout. ### Quantization – MXFP4 Quark schemes (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/`) - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`**: On gfx1250 with `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`, dequantize FP4 weights to bf16 at load time (since no dense fp4 GEMM is available) and run a plain bf16 linear forward. Includes a pure-Python MXFP4 e2m1 → bf16 dequantization LUT. - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) for W4A4 MoE weight scales (instead of `e8m0_shuffle`). Shuffle weights with the (16,16) aiter layout when `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` is set. - **`quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py`**: Added a dedicated gfx1250 W4A8 MoE path (`_use_gfx1250_w4a8`): bypasses the aiter CK/ASM fused_moe entirely; uses aiter's triton `moe_gemm_a8w4` kernel with a contraction-major, gate/up-interleaved, unshuffled weight layout. Weight preparation (`_process_weights_gfx1250`) and forward (`aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward` in new file `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`) are implemented separately from the gfx950 path. ### New file: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py` - Implements MXFP4 W4A8 GPT-OSS MoE forward for gfx1250 via `moe_gemm_a8w4`: routing, manual activation gather (in-kernel TDM gather disabled on gfx1250), static-FP8 downcast, two-GEMM (gate_up + down) execution with fused SwiGLU, and scatter back to token order. ### RoPE (`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py`) - Fall back from aiter's CK rope kernels to SGLang's native rope on gfx1250 (aiter rope does not build on this arch). ### Communicator / fused quant (`python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py`) - On gfx1250, use `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` (triton, group_size=hidden_size = per-token) instead of aiter's CK `rmsnorm_quant` / `add_rmsnorm_quant` kernels. ### Sampler (`python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py`) - Disable aiter's greedy sample kernel on gfx1250 (not supported), falling back to `torch.argmax`. ### Capture mode (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/capture_mode.py`) - Disable `torch.compile` during CUDA graph capture on gfx1250 (compilation + capture together triggers issues on this arch). ### MLA attention (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py`, new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`) - On gfx1250 (`AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`), substitute the aiter `fused_qk_rmsnorm` (CK-backed, doesn't build) with a self-contained Triton RMSNorm or pure-torch fallback from the new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`. - Fixed the RoPE skip condition to check membership in `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` (not a string equality check), preventing an incorrect empty-K bug on non-aiter backends. ### DSv4 decoder layer (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_common/utils.py`, `amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`) - Extended all `_is_gfx95_supported` guards that gate MXFP4 fused quant, MQA q/k-norm, post-attention layernorm fused rmsnorm, and the fused MHC post/pre path to also include `_is_gfx1250_supported`. - On gfx1250, the fused MHC path is enabled by `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE` alone (no TileLang dependency), and the aiter Triton `try_fused_hc_post_pre` is used at all token batch sizes (no M-threshold cap, since there is no TileLang fallback). - gfx1250 does not skip the post-layernorm step after the Triton MHC kernel (since `norm_fused=False` for the aiter path). ### C4 attention indexer (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py`) - Added `_use_torch_fn` guard so the `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH` env var correctly prevents the 1D c4sl unsqueeze on gfx1250. ### Server args (`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`) - Track `_mem_fraction_static_set_by_user`: when the user explicitly sets `--mem-fraction-static`, skip the automatic 0.85 scaling for `aiter` backend with long contexts (instead, emit a warning so the user knows what is happening). ## Accuracy Tests Passed E2E accuracy tests of DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B. GPT-OSS-120B > AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8/ --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --prefill-attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter --max-running-requests 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache --page-size 64 DSR1 > ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 SGLANG_MOE_SHUFFLE_GFX1250=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=0 SGLANG_INT4_WEIGHT=0 SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=1 SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1 SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --attention-backend triton --max-running-requests 128 --kv-cache-dtype auto --page-size 64 DSv4-Flash > SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0 SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --max-running-requests 256 --disable-radix-cache --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ## signals.title: [AMD] Fix DeepSeek-V4 fused-RMS FP8 scale metadata on gfx950
signals.text: ## Summary DeepSeek-V4's fused-RMS FP8 producer calls AITER with `transpose_scale=True`, which writes CK-ready transposed scale storage but returns contiguous-looking `[M, G]` metadata. For logical scales `[[a,b,c],[d,e,f]]` the storage is `[a,d,b,e,c,f]` and needs stride `(1, M)`; read as contiguous it is misinterpreted as `[[a,d,b],[e,c,f]]`. The CK materializer from #29275 trusted that metadata and associated scales with the wrong token/group cells whenever `M > 1`, producing a ~1-2 point GSM8K regression on DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8/FP4 on gfx950/ROCm 7.2 (tracked in #31490). This restores the truthful `[M, G]` strides at the DeepSeek-V4 producer with a zero-copy view before the scale reaches CK. The aiter GEMM path stays byte-identical to #29275, so GLM-5.2-FP8 (which #29275 fixed) is unaffected **by construction** — the repair lives only in `deepseek_v4._fused_rmsnorm_fp8_quant`. Carries forward @hdt98's fix from #31727 (which was approved but stalled on large-topology validation); mechanism analysis and unit tests are theirs. `Fixes #31490`. ## Validation MI355X, GSM8K 1319Q / 8-shot, stock (buggy image) vs. this change, overlaying only the two changed source files: | topology | leg | stock | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | dp8ep8 1P1D | dsv4flash-fp4 | 0.913 | **0.926** | | dp8ep8 1P1D | dsv4flash-fp8 | 0.915 | **0.924** | | wide-EP16 2P1D | dsv4flash-fp4 | 0.901 | **0.933** | | wide-EP16 2P1D | dsv4flash-fp8 | 0.902 | **0.924** | | wide-EP16 2P1D | dsv4flash-fp4-mtp | 0.918 | **0.929** | | wide-EP16 2P1D | dsv4flash-fp8-mtp | 0.915 | **0.924** | | wide-EP16 2P1D | dsv4pro-fp8 (control) | 0.923 | **0.951** (no regression) | The dp8ep8 numbers reproduce the table in #31727; the wide-EP16 2P1D rows are additional coverage. On EP16 the two non-MTP Flash legs were below the 0.91 gate on a 3-run mean before this change and clear it after; Pro was already green and stays green. ## Test plan - [x] `test/registered/quant/test_fused_rms_fp8_group_quant.py` — transposed-scale layout contract (gfx950) - [x] `test/registered/unit/layers/test_fp8_bpreshuffle_scale.py` — repair + idempotence + producer wiring (CPU) - [x] Real MI355X dp8ep8 1P1D and wide-EP16 2P1D GSM8K runs (table above) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #30504984465](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30504984465)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #30504984117](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30504984117)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [CPU] Fix NUMA/core binding for DP ranks
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Before this PR, `ModelRunner.init_threads_binding` picked the NUMA node / core group for a worker using `tp_rank`. Under DP, DP rank 0 and DP rank 1 both resolve to tp_rank=0 and get bound to the same NUMA node/cores instead of being spread across the machine. This PR fixes this incorrect binding. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> `init_threads_binding` now takes `numa_index` (the worker's global device id) and `world_size = dp_size * tp_size * pp_size`, instead of `tp_rank` and `tp_size`, so every rank across every DP replica maps to a distinct NUMA node / core group. Removed the `world_size == len(threads_bind_list)` equality assert for the explicit `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` path, replacing it with only the per-rank bounds check. This permits the router-mode case (local `world_size=1`, multi-group bind string) while still catching a bind list that's too short. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: docs(cookbook): Qwen3.6 config-driven deployment + measured speed benchmarks
signals.text: Migrates the Qwen3.6 cookbook page to the **config-driven Deployment/Playground engine** (as for DeepSeek-V4 / Qwen3.5) and adds **measured speed benchmarks**. The legacy `qwen36-deployment.jsx` generator is removed. ## Config — `configs/qwen/qwen3.6.jsx` (44 cells) `h100/h200/b200/b300` × `{35B-A3B (MoE), 27B (Dense)}` × `{bf16, fp8, +nvfp4 on Blackwell}` × `{low-latency, high-throughput}`, plus **Xeon `balanced`** (27B/35B-A3B × bf16/fp8). low-latency = MTP/EAGLE + mamba radix-cache v2; high-throughput = MTP off; Xeon = spec unsupported → single `balanced` recipe (`--device cpu`, tp 3/6). GPU cells tp=1 single-node. ## Faithfulness - Cells reproduce the generator command **verbatim** — verified by executing `generateCommand()` across the matrix: **42/44 exact**. Parsers (`--reasoning-parser`/`--tool-call-parser`) omitted (Playground-only; DSv4 convention). - The 2 non-verbatim cells are **b300 35B-A3B NVFP4**, adding `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`: the generator's default moe runner crashes on that model on 0.5.16, and this is exactly how b300 was measured. - Bench = `bench_serving` random isl 8192 / osl 1024, `--random-range-ratio 1.0 --warmup-requests 64 --flush-cache`; LL @ conc 1+16, HT @ conc 1024+4096. `tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = output_throughput / tp × (isl+osl)/osl`. ## Coverage — 32/44 measured - Measured: **B200 (12) @ 0.5.15, H200 (8) + B300 (12) @ 0.5.16**. - Pending (render "pending"): **H100 (8)** — no 8×H100 capacity this run; **Xeon (4)** — no CPU box (Deploy command shown, no speed). - Blackwell NVFP4 version note: b200 on 0.5.15 (default moe runner works → plain command), b300 on 0.5.16 (needs the flag) — **each cell matches its own bench**. ## Follow-ups - Bench H100 (8) once capacity frees. - Re-bench b200 35B-A3B NVFP4 on 0.5.16 with `flashinfer_cutlass` to unify the Blackwell backend. - Apply the +13% mem0.92 tune to h200 35B-A3B bf16 HT (clean conc 1024+4096 re-bench). signals.title: [NPU] Fix Qwen3.5 NPU prefix cache
signals.text: ## Motivation Support prefix cache for Qwen3.5 on Ascend NPU. When serving Qwen3.5 with the Ascend attention backend, the NPU backend defaults `page_size` to 128. Qwen3.5 uses the Mamba radix cache path, whose `no_buffer` mode requires `page_size == 1`. This caused scheduler initialization to fail with: ```text AssertionError: Page size must be 1 for MambaRadixCache v1, got 128 ``` Fixes https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/522. ## Modifications - Recognize Qwen3.5 text architectures in model-specific Mamba radix cache handling. - Automatically switch Qwen3.5 Ascend NPU runs from `no_buffer` to `extra_buffer` when radix cache is enabled and `page_size != 1`, preserving the Ascend default `page_size=128` while keeping prefix cache enabled. - Register Qwen3.5 text model entry classes so text checkpoints can resolve to the local implementation. - Include Qwen3.5 text architectures in draft/MTP architecture rewriting. - Add a unit test covering Qwen3.5 CausalLM, Moe CausalLM, MTP, and conditional architectures on Ascend NPU page-size handling. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not modify model forward math or kernels. Validation performed: ```bash PYTHONPATH=/data/sglang/python python3 -m pytest /data/sglang/test/srt/test_server_args_mamba_cache.py -q ``` Result: ```text 1 passed, 5 subtests passed ``` NPU smoke test with real weights: ```bash source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh cd /data/sglang export PYTHONPATH=/data/sglang/python:${PYTHONPATH:-} python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /data/models/Qwen3.5-9B \ --max-running-requests 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --attention-backend ascend \ --port 30000 ``` Observed: ```text Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration with Ascend attention uses page_size=128 ... Automatically using --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer to keep prefix cache enabled. Mamba Cache is allocated. Tree cache initialized: source=default impl=MambaRadixCache hybrid_swa=False hybrid_ssm=True hierarchical=False streaming_wrapped=False ``` A `/v1/chat/completions` request returned HTTP 200 and generated tokens successfully. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed benchmark was run. The change only adjusts server argument handling for the Ascend NPU Qwen3.5 prefix-cache configuration and adds model architecture registration coverage. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). `git diff --check` passed; full pre-commit was not run. - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: fix(xpu): enable compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8 on XPU (RedHatAI FP8-dynamic models)
signals.text: ## Motivation compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8 quantized models (e.g. RedHatAI's `*-FP8-dynamic` family — `Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic`, `Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503-FP8-dynamic`, `granite-4.0-h-small-FP8-dynamic`, `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-FP8-dynamic`) currently fail to serve on XPU. The very first failure happens at layer-construction time, before any kernel dispatch: ``` AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled ``` Fixing that surfaces two further, distinct XPU-specific issues before the model actually serves and generates correctly. ## Modifications - `compressed_tensors.py` (`CompressedTensorsConfig`): `_check_scheme_supported` unconditionally called `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()`, which is CUDA-only. Only `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` has a real XPU-usable kernel path today (via the existing device-agnostic `_apply_fallback_scaled_mm` in `fp8_utils.py`, not a missing native kernel); every other capability-gated scheme (NVFP4/cutlass, Marlin-based W8A16Fp8, WNA16, ...) is explicitly rejected with a clean `RuntimeError` on XPU instead of crashing on the CUDA-only call. - `fp8_kernel.py`: the non-CUDA/non-MUSA branch never imported `sgl_per_token_quant_fp8`/`sgl_per_tensor_quant_fp8` for XPU, even though sgl-kernel-xpu registers both natively — this caused a `NameError` on the first forward pass once the above crash was fixed. - `fp8_utils.py` (`apply_fp8_linear`): the activation-quant padding decision (`num_token_padding=17`, meant to make `torch._scaled_mm` more performant on CUDA for small batches) was only skipped when `cutlass_fp8_supported` (CUDA-only). sgl-kernel-xpu's per-token quant kernel requires `output_q` to exactly match `input`'s shape and doesn't support padded output, raising a shape-mismatch `RuntimeError` whenever a forward pass had fewer than 17 rows (e.g. small prefill/decode steps). - fp8.py (Fp8MoEMethod.apply): the native sgl-kernel-xpu MoE fast path was taken unconditionally on XPU, before checking the explicitly-selected MoE runner backend. This made --moe-runner-backend triton a no-op on XPU for this quantization scheme — the native kernel path was still hit and raised "current MoE does not support use_fp8_w8a8" even when the Triton runner had been explicitly requested. Now skips the native XPU path when the runner backend is explicitly triton, falling through to the existing Triton dispatch below. - internvl.py: InternVLChatConfig has no top-level num_experts — the MoE config lives on the nested llm_config (the text-backbone config). Fixes an AttributeError when loading MoE-based InternVL variants. - runtime_context.py (get_stream): replaced a hardcoded torch.cuda.Stream() with torch.get_device_module(device).Stream(), so the named process-level side stream is created on whichever device backend is active instead of always assuming CUDA. - topk.py (biased_grouped_topk_gpu, XPU path): the topk_sigmoid kernel requires correction_bias to be float32. The CUDA branch a few lines above already casts it; the XPU branch passed it through unchanged, raising RuntimeError: correction_bias must be float32 on the first generation request for some MoE models. Now cast to float32 before the call, matching the CUDA branch. ## Accuracy Tests Verified locally end-to-end in a docker container (XPU backend, Intel Arc Pro/BMG) with the patched sglang installed in place of the image's baked-in copy: - `RedHatAI/Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic` (TP=1, `--attention-backend intel_xpu`) serves and evaluates gsm8k (5-shot) correctly: - `exact_match,flexible-extract = 0.5891 ± 0.0136` - `strict-match = 0.5390 ± 0.0137` - Regression check that the shared code paths touched here don't affect other backends/schemes: - All three changes are gated behind `if _is_xpu:` / `elif _is_xpu:` branches that are new no-ops on every other platform; `cutlass_fp8_supported`-driven CUDA behavior is unchanged (verified by re-reading every other call site of the touched functions — `scaled_fp8_quant`'s other callers in `fp8_utils.py` are gated by `if _is_cuda:`/`if _is_hip:`, never reaching the changed XPU branch on other devices). - No currently-passing XPU model can regress from these changes: any compressed-tensors quantized model on XPU previously hit the `_check_scheme_supported` crash unconditionally at layer-construction time (before this PR), so none could have been passing beforehand. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — these are correctness/compatibility fixes for an existing fallback code path (`_apply_fallback_scaled_mm`), no new kernel or scheduling changes. The activation-quant padding skip on XPU has a minor performance implication (an extra kernel-launch on small batches that would otherwise reuse a padded buffer), but padding was never functional on XPU before this PR (it crashed), so there's no regression relative to current behavior. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32006682399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32006682399)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32018554309](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32018554309)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU] Add sparsity-driven KV offload for DeepSeek DSA on Ascend
signals.text: # [NPU] Add sparsity-driven KV offload for DeepSeek DSA on Ascend USTC: Yinhe Chen, Chengru Yang, Chengjie Tang(SXU, intern at USTC-IAI), Youhui Bai, Cheng Li Ascend NPU Network Lab\*\*: Ning Zhao, Heyuan Li, Biao Wang, Pengcheng Wang, Chen Sun ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in sparsity-driven KV offload path for DeepSeek DSA models using the Ascend MLA attention backend. When enabled, the runtime: - keeps the DSA index KV cache on the NPU; - stores the full MLA latent KV cache in NPU-registered host shared memory; - maintains a per-request, 2,048-token selected-KV cache on the NPU; - resolves top-k cache hits through a device slot map; - fetches cache hits from device memory and misses from registered host memory; and - runs sparse flash attention over the compact selected-KV buffer. The feature is disabled by default. Without the environment variable, the existing Ascend MLA KV-cache and attention paths remain unchanged. Related to sgl-project/sglang#31779 (including motivation, accuracy tests, speed test profiling, etc.) Kernel dependency: sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#636. ## Accuracy Tests Accuracy tests based on GSM8K. ## Design ```text DSA top-k indices | v device slot-map lookup |-----------------------------| | hit | miss v v selected-KV device cache registered host KV | | |-------------+---------------| v compact selected-KV buffer | v NPU sparse flash attention | v selected-KV cache refill ``` ### Feature gating The path is enabled with: ```bash export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPARSITY_DRIVEN_KV_OFFLOAD=1 ``` The configuration is accepted only when all of the following are true: - the runtime device is NPU; - `--attention-backend ascend` is selected; - the model uses the MLA backend; - the model is recognized as a DeepSeek DSA model(DeepSeek V3.2); and - `--max-running-requests` is set explicitly. Invalid combinations fail early with a configuration error. The explicit request limit bounds the per-process host and device allocations, both of which scale with request capacity. ### KV storage and pool sizing With offload disabled, `NPUMLATokenToKVPool` allocates the native latent K/V buffers and the DSA index buffer as before. With offload enabled: - native NPU latent K/V buffers are not allocated; - the DSA index buffer remains device-resident; - the KV-token cell size is calculated from `index_head_dim * num_layers * element_size`; and - attempts to use native K/V accessors fail explicitly instead of dereferencing an absent buffer. The small hook in `model_executor/pool_configurator.py` is required so the scheduler's token capacity matches the physical index-only device pool. It delegates to the NPU-specific configuration only when this feature is enabled and otherwise preserves the existing calculation. ### Host storage and request lifecycle `SparseKVCacheManager` allocates per-layer host shared-memory tensors and registers them with the current NPU. The registered device-visible address is used by the custom indexed-copy operator for D2H/H2D movement. The manager also: - resets per-request slot-map state whenever a request slot is newly allocated; - includes the request-pool padding row when sizing sparse buffers; - reserves sentinel rows and columns for padded or invalid graph entries; and - validates request IDs, sequence lengths, tensor ranks, and index shapes before copying. ### Prefill and decode For prefill/extend, newly produced latent KV rows are copied to host storage. The sparse attention path can gather the request KV into a compact TND buffer and invoke NPU sparse flash attention with normalized DSA sparse-index shapes. For decode: 1. the DSA top-k indices are checked against the per-layer slot map; 2. device-cache hits and host-cache misses are copied on separate NPU streams; 3. stream events join both copies before the selected-KV cache is refilled; 4. the compact selected K/V tensors are passed to NPU sparse flash attention in BSND layout; and 5. the slot map is updated for the next decode step. ACL report processing is registered for graph streams so host callbacks can be serviced when graph execution is used. ## Code changes | File or module | Change | | --- | --- | | `hardware_backend/npu/sparsity_driven_kv_offload/config.py` | Adds the environment switch, platform/model validation, and index-only cell-size calculation. | | `hardware_backend/npu/sparsity_driven_kv_offload/manager.py` | Adds registered host KV storage, request lifecycle handling, slot-map maintenance, multi-stream prefetch, and cache refill. | | `hardware_backend/npu/sparsity_driven_kv_offload/attention.py` | Adds the dedicated prefill/decode sparse-attention path and DSA index-shape normalization. | | `hardware_backend/npu/sparsity_driven_kv_offload/host_callback.py` | Adds ACL report-thread and stream-subscription support. | | `hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py` | Makes native latent K/V allocation conditional and retains the device index cache. | | `hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py` | Initializes the manager and dispatches DSA sparse attention to the offload path only when enabled. | | `model_executor/pool_configurator.py` | Uses the NPU index-only cell size when offload is enabled. | ## Benchmark results Model: GLM-5.1 Accuracy: no-loss compared to baseline (AIME-26) Throughput (Decode): 39.42 TPS (baseline) -> 63.06 TPS **(1.6x faster)** Settings: TP16, colocation deployment with graph optimization enabled, details included in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31779 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #31602307140](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31602307140) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31602306885](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31602306885)
