signals.title: fix(moe): follow the built runner's expert-ID namespace, not the configured backend
signals.text: ## Problem `StandardDispatcher` decides whether to remap `topk_ids` into the rank-local expert range from `get_moe_runner_backend()`. Only the AITER runner keeps global expert IDs, which its comment states correctly — but the *configured* backend is not necessarily the backend of the runner this layer got. On ROCm, compressed-tensors W4A16 selects `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE`, which builds a Triton runner: ```python # compressed_tensors_wNa16_moe.py:540 self.runner = MoeRunner(MoeRunnerBackend.TRITON, moe_runner_config) ``` With the configured backend at `auto` and `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (which the ROCm images set), the dispatcher concludes "AITER runner, keep global IDs" and skips the `local_expert_mapping` remap in `StandardDispatcher.dispatch`. The Triton path then sizes its buffers from the rank-local expert count — `moe_align_block_size` allocates `cumsum_buffer` with `num_local_experts + 2` int32 — while `topk_ids` still holds global IDs, so `sgl-kernel/csrc/moe/moe_align_kernel.cu:40` does `atomicAdd(&cumsum_buffer[topk_ids[i] + 1], 1)` with an index up to 384 on a 98-entry buffer. Every rank dies during warmup: ``` Memory access fault by GPU node-N (Agent handle: 0x...) on address 0x7f... Reason: Unknown. ``` one per rank, reasons varying between `Unknown` and `Write access to a read-only page`. It reproduces with plain `sglang.launch_server`, no LoRA and no training framework: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Kimi-K2.5> \ --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend triton --trust-remote-code ``` and `--moe-runner-backend triton` avoids it, which is the clue. On CUDA the same code is safe: `_use_aiter` requires HIP, and CUDA + `auto` selects the Marlin scheme instead. Any EP>1 MoE on ROCm whose quant method builds a non-AITER runner under `--moe-a2a-backend none` reaches this — W8A8-FP8 with `CHANNEL` strategy builds an AITER runner and was never affected. ## Fix `MoeRunner` already receives the same `MoeRunnerConfig` object the dispatcher is built from a line later (`fused_moe_triton/layer.py:357-358`). Record the backend on the config at runner construction, and let the dispatcher use it to **override the inference only when the built runner is not AITER**. Narrowing only, deliberately: `new = old and (recorded is None or recorded.is_aiter())`, so the set of layers that keep global IDs can only shrink. Several quant methods promote `auto` to AITER without consulting `_use_aiter` — `mxfp4.py:1436`, `fp8.py:2115` under `SGLANG_INT4_WEIGHT`, `quark_int4fp8_moe.py` and `quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` among them — so on a ROCm box without `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` they build an AITER runner while the old inference returns False. That is the mirror-image mismatch; it may well be a real bug, but it needs hardware testing for those schemes, and narrowing-only keeps it exactly as it is today. Every backend reachable here on ROCm (Triton, DeepGEMM, Humming) sizes its kernels from `num_local_experts`, so the override is only ever correcting the direction that writes out of bounds. `skip_local_expert_mapping` in the same constructor still reads the configured backend, unchanged and commented as deliberate. ## Test `test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py` execs `StandardDispatcher.__init__` against a hand-built config, so it gains the new field plus a case over all four configured/recorded combinations, and one asserting `MoeRunner.__init__` writes the field on the shared config in the first place. Verified on MI350X / ROCm 7.2 at `--tp 4 --ep-size 4`: | probe | before | after | |---|---|---| | Kimi-K2.5 W4A16, default backend | memory access fault on all 4 ranks | serves | | same with `--moe-runner-backend triton` | serves | serves | Paths where the built runner is AITER, including unquantized BF16 MoE, are untouched by construction: the override cannot set the flag True. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31995985292](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995985292)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31995985010](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995985010)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(lora): build the MoE LoRA align JIT kernel on ROCm
signals.text: ## Problem `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/lora/moe_lora_align_kernel.cu` does not compile on ROCm, so MoE LoRA cannot run there: ``` moe_lora_align_kernel.cu:9:10: fatal error: 'cub/cub.cuh' file not found ``` and once that include is resolved, `cudaFuncSetAttribute`, `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` and `cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin` are undeclared as well. The AOT build hipifies its sources, so they can spell CUDA names directly; the JIT path hands the `.cu` to `hipcc` with `-DUSE_ROCM` and no rewrite, so this file has to provide the names itself. ## Fix - Include `hipcub` under `USE_ROCM` the way `sgl-kernel/csrc/moe/moe_topk_softmax_kernels.cu` does, plus a `namespace cub = hipcub` alias, because on the JIT path there is no hipify to rewrite `cub::` for us. The alias sits inside `namespace moe`, where the single `cub::BlockScan` use lives. - Add the three missing names to the ROCm alias block in `jit_kernel/include/sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`, which this file already includes. - Pass the kernel through `std::bit_cast<const void*>` as `csrc/deepseek_v4/paged_mqa_metadata.cuh` does: HIP's `hipFuncSetAttribute` takes `const void*` where CUDA has a templated overload. These three aliases are what this kernel needs. Other `jit_kernel` files that spell `cudaFuncSetAttribute` still fail on other CUDA-isms, so this does not make them ROCm-clean — it also cannot regress them, since anything referencing these names under ROCm already failed to compile. ## Test Registers the kernel's existing unit test for AMD so this cannot regress unnoticed. Verified on MI350X / ROCm 7.2: the kernel JIT-compiles from a cold cache and `test/registered/jit/test_moe_lora_align_block_size.py` passes 32/32, two of which exercise the `std::bit_cast` branch. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31995488415](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995488415)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31995488235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995488235)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Spawn, don't fork, the benchmark server process
signals.text: `sglang.benchmark.*` launched the server with the platform-default start method (fork on Linux), but the parent already initializes the accelerator in ServerArgs.__post_init__ -- get_xpu_memory_capacity() calls torch.xpu.mem_get_info(), get_device_sm() calls torch.cuda.get_device_capability(). The forked child inherits a dead context and dies on its first device op: RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize XPU in forked subprocess. launch_server() does force spawn, but only via _set_envs_and_config() once it is already running inside the child, which is too late. Use an explicit spawn context for the process itself. Latent on text-only CUDA runs, where the forked child touches the device only after handing off to spawned scheduler workers; reproducible on XPU and on any backend once the child does device work during warmup (e.g. a VLM processor's image.to(device)). Fixes #34709 <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation sglang.benchmark.* launches the server with the default start method (fork on Linux), but the parent already initialized the accelerator in ServerArgs.__post_init__ (XPU: torch.xpu.mem_get_info(); CUDA: torch.cuda.get_device_capability()). The forked child inherits a dead context and fails on its first device op: RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize XPU in forked subprocess. launch_server() forces spawn, but only from inside the already-forked child (entrypoints/engine.py:1703) — too late. Latent on text-only CUDA (the child does no device work before spawning scheduler workers); fatal on XPU, and on any backend once the child touches the device during warmup (e.g. a VLM processor's image.to(device)). ## Modifications endpoint.py: launch_or_reuse_server() — create the server process with an explicit spawn context: proc = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process(...) Payload is picklable; the child already expects spawn semantics. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no kernel/model-forward change; outputs bit-identical. Verified on Nvidia GPU and Intel XPU backend environment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No inference-path impact. Spawn adds a few seconds of one-time startup cost, outside every measurement window (benchmarks start only after server_is_up()). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31908209035](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31908209035)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31908208627](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31908208627)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Decouple encoder parallelism from the DiT parallel layout
signals.text: ## Motivation A pipeline DP replica owns one request batch. Encoder parallelism should be selected inside that replica, independently of the DiT TP/SP layout, without mixing requests across `--dp-size` replicas. The previous version of this PR assumed that every rank under pure DiT TP held a complete encoder. That is not true after main centralized the encoder TP context: native encoder weights are sharded across the DiT TP group. This update preserves that contract and composes batch DP only across independent encoder copies. ## Design - Add a replica group over `tp-sp-pp-cfg`, excluding the pipeline DP axis. Explicit `--encoder-parallel fold` uses this group, so every GPU in each replica participates without crossing replicas. - Add an encoder-DP group over `sp-pp-cfg` at a fixed TP coordinate. Every TP rank in one encoder copy receives the same batch slice; corresponding TP lanes gather outputs across encoder copies. - A pure-TP replica has one TP-sharded encoder copy. All GPUs already participate in its forward, so there is no additional rank-level batch DP. - In a common TP x SP replica, each SP position owns one TP-sharded encoder copy, allowing TP and encoder batch DP to compose. - `auto` now checks the actual encoder-DP group when choosing DP over folding. Explicit `dp` and `fold` remain operator-controlled policies. - Keep main's `EncoderTensorParallelMixin` and bound TP context intact. ## Testing - Unit coverage verifies the `tp2 x sp2 x dp2` encoder-DP groups: `[0, 2]`, `[1, 3]`, `[4, 6]`, `[5, 7]`. - Unit coverage verifies pure TP, TP + encoder DP, per-replica isolation, folded-encoder exclusion, policy gates, and explicit replica folding. - Removed the former elementwise 2-GPU toy test because it had no TP-sharded layers and therefore could not validate the real encoder TP contract. - Pre-commit passes on the complete PR diff. GPU CI was triggered by the updated branch; no new local GPU result is claimed for this merge update. ## Documentation The encoder parallelism guide, CLI reference, and MiniMax H3 cookbook now describe the replica boundary, pure-TP behavior, and TP + encoder-DP composition. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add focused unit coverage. - [x] Update documentation and docstrings. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32030136897](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32030136897)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32030136540](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32030136540)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Metrics] Add kv_cache_usage_perc Prometheus gauge (#5979)
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #5979 — users migrating from vLLM expect a Prometheus gauge for KV cache utilization (`vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc`); SGLang currently has no KV-cache-only gauge. Three earlier attempts (#20158, #22612, #27701) all exposed `stats.token_usage` under a new name and stalled for the same reason: - `token_usage` is `max(full, swa, mamba)` — the scheduler's *bottleneck* signal. On hybrid SSM models (Qwen3-Next, Kimi Linear) it reports Mamba state-pool pressure as "KV cache usage" (flagged by Codex review on #27701). - Aliasing an existing value adds no information — #20158 was closed after review for exactly this. Design discussed in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/5979#issuecomment-5232386783. ## Design `sglang:kv_cache_usage_perc` = **`max(full, swa)`, Mamba excluded** — precisely the semantics `PoolStats.get_kv_token_stats()` already computes ("NOTE: mamba pool is not included in the token usage calculation"). The ratio was previously computed there and then discarded in `update_scheduler_stats()`; this PR stores it and wires it to a gauge. Reported unrounded (unlike `token_usage`, which rounds to 2dp). | gauge | semantics as a KV-cache signal | |---|---| | `sglang:token_usage` | `max(full, swa, mamba)` — bottleneck across all pools; over-reports on hybrid SSM | | `sglang:full_token_usage` | full-attention pool only; under-reports on hybrid SWA (SWA pool is also KV cache) | | `sglang:kv_cache_usage_perc` (new) | `max(full, swa)` — KV cache pools only | For plain-attention models the new gauge equals `full_token_usage`, giving vLLM users a drop-in equivalent of `vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc`. Purely additive — no renames, no behavior changes. ## Changes - `pool_stats_observer.py`: keep the previously-discarded KV usage ratio and store it on `SchedulerStats` (all three report paths — prefill / decode / idle — go through this one function) - `metrics_collector.py`: `SchedulerStats` field, gauge definition, `log_stats` wiring - `test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py`: register the metric in `essential_metrics` - `docs/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx`: document with example output ## Testing E2E on RTX 4090 (this branch, `--enable-metrics`, Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, after serving a request): ``` sglang:token_usage{...} 0.0 sglang:full_token_usage{...} 0.00022778178504992218 sglang:kv_cache_usage_perc{...} 0.00022778178504992218 ``` Plain model: new gauge equals `full_token_usage` as designed (and shows the value `token_usage` hides by rounding). Pool-semantics matrix (direct `PoolStats.update_scheduler_stats()` check, all passing): | scenario | kv_cache_usage_perc | token_usage | |---|---|---| | plain, full=0.72 | 0.72 | 0.72 | | hybrid SWA, full=0.5, swa=0.3 | 0.5 | 0.5 | | hybrid SWA, full=0.3, swa=0.5 | 0.5 | 0.5 | | hybrid SSM, full=0.5, mamba=0.9 | **0.5** | 0.9 | | hybrid SWA+SSM, full=0.5, swa=0.3, mamba=0.9 | **0.5** | 0.9 | The hybrid SSM rows are exactly the cases where an aliased `token_usage` gauge would have reported 0.9 as "KV cache usage". <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32000755269](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32000755269)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32000755088](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32000755088)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [SM120] dspark: widen SWA index width to an instantiated sparse-MLA shape
signals.text: ## Purpose DSPARK does not start on consumer Blackwell (SM120). CUDA graph capture aborts: ``` Check failed: (ok) is false: Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration: model=DSV4 num_heads=16 topk=192 page_block_size=64 topk_extra=0 extra_page_block_size=0 ``` `build_dspark_swa_page_indices` derives its index width from `swa_window + block_size`, which lands on **192** for the DSPARK shape (128 sliding-window entries + the draft block). FlashInfer's SM120 sparse-MLA prefill matrix instantiates `topk` in `{128, 512, 1024, 2048}`, so the host gate rejects 192 — and it rejects it by aborting the process, not by falling back. `num_heads=16` itself is supported. ## What this does Widen an uninstantiated index width to the next instantiated one. The padded tail is `-1` and the kernel already masks per row through `topk_length`, so the extra columns are inert. `128` stays in the set deliberately: it is the only width the DSv4 dual (SWA extra-cache) dispatch instantiates, and widening it breaks the MTP path. ## Relationship to flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4380 The exact-192 shape is the better long-term answer and now exists upstream — #4380 added `topk` 192/256 for DSV4 decode and single-cache prefill, and vLLM builds on it in vllm-project/vllm#51538 by carrying the true dense width (aligned to the kernel's 64-entry tile) instead of rounding. That path is not available here yet: | FlashInfer | prefill dispatch widths | | --- | --- | | 0.6.15.post1 (pinned by sglang) | 128, 512, 1024, 2048 | | v0.6.17 (latest stable) | 128, 512, 1024, 2048 | | nightly 0.6.18 | 128, **192**, **256**, 512, 1024, 2048 | sglang pins `flashinfer_python==0.6.15.post1`, so this change is what works on the pinned dependency. When the pin moves to a release carrying #4380, switching to the exact width is a one-line follow-up. I prototyped that follow-up (probe `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` at runtime, use 192 when present, fall back otherwise) and measured it — see below. It made no measurable difference, so it is not included here rather than carrying the extra complexity and its two fragile assumptions (intersecting across head counts, and using the decode table as a proxy because FlashInfer exposes no prefill capability query). ## Measurements 4x RTX 6000D (SM120), TP4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.80`. ISL 8192 / OSL 1024. Rounded 512 (this PR) vs exact 192 (nightly-0.6.18 build), same tree, same FlashInfer: | bs | width | throughput (tok/s) | TPOT (ms) | ITL (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 192 | 91.00 | 10.87 | 9.82 | | 1 | 512 | 92.13 | 10.73 | 9.82 | | 8 | 192 | 313.41 | 18.00 | 10.62 | | 8 | 512 | 311.69 | 17.09 | 10.63 | | 32 | 192 | 520.8 / 522.2 | 37.7 / 39.0 | 21.4 / 22.4 | | 32 | 512 | 524.5 / 522.7 | 38.4 / 38.4 | 21.2 / 21.9 | Identical within run-to-run noise at every batch size (bs=32 was repeated twice per arm; the within-arm spread is as large as the between-arm difference). Accuracy, `sgl-eval run aime25 --n-repeats 16 --max-tokens 200000` (480 samples): | arch | pass@1 | spread | truncated | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SM120, 4x RTX 6000D | **98.54%** (473/480) | 96.7–100%, stdev 1.71% | 0 | | SM100, 4x B200 (reference, no patch needed) | 98.96% (475/480) | 93.3–100%, stdev 2.01% | 0 | The SM120 row is re-measured on the exact commit in this PR. An earlier run of the same eval on the pre-cleanup variant of this patch (module-level arch detection instead of the lazy call) gave 98.33% / stdev 3.65%, i.e. the same result within noise. Without this change the SM120 server never reaches ready state, so there is no same-arch baseline to compare against. ## Regression check No effect off SM120: `_sm120_index_width` returns its argument unchanged when `is_sm120_supported()` is false, and arch detection is called inside the function so it does not pull CUDA into module import. On SM120 with `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (fp8), FlashInfer 0.6.18, GSM8K 50q: | config | accuracy | TPOT (ISL 8K, bs1) | | --- | --- | --- | | deep_gemm MoE | 0.980 | 12.41 ms | | MTP-2 | 0.960 | 6.97 ms | Both match their pre-existing baselines. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31684742437](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31684742437)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31684742223](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31684742223)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] [NPU] Optimize LTX-2/2.3 inference performance for NPU

## Motivation NPU compatibility and performance optimizations for LTX-2/2.3 inference, along with fixing crashes on the main branch. ## Modifications Performance improvements: - Converted all `float64` computations to `float32` for NPU (NPU does not support float64 precision) - Use sglang's NPU-optimized `RMSNorm` instead of `torch.nn.RNSNorm` - Reuse CUDA Triton kernel for NPU paths ## T2V Accuracy Tests Fails in the main branch on 14 Aug. signals.title: [kernel] One rmsnorm kernel for every hidden size, tuned from Python
signals.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation Three rmsnorm kernels (`rmsnorm.cuh`, `fused_add_rmsnorm.cuh`, `rmsnorm_hf.cuh`) with three hand-written dispatches covered a fraction of the hidden sizes SGLang serves. `_is_supported_rmsnorm_hidden_size` admitted only multiples of 256 (512 above 8192); fused-add only multiples of 16 up to 8192. **1536, 2304, 2560 — Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-30B, Gemma — all fell back to `forward_native`.** The HF-semantics variant was a separate file only because the flag could not be threaded through, and reaching it cost a `.contiguous()` copy. ## Modifications **One kernel.** `kFusedAdd` and `kCastXBeforeOutMul` become template flags. A tile may over-cover its row: `in_bound` predicates the surplus lanes and folds away entirely when the row divides the tile, so **any even hidden size up to 16384** works. The launcher takes an arbitrary row stride and checks alignment at runtime, which drops the `.contiguous()`. **Schedule moves to Python.** `(vec_size, num_threads, copy_mode)` are the trailing template arguments; C++ only validates them. Retuning now costs one JIT compile per configuration instead of invalidating every module built from the file. Parameterizing by thread count rather than unroll makes padded tiles expressible, and they sometimes win — 5120 gains 17% at batch 1 from a tile that idles 17% of its lanes. **Weight staging (`CopyMode`)**, the one new idea, is taken from [flashinfer's CuTe DSL rmsnorm](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.6.15.post1/flashinfer/norm/kernels/rmsnorm.py) — credited in the file header. RMSNorm reads its row twice, so something must survive the reduction; flashinfer parks the *input* tile in smem to keep it out of registers. Applying the same trick to the *weight* tile frees `kUnroll` vectors of register file: | config | unroll | registers | cp.async | TMA | |---|---|---|---|---| | rmsnorm 12288, 256t | 6 | 87 | **64** | **64** | | rmsnorm 16384, 128t | 16 | 254 | 154 | 168 | | fused_add 12288, 256t | 6 | 102 | **64** | **63** | 12288/256t crossing 64 registers doubles occupancy, 2 → 4 blocks/SM. `cp.async` fills the tile on SM80+; a single `cp.async.bulk` under `elect.sync` on SM90+. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_rmsnorm.py` + `test_fused_add_rmsnorm.py`: **2587 passed** - A correctness matrix over both kernels x bf16/fp16 x both semantics x padded and exact tiles x warp and CTA traits x block sizes from 16 to 1024: **2160 comparisons, 0 over tolerance**, and all three copy modes **bit-identical** to each other (1296 tensor pairs via `torch.equal`) - `sm_80` and `sm_90` cross-compiles of every schedule the Python side emits; TMA is correctly rejected below sm90 (`Feature 'elect' requires .target sm_90`) - End to end on B200: **Qwen3-8B gsm8k 0.927** (300 examples, TMA path live at dim=4096), Qwen3-0.6B 0.635 ## Benchmarking and Profiling B200, bf16, vs the best configuration found by an exhaustive sweep of the previous kernel: | dim | bs=1024 | bs=4096 | bs=8192 | |---|---|---|---| | 4096 | 0.97x | **1.04x** | 1.01x | | 8192 | **1.08x** | **1.04x** | **1.03x** | | 12288 | **1.03x** | **1.05x** | **1.03x** | | 16384 | 1.01x | **1.07x** | **1.04x** | 16384 at batch 8192 lands at 83.9 us, **matching flashinfer for the first time** (previously 3.6% behind). Small batches keep the existing lead — 3072 is 1.78x flashinfer at batch 4. Staging is worth 1.29x (cp.async) / 1.31x (TMA) over the register path at dim=12288, batch 8192, and nothing below unroll 4. The win is proportional to **unroll**, not to hidden size: 16384's best shapes use many threads and low unroll, so they gain least. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32027150214](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32027150214)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32027149890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32027149890)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature][DSpark] Support Speculators-format checkpoints and ragged multimodal CUDA graphs
signals.text: <!-- Suggested title: [Feature][DSpark] Support native Speculators checkpoints and ragged multimodal CUDA graphs --> > **Status:** implementation, public-checkpoint compatibility, and paired > fixed-output performance tests are complete. Greedy target-output equivalence > remains unresolved, so this PR does not claim lossless output. ## Motivation This PR extends SGLang's DSpark path to run native Speculators checkpoints end to end in eager mode, CUDA Graph replay, and ragged multimodal verification. It covers the checkpoint config and weight formats, both DSpark anchor layouts, independent draft vocabularies, and the runtime paths needed to verify them. Native Speculators checkpoints are not limited to the shared-vocabulary layout that DSpark originally supported in SGLang. They may contain an independent reduced-vocabulary LM head plus a draft-to-target (`d2t`) mapping. For example, the public [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark) checkpoint has: - target vocabulary: 248,320 tokens; - draft `lm_head`: 32,000 tokens; - `markov_w1`: target-vocabulary input; - `markov_w2`: draft-vocabulary output; - `d2t`: a 32,000-entry mapping from sampled draft IDs to target IDs. Treating these tensors as a shared-vocabulary model either fails during loading or feeds/scatters IDs in the wrong vocabulary space. Speculators checkpoints can also use either DSpark draft-block layout: - `sample_from_anchor=false`: the anchor is only a conditioning token. The draft forward has `gamma + 1` slots, and slot 0 is excluded from sampling and verification. - `sample_from_anchor=true`: the anchor is a trained prediction. The draft forward has `gamma` slots. Using the wrong width does not always crash; it can shift real draft positions and reduce the acceptance length toward 1. After checkpoint loading and draft geometry were working, mixed image/text validation exposed separate problems in ragged mRoPE and linear attention. The ragged-path changes make multimodal verification work under CUDA Graphs. During the same validation, I found a pre-existing interaction between `/flush_cache` and DSpark draft CUDA Graphs: emptying the allocator cache can invalidate addresses retained by a captured graph. This is included as a separate DSpark graph-lifecycle fix. ## Modifications - Normalize the native Speculators DSpark config format, whose backbone lives under `transformer_layer_config`, without importing checkpoint-side remote config code. This path is gated on `speculators_model_type=dspark` and reuses the existing config-dictionary fetch. - Load an independent tensor-parallel `ParallelLMHead` when `draft_vocab_size != target_vocab_size`; preserve the original shared-head path for full-vocabulary DSpark checkpoints. - Support the asymmetric Markov geometry: `markov_w1` consumes target IDs while `markov_w2` and the draft LM head produce draft-vocabulary logits. - Map sampled draft IDs through `d2t` before storing tokens or feeding the next Markov step. For probabilistic acceptance, scatter draft probabilities into target-vocabulary columns and leave unmapped target tokens at `-inf`. - Validate mapping shape/range and fail early for unsupported reduced-vocabulary checkpoints without `d2t`. Load `t2d` as checkpoint metadata without using it in the decode path. - Read authoritative `gamma` and `sample_from_anchor` metadata, reject inconsistent checkpoint geometry at startup, and propagate the same draft width through eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. - Keep verification, KV commit, and acceptance accounting at `gamma` real draft tokens. Only the draft forward width changes. - Build speculative mRoPE positions from each request's actual verify length; CUDA Graph padding uses zero-delta ghost positions. - Add packed-to-dense scatter/gather support for ragged linear attention and declare ragged CUDA Graph support per attention backend. - Preserve captured DSpark draft graph allocations across `/flush_cache` while still clearing logical request, KV, radix, grammar, and metrics state. - Use an 8-token SPS `M` bin for compact scheduling and recompute the simulated bonus token at the acceptance boundary. - Add regression coverage for full/reduced vocabularies, configuration normalization, tensor-parallel LM heads, Markov shapes, `d2t` mapping, corrected-logit scatter, both checkpoint layouts, CUDA Graphs, ragged mRoPE, linear attention, cache flushing, and SPS fitting. ## Status - [x] Bonus-anchor and dense anchor-first checkpoint layouts - [x] Full-vocabulary DSpark checkpoint regression - [x] Independent reduced-vocabulary LM head - [x] Draft-to-target vocabulary mapping and probabilistic corrected logits - [x] Eager and CUDA Graph draft-width propagation - [x] TP=1 and TP=2 public RedHat checkpoint inference - [x] Greedy and non-greedy sampling - [x] Ragged multimodal mRoPE and linear-attention layouts - [x] DSpark CUDA Graph behavior after `/flush_cache` - [ ] Greedy token-level equivalence with target-only decoding - [x] Same-GPU paired performance benchmark at concurrency 1 and 8 ## Correctness Tests On the PR branch rebased onto upstream `main` on 2026-08-13, the focused suite reports `212 passed, 54 subtests passed`; the reduced-vocabulary file reports `26 passed, 2 subtests passed`. Python compilation, formatting, focused Ruff checks, and `git diff --check` also pass. The public-checkpoint validation uses [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4) as the target and [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark) as the draft. The environment has PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, and FlashInfer 0.6.17. The official workloads are MT-Bench (80 two-turn conversations, 160 requests) and the MMSpec test split (600 conversations, 723 turns). Correctness runs compare target-only autoregressive (AR) decoding with DSpark under greedy decoding at concurrency 1. | Workload | AR repeat | DSpark completed | Exact first-turn AR/DSpark token sequences | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 160/160 | 160/160 | 8/80 | | MMSpec | 723/723 | 723/723 | 18/600 | The AR repeat is exact on both workloads, confirming a deterministic baseline. DSpark completes every request, but target-output equivalence is not established. A separate 20-prompt eager probe also mismatches on all 20 prompts, so disabling decode CUDA Graph does not remove the divergence; its cause remains unresolved. Acceptance is aggregated from raw server counters. The acceptance length below includes the target bonus token. | Workload | Draft acceptance rate | Acceptance length including bonus | | --- | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 32.863% | 3.6257 | | MMSpec | 24.956% | 2.9925 | Separate focused lanes also pass TP=1 and TP=2 inference, greedy and non-greedy sampling, ragged multimodal CUDA Graph replay, and a post-`/flush_cache` request. ## Fixed-output Performance The formal fixed-output benchmark consists of three same-GPU paired repeats with service restart and unmeasured warm-up before each mode: - MT-Bench first turns with exactly 256 output tokens per request; - a deterministic 20-per-topic MMSpec subset with exactly 128 output tokens per request; - closed-loop concurrency 1 and 8; - pair order `target -> DSpark`, `DSpark -> target`, `target -> DSpark`. All 2,400 measured requests completed with the required output length. Values below are medians across the three runs; the interval is the range of the three paired throughput ratios. The raw service logs and result manifests bind these runs to the reported source commit and execution-environment freeze; strict reanalyzing after the provenance audit produced an identical summary. | Workload | C | Target tok/s | DSpark tok/s | Paired throughput | p50 E2E target -> DSpark | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 1 | 151.64 | 262.32 | 1.730x [1.726, 1.741] | 1.687s -> 1.008s | | MT-Bench | 8 | 715.30 | 942.30 | 1.317x [1.300, 1.327] | 2.853s -> 2.076s | | MMSpec | 1 | 132.89 | 178.49 | 1.343x [1.343, 1.346] | 0.937s -> 0.715s | | MMSpec | 8 | 467.98 | 519.74 | 1.111x [1.110, 1.124] | 2.086s -> 1.754s | The gain is not uniform across the latency distribution. MT-Bench C=8 p99 E2E regresses in all three repeats (paired target/DSpark ratios 0.906-0.920). MMSpec C=8 has about 9% higher p50 TPOT and mixed p99 E2E results (paired ratios 0.938-1.092, median 0.961). This supports a stable fixed-output throughput and p50 E2E improvement under the reported configuration, not a universal tail-latency improvement. SSE chunk gaps are not reported as token-level ITL because one speculative event can expose multiple tokens. TPOT is client-observed and amortized from the first to last token-bearing event. ## Known limitation Greedy token-level equivalence with target-only decoding has not been established for the tested public checkpoint. The reported results demonstrate checkpoint compatibility, request completion, online acceptance, and fixed-output performance, but do not support a lossless-output claim. ## Related work - Original SGLang DSpark implementation: [#30261](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30261) - Bonus-anchor checkpoint layout: [#30982](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30982) - vLLM Speculators checkpoint support: [vLLM #47093](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47093) Thanks to the authors and reviewers of these changes for the checkpoint-layout analysis and reference behavior. ## Contributors Engine Architecture Group 5, Engine Infrastructure Department, Xiaohongshu (RedNote): Su Zhan, Fei Ziyu, Hong Chenchen, Luo Zhaokai, Jin Huayi. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32011377578](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32011377578)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32011377305](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32011377305)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [HiCache] Buffer-only mode for HiCache host memory layer
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation There has been extensive discussion around making HiCache work better for small host-memory setups: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28614, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20535, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16909, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14056. Out of this, we've converged on the following design: use the L2 host-memory layer as a buffer. This decouples L2 from the complex tree management and the frequent, pressure-driven evictions it would otherwise incur, while still capturing the full benefit of IO latency hiding and maximizing cache hit rate through the larger L3 layer. signals.title: [PD] Preserve decode KV across retraction in HiCache
signals.text: ## Motivation PD decode retraction currently preserves KV in per-request CPU tensors. Reusing HiCache host pools avoids a second host-memory path and also lets speculative draft KV survive retraction. ## Modifications - Add explicit and inferred `cpu_tensor` / `host_pool` retraction backends behind `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup`. - Resolve the backend once the decode KV pool exists, since it cannot be decided in `ServerArgs.__post_init__`. The resolved value lands on the config bags via `get_context().override(...)`, and every reader goes through `get_disagg()` — `server_args` stays the pristine read-only record. - Make `--hicache-ratio` `Optional` and give it its default at that same point (`1.0` for host-pool retraction, `2.0` otherwise), so a decode server can size the host pool 1:1 with the device pool. The `hicache_ratio` reads in `hiradix_cache.py` and `hybrid_pool_assembler.py` move to `get_memory()` accordingly — that is the only reason those two files appear in the diff. - Reserve and validate HiCache capacity for compatible MHA and hybrid-SWA decode pools. - Back up, restore, and discard target plus speculative draft sidecar KV through the flattened L2 transfer path from #34793. - Force host-pool retraction in the PD EAGLE3 integration test and assert retracted requests retain speculative acceptance above the calibrated 1.3 gate. - Add a CUDA round-trip test that poisons both target and draft device KV before restoring them at different slots. ## Accuracy Tests Run on the current revision: - Python compilation for all changed files - All applicable pre-commit hooks on the changed files - The `_EXPOSED` / `_OVERRIDDEN_AND_READ` pin sets in `test_supplied_instance_exposure_ratchet.py` are unchanged by this PR, and the mutation / global-config-read ratchets stay at their zero baselines Run on an earlier revision of this branch, before the rebase onto post-#34793 main: - `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py` - `test_runtime_context_override.py` - `test_runtime_context_config_bags.py` The CUDA target/draft round-trip and the PD EAGLE3 integration test have not been executed locally (no GPU on the dev host). They are registered in CI. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. The new transfers execute only when decode requests are retracted; the steady-state decode path is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit and integration tests. - [ ] Update documentation (no user-facing documentation change needed). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (GPU tests are delegated to CI; no steady-state performance change). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31984438697](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31984438697)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31984438611](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31984438611)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [LoRA] Add the sgl_lora MoE execution engine with JSON config resolution
signals.text: ## Motivation MoE (expert-weight) LoRA serving in SGLang currently runs through the experimental TRT-LLM path (`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm` + virtual experts). That path has structural limits: - **Blackwell-only**: the trtllm-gen kernels require SM100/120, so there is no expert-LoRA path at all on Hopper (H200). - **Virtual-expert routing scales with `max_loras_per_batch × num_experts`**, so multi-adapter serving degrades sharply as slot capacity grows. - **No prefill CUDA graphs with LoRA**, and no support for shared-outer adapter factors (gate_up A / down B shared across experts, `expert_dim=1` — the native format of some recent MoE adapters). This PR adds `sgl_lora`: a self-contained MoE-LoRA execution engine selected with `--lora-execution-engine sgl_lora`, built from an exhaustive kernel/fusion/overlap sweep on GB300, B200, and H200 across three models (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B, Inkling-Small; per-expert and shared-outer adapters, ranks 8–64). ## Modifications - **Engine** (`python/sglang/srt/lora/sgl_lora/`): masked expert-major decode path and route-major serial prefill path; per-expert and shared-outer factor layouts; two base-GEMM providers (DeepGEMM, CuTeDSL); side-stream overlap windows for the shared-decode path; capacity-flat routing (cost scales with *active* adapters, not slot capacity). - **JSON config resolution** (`sgl_lora/configs/{gb300,h200,default}.json`): every kernel-family/fusion/overlap/tile decision is data, resolved per (layout, activation, phase, batch shape) through ordered first-match scenario rows with fail-closed validation — a malformed row, unknown plan field, or unknown predicate key aborts startup instead of serving a wrong plan. `SGLANG_SGL_LORA_CONFIG_DIR` points at an override config root (arch JSONs at top level, M-bucketed base-GEMM tile tables under `gemm/`). Every shipped row carries real-model sweep provenance; unknown architectures fall to a conservative serial fallback (`default.json`). - **Prefill CUDA graphs with MoE LoRA** (breakable backend), including graph-stable LoRA workspaces. - **Dense-module gate**: adapter targets are pruned to weight-backed modules at registration, and per-module effective ranks let mixed multi-adapter batches skip dense-LoRA work for adapters that carry no weights for a module (the shared dense kernels in `kernels/ops/gemm` stay byte-identical to upstream — the gate enters as a batch-info view). - **Onboarding tuner** (`benchmark/kernels/lora_moe/tune_lora_config.py`): `--check` (CI-gateable coverage report), `--emit-seed` (serve a new geometry immediately), `--sweep` (e2e-tunes the two geometry-sensitive axes; writes winners back into the seed). - Guards: expert LoRA + DP-attention / elastic-EP / EPLB fail closed at startup (the DP-attention token-axis limitation exists silently in the legacy path today). Scope: bf16 serving path. fp8/nvfp4 qlora support is planned as a follow-up in this PR (the tuner carries a `TODO(quant)` and the config resolver already fails closed on future `quant` predicate keys). Structure note: the first commit is the engine; subsequent commits are review-round changes and will be squashed before undrafting. Two orthogonal fixes found during this work ship separately: `fix/chunked-sgmv-cache-key` (csgmv compile-cache key omits codegen parameters) and `fix/swa-kvpool-v-head-dim` (SWAKVPool lacks `get_v_head_dim`, crashing hybrid-SWA models on the triton attention backend). ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/unit/lora/`: 248 passed / 6 skipped (H200), including config-resolution pins, kernel numerics vs an fp32 oracle, byte-identity pins for the decode kernel policy, and prefill graph-vs-eager bit-exactness. - Greedy-decode correctness on real adapters vs the legacy triton reference: per-token logprob deltas at the measured bf16 noise floor (per-expert and shared-outer, all three campaign models). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Protocol: `bench_one_batch_server`, input 4096 / output 1024, bs 1/8/16/32, `max_loras_per_batch=4` distinct adapters, medians after first-pass discard. Baseline = experimental TRT-LLM LoRA path at its best posture (incl. prefill graphs where it can use them). - **Qwen3.5-35B (GB300, TP4)**: prefill +15–19%, decode parity. - **Qwen3.5-397B (B200, TP8)**: prefill +23%, decode −1.2%…+4.5% across bs. - **Inkling-Small (GB300)**: decode +0.5%…+11.9% with the model's shared/routed-expert parallelism active on both engines; prefill +2–5%. - **H200 (fa4 posture)**: the TRT engine cannot run (SM100/120-only kernels); vs the only runnable incumbent (legacy virtual experts on triton fused_moe): decode +1.7%…+19.7%, prefill +1.0–1.5% at bs≥8 (−13% at bs1). - **Prefill CUDA graphs**: 2.5–3.0× prefill throughput vs eager at equal chunking (the incumbent disables prefill graphs under LoRA). - **Multi-adapter**: routing cost is capacity-flat; with 4 distinct adapters/ranks resident, +15–24% prefill and +2–17% decode vs the incumbent. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Surface AMD ROCm 7.2 state in the PR CI-states block
signals.text: ## Motivation `pr-states.yml` maintains the **CI States** block at the bottom of every PR body, but it only queries `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml`. A merge oncall reading the PR description therefore sees the CUDA result and nothing else, even though `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` is a full PR gate that most PRs dispatch. ## Modifications **`.github/workflows/pr-states.yml`** - New row `Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2)` with its own `<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720 -->` markers, reusing the existing `runIcon` / `runLink` rendering. - `"PR Test ROCm 7.2 (AMD)"` added to the `workflow_run` subscription, so the block refreshes when the AMD run is requested and when it completes. This is also the path that covers fork PRs, whose `pull_request` token is read-only. - One AMD-specific state: unlike `pr-test`, the AMD gate has an `on.pull_request.paths` filter, so "no run for this SHA" legitimately means *nothing ROCm-relevant changed* rather than a missed dispatch. It renders as `:heavy_minus_sign: **Not triggered for this commit**` instead of the stale-push warning the Extra row uses, and its lookup skips the retry budget for the same reason — retrying cannot conjure a run that was never dispatched, and a later dispatch refreshes the block through its own `workflow_run` event. - Two adjustments keep the added row from degrading the existing ones. The three lookups are independent, so they now run concurrently and the extra query costs no wall-clock time. The per-workflow query also asks for more than one run and skips `skipped` records, because `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml` subscribe to `labeled` events and a label-only dispatch can leave a deliberately skipped run ahead of the substantive attempt for the same SHA. **`.github/workflows/pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** - A `notify-pr-states` job mirroring the one already in `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml`. `workflow_run.completed` fires only once per run record, and rerunning (`/tag-and-rerun-ci`) is how a PR recovers a gate-blocked AMD run, so without this the row would go stale precisely when it starts carrying real results. The workflow already declares `actions: write`, and fork PRs are excluded for the same read-only-token reason documented on the existing jobs. Example rendering with `run-ci` present, CUDA green, and a PR that touches no ROCm-relevant paths: ``` ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): ✅ [Run #1](…) Latest PR Test (Extra): ⚠️ **Not enabled** -- add `run-ci-extra` label to opt in. Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): ➖ **Not triggered for this commit**. ``` ## Verification The rendering is tested offline, because it structurally cannot be tested by a PR: `pull_request_target` always runs the **base branch** version of the workflow, so this branch's copy never executes on its own PR. The inline `actions/github-script` body was extracted from the YAML and run under Node against a mocked Actions API, covering: no `run-ci` label; a path-filtered AMD gate; in-progress and failed AMD runs; a skipped record not masking the real run; and re-patching an already-patched body without duplicating the block or drifting between passes. `scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py`, `check-yaml`, `codespell`, and the whitespace hooks pass on both files, as does `actionlint` (excluding warnings this workflow already carries on `main` for the empty dropdown option and the self-hosted runner labels). ## Known limitation A red AMD row is still ambiguous between "`pr-gate` blocked it" and "tests actually failed" — the same ambiguity the existing rows have, noted in the file's own comment above `runIcon`. Distinguishing them needs a per-run jobs lookup; worth doing, but kept out of this PR to hold the diff to one reviewable concern. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CI reporting only, no runtime code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — no change to runner allocation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — n/a, no unit-test harness exists for the inline workflow scripts; tested as described above. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — n/a. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: Store mamba prefix-cache checkpoints at the configured SSM state dtype
signals.text: The mamba radix track path snapshots the SSM state at the last chunk boundary of chunk-unaligned sequences so a later prefix-cache hit can restore it. That path read the per-chunk states `h`, which are always stored in the activation dtype (bf16) — so the checkpoint was pinned to bf16 regardless of `--mamba-ssm-dtype`. With the default fp32 pool (and likewise for fp16), a cache hit restored a lower-precision state than a cache miss keeps, making cached and uncached runs numerically diverge. The chunk-aligned path and the in-place final-state path already wrote at the pool dtype; only this intermediate-state path could not honor it. This PR snapshots the in-kernel fp32 accumulator and casts it once to the pool dtype, so checkpoints on this path faithfully follow `--mamba-ssm-dtype` (float32 / bfloat16 / float16): - Triton `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` gains `track_state`/`track_chunk_idx`: at the tracked chunk boundary it stores the fp32 accumulator into a per-sequence buffer, and `_track_mamba_state_extend` copies that buffer (instead of the rounded `h`) into the track slots, converting to `ssm_states.dtype` once. - The Helion prefill kernel gets native support for the same snapshot (separate varlen kernel configs so the tuned non-track configs are untouched). - New `LinearAttnKernelBase.supports_track_state_snapshot` capability flag; `KDAAttnBackend` asserts it before allocating the snapshot buffer, so a prefill kernel that cannot honor the snapshot fails loudly instead of silently caching unwritten state. FlashKDA's Triton fallback now forwards the track arguments (it previously dropped them, which would have written zeros into the checkpoint slots). - Tests: `test_kda_track_state.py` checks the snapshot matches an fp32 truncated-run reference and is strictly more precise than the bf16 `h` row, for both the Triton and Helion backends; a CPU bookkeeping test pins every KDA prefill kernel's declaration of the new capability flag. ## Accuracy Cold vs warm teacher-forced logprob comparison across a prefix-cache resume, in the style of #34808, on a single GB300 (TP1, no DCP — this defect needs no page/chunk grid mismatch, only the default fp32 pool and a chunk-unaligned prompt): ```bash SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 1 --page-size 64 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --disable-overlap-schedule --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --port 30000 ``` Cold scores the full sequence on an empty cache; warm flushes, prefills the prompt alone (both prompts are 34 mod 64, so the resume lands on the tracked intermediate checkpoint), then scores the full sequence again. One setup caveat: with `return_logprob` the prefix match is capped at `logprob_start_len` (`_compute_max_prefix_len`), so the compared window must start past the tracked checkpoint — a window starting below it resumes from an older, aligned checkpoint and does not exercise this path. ``` main prompt=8226 cached=8192 n_cmp=1000 n>0.5=0 n>2=0 max|dlp|=0.007 this PR prompt=8226 cached=8192 n_cmp=1000 n>0.5=0 n>2=0 max|dlp|=0.0 main prompt=20450 cached=20416 n_cmp=1000 n>0.5=0 n>2=0 max|dlp|=0.0002 this PR prompt=20450 cached=20416 n_cmp=1000 n>0.5=0 n>2=0 max|dlp|=0.0 ``` The 8226-prompt rows reproduced identically across 2 rounds. With the fp32 snapshot the warm run matches cold exactly; main restores the bf16-rounded `h` row and drifts. The 20450-prompt row also confirms multi-chunk prefill donates the checkpoint at the last chunk boundary of the full sequence (cached=20416, not the 16384 chunk-split handoff). Measured on the v0.5.17 release branch with this PR's diff applied (helion files excluded, not present on that branch); `test_kda_track_state.py` also passes on GB300 (10 passed, 2 subtests). Prefill-kernel coverage (`--linear-attn-prefill-backend`, prompt=8226 setup, 3 rounds each, all cached=8192 with n_cmp=1000): ``` backend main max|dlp| this PR max|dlp| triton 0.007 0.0 flashkda 0.007 0.0 nvidia_kda 0.0012 0.0 ``` Every round reproduced its cell value exactly. Two backends are not measurable this way, identically on both builds: `ptx_kda` returns None input logprobs on this base (pre-existing, unrelated to this PR), and `cutedsl` rejects `extra_buffer` loudly with a pre-existing `NotImplementedError` (its extend cannot return intermediate chunk states at all). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32001342501](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32001342501)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32001342335](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32001342335)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Qwen] Disable fused shared-expert gate under deep_gemm MoE backend
signals.text: ## Motivation Running MoE models that go through `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` (e.g. qwen3.6-35b-a3b, via `qwen3_5_text.py`, which imports this block from `qwen2_moe.py`) with the DeepGemm MoE runner backend errors out. Root cause: `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock.forward` defers the shared-expert gate to `fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add(hidden_states, ...)`, which reads `hidden_states` **after** `_forward_router_experts(hidden_states)` runs. The DeepGemm MoE runner calls `dispose_tensor(hidden_states)` once it has consumed the input (`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`), so the deferred fused gate reads freed memory — a use-after-free. ## Modifications Exclude the DeepGemm backend from the `use_fused_gate` condition in `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock.forward`. With `use_fused_gate=False`, the shared expert applies the gate itself (`apply_gate=True`) before the routed experts run, and the final combine (`final_hidden_states += shared_output`) no longer reads `hidden_states` after it may have been disposed. This mirrors the existing deepseek_v2 handling, where `dispose_tensor` is disabled during CUDA graph capture for the same reason ("the routed deep_gemm does not free hidden_states, which the shared expert reads on the alt stream", `deepseek_v2.py`). No behavior change for other MoE runner backends (triton, flashinfer_*, cutlass, ...). ## Accuracy Tests Verified locally on qwen3.6-35b-a3b with `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`: the model previously errored during forward; with this change it serves normally. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — the change only selects the non-fused shared-expert gate path when the DeepGemm backend is active; other backends are untouched. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31802230496](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31802230496)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31802230139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31802230139)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix NPU Ring Attention varlen dispatch & restore 2-NPU CI testcase
signals.text: ## Motivation Ring Attention on Ascend NPU currently breaks when execution reaches the packed variable-length FlashAttention fallback (added for Minimax-H3 support). The shared Ring Attention path uses `flash_attn_varlen_func` for variable-length packed sequences, but that entry point did not have an NPU implementation. As a result, Ring Attention regressed on NPU in the current `main` branch. This PR implement the NPU path by adding Ascend support for packed variable-length attention and wiring it into both the generic FlashAttention compatibility API and the diffusion Ascend attention backend. The implementation is based on the Ascend varlen attention work from [#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569), extracted here as a focused Ring Attention compatibility fix. ### Before ### After This PR fix this behavior by implementing this fallback: ## Modifications ### Ascend packed variable-length attention - Add `ascend_fused_infer_attention_varlen`, backed by `torch.ops.npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score`. - Use the Ascend `TND` layout with packed sequence boundaries supplied through `actual_seq_lengths` and `actual_seq_lengths_kv`. - Validate Q/K/V layout, device placement, dtype, head dimensions, and cumulative sequence lengths. - Support optional host-side cumulative sequence lengths to avoid unnecessary device-to-host synchronization when they are already available. - Handle empty packed segments and non-contiguous Q/K/V views. - Support returning softmax LSE when requested. ### `flash_attn_varlen_func` NPU dispatch - Route NPU tensors from the generic `flash_attn_varlen_func` compatibility API to the Ascend packed-attention implementation. - Explicitly reject FlashAttention options that are not supported by the Ascend implementation instead of silently producing incorrect behavior. - Leave the existing CUDA/FlashAttention v3 path unchanged. ### Diffusion Ascend attention backend - Implement `AscendFlashAttnImpl.forward_varlen`. - Use the shared fused `TND` implementation for non-causal packed attention. - Preserve sequence boundaries for causal attention by processing each packed segment independently through the existing Ascend attention path. ## Accuracy Tests - **Before this PR:** the packed variable-length fallback used by Ring Attention does not have a working NPU implementation. - **After this PR:** the same Ring Attention path successfully dispatches through the Ascend varlen implementation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR is primarily a correctness and dispatch fix; no standalone end-to-end performance benchmark was collected. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [SM12x] Add b12x MoE runner backend for DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 experts on GB10
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4's MXFP4 experts (`fp4_e8m0_k32`) have no fused MoE path on the SM12x family (GB10 / DGX Spark, RTX PRO 6000 class). This PR adds an opt-in `--moe-runner-backend b12x` that maps them onto NVIDIA b12x W4A16 fused MoE kernels, making DeepSeek-V4-Flash practical to serve on 2x DGX Spark. ## Modifications - **`mxfp4_b12x_moe.py`** (new): `Mxfp4B12xMoEMethod` — weight prep hands the checkpoint tensors to b12x (E8M0 scales consumed natively, Parameters released after prepare), plus a frozen scratch plan shared per shape across all expert layers. - **Warmup ladder**: b12x refuses to compile kernels during CUDA graph capture and falls back to a pinned tile config that does not fit every block size, so every token count a captured graph can present is compiled eagerly first (decode `bs x spec_window` plus a power-of-two ladder for chunked prefill, sized by `SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS`). - **`moe_runner/b12x.py`** (new): fused-path runner registration. - **Version pinning escape hatch**: `SGLANG_B12X_PATH` selects an alternate b12x checkout. Rationale: 1.2.2 passes weights as raw pointers and rebuilds layouts at runtime, measuring 875.6 us/call vs 707.9 us/call for 0.15.3's static-stride `cute.Tensor` path on DSv4-Flash decode (bit-identical output). Both are supported; the env lets deployments keep the faster one. - **`mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py`**: register the new method in the `routed_scaling_factor` whitelist (it is silently dropped otherwise, compressing the whole MoE block by the scaling factor). - Env knobs registered in `environ.py` per conventions (`SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS`, `SGLANG_B12X_RELAX_BLOCKS_PER_SM`, `SGLANG_B12X_PATH`). ## Validation 2x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=2 cross-node, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with DSPARK speculative decoding (`gamma=5`), chunked prefill 4096: | Metric | Result | |---|---| | GSM8K 1319q (few-shot, parallel 8) | accuracy **0.945**, invalid 0 | | decode (8k ctx, bs=1) | 73-77 ms/step, accept-length 5.4-5.9 | | prefill 30k input | ~1.9k tok/s input throughput | Also boots and passes GSM8K (200q sampled: 0.960) on current main. Related: #34018 (FP8 wo_a GEMM on sm12x) is complementary and kept separate on purpose. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32004868000](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32004868000)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32004867794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32004867794)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Stop losing Kimi-K3 tool calls to reasoning, constraint conflicts, and truncation
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #34604. The issue reports ~190 `Tool call parsing error` logs/day on a Kimi-K3 agentic workload, attributed to `kimik3_detector.py`. The detector isn't the source — it uses stdlib `json` (message: `Expecting value`), the reported strings are `orjson`'s, and `detect_and_parse` already swallows every exception. Tracing it produced four distinct defects; **two of them are entirely silent, so 190/day is a floor, not the rate.** ### 1. Native-format output pushed through the JSON-array decoder `_process_tool_calls` falls through to the `required` json_schema fallback whenever the native parser finds no tool call. That decoder is wrong for detectors that constrain generation themselves: `_process_messages` deliberately attaches no json_schema constraint for them (kimi_k3 is excluded explicitly), so the text is native XTML or prose, never a JSON array. Accounts for every reported error string: | Error | Cause | |---|---| | `unexpected character: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` (84x) | `orjson.loads` on the model's prose | | `Input is a zero-length, empty document` (1x) | `orjson.loads("")` | | `string indices must be integers` (106x) | `orjson.loads` returned a dict, so `enumerate()` walks keys and `tool["name"]` indexes a string | The streaming path already gates this correctly; the non-stream path now matches it. ### 2. `response_format` + `required` silently discards the tool-call constraint `protocol.py` dropped the tool-call constraint with only a warning when the request also carried `response_format` / `regex` / `ebnf`. Verified: ``` response_format=none -> constraint in flight: structural_tag response_format=json_object -> constraint in flight: json_schema: {"type": "object"} response_format=json_schema -> constraint in flight: json_schema: {...} ``` The model is then *forced* to emit JSON and *forbidden* from emitting a tool call — the request cannot be satisfied, and the failure surfaces as the cryptic `string indices` TypeError above. Now a 400. `auto` keeps warn-and-continue, since it doesn't promise a call. ### 3. A tool call emitted before `<|close|>think<|sep|>` was eaten (silent) The tools-channel rescue in the kimi_k3 reasoning detector only ran when `think_end` was **absent**. With think-close present, everything before it — including a complete tools section — became `reasoning_content`. The model is free to do this: the reasoner grammar backend defers the tools constraint until think closes (`fill_vocab_mask` returns unmasked while thinking), and K3 leaves `tools` out of `think_excluded_tokens` on purpose. Now split on whichever marker comes first, in both overrides. ### 4. A truncated tools section vanished at end-of-stream (silent) `KimiK3Detector` didn't override `finish()`, so `parse_stream_end` returned nothing: a tools section cut off before its closing tag produced no call, no text, and no log. Now reported, with genuinely held-back text released the way `detect_and_parse` already does. ### Full pipeline, before → after ``` auto required 1 think+response+tools (happy) 1 -> 1 1 -> 1 2 tools only, no response channel 1 -> 1 1 -> 1 3 cut in response (no tools) 0 -> 0 err -> warn 4 cut inside reasoning 0 -> 0 err -> warn 5 cut mid tool call 0 -> 0 silent -> reported 6 JSON object (constraint dropped) 0 -> 0 err -> 400 upstream 7 tools inside think, then close 0 -> 1 0 -> 1 8 tools straight from think (no close) 1 -> 1 1 -> 1 ``` ### Not fixed here `required` still isn't a hard guarantee. EOS *is* grammar-masked until the call completes (verified by compiling the structural tag and querying the bitmask), but `max_tokens` and client `stop` sequences terminate generation on decoded text with no grammar involvement (`schedule_batch.py` `_check_str_based_finish`). Worth its own issue. The same think_end/tool_start ordering bug exists in `BaseReasoningFormatDetector` for six other detectors that set `tool_start_token`. Left alone deliberately — only demonstrated for kimi_k3, and not worth regressing six model families in this PR. ## Modifications - `serving_chat.py` — gate the json_schema fallback on detector capability; harden the fallback for parsers that do use it (bare object accepted as a one-element array, missing `parameters` defaults to `{}`, non-conforming shapes get a readable error); raw output at debug level. - `serving_responses.py` — same capability gate. - `protocol.py` — 400 on `required`/named + another output constraint. - `reasoning_parser.py` — kimi_k3 overrides split on the earlier of tools-open / think-close. - `kimik3_detector.py` — `finish()` reports a dropped tools section and releases held-back text. Behavior change worth calling out: for a structural-tag parser with `tool_choice=required`, a completion that happens to be a valid JSON array of tool calls used to be decoded as tool calls. It no longer is — such a model is never constrained to emit that shape, and the streaming path already returned no calls for it. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable; no change to model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; request-path bookkeeping only. ## Tests Five new cases across three files, each verified to fail on pre-fix code and pass after: ``` 8 failed, 6 passed <- pre-fix (the 6 are chunk sizes that already worked + the auto negative case) 0 failed <- post-fix ``` Full affected suites: 661 passed, 65 subtests passed. Five failures in `test_serving_chat.py` are pre-existing on unmodified `main` in this environment (they need real model configs). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
