signals.title: Fix MoE MORI Accuracy Issue
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes a bug where MoE models served with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` produce garbage output (0/10 on known-answer accuracy), while the exact same model/config with `--moe-a2a-backend none` is correct (10/10). This reproduces on: - Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8) - Hy3-preview / Hunyuan (`HYV3ForCausalLM`, 192 experts, top-8, with shared experts) It reproduces at single node (where MoRI runs its IntraNode kernel) and at multi-node (InterNode/RDMA kernel), so it is not tied to a specific transport. ### Root Cause After the experts run, `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock` / `HYV3MoEFused` apply a post-experts all-reduce (`moe_expert_parallel_all_reduce` / `moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`), gated by `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(...)`. That all-reduce is correct for backends whose experts return a partial result per rank. But MoRI's `combine` already all-to-all-reduces each token's expert outputs back to the source rank — the routed output is already complete and replicated across the group, exactly like the `flashinfer` and `pplx` dispatchers, which are already excluded from the post-experts all-reduce. Because `mori` was not in the skip list, the extra all-reduce re-reduces an already-complete result, summing it `ep_size`/`tp_size`× and destroying the output. We confirmed this directly by dumping per-rank MoE tensors on the failing server: the routed MoE output is identical across all ranks (already reduced by MoRI combine), and the post-experts `final_out` equals `Σ_ranks(routed)` (i.e. `ep_size × routed`), the fingerprint of the erroneous re-reduce. A reference-trajectory comparison against a correct HuggingFace forward on the same prompt showed layer-0 attention matching (cosine ≈ 1.0) but the trajectory diverging starting at the first MoE layer's output — isolating the defect to the post-experts reduce, not to MoRI's dispatch/GEMM/combine (which produce numerically correct values). ### Specific to Hunyuan 3 `HYV3MoEFused` adds a shared expert (`shared_mlp`, built with `reduce_results=False`) to the routed output before the all-reduce. Under MoRI, the routed output is already full/replicated (must not be reduced again), but the shared output is still a TP/EP partial (still needs reducing). So simply skipping the blanket all-reduce fixes the routed part but leaves `shared` at a fraction (`1/group_size`), which still corrupts the sum. The fix reduces only the shared partial over the same group(s) the blanket reduce would have used, then adds it to the already-full routed output. Qwen3 has no shared experts, so it needs only the skip. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py` — `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(...)`: add an `is_mori()` skip alongside the existing `is_flashinfer()` / `is_pplx()` skips (same "combine already reduces to source rank" rationale). This alone fully fixes models without shared experts (e.g. Qwen3). - `python/sglang/srt/models/hunyuan_v3.py` — in both `_forward_single_stream` and `_forward_dual_stream`, for the MoRI path only, reduce the shared-expert partial over the EP/TP group before adding it to the already-full routed output; plus the `get_moe_a2a_backend` import. Required for Hunyuan/Hy3 and any MoRI model with shared experts. Both changes are gated on `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()`, so `none`, `flashinfer`, `deepep`, and `pplx` behavior is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Accuracy = greedy known-answer probe (10 factual prompts, temperature 0). Baseline `mori` is the unpatched image; `none` is the reference-correct control. ### Probe Test | Model | Nodes | Geometry | Backend | Before Fix | After Fix | |-------|:-----:|----------|---------|:--------:|:--------:| | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 | TP/EP=8 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 2 | TP/EP=16 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | TP/EP=32 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 1 | TP/EP=8 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 2 | TP/EP=16 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 4 | TP/EP=32 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | - Qwen3: clean PASS at 1/2/4 nodes (0/10 degenerate). - Hy3: all answers correct at 1/2/4 nodes. At multi-node the probe's separate degenerate-tail heuristic flags 3–4/10 (the base model repeats after answering), but the correct `none` reference shows the same 2–4/10 — i.e. it's a base-model/prompt artifact, not a regression from this fix. - Controls: `--moe-a2a-backend none` remains 10/10 (unchanged), confirming the fix is scoped to MoRI. Both single-node (MoRI IntraNode) and multi-node (MoRI InterNode/RDMA) paths verified. ### GSM8K (exact-match, 40 problems, 5-shot) | Model | Nodes | Geometry | none (control) | mori (before fix) | mori (after fix) | |-------|:-----:|----------|:--------------:|:-----------------:|:----------------:| | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 | TP/EP=8 | 87.5% (35/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 90.0% (36/40) | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 2 | TP/EP=16 | 90.0% (36/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 90.0% (36/40) | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | TP/EP=32 | 85.0% (34/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 92.5% (37/40) | | Hy3-preview | 1 | TP/EP=8 | 77.5% (31/40) | 2.5% (1/40) | 77.5% (31/40) | | Hy3-preview | 2 | TP/EP=16 | 80.0% (32/40) | 2.5% (1/40) | 77.5% (31/40) | | Hy3-preview | 4 | TP/EP=32 | 80.0% (32/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 80.0% (32/40) | - Before the fix, mori is broken at every scale (Qwen3 0%, Hy3 0–2.5%), consistent with the garbage output on the known-answer probe. - After the fix, mori tracks the none reference at every scale: Qwen3 lands at or slightly above none (within noise at N=40), and Hy3 matches the reference closely (exactly equal at 1 and 4 nodes: 31/40 and 32/40). - The absolute score reflects each base model's own capability (Hy3-preview is a preview model, so its ceiling is lower); the fix restores reference-equivalent accuracy on the MoRI path rather than changing model quality. - Single-node exercises MoRI's IntraNode kernel; 2-node and 4-node exercise MoRI's InterNode (RDMA) kernel. Scored offline against the staged GSM8K test split via final-integer exact-match. ### Test Environment - Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm700-mi30x-20260728` (SGLang upstream `main` @ `84cdfde`, version `0.5.16.dev20260728`), 8× MI300 per node, pure TP (`tp==ep`), `--disable-custom-all-reduce`. - Hy3 runs also apply an orthogonal, environment-specific workaround for AITER's `biased_grouped_topk` on ROCm (falls back to the reference impl when `apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output=True`); this is unrelated to the all-reduce fix. ## Follow Up - Other MoRI models with shared experts (beyond Hunyuan) would need the same shared-expert handling in their model file; consider factoring the "reduce shared partial only" step into a shared helper. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32048833857](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32048833857)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32048833336](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32048833336)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Split TRTLLM MHA decode batches by KV sequence length
signals.text: ## Motivation TRTLLM-GEN decode attention can pay a large tail-latency tax when requests in the same batch have very different KV sequence lengths. On GB300, a matched mixed-context profile attributed `8.377 ms` of a `9.822 ms` decode-step delta to attention, with `7.601 ms` coming from the main SM100 variable-sequence FMHA kernel. At BS44/rank on a 148-SM GB300, the unsplit launch has only one KV CTA per request and selects the persistent kernel. Long requests then form the tail of the shared wave. Splitting a fixed-query-length batch into length-sorted groups increases CTA parallelism and prevents the longest requests from delaying the short groups. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_DECODE_SEQ_LEN_SPLITS`, with default `1` preserving the existing single-call behavior. - For values above one, sort requests by KV length, form equal-count groups, gather their query/page-table/length metadata, invoke TRTLLM MHA per group, and scatter outputs back to request order. - Reuse the same helper for ordinary fixed-query decode and frozen-KV MTP target verification, including NVFP4 KV-cache scaling. - Validate the split count and cap it at the request count. The ragged-query path is unchanged. - Extend two existing TRTLLM-MHA test cases to cover split eager decode and frozen-KV MTP CUDA-graph replay; no new test method or module is added. The refreshed commit is rebased onto current upstream `main@f019f0b064`. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 requests, 5-shot chat evaluation on `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Accuracy | **0.985** (197/200) | | CUDA graph request fraction | 1.0 | | Retractions | 0 | | Error markers | 0 | Acceptance was generated naturally; no simulated-accuracy path was enabled. Targeted GB300 correctness coverage on the refreshed upstream commit: - existing eager dense-decode case with two sequence-length groups; - existing frozen-KV MTP CUDA-graph case with two groups; - `2 passed`, covering `5` subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Feature isolation: no split versus two groups Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, TRTLLM MHA, NEXTN draft length 6, BS44/rank on GB300: | Workload | Splits=1 | Splits=2 | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mixed ISL decode iteration | 57.485 ms | 51.639 ms | **-10.17%** | | Uniform 92k, exact matched points | 49.907 ms | 50.008 ms | +0.20% | | q_len=1 attention micro | 0.757 ms | 0.637 ms | **-15.9%** | | q_len=6 attention micro | 1.066 ms | 0.711 ms | **-33.3%** | The mixed run held batch size, average context, request count, and draft settings constant. Length splitting closed `75.5%` of the isolated mixed-ISL attention tax without a material steady-state regression on uniform lengths. ### Production split-count tuning AgentX 393-trace workload, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, 24 GB300 GPUs, 4P+1D, concurrency 896. Exact-shape matching used each arm's independently aligned formal `180-900 s` window. | Metric | Split-3 | Split-4 | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Exact-shape output TPS/User | 67.352353 | 70.623070 | **+4.8561%** | | Strict matched TPS/running request | — | — | **+1.82848%** | | ITL | — | — | **-4.0306%** | | Full decode duration | — | — | **-3.6644%** | Both arms had CUDA graph fraction `1.0` and zero retractions. This second table is split-count tuning enabled by the PR, not an additional additive estimate on top of the no-split comparison. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The opt-in setting is documented inline at its declaration. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [DCP]Localize HiCache DCP indices once per transfer, not per layer
signals.text: ## Motivation Under DCP, `MLATokenToKVPoolHost.load_to_device_per_layer()` translated the widened logical slots into this rank's physical rows on every call: ```python host_indices = self.dcp_kernel_indices(host_indices) device_indices = self.dcp_kernel_indices(device_indices) ``` The result is layer-independent, but the load loop calls the method once per layer. The cost is worse than the launch count suggests. `indices[indices % dcp_size == dcp_rank]` is boolean-mask indexing, which goes through `nonzero` — and `nonzero` must read the selected count back to the host to size its output. That is a **device→host sync**, and it runs inside `with device_module.stream(self.load_stream)`, so each layer's translation blocks on the previous layer's transfer kernel. The loop serialises. `start_loading()` runs on the scheduler thread (`get_new_batch_prefill` → `ready_to_load_host_cache`), so the stall sits directly in front of the forward launch. ## Modifications - `HostKVCache.dcp_localize_indices(host_indices, device_indices)` translates a transfer's index pair once. - `load_to_device_per_layer()` now *takes* this rank's physical rows — the translation is gone from the MLA implementation. This makes explicit the precondition `_backup_from_device_per_layer` already relies on ("Indices arrive already translated…"). - `HiCacheController.start_loading()` localizes once ahead of its layer loop. - `backup_from_device_all_layer()` keeps translating internally — it owns its own layer loop, so it already paid the cost once per write-back. Not touched: the draft, HiSparse, and `HostPoolGroup` load paths. All three are rejected or non-DCP under `_resolve_hicache_dcp_compatibility`, so the translation is the identity there and un-localized indices are already correct. Pools that are not DCP-sharded return the inputs unchanged, so nothing changes unless `--dcp-size > 1`. ## Profiling Before After ## Benchmarking 8×B300, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MLA, 27 layers), `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --page-size 64 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4`, 16384 tokens/rank. Workload `generated-shared-prefix`: 96 groups × 4096-token prefix, 768 requests, concurrency 16 — ~3× logical KV capacity, so prefixes evict to L2 and are pulled back constantly. Both arms moved an identical **14.35M tokens** through the load path. **Scheduler-thread cost of one 27-layer load loop**, with a no-DCP run as the floor. Averaged over the complete loops in one profiler window per config (12 / 12 / 15): | | loop span | translations in loop | |---|---|---| | base | 8.99 ms | 52 | | **patched** | **1.06 ms** | **0** | | TP8, no DCP (control) | 1.02 ms | 0 | The patch lands within 4% of the no-DCP baseline. `aten::nonzero` is absent entirely from the control trace, confirming every one under DCP came from `dcp_kernel_indices`. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical change: the indices reaching the transfer kernels are identical, only computed once per transfer instead of once per layer. Two unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py`: the per-layer path forwards localized rows untouched, and `start_loading` localizes exactly once for all layers. The first guards a *silent* failure — re-translating at `dcp_size=8` turns 64 rows into 8 and still passes the `numel` assert inside `dcp_kernel_indices`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Provide accuracy results. - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials if this PR changes the behavior of the code. - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31994533283](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31994533283) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31994532982](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31994532982)

signals.title: [Spec] Publish EAGLE v2 shared-read-done at verify with staged draft-extend
signals.text: Stacks on #35126. When the draft-extend backend declares its metadata init stageable (`supports_draft_extend_metadata_staging`: DSV4, non-SWA flashinfer), point EAGLE v2's `last_shared_read_runner` at the target runner so the scheduler's WAR barrier waits on the verify-time record instead of the draft-extend step-tail one; non-staged steps re-publish the record at the step tail (the previous fence position). Also hoist the DSV4 draft-extend SWA write-loc translate out of the captured graph (filled ahead of the verify launch), removing its post-record shared read. +36% decode throughput (fwd occupancy 65% -> 94%) with EAGLE at tp4 / concurrency 128. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32089621526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32089621526)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32089621428](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32089621428)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Tokenizer] Keep dispatched request state so the delayed abort can fire
signals.text: ## Motivation When a streaming client disconnects, SGLang may leave the request running on the scheduler. `create_abort_task` waits 2 seconds before sending the abort. On the failing path, `generate_request` handles cancellation first and `_discard_pending_req_states(obj)` removes the request from `rid_to_state`. In single-tokenizer mode, `abort_request` then treats the missing state as already finished and returns without dispatching an `AbortReq`. The cleanup was intended for failures before scheduler IPC enqueue, such as input-length validation. Removing the state after dispatch instead strands a request that the scheduler is still running. The same guard can also make `/abort_request` return 200 without dispatching an abort. This was observed on one TP4 replica in a four-replica deployment, with each replica using the default `--tokenizer-worker-num 1`. A client disconnected after 3 seconds, but the request continued for another 71.4 seconds and generated 1,803 tokens before finishing normally. During a 1,800-second observation window on that replica, 16 abandoned requests averaged 477 seconds of observed post-disconnect decoding; one remained active for the full window. This corresponds to approximately 4.24 continuously occupied slots, or ~13% of the configured `--max-running-requests=32`. At one sampled instant, abandoned requests occupied 5 of the 32 slots. ## Modifications 1. Add `ReqState.dispatched`, set after successful scheduler IPC enqueue. 2. Make `_discard_pending_req_states` remove only requests that were never dispatched. Dispatched states remain until `_handle_batch_output` or `_handle_abort_req` removes them. 3. Add `expect_obj` to `abort_request` so delayed aborts target the request instance that created them. 4. Pass the originating object from `create_abort_task`, including the cached `obj[i]` objects for batched requests. The identity check prevents a delayed abort from killing a newer request that reused the same rid. It applies in both single- and multi-tokenizer modes. Explicit `/abort_request` calls do not pass `expect_obj`. In multi-tokenizer mode they still dispatch when the rid is absent locally, since the request may belong to another tokenizer worker. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. No kernel or model-forward code is changed, and tokens delivered before a disconnect are unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput impact is expected. The change recovers scheduler capacity occupied by abandoned requests. A 12-hour A/B run on the same machine produced: | | Patched | Unpatched | |---|---:|---:| | Decode batches | 26,119 | 25,258 | | Disconnected rids | 142 | 333 | | Post-disconnect decode lines per rid | 17 | 6,262 | Post-disconnect decoding per rid fell by 99.7%. This run used a simplified version that removed the guard outright, rather than the exact implementation in this PR. signals.title: [DCP] Build the MHA-extend reorg offsets on the host
signals.text: ## Motivation `all_gather_kv_cache_for_mha_extend` builds its two cumulative-length tensors on the **device**, then uses them as Python slice bounds: ```python prefix_lens_cu = torch.zeros(len(seq_lens) + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=kv_a.device) extend_lens_cu = torch.zeros_like(prefix_lens_cu) prefix_lens_cu[1:] = torch.cumsum(extend_prefix_lens, dim=0) extend_lens_cu[1:] = torch.cumsum(extend_seq_lens, dim=0) for i in range(len(seq_lens)): kv_a_tuple += (prefix_kv_a[prefix_lens_cu[i] : prefix_lens_cu[i+1]], kv_a[extend_lens_cu[i] : extend_lens_cu[i+1]]) k_pe_tuple += (prefix_k_pe[prefix_lens_cu[i] : prefix_lens_cu[i+1]], k_pe[extend_lens_cu[i] : extend_lens_cu[i+1]]) ``` Each bound goes through `__index__` → `.item()` → a **device→host sync**: 8 per request, per call. This runs inside the forward on the scheduler thread, so the CPU cannot run ahead and batch prep stops overlapping GPU work. Profiled on 8×B300 with DCP8, this was **27,982 `aten::item` calls costing 430 ms in a 6.7 s window**, plus 14,878 `cudaStreamSynchronize`. The same profile of a `--tp-size 8` run with no DCP shows 243 stream syncs total. The sibling `all_gather_kv_cache_for_dcp` already builds its offsets on the host and does not have this problem. ## Modifications The host-side lengths already exist — the function is handed `extend_prefix_lens_cpu`, and `ForwardBatch` carries `extend_seq_lens_cpu` right beside it (`forward_batch_info.py:535-536`, set together). Accumulate both on the host with `itertools.accumulate` and slice with plain ints. `extend_prefix_lens` / `extend_seq_lens` are then unused, and `seq_lens` was only supplying a length, so all three drop out of the signature. Both call sites updated (`forward_mha.py`, `forward_mha_rocm.py`). ## Accuracy Tests Greedy decode over a shared prefix reused by four queries of differing extend lengths — the exact path this function reorganizes. Output digest is **identical** before and after (`752a08531231e97a`), so the reorg is unchanged. `test/registered/dcp/test_dsv31_dcp8_gsm8k.py` covers this path in CI. ## Benchmarking and Profiling 8×B300, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MLA, 27 layers), `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --page-size 64`, shared-prefix workload (96 groups × 4096-token prefix, 768 requests, concurrency 16). | | before | after | |---|---|---| | `aten::item` | 27,982 / 430.4 ms | 13,152 / **20.3 ms** | | `cudaStreamSynchronize` | 14,878 / 307.7 ms | 832 / **16.5 ms** | | `all_gather_kv_cache_for_mha_extend` | 4.35 ms/call | **2.05 ms/call** | | `run_batch` | 22.4 ms/call | **17.9 ms/call** | Stream syncs drop **94%**, landing near the 243 of a no-DCP run. The remaining `.item()` calls are on CPU tensors in `all_gather_kv_cache_for_dcp` and cost 20 ms rather than 430 ms. End to end (fresh server per arm, 2 reps, no profiler): median TTFT **−15.0%** (451.8 → 384.1 ms), mean TTFT −7.6% (465.2 → 430.0 ms), throughput +1.0%. The workload is concurrency-bound, so latency moves more than throughput. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Provide accuracy results. - [ ] Add unit tests — the sync is only observable on a live CUDA + DCP process group; suggestions for a cheap guard welcome. - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials if this PR changes the behavior of the code. - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31865166090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31865166090)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31865167030](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31865167030)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Support Intern-S2-Mobius FP8
signals.text: ## Motivation `internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8` is now public, but it does not load on current SGLang. The serialized FP8 config lists `.linear_attn` parents as exact `modules_to_not_convert` entries, while SGLang treats ignored-layer names as prefixes and consequently skips quantized child projections. Strict loading then also needs to map the checkpoint's fused expert scale tensors and allow omitted KV-cache scales. The existing Intern-S2-Mobius cookbook only exposes the BF16 checkpoint. ## Modifications - Preserve FP8 quantization for Mobius linear-attention qkv/z and output projections while retaining the checkpoint's child exclusions. - Load `gate_up_proj_scale_inv` and `down_proj_scale_inv` into the fused expert scale parameters. - Treat Mobius `attn.k_scale` and `attn.v_scale` as optional while still loading them when present. - Add the FP8 checkpoint to the cookbook selector with verified 1xH200 TP=1 high-throughput and NEXTN recipes. B200 recipes remain explicitly unverified. - Separate the existing BF16 benchmark claims from the new FP8 launch verification. No unit test is added: this is a serialized-checkpoint integration path, and a mock loader test would only restate the configured parameter mappings. The real checkpoint path is covered by the end-to-end gate below. ## Accuracy Tests Verified commit `59c8810358` on 1xH200 with checkpoint revision `ea369586a687b1f31d29c8b10868acf2cb8e2889`: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \ --context-length 262144 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 sgl-eval run gsm8k \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \ --model internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8 \ --num-examples 1319 \ --num-threads 64 ``` | Examples | Accuracy | Stop rate | Truncated | Error | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1319 | **96.82%** | **100.00%** | 0.00% | 0.00% | All 1319 prediction records reported `finish_reason=stop`. The documented NEXTN recipe also passed live smoke tests: - Text: `15% of 240` returned `36`, `finish_reason=stop`. - Vision: the standard tiger image returned `tiger`, `finish_reason=stop`, with 70 image tokens. - A 292-token bounded generation stopped normally; telemetry reported accept length 4.00 and accept rate 1.00 with decode CUDA graphs enabled. Local validation passed: changed-file `pre-commit`, `py_compile`, cookbook config consistency, `git diff --check`, and `mint validate`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No FP8 speed benchmark is claimed in this PR. The NEXTN target+draft process used about 94 GB on H200 with the documented settings. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signals.title: Avoid deadlock when shared-memory node probe fails
signals.text: Fixes #34800 ## Summary - Keep every rank in `in_the_same_node_as()` on the same broadcast when the source shared-memory probe fails. - Add a two-rank Gloo regression that forces source shared-memory creation to raise `OSError`. ## Root cause `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` previously covered both local shared-memory operations and `broadcast_object_list()`. If source-rank creation failed, it skipped the broadcast while peers waited forever. ## Fix Limit the `OSError` suppression to local shared-memory creation/opening. The source broadcasts `None` on creation failure, reports itself as colocated, and peers report that they are not on the source node. Downstream readers therefore fall back to the remote path without a negative local-reader count. The macOS shared-memory name-length error is one trigger. The regression injects the same `OSError` and is registered in the Linux CPU CI lane to validate the platform-independent collective-safety invariant. Shared-memory name generation is intentionally unchanged. ## Validation - `PYTHONPATH=python python/.venv/bin/python -m pytest test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py::test_shm_creation_failure_keeps_all_ranks_in_the_collective -q` - `SKIP=no-commit-to-branch uvx pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py --show-diff-on-failure` - GitHub Lint: [Run #31923509772](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31923509772) - `git diff --check` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31893507153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893507153)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31893507005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893507005)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Avoid padded Q for unified DSV4 prefill
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 TP prefill currently allocates a decode-oriented 64-head padded Q tensor, then passes the local-head slice to the unified-KV attention backend. At TP=8 that slice has 16 heads and is noncontiguous, so the OPUS wrapper materializes it with `q.contiguous()` before launching the kernel. The 64-head layout is useful for the FlashMLA sparse decode specialization, but unified-KV extend/prefill does not require it. ## Modifications - reuse one unified-KV gate result within `MQALayer.forward` so layout selection and backend dispatch use the same decision (a readability change, not a measured performance source) - skip TP head padding for unified-KV extend modes and write Q directly in contiguous local-head layout - retain the existing 64-head padded layout for decode - retain existing behavior for non-unified backends - add real `MQALayer.forward` control-flow tests plus a backend-level TARGET_VERIFY routing test ## Accuracy Tests The focused suite runs through the real `MQALayer.forward` control flow and verifies: - every mode currently selected by `ForwardMode.is_extend()` uses contiguous local-head Q (EXTEND, MIXED, TARGET_VERIFY, SPLIT_PREFILL, and DLLM_EXTEND) - the unified local-head Q owns only its logical storage (`storage_nbytes == numel * element_size`), preventing a hidden 64-head backing allocation - TARGET_VERIFY enters the production unified decode route and does not call prefill - unified DECODE retains the existing 64-head padded backing layout - non-unified modes retain the previous padded behavior - active prefill-CP disables the multi-stream branch and preserves the unpadded layout The former mocked ROCm multi-stream + unified case was removed because DeepSeek-V4 disables that production combination; the HIP multi-stream helper does not implement unified-KV cache writes. Result: `5 tests passed`, `14 subtests passed` in the official ROCm MI355X image. Static validation also passed: Ruff (`F401,F821,UP037`), `py_compile`, registered-test validation, and `git diff --check`. Review also found a pre-existing nonzero-TP-rank `attn_sink` routing bug shared by both benchmark arms. It is fixed and independently reference-validated in #35092. The A/B results below remain valid as relative layout-performance evidence, while matching output tokens between two arms that shared that bug are not presented as absolute model-accuracy proof. ## Speed Tests and Profiling At the production sparse-prefill shape, the OPUS wrapper-to-kernel delta was 43.5-44.7 us per call across three runs. That delta includes wrapper dispatch and argument handling, so it is an upper bound on the removable contiguous-copy cost, not a model-level or TTFT result. ## Model E2E (MI355X, TP8 / DP1) The branch was rebased onto current `main` (`ab9e7abad`; parent `c87a2ced1`) and tested in the pinned ROCm image on 8 x MI355X. Both arms used unified-KV DSV4 attention, TP8/DP1, chunked prefill 8,192, OSL=1, distinct uncached token sequences, one warmup, and repeated scored requests. - 8K: baseline median **318.23 ms**, candidate **315.29 ms** (**0.93%** improvement); all five output tokens matched. - 64K first sandwich: baseline median **2,790.31 ms**, candidate **2,771.56 ms** (**0.68%** improvement); all five output tokens matched. Candidate had one server-side **11.90 s** outlier, so the five-sample P90/mean regressed despite the steady-state median gain. - 64K candidate follow-up: ten fresh uncached prompts, median **2,772.25 ms**, P90 **2,782.55 ms**, range **2,765.25-2,808.13 ms**, zero retractions; the outlier did not reproduce. - 64K A2/B with the same ten fresh prompt indices: baseline median/P90/mean **2,793.65 / 2,795.65 / 2,793.33 ms**; candidate **2,772.25 / 2,782.55 / 2,775.21 ms**, improving **0.77% / 0.47% / 0.65%**. All ten output tokens matched; neither arm had an outlier above 2x its median. - Baseline A1 -> A2 drift on the original five prompt indices was **0.30%** at the median (A2 slower), below the candidate's steady-state improvement. The result is a small steady-state E2E win, not the larger wrapper-level upper bound. The isolated 11.90 s event is retained as a tail-risk observation; it did not reproduce in either ten-request arm and is not attributed to this Q-layout change. ## Checklist - [x] Add focused unit tests - [x] Preserve decode and non-unified behavior - [x] Provide accuracy and operator profiling evidence - [x] Complete model E2E and graph-capture validation - [ ] Documentation update (not needed for this internal layout change) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31995871474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995871474)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31995871369](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995871369)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Suppress expected FlashInfer TRT-LLM workspace warnings
signals.text: ## Summary FlashInfer TRT-LLM warns on every oversized all-reduce during prefill CUDA graph capture, even though SGLang safely falls back. One startup produced **28,032 repeated warnings / 56,064 warning lines** like this: ```text Workspace is insufficient for problem size. Workspace validation failed: - token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2880) exceeds workspace max_token_num (2048) * hidden_dim (2880). This may cause Illegal Memory Access. ``` This skips the noisy TRT-LLM validator only when cached workspace metadata already proves the request cannot fit. It preserves valid total-capacity reuse and FP32 Lamport compatibility, while leaving MNNVL's validator untouched. Added focused regression coverage and confirmed on 4x H100 with TP4: full prefill graph capture through 8192 tokens completed without the warnings, while TRT-LLM fusion stayed enabled. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31873437993](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31873437993)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31873437892](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31873437892)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Summary - configure `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` before CUDA DeepEP low-latency buffer initialization - enforce `max(existing value, 1024, 2 * (num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank + 1))` - preserve larger user-provided values and leave NPU and normal DeepEP paths unchanged - force reinstall `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` in CUDA 13 CI and the main CUDA 13 image; CUDA 12 remains unchanged - bump the runtime dependency to `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` ## Motivation DeepEP v2 requires NCCL Gin from NCCL 2.30.7 and an NVSHMEM QP depth of at least twice the low-latency dispatch capacity plus two. For the DeepSeek V4 configuration with 1024 dispatch tokens per rank, the required QP depth is 2050, which is larger than NVSHMEM default of 1024. ## Validation - SGLang pre-commit hooks passed for all changed files - PyPI reports `sgl-deep-ep` 0.1.1 as the latest release with 8 wheel files - CI dependency script passes shell syntax validation - mocked CUDA-major checks confirm CUDA 13 installs `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7 --force-reinstall --no-deps` and CUDA 12 skips it - GB300, four GPUs, with `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` explicitly unset: `TestDSV4FlashFP4B200Balanced` passed all 9 tests in 165.585 seconds - GSM8K score: 0.965 - average speculative accept length: 1.9488 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32053259045](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32053259045)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32053258749](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32053258749)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] Fix SWA eviction bookkeeping for DFLASH-family decode
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation DFLASH-family speculative decode, including DSPARK, reserves target KV headroom through `DFlashDraftInputV2.prepare_for_decode()`, but this path did not run SWA eviction bookkeeping or advance the per-request decode clock used by `ScheduleBatch.maybe_evict_swa()`. For hybrid-SWA models such as DeepSeek V4 Flash, SWA KV usage can then grow roughly linearly with full KV usage during long DSPARK decode, instead of reclaiming out-of-window SWA slots. This can fill the SWA pool and trigger repeated KV cache retractions/OOM behavior even when the model sliding window is small. Validated scenario: - Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (`sliding_window=128`) - Speculative decoding: `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5` - `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1` - Base commit: `8720a72` - Environment: H100 80G x 4, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.13 ## Modifications This PR updates `DFlashDraftInputV2.prepare_for_decode()` to run the decode bookkeeping expected by the SWA eviction path: - Call `batch.maybe_evict_swa()` before reserving new target KV headroom. - Increment `req.decode_batch_idx` once per decode iteration for each active request. `DSPARK` is routed through `SpeculativeAlgorithm.is_dflash_family()`, so it uses this DFLASH-family prepare path. ## Accuracy Tests Not run. This change only updates decode-time KV/SWA bookkeeping. It does not change model forward computation, sampling logits, attention kernels, or accepted token selection. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Functional validation and a lightweight serving benchmark were run on H100 x 4. Server command highlights: ```bash export SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact export SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESS_STATE_DTYPE=bf16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --port 8000 \ --model-path ./models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --context-length 1048576 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ ``` Benchmark command: ```bash python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang-oai-chat \ --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 32 \ --random-input-len 1024 \ --random-output-len 32768 \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --request-rate inf \ --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 ``` Results: | Metric | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | KV cache full / retractions | Yes, repeated `KV cache pool is full` | No | | Successful requests | 32 | 32 | | Benchmark duration | 468.00 s | 369.78 s | | Output token throughput | 2240.55 tok/s | 2835.66 tok/s | | Mean TPOT | 8.01 ms | 4.42 ms | | Mean ITL | 8.06 ms | 4.45 ms | | Max ITL | 129233.10 ms | 6761.81 ms | | Accept length | 5.22 | 5.25 | Log behavior: - Before the fix, single-request decode showed `#swa token` growing together with `#full token`. - After the fix, single-request decode kept SWA usage near the sliding-window footprint while full KV continued to grow. - Under the benchmark workload, the pre-fix run repeatedly triggered `KV cache pool is full`; the fixed run did not. Example pre-fix single-request log: ```text [2026-08-15 07:04:18 TP0] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 256, #cached-token: 0, full token usage: 0.00, swa token usage: 0.00, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 0, #pending-token: 0, cuda graph: False, input throughput (token/s): 0.05 [2026-08-15 07:04:18 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 512, full token usage: 0.00, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 4.12, accept rate: 0.62, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 0.03, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 07:04:19 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 512, full token usage: 0.00, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 3.85, accept rate: 0.57, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 411.23, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 07:04:19 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 768, full token usage: 0.00, #swa token: 768, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 4.60, accept rate: 0.72, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 491.59, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 07:04:19 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 1024, full token usage: 0.00, #swa token: 1024, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 4.17, accept rate: 0.64, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 446.68, #queue-req: 0 ...... [2026-08-15 07:05:28 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 32512, full token usage: 0.01, #swa token: 32512, swa token usage: 0.12, accept len: 5.35, accept rate: 0.87, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 539.91, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 07:05:28 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 32768, full token usage: 0.01, #swa token: 32768, swa token usage: 0.12, accept len: 5.58, accept rate: 0.92, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 561.68, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 07:05:28 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 33024, full token usage: 0.01, #swa token: 33024, swa token usage: 0.12, accept len: 5.53, accept rate: 0.91, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 559.27, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 07:05:29] INFO: 127.0.0.1:55390 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` Example fixed single-request log: ```text [2026-08-15 05:37:24 TP0] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 256, #cached-token: 0, full token usage: 0.00, swa token usage: 0.00, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 0, #pending-token: 0, cuda graph: False, input throughput (token/s): 3.12 [2026-08-15 05:37:25 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 512, full token usage: 0.00, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 4.22, accept rate: 0.65, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 3.08, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 05:37:25 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 768, full token usage: 0.00, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 4.25, accept rate: 0.65, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 453.13, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 05:37:25 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 768, full token usage: 0.00, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 3.50, accept rate: 0.50, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 373.22, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 05:37:26 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 1024, full token usage: 0.00, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 3.70, accept rate: 0.54, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 392.30, #queue-req: 0 ...... [2026-08-15 05:38:24 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 32512, full token usage: 0.01, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 5.88, accept rate: 0.97, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 589.29, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 05:38:24 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 32768, full token usage: 0.01, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 5.60, accept rate: 0.92, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 561.77, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 05:38:24 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 33024, full token usage: 0.01, #swa token: 512, swa token usage: 0.00, accept len: 5.47, accept rate: 0.90, cap len: 6.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 549.11, #queue-req: 0 [2026-08-15 05:38:25] INFO: 127.0.0.1:56080 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. signals.title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
signals.text: ## Motivation For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused. This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`). - When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output. - When breakable CUDA graph is active, skip this optimization and retain the existing serial shared-expert path; cross-segment overlap across the eager DeepEP break is out of scope. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests The accuracy evidence below was collected on predecessor `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Current head `76815b3766deb3a3c9aceef1cb346093f691d976` differs only by making breakable CUDA graph use the pre-existing serial fallback instead of an alternate-stream path with an immediate wait; the non-breakable overlap implementation measured below is unchanged. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance. | Metric | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 | | Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 | | Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- | | Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- | All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. Breakable CUDA graph is now intentionally excluded from this optimization, and no performance gain is claimed for that fallback. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K. The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay. | AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** | | Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** | | Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** | | Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** | | Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp | These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signals.title: [Diffusion] Fix H3 swap PEFT SwiGLU lora_B halves when loading FFN Lora
signals.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 fuses SwiGLU `gate` / `up` into one `(28672, 5376)` matrix. The two official layouts store that fused tensor with opposite row order: - diffusers / LightX2V: `ff.net.0.proj` = `[up; gate]` - sglang native: `mlp.fc1` = `[gate; up]` Loading a LightX2V LoRA already renames `ff.net.0.proj` → `mlp.fc1`, but does not swap `lora_B` rows. Shapes match and nothing errors, so the FFN adapter is applied with the two halves reversed. Attention LoRA is unaffected. The two layouts are defined by the `forward` implementations: diffusers [`SwiGLU`](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/v0.37.0/src/diffusers/models/activations.py#L143-L146) (`ff.net.0.proj`): ```python hidden_states, gate = hidden_states.chunk(2, dim=-1) return hidden_states * self.activation(gate) # [up; gate] ``` sglang [`_silu_mul`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py#L271-L272) (`mlp.fc1`): ```python gate, up = hidden.chunk(2, dim=-1) return F.silu(gate) * up # [gate; up] ``` The MiniMax-H3 repo ships the same DiT twice, which confirms the row-order mismatch is in the official weights, not a sglang-only convention: - `FL2VA/transformer/` → `blocks.N.mlp.fc1.weight` (what sglang loads) - `transformer/` → `transformer_blocks.N.ff.net.0.proj.weight` (what LightX2V trains against) | tensor | as-is | after swapping the two 14336-row halves | |---|---|---| | fused FFN `fc1` / `ff.net.0.proj` (52 / 52 blocks) | 0 exact | **52 / 52 exact** | | `fc2` / `ff.net.2` | exact | n/a | They are the same model: native fused `qkv_proj` is bit-identical to diffusers `to_q/to_k/to_v` after the documented per-head `[q,k,v]` pack. LightX2V's own two exports of the same adapter repeat the same signature: | | as-is | swapped | |---|---|---| | `fc1` `lora_A` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a | | `fc1` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | 0 exact | **50 / 50 exact** | | `fc2` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a | `lora_A` lives on the input side, so it does not need a row swap. ## Modifications Swap the two 14336-row halves of `lora_B` only on the `ff.net.0.proj.lora_B` → `mlp.fc1.lora_B` path in `load_lora_adapter`. Leave `lora_A` and `fc2` unchanged. Native fused `mlp.fc1` keys and other models' `ff.net.0.proj` (e.g. Flux) do not match both sides of the guard, so they are not rewritten. ## Accuracy Tests Prompt: `A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves.` Config: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA + `lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo` (`minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_4step_v0.1.safetensors`), 1344×768 / 5 s, `seed=1101`, `lora_scale=0.0625`, `flow_shift=12`, `audio_flow_shift=3`, one H200. Same LoRA, 4-step and 8-step, before vs after this change. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37ee7943-0d37-462a-96c3-fc2be88fca26 Before the fix the fur is smeared; after the fix hair, face, and eyes resolve. Audio RMS also rises (4-step 0.0063 → 0.0097, 8-step 0.0067 → 0.0129). Latency and peak memory are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31880164198](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880164198)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31880164099](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880164099)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU]fix(dspark): preserve parity in folded NPU paths
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. --> This PR fixes numerical and graph-replay parity issues in DSpark's folded NPU paths, then optimizes the enabled paths so they preserve acceptance quality while outperforming the previous all-disabled fallback. ## Modifications - Replace folded sampling based on `softmax(logits / temperature) / Exp(1)` with the equivalent log-space exponential race: - stochastic: `argmax(logits - temperature * log(Exp(1)))` - greedy: direct `argmax(logits)` - Stage exponential noise immediately before graph replay only for stochastic requests. All-greedy requests avoid full-vocabulary RNG and corrected-logit stores. - Keep the dense Vanilla Markov W2 projection aligned with the target LM-head TP vocabulary shard: - compute only the local vocabulary slice; - reduce each local slice to one `(value, token_id)` candidate; - all-gather only the small candidate tensor and select the global top-1 with an NPU Triton kernel; - preserve the eager full-logit path for stochastic sampling. - Add contiguous KDA conv-snapshot and strided temporal-state commit kernels for Ascend, with the existing generic kernels retained as layout fallbacks. - Reshape flattened K tensors to `[tokens, heads, head_dim]` before the Ascend RoPE kernel and apply the same 3-D contract to stacked context KV. - Add NPU and NPUGraph regression tests for proposal parity, near ties, stochastic replay, TP-sharded top-1, production-size vocabulary reductions, and production KDA state layouts. The proposal changes are gated by `is_npu()` and the new state kernels live in the Ascend backend, so GPU execution paths are unchanged. ## Correctness | Check | Result | |---|---:| | Folded proposal vs. eager proposal with actual weights | Draft tokens exactly identical | | Corrected logits maximum absolute error | `0` | | Greedy near-tie case | Matches direct-logit `argmax` | | Mixed sampling with identical exponential noise | Token-by-token identical | | Stacked context K maximum absolute error | `<= 4.88e-4` | | Stacked context V maximum absolute error | `<= 2.44e-4` | | KDA conv/temporal state commits, ordinary + NPUGraph | Bitwise exact | The near-tie regression came from converting logits to softmax probabilities before greedy selection: distinct logits can round to equal probabilities and change tie-breaking. Direct-logit argmax preserves their ordering. ## Performance Tested on four Ascend nodes with Kimi K3 W4A8, TP64/DP4, exact 8,000 input / 1,000 output tokens, one request, four warm-up requests, and seeds 42-46. ### Group A reference: parent code, all four paths disabled ```text SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_STACKED_CTX_KV=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_EMBED_IN_GRAPH=0 ``` | Metric | Five-run mean | |---|---:| | TTFT | `7609.13 ms` | | TPoT | `15.6189 ms` | | ITL | `15.6189 ms` | | Acceptance length | `~7.392` | ### Final code: optimized paths enabled (`1111`) ```text SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=1 SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=1 # AUTO selects greedy folded sampling; stochastic requests stay eager SGLANG_DSPARK_STACKED_CTX_KV=1 SGLANG_DSPARK_EMBED_IN_GRAPH=1 ``` | Seed | TTFT (ms) | TPoT (ms) | Acceptance length | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 42 | 7731.116 | 15.806716 | 7.1667 | | 43 | 7767.762 | 14.556558 | 7.4667 | | 44 | 7758.790 | 15.001659 | 7.3667 | | 45 | 7789.845 | 15.106276 | 7.3500 | | 46 | 7533.141 | 14.453775 | 7.6633 | | **Mean** | **7716.131** | **14.984997** | **7.4027** | Compared with Group A, mean TPoT improves by `0.6339 ms/token` (`4.1%`) while mean acceptance length remains above 7.4 and mean TTFT remains below 7.8 seconds. ### State-commit microbenchmarks | NPU Event mean | Generic | Optimized | |---|---:|---:| | Conv snapshot, ordinary | 3.0991 ms | 0.0903 ms | | Conv snapshot, NPUGraph replay | 3.1370 ms | 0.0451 ms | | Temporal snapshot, ordinary | 0.6749 ms | 0.1334 ms | | Temporal snapshot, NPUGraph replay | 0.6800 ms | 0.0760 ms | ## Accuracy | Benchmark | Result | Notes | |---|---:|---| | GSM8K-200 | `96.5%` | Initial parity implementation; invalid `0.5%` | | GSM8K-1319 | `94.5%` | Final code; invalid `0.1%`; 1319/1319 complete; no request errors | | GPQA-Diamond | `92.42%` (`183/198`) | Final code; 198 predictions and reviews; no request errors | GPQA uses `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, and `reasoning_effort=max`. The final score is within the existing same-model run range observed on this machine (`91.41%` to `94.44%`). ## Validation - Full pre-commit suite: passed. - Python compileall: passed. - Final NPU/NPUGraph gate: `10 passed`. - Five random 8k/1k runs: 5/5 completed, exactly 1,000 output tokens, no errors. - GSM8K-1319 and GPQA-Diamond: complete, with no API, HTTP, or connection errors. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add NPU and NPUGraph unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (not required; no public API change). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers. 3. signals.title: [KDA] Route Kimi-Linear through native Cake kernels
signals.text: Depends on #34299 for the checkpoint-capable KDA serving surface and on FlashInfer [#4535](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4535) for the native `lower_bound=None` kernels. The incremental commits after #34299's head will narrow automatically when the dependency lands. ## Summary - Auto-select BF16 recurrent state and native Cake prefill/decode for Kimi-Linear-48B's D128 equal-head contract at TP-local H4/H8/H16/H32 (TP8/TP4/TP2/TP1). - Read prefill selection from the runner-scoped linear-attention dispatcher, preserving current server configuration ownership after the upstream backend refactor. - Feed packed projection Q/K/V, raw gate, and beta views directly to FlashInfer without `contiguous()` staging or state gather/scatter copies. - Preserve the native prefill route under breakable CUDA Graph padding by slicing only the live token prefix as storage-sharing row views; unpadded calls preserve exact tensor identity. - Keep admission fail-closed and retain structured per-layer route events and aggregate counters proving eligibility, native success, zero fallback/fatal outcomes, graph phase, and static zero-copy ownership. Per-event JSON logging is an explicit diagnostic opt-in so serialization and log I/O stay off the default serving replay path. ## Validation - B200 and B300 each pass 85 focused unit tests, 12 GPU decode integration tests, and seven GPU prefill integration tests, including bounded rows, native H4/H8/H16/H32 unbounded routes, checkpoints, packed rows, graph padding, and exact-identity inputs. - The exact-stack FlashInfer matrix passes 93 source/API/JIT contracts, eight prefill GPU rows, and 30 decode/export tests on both architectures. - After the telemetry logging change, 23 focused route, CUDA Graph ownership, Frozen-KV/MTP, and prefill CP/BCG tests pass, as do the changed-file formatting and Python compilation checks. - A full-model TP8/local-H4 check completed every serving request, stayed above the accuracy threshold, matched the required stop-token behavior, and recorded zero fallback, fatal outcomes, or input copies. ## Cold-L2 performance versus FLA Triton All rows use CUPTI GPU activity timing with L2 flushing. Ratios are `FLA / Cake`, so values above 1.0 mean Cake is faster. | Arch | Decode B1 | B4 | B8 | B16 | B32 | B64 | B128 | Geomean | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | B200 | 0.9932x | 0.9501x | 0.9911x | 1.0748x | 0.9899x | 0.9733x | 0.9188x | 0.9835x | | B300 | 0.9854x | 0.9200x | 0.9724x | 1.0571x | 0.9966x | 0.9778x | 0.9321x | 0.9765x | The selected decode topology is `1.0105x` faster than the prior Cake checkpoint on B200 and `1.0386x` faster on B300, reducing the FLA gap from 3.10%/6.12% to 1.68%/2.41%. FLA's multi-kernel prefill active-union/Cake speedups at T=512/1024/2048/4096/8192 are `1.4917x/1.4084x/1.3418x/1.3114x/1.2670x` on B200 and `1.4775x/1.4031x/1.3687x/1.3374x/1.2972x` on B300, for `1.3618x/1.3754x` geometric means. A separate local-H4 split-8/split-16 screen at B=1/4/8/16/32/64/128 found split-16 faster at every row on both targets, by `1.2118x/1.2050x` geometric means. The existing work-based selector therefore already chooses the faster topology throughout the new TP8/H4 route. The final same-stack local-H4 Cake-versus-FLA ratios at B=1/4/8/16/32/64/128 are `0.9927x/0.9648x/0.9526x/0.9748x/0.9451x/0.9955x/1.0617x` on B200 and `0.9688x/0.9626x/0.9638x/0.9797x/0.9649x/0.9716x/1.0647x` on B300, for `0.9832x/0.9817x` geometric means (Cake 1.71%/1.86% slower). Cake is 6.17%/6.47% faster at B128. ## Kimi-Linear-48B TP8/local-H4 serving The reference arm uses SGLang's Flash Linear Attention-derived `TritonKDAKernel`. The audit used one eight-B200 node, automatic Cake routing versus explicit Triton, 32 workload-shaped warmup requests, then 64 measured requests at nominal 2,048 input / 256 output tokens, concurrency 32, seed 20260814, and cache flush. Every measured arm processed the identical 63,573 input and 8,997 output tokens. The order was `Cake log-off → Cake log-on → Triton → Triton → Cake log-on → Cake log-off`. This exposed two independent effects that the earlier one-shot comparison conflated: 1. The first occurrence of each backend was cold. Cake's first scheduler initialization took 389.6 s versus about 41.4 s later; Triton's took 68.3 s versus 40.5 s later and emitted 75 serving-time compilation warnings versus zero on its repeat. 2. Raw per-event JSON logging expanded one hot Cake server log from 123,932 to 45,571,311 bytes (367.7x). Disabling it did not change routing or retained telemetry contracts; the adjacent hot log-off/log-on throughput difference was only +0.06%, so logging was noise reduction rather than the cause of the old full-model gap. ### Serving measurements | Order / arm | Total throughput (token/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Scheduler init (s) | Route-log bytes | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1. Cake, cold, log off | 25,649.12 | 123.511 | 7.520 | 389.6 | 123,904 | | 2. Cake, warm, log on | 29,534.20 | 127.385 | 6.211 | 41.9 | 45,770,842 | | 3. Triton, cold | 24,320.67 | 144.926 | 7.989 | 68.3 | 135,588 | | 4. Triton, hot | 30,371.90 | 114.727 | 6.016 | 40.5 | 120,203 | | 5. Cake, hot, log on | 30,714.85 | 108.904 | 6.007 | 41.4 | 45,571,311 | | 6. Cake, hot, log off | 30,734.67 | 105.940 | 5.992 | 41.5 | 123,932 | The old `25,490.40` versus `30,404.58` token/s result compared one cold Cake occurrence with a later hot reference occurrence. It is not a steady-state backend regression. In the new hot rows, Cake log-off versus Triton measured `1.0119x` throughput (+1.19%), 7.66% lower mean TTFT, and 0.40% lower mean TPOT while using 1,370,960 versus 1,373,968 MiB across eight GPUs. Because these rows are sequential rather than simultaneous, the conservative conclusion is hot steady-state parity with no demonstrated 16.16% Cake deficit, not a claimed kernel-attributable full-model speedup. ### Accuracy, stop behavior, and routing All arms use a 200-example, five-shot GSM8K evaluation at temperature 0, 512 maximum tokens, 128 request threads, and stop token `163586`. | Metric | Cake log off | Cake log on | FLA Triton | |---|---:|---:|---:| | GSM8K accuracy | 0.895 | 0.895 | 0.890 | | Required accuracy | >0.88 | >0.88 | >0.88 | | Stop-token completions | 200/200 | 200/200 | 198/200 | | Length-capped completions | 0/200 | 0/200 | 2/200 | Every reported stop matches token `163586`; the two Triton responses without it validly reached the 512-token cap. The two logging-on performance arms recorded 26,720 prefill and 265,440 decode Cake successes in total, with zero Triton fallback, zero fatal outcomes, and zero copied inputs. Logging-off arms emitted no raw JSON events by design while preserving in-memory route events and aggregate counters. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Perf] Restore the 16-token router GEMM threshold on SM10X
signals.text: ## Motivation #29470 dropped `max_router_gemm_tokens` from 16 to 4 on SM10X. That doesn't hold anymore: I re-ran its sweep and the JIT `dsv3_router_gemm` wins every `M` up to 12, ties 13-16. Likely #29783, which swapped the fallback it was measured against (`F.linear` → `linear_bf16_fp32`). Unverified. Speculative decoding never gets the fast path: the router sees `M = batch_size * num_draft_tokens`, so EAGLE 5/1/6 is at `M = 6` from concurrency 1. Plain decode keeps it to concurrency 4. So put it back to the kernel's compiled `1..16` range, the same bound `linear_with_fused_a_gemm` already uses. Literal revert of #29470. ## Speed Tests and Profiling 4x GB300, `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP4, `--quantization modelopt_fp4`. ### M sweep, current main Not an exact replication of #29470's: all 16 points instead of 8, and 8192/1024 instead of 1K/1K. No MTP, so router `M == concurrency`. WITH = JIT forced on, WITHOUT = cuBLAS forced on. | M | ITL WITH | ITL WITHOUT | ΔITL | tok/s WITH | tok/s WITHOUT | Δtok/s | winner | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---| | 1 | 6.63 | 6.85 | −3.21% | 144.13 | 140.08 | +2.89% | JIT | | 2 | 7.21 | 7.54 | −4.38% | 256.41 | 246.73 | +3.92% | JIT | | 3 | 8.18 | 8.51 | −3.88% | 332.53 | 321.75 | +3.35% | JIT | | 4 | 8.11 | 8.44 | −3.91% | 435.57 | 421.00 | +3.46% | JIT | | 5 | 9.28 | 9.53 | −2.62% | 470.70 | 461.76 | +1.94% | JIT | | 6 | 9.56 | 9.80 | −2.45% | 536.96 | 527.81 | +1.73% | JIT | | 7 | 9.87 | 10.09 | −2.18% | 599.41 | 588.15 | +1.91% | JIT | | 8 | 9.81 | 10.04 | −2.29% | 672.72 | 660.05 | +1.92% | JIT | | 9 | 10.81 | 10.94 | −1.19% | 684.09 | 679.03 | +0.75% | JIT | | 10 | 11.10 | 11.23 | −1.16% | 730.54 | 724.47 | +0.84% | JIT | | 11 | 11.40 | 11.51 | −0.96% | 773.95 | 767.62 | +0.82% | JIT | | 12 | 11.31 | 11.39 | −0.70% | 834.13 | 829.49 | +0.56% | JIT | | 13 | 12.20 | 12.18 | +0.16% | 837.63 | 839.08 | −0.17% | tie | | 14 | 12.47 | 12.42 | +0.40% | 872.36 | 875.12 | −0.32% | tie | | 15 | 12.67 | 12.63 | +0.32% | 909.12 | 911.54 | −0.27% | tie | | 16 | 12.57 | 12.55 | +0.16% | 960.27 | 961.61 | −0.14% | tie | Against what #29470 reported: | M | #29470, Jun 2026 | current main | |---:|:---|:---| | 1-4 | JIT +1.0 to 2.1% | JIT +2.9 to 3.9% | | 5 | **cuBLAS +1.8%** | **JIT +1.9%** | | 8 | **cuBLAS +1.7%** | **JIT +1.9%** | | 12 | **cuBLAS +1.7%** | **JIT +0.6%** | | 16 | **cuBLAS +3.4%** | tie | Each column is JIT against the fallback of its day (`F.linear` then, `linear_bf16_fp32` now), so this isn't a controlled A/B against their baseline. Every router call in a run sees the same `M`, so this grid derives any threshold `T`: `perf(T, M) = WITH(M) if M <= T else WITHOUT(M)`. `T = 16` wins or ties everywhere. ### E2E, speculative decoding ``` sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tp-size 4 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 5 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 ``` ``` python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang \ --model nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts 8 \ --max-concurrency 1 \ --warmup-requests 64 \ --flush-cache ``` 19 runs over 7 server launches (9 before / 10 after): | metric | before (M=6 → cuBLAS) | after (M=6 → JIT) | Δ | |:---|---:|---:|---:| | Benchmark duration | 17.041 s | **16.681 s** | **−2.11%** | | Output token throughput | 480.76 tok/s | **491.13 tok/s** | **+2.16%** | | Mean E2E latency | 2127.7 ms | **2082.7 ms** | **−2.11%** | | Mean TPOT | 1.772 ms | **1.730 ms** | **−2.38%** | | Median ITL | 1.750 ms | **1.710 ms** | **−2.29%** | Ranges don't overlap: slowest run after (16.73 s) beats the fastest run before (16.93 s). ITL and TPOT had zero within-arm variance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31927191884](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927191884)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31927191623](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31927191623)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
