signals.title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 CUTLASS MoE
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion. This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in: ```bash --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 ``` The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged. Related work: - SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816 - FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738 ### FlashInfer version requirement This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP. The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI. The new option therefore requires both: - `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18` - `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change. GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431. ## Modifications ### Runtime selection and compatibility - Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`. - Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90. - Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior. - Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths. - Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI. - Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility. ### Weight preprocessing - Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing. - Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer. - Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2. - Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules. - Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range. - Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path. ### Kernel invocation Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API: 1. FC1 folded weight block scales 2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation 3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale 4. FC2 folded weight block scales 5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale. ### Tests and benchmark - Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with: - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales - EP rank with global expert IDs - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18 - Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare: - SGLang Marlin W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 - Update the server-argument documentation. ## Accuracy Tests The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed: ```bash python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v ``` ```text 18 passed, 1 skipped ``` The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \ --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang #24816. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision` changed between `bf16` and `fp8`. ```bash PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \ python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --port 30000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 \ --api chat \ --max-tokens 1024 \ --num-threads 32 \ --temperature 0 \ --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl ``` | MoE precision | GSM8K score | Total latency | Output throughput | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | W4A16 (`bf16`) | 0.985 | 37.301 s | 611.809 token/s | | W4A8 (`fp8`) | 0.985 | 32.952 s | 683.574 token/s | W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang #24816. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang #24816: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU. The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py ``` Results on NVIDIA H20-3e: | Tokens | CUTLASS W4A16 median (min) | CUTLASS W4A8 median (min) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 | 0.275 ms (0.272 ms) | 0.164 ms (0.162 ms) | 1.68x | | 16 | 0.842 ms (0.840 ms) | 0.463 ms (0.460 ms) | 1.82x | | 64 | 1.894 ms (1.892 ms) | 1.037 ms (1.019 ms) | 1.83x | | 256 | 2.410 ms (2.403 ms) | 1.478 ms (1.383 ms) | 1.63x | | 1024 | 3.912 ms (3.906 ms) | 2.093 ms (1.999 ms) | 1.87x | | 2048 | 6.973 ms (6.954 ms) | 3.394 ms (3.384 ms) | 2.05x | | 4096 | 13.013 ms (12.971 ms) | 6.295 ms (6.210 ms) | 2.07x | | 8192 | 25.624 ms (25.546 ms) | 12.308 ms (12.293 ms) | 2.08x | FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed. ## Scope and Limitations - The implementation is SM90-only. - It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path. - A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions. - [x] Update server-argument documentation. - [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18. - [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result. - [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31955085259](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955085259)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31955085154](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955085154)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Native Hunyuan3D image encoders
signals.text: ## Summary - replace the Transformers CLIP and DINOv2 neural modules in the Hunyuan3D Shape conditioner with native SGLang implementations - add a native DINOv2 encoder with packed QKV, tensor-parallel linear layers, explicit checkpoint loading, and layerwise offload support - fix native CLIP vision attention to be non-causal while preserving causal CLIP text attention - make the Hunyuan3D conditioner weight-loading contract explicit and validate complete checkpoints ## Why Hunyuan3D Shape instantiated full Transformers vision models inside an otherwise native pipeline. This bypassed SGLang tensor parallelism and layerwise offload. It also exposed a latent correctness bug in the shared native CLIP implementation: vision attention was configured as causal. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files` for all changed files - `pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_hunyuan3d_image_encoder.py` - `pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_disagg_roles.py` - DINOv2-Giant checkpoint parity for TP=1 and TP=2 - 40-layer DINOv2 layerwise-offload parity against resident execution For DINOv2-Giant on H100 with Torch SDPA, the 20-run median encoder latency changed from 10.42 ms to 9.68 ms (-7.1%). TP=1 cosine similarity against Transformers was 0.9999989; TP=2 was 0.9999966, with identical outputs across ranks. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31901159523](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31901159523)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31901159320](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31901159320)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
signals.text: ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and `sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across the 61 target layers. This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache store left off**. The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another. Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to 0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this PR fuses. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`) - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M), so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it already handles. - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`, so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing. `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a store this path no longer performs. - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did. - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not added overhead. - **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY` (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path. Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched. ### Kernel-level evidence Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61 `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope` and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel` replaces them; no other kernel is added. | layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective | |---|---|---| | CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) | | HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) | "excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work this change moves. ## Accuracy Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. | run | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 | Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high # flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched) export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32 ``` ## Performance Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in `off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ). | concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 | | 8 | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 | | 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 | | 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 | Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a shift in speculation behaviour. ```bash # same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY # flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env: export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token # CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC # capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48). CONC=16 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \ --max-concurrency $CONC ``` `bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers `--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and neither arm can win by generating less. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32085368996](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085368996)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32085368826](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085368826)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(unified-cache): allow multiple concurrent load-back pins per node
signals.text: ## Motivation Under heavy device-eviction↔load-back cycling (small-VRAM GPUs with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, hybrid GDN/mamba models), the scheduler crashes with: ``` AssertionError: node 2498 pinned by load-back 2563, new anchor 2498 ``` at `UnifiedTreeCore.commit_load_back` (`unified_tree_core.py`). Hit repeatedly serving `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` + EAGLE + hicache ratio-12 on RTX 5090 (32GB) under a production-trace replay; 96GB GPUs never trip it (no deep evicted chains → no overlap). ## Root cause `UnifiedTreeNode.load_back_pending_id` is single-valued, but two live load-backs can legitimately pin the same node: 1. Request A load-backs anchored at a **descendant**; its Full-KV chain covers the evicted **ancestor** and pins it (`load_back_pending_id = A`). 2. Before A's ack, request B anchors **at that ancestor** to restore its **independently-evicted mamba state** (`mamba_component.build_hicache_transfers` pins `[node.id]`). 3. The single pin slot can't represent both live pins → assertion (`new anchor` == the node itself, matching the production message shape exactly). The overlap is semantically safe: both in-flight DMAs only **read** the shared host slots, and their writes target disjoint destinations (Full-KV pool vs mamba pool). Only the bookkeeping cannot represent it. ## Modifications - `load_back_pending_id: Optional[int]` → `load_back_pending_ids: set[int]`. - `commit_load_back` adds the anchor id (idempotent for a node sitting in both the Full and an aux transfer list of one anchor). - `finish_load_back` discards its anchor id along the root path; duplicate tracking updates once the last pin drains. - Reclaim guards (`_is_settled_full_host_duplicate`, `_can_reclaim_full_host_duplicate`) and the sanity check test set-emptiness; split inheritance copies the set. ## Test / repro `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_loadback_multipin.py` — a deterministic CPU repro built on the existing `UnifiedRadixCacheSuite` fixtures (FULL+MAMBA): backup → full evict → load-back anchored at the leaf (ack withheld) → load-back anchored at the pinned ancestor. - **Unpatched**: fails in 0.3s with the exact production assertion. - **Patched**: passes; pins drain to empty after both acks; `sanity_check` clean. - Full inherited FULL+MAMBA suite under the new class: 107 tests green. - Serving-level: the patched server sustains 400-span production-trace replays at hicache ratio-12 on RTX 5090 with zero assertions (previously crashed mid-run). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings as needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31902335393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902335393)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31902335225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902335225)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Expose selected worker ID in sglang model gateway responses
signals.text: ## Why is this change needed? Clients can provide a stable `x-smg-routing-key`, but today they cannot verify which backend worker served each response. This makes it difficult to diagnose whether multi-request agent sessions actually preserve worker affinity. The HTTP regular router now returns an opaque, deterministic `x-smg-worker-id` derived from the selected worker URL (including its data-parallel rank, when present). The identifier is added to both streaming and non-streaming responses after worker selection, including the final response after gateway retries, without exposing the worker IP or URL. For example, two requests routed to the same worker can now be correlated directly from their response headers: ```text request 1 -> x-smg-worker-id: 0f3a...c912 request 2 -> x-smg-worker-id: 0f3a...c912 ``` ## Test Plan - `cargo fmt --check` - `cargo test --lib test_insert_worker_id_is_stable_and_opaque` - `cargo test --test routing_tests test_worker_id_is_stable_for_streaming_and_non_streaming_responses` The integration test verifies that both streaming and non-streaming chat-completion responses expose the same worker ID when routed to the same backend. -Robot <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31902512993](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902512993)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31902512922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902512922)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Motivation Prefill context parallelism still carried both the v1 and v2 implementations behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2`. This duplicated server-argument compatibility handling, coupled model implementations to CP internals, and left legacy paths in attention backends and DSA. This PR makes the current v2 implementation the only prefill CP implementation and removes the version distinction. It is intentionally stacked on `clean-dsv4`. ## Modifications - Remove `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` and the legacy CP server-argument aliases and compatibility rewrites. - Delete the legacy `python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/cp_utils.py` implementation. - Remove prefill CP branches from model files, including DeepSeek and Qwen MoE implementations, so modeling code no longer owns CP data movement. - Remove CP v1 branches from CUDA, NPU, and MUSA attention backends and delete stale DSA v1 helpers. - Rename versioned APIs and fields, for example `is_cp_v2_active` to `is_cp_active`. - Delete v1-only and old parity tests while retaining the canonical CP test coverage. - Handle DSA CP warmup batches without speculative metadata and add regression coverage for that case. - Update documentation and examples to use `--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy ...`. ## Accuracy Tests Passed: - `test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py`: 26/26 tests. - `test/registered/cp/test_dsa_prefill_cp.py`: 1/1 test on H200; GSM8K score 0.946. - `test/registered/cp/test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4_cp.py`: 1/1 test on B200; GPQA score 0.6566 (threshold 0.58). - Two compatible configurations in `test_gqa_prefill_cp.py`: GSM8K score 0.98 each. Environment-blocked configurations: - GQA CP4: FA3 architecture restriction on B200; the H100 retry was blocked during backend initialization. - DeepSeek V3: JIT CUDA `silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant` / NVSHMEM initialization failure before CP evaluation. - DeepSeek V4: the B200 image lacked `aiter` for two configurations; the final configuration timed out during weight validation/prewarm before serving requests. Additional validation: - Full changed-file pre-commit suite. - Python `compileall` for `python/sglang/srt` and `test/registered/cp`. - Registered-test registry validation. - Diff whitespace validation and scans confirming removal of the legacy flag, aliases, and versioned CP API names. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. This is a legacy-path removal and API cleanup; no performance claim is made. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add/update unit tests. - [x] Update documentation. - [x] Provide available accuracy results and document environment-blocked runs. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] Add the Kimi-K3 MI35x perf benchmarks in nightly
signals.text:
Follow-up to #32568. Adds the Kimi-K3 MI35x performance benchmarks to the nightly, running immediately after the existing accuracy step in the same job so throughput is only measured once the model is known to produce correct tokens. ## Hardware result [Run 32074996819 summary](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32074996819/attempts/1#summary-95526175371) — both accuracy and performance steps passed on 8×MI355X with ROCm 7.2, on head `33d2793ae0`. **Accuracy** | Metric | Result | | --- | ---: | | GSM8K accuracy | **0.953** (threshold 0.92) | | Invalid responses | 0.1% | | Eval latency | 270.60 s | | Eval output throughput | 501.01 tok/s | **Performance sweep** | batch size | input len | latency (s) | input throughput (tok/s) | output throughput (tok/s) | ITL (ms) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 4096 | 9.34 | 13,530.74 | 56.62 | 17.66 | | 8 | 4096 | 13.85 | 18,097.61 | 340.10 | 23.52 | | 16 | 4096 | 17.68 | 18,196.44 | 581.97 | 27.49 | | 64 | 4096 | 37.73 | 18,217.66 | 1,403.86 | 45.59 | **Runtime** | Phase | Runtime | | --- | ---: | | Container setup | 4m 23s | | Dependency install | 1m 59s | | Accuracy step (server load + eval) | 45m 57s | | └ GSM8K request phase | 4m 31s | | Performance step | 5m 51s | | **Full job** | **58m 17s** | The accuracy step dominates because it includes loading the 1.56 TB checkpoint and server warmup. Perf runs immediately afterward in the same job, reusing the node's on-disk model cache and avoiding another container setup. > The sweep above was measured with `batch_sizes = [1, 8, 16, 64]`, before the warmup change below. Its batch-1 row therefore includes first-request warmup; with the repeated leading `1` that row becomes a post-warmup measurement and should land above 56.62 tok/s. The other three rows are unaffected. The perf step should gain roughly one batch-1 iteration of wall time, about 9 s. ## Review follow-up Three notes from @bingxche, all addressed: - **Use the shared report helper.** `sglang.test.nightly_bench_utils` already exports `generate_simple_markdown_report`, and its `default_gpu_config` parameter covers the `"MI35x"` label that the local copy hardcoded. The shared version is otherwise line-for-line identical, and it guards the ITL division against a zero `output_throughput` where the copy did not, so this removes duplication and closes a latent `ZeroDivisionError`. `test_gpt_oss_perf_mi35x.py` already imports it this way. Dropping the copy left `typing.List` and `BenchmarkResult` unused, so both imports are gone. - **Make the warmup skip actually fire.** The helper detects a warmup run by a repeated leading batch size, so with `[1, 8, 16, 64]` that branch was dead and the batch-1 row absorbed first-request warmup. Now `[1, 1, 8, 16, 64]`. - **Fix the circular `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` comment.** It claimed the value was "matched to `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`" when `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` is what that flag is set from, so it explained nothing. It now states the constraint the accuracy test records — the ~53 GB per GPU left after the MXFP4 weights — and keeps only the non-circular half, that graphs are not captured for batches the server would never admit. ### Why a warmup batch, given perf runs right after accuracy Running after the eval does not leave the perf sweep warm, because what it inherits is only on-disk state: - `run_benchmark_for_model` calls `popen_launch_server(...)` and then `kill_process_tree(...)` in its `finally`. The accuracy test does the same, so its server is already gone when the perf step starts and the sweep measures a brand-new process. The step still finished in 5m51s against ~41 min of loading in the accuracy step, which is the on-disk checkpoint and page cache being reused — not process state. - The server's own startup warmup is on by default but sends `input_ids=[10, 11, 12]` with `max_new_tokens=8`. The first measured run is a 4096-token prefill with 512 output tokens, so shape-keyed Triton/AITER autotuning and allocator first-touch for those buffers still land on it. HIP graph capture does happen during init, so that cost is already outside the measurement, and `--disable-radix-cache` means there is no prefix reuse between runs. - `test_gpt_oss_perf_mi35x.py`, the one MI35x perf test that already repeats the leading batch size, runs in `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-rocm720` — an accuracy step followed by a perf step in the same job on the same runner class. So the precedent comes from exactly this arrangement. Worth knowing for review: it is a precedent of one. The other fourteen MI35x perf tests use `[1, 8, 16, 64]` and so fold warmup into their batch-1 row, which means K3's batch-1 number will not be directly comparable to theirs. The tradeoff is a cleaner regression signal for K3 over time against cross-model comparability, at a cost of about 9 s per nightly. Happy to drop it if the reviewer would rather K3 match the majority. ## Test plan Verified with a harness that loads the real `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` and the real `nightly_bench_utils` with only the torch-backed leaf imports stubbed, so the code under test is the tree's: - [x] `setUpClass()` runs to completion and creates `performance_results_kimi_k3_mi35x` - [x] Every `runner.*` attribute the test touches exists on `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` - [x] The `run_benchmark_for_model(...)` call binds against the real signature - [x] No local `generate_simple_markdown_report` remains; the call site resolves to the shared function by identity, and the only symbol imported from `nightly_bench_utils` is that function - [x] No unused imports remain (checked by AST, so the dropped `List` / `BenchmarkResult` cannot silently linger) - [x] Rendering a five-run sweep through the shared helper emits four rows, so the warmup row is genuinely dropped, and the `[MI35x]` label still appears via `default_gpu_config` - [x] Workflow YAML parses; job count, `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` entries are unchanged from the base - [x] The K3 job runs `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` first, then directly invokes `registered/amd/perf/mi35x/test_kimi_k3_perf_mi35x.py` in the same job; `test/run_suite.py` is unchanged - [x] `codespell --config .codespellrc` clean repo-wide; `black --check` and `isort --check-only` clean - [x] Direct file invocation validated on hardware at head `33d2793ae0`; see **Hardware result** above - [ ] Re-run on hardware to capture the post-warmup batch-1 number. The review changes touch only the batch list and the report helper, not the server args, so accuracy is unaffected and the other three sweep rows should reproduce.

signals.title: [diffusion] feat: load quantized H3 text encoder checkpoints
signals.text: ## Summary - detect serialized quantization metadata from an overridden native text-encoder checkpoint - opt MiniMax-H3's native Qwen3-VL language stack into checkpoint FP8 while keeping embeddings, normalization, and the vision tower in BF16 - use the generic component-path interface (`--component-paths.text_encoder`, with `--text-encoder-path` as an alias) and fail closed for encoder/format combinations that have not explicitly opted in - document the checkpoint-first workflow without adding text-encoder-specific online quantization flags ## Why MiniMax-H3 uses a large Qwen3-VL prompt encoder, and users commonly want to select a concrete pre-quantized checkpoint for that component. The native encoder loader previously did not resolve the checkpoint's quantization metadata, pass it into the language model, or run post-load processing for quantized linears. The component path is generic, but quantization contracts are not: VAE, image-encoder, and text-encoder checkpoints can use different layer types, scale layouts, and kernels. This change therefore keeps support capability-based instead of claiming blanket quantization support for every component. ## Validation - H100 serialized `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-FP8` load through the normal `sglang serve` download path - complete 5-second 1344×768 T2VA request with the serialized checkpoint and layerwise offload - serialized FP8 TP1/TP2 load and forward comparison - after rebasing onto current `main` and removing the online-only API: `23 passed` in the focused loader/admission suite - changed-files pre-commit passed on the remote checkout <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32047889415](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32047889415)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32047889172](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32047889172)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] Bound tokenizer-side GPU memory in Kimi GPU image preprocessing
signals.text: ## Motivation `_gpu_preprocess_images` (Kimi K2.5/K3) keeps every image's fp32 patch tensor alive in a list and ends with a request-wide `torch.cat`. Peak GPU memory therefore grows with the request's total patch data because the accumulated outputs coexist with the final concatenation. On deployments running a high `--mem-fraction-static`, a large multi-image request can OOM device 0. The CUDA caching allocator may retain the resulting high-water reservation for reuse, reducing headroom for later requests. ## Modifications - `_gpu_preprocess_images`: process size-groups in sub-batches capped by `SGLANG_MM_GPU_PREPROCESS_CHUNK_BYTES` (default 512 MB); return per-image tensors instead of a request-wide concat; optionally hand each image to a `per_image_sink` as it is produced. - `MMFeatureStreamSink` (K2.5/K3): hash each image and wrap it into the CUDA-IPC pool (or move it to host for non-IPC transports) at production time, so preprocessing no longer retains every image's GPU output at once. - `get_new_expanded_mm_items`: split list-shaped bundled features by element and preserve production-time hashes (`PRECOMPUTED_FEATURE_HASHES_KEY`) instead of re-hashing wrapped features. - Kimi-K3's deferred model-side GPU preprocessing path materializes the per-image list before its grouped feature validation and splitting. `mimo_v2` has the same accumulate-and-concat pattern and can be ported in a follow-up. ## Validation Outputs are bit-exact with the previous pipeline and hashes are unchanged (same bytes and algorithm), so radix-cache keys remain stable. `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_kimi_mm_preprocess_bounded.py` checks parity across size groups, chunking, and K3 RGBA compositing. On H100, `test_peak_memory_bounded` measures an unchunked peak of at least 2× the total patch bytes and a bounded-path peak of at most 4× the configured chunk size for the test workload. Kernels are unchanged; chunking only splits batched launches. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) (no user-facing interface beyond the environment variable). - [x] Provide accuracy and memory validation results. - [ ] Provide a speed benchmark (kernel math is unchanged; out of scope for this memory-bound change). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32091205228](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091205228)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32091204861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091204861)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] fix: make MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache rebuild transactional
signals.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 can rebuild AdaLN outputs from checkpoint weights on demand and memoize the resulting timestep plans across requests. Two cache bookkeeping paths could leave the cache inconsistent: 1. When a new request exceeded `max_plans`, the cache cleared all resident plans but rebuilt only the plans that had been missing before the clear. If the request also reused an existing plan, that plan disappeared from the slab and its later lookup failed during denoising. 2. A plan was added to the host-side `_slots` index before all checkpoint reads and projections completed. If rebuilding raised midway, a retry treated the incomplete plan as a cache hit, skipped rebuilding it, and then failed because its zero `plan_lengths` entry remained invisible to lookup. The cache also accepted non-positive plan capacities, which could create degenerate slabs and fail later with less actionable errors. ## Modifications - Rebuild every plan required by the current request after a capacity reset, including plans that were cache hits before the reset. - Validate the request's plan count and width before clearing resident cache metadata, so an invalid request does not destroy a usable cache. - Keep new slot assignments in a pending host-side map while checkpoint weights are read and projected. - Publish `_slots` only after every layer has been written and the corresponding `plan_lengths` entries have been activated. A failed rebuild therefore leaves the incomplete slots invisible and allows a later request to retry. - Reject non-positive `max_plans` and `max_plan_width` values at cache construction time. ## Accuracy Tests The change only updates cache admission and metadata publication. It does not change timestep embeddings, checkpoint reads, tensor-parallel sharding, GEMM shapes, collectives, or cached output tensors. - Forced the capacity-reset path with a request containing both a previously resident plan and a new plan. All plans required by the request remained available to lookup after rebuilding. - Checked 470,367,744 AdaLN output elements against resident `adaln_proj` projections at both TP1 and TP2: zero mismatches. - Compared online-rebuild and resident-weight end-to-end outputs at TP1 and TP2. For both cold and cached cases, the online-rebuild MP4 MD5 matched the corresponding resident-weight run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This is a correctness-only cache bookkeeping change. The normal successful rebuild path performs the same checkpoint reads, projections, and collectives as before. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32036737012](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32036737012)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32036736957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32036736957)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Reuse SRT CLIP encoder blocks
signals.text: ## Summary - remove the duplicated CLIP embedding, attention, MLP, and encoder blocks from `multimodal_gen` - reuse the native SRT CLIP modules and tensor-parallel linear layers while keeping the diffusion output/loader wrappers - give the shared CLIP attention explicit text-causal vs. vision-bidirectional semantics - centralize encoder TP-group execution for all native text/image encoders and reused SRT modules - add a two-GPU tiny-SD3 end-to-end guard for encoder `fold` vs. `replicate` ## Why The two CLIP implementations had drifted in both behavior and maintenance: - padded CLIP text input dropped causal masking in the diffusion copy - SRT CLIP vision attention was accidentally causal - model blocks, TP loading, and mask handling were implemented twice Encoder folding also built and sharded a reused SRT encoder under the folding group, then restored the DiT TP group before forward. SRT layers that resolve their collective group at execution time could therefore run their folded weights with the wrong group. Model-specific group patches had started to grow around this behavior and did not protect every encoder entry point. `use_tensor_parallel_group` now switches MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP as one nested context and restores each previous value on exit. Native encoder roots bind the group used to build their shards through `EncoderTensorParallelMixin`, so construction, weight loading, and every public forward use the same group. The retained CLIP wrappers own only diffusion-specific output selection, pooling, and weight loading. The duplicated MMGen implementation is removed. ## Validation - H100, real `openai/clip-vit-base-patch32` BF16 weights: all 148 text and 151 vision parameters loaded - TP=1 parity after the fix: text (masked and unmasked) and post-norm vision outputs match Transformers exactly - TP=2: both ranks produce identical outputs; mean absolute difference vs. the replicated BF16 Transformers reference is `0.0141` - layerwise offload: text and vision encoder stacks are detected and two consecutive streamed runs match resident outputs exactly - H100 batch=4, 500 measured iterations: vision encoder median `1.814 ms -> 1.584 ms` (`-12.7%`) - tiny SD3 native e2e, identical 2-GPU Ulysses topology: encoder `fold` vs. `replicate` gives SSIM `0.994886`, PSNR `43.625576`, MAD `0.771159` - negative control on the pre-fix runtime gives SSIM `0.924886`, PSNR `30.782886`, MAD `5.275228`, and the new e2e fails as intended - exact final SHA `33a240aa067b5`: standalone fold suite `2 passed`; focused group/folding/SigLIP unit suite `40 passed` - full pre-commit range passed; no consistency GT or threshold was changed ## Correctness regressions fixed With the previous CLIP implementation and the same real weights: - padded text vs. Transformers: max absolute difference `31.375` - post-norm vision vs. Transformers: max absolute difference `10.5` Both are `0.0` after this change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32006713795](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32006713795)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32006713580](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32006713580)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Reuse SRT Qwen vision and text modules
signals.text: ## Motivation The multimodal generation Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3, and Qwen3-VL encoders duplicated pure modules already implemented in SRT. Maintaining both copies also left the MMGen paths without reusable SRT tensor-parallel projections, embeddings, activation kernels, and checkpoint loaders. ## Modifications - Reuse SRT Qwen vision patch embeddings, MLPs, patch mergers, RMSNorm, and tensor-parallel linear layers from MMGen. - Reuse SRT Qwen2.5 text projections, split `Qwen2_5_VLMLP`, HF-semantics `RMSNorm`, and `VocabParallelEmbedding`. - Reuse SRT `SiluAndMul` and `RMSNorm` in the native Qwen3 and Qwen3-VL text paths. - Extend SRT RMSNorm kernels to flatten and restore higher-rank activations when a residual is present. This is required by diffusion text encoders with `[batch, sequence, hidden]` states. - Keep the Qwen2.5 split gate/up execution order as `act(gate) * up`; this avoids a concatenation and preserves HF numerical behavior. - Use replicated SRT linears at TP=1 and explicit TP rank/size at TP>1, while retaining the existing replicated fallback when a dimension is not TP-divisible. - Share one MMGen packed-sequence attention adapter between Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL. It remains MMGen-owned because diffusion backend selection and segmented SDPA fallback differ from SRT serving's attention contract. - Reuse SRT MRoPE in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL text attention. Keep MMGen LocalAttention and Qwen3-VL quantized linears because their diffusion runtime and quantization contracts differ from SRT serving. - Map MiniMax-H3 checkpoint `.attn.qkv.` names to the native SRT `.attn.qkv_proj.` parameters. - Keep `model.visual.blocks` and language-model layer ownership unchanged so layerwise offload and FSDP selection continue to work. - Bind each native encoder root to the TP group used to construct and shard it. One nested context now switches MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP together for construction, loading, and forward, then restores their previous values independently. ## Accuracy and Integration Tests Latest validation on H100 at exact head `0844a9a3088f3`: - Focused Qwen, encoder-folding, and group-lifecycle unit tests: `55 passed`. - The new two-GPU no-download guard uses a real SRT `RowParallelLinear` with DiT TP=1 and folded encoder TP=2. Its output matches the complete unsharded linear reference, and MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP all restore to size 1 after forward (`1 passed`, 24.63s). - Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL SRT MRoPE versus Transformers: FP32 maximum absolute error `2.38e-7`; BF16 maximum absolute error `0.015625` (1-2 ULP), with mean absolute error between `1.8e-4` and `4.0e-4`. - Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3-VL batched GQA layout, three-axis positions, Transformers v5 RoPE config, and attention wiring are covered by focused tests. The full native server/pipeline encoder `fold` versus `replicate` e2e guard is in #35004. On its pre-fix runtime negative control it fails with SSIM `0.924886` and MAD `5.275228`; after the shared group fix it passes with SSIM `0.994886` and MAD `0.771159`. No consistency GT or threshold was changed. Broader component and E2E validation at parent head `6e57d71d6efe2`: - Focused GPU unit/component suite: `26 passed`, plus 2 parameterized subtests. - Qwen2.5 TP=2 MLP matches the previous MMGen implementation exactly; TP=2 embedding output is exact. - Qwen2.5 full-GEMM comparison differs only by expected BF16 TP reduction order (`max_abs=3.81e-6`). - Real Z-Image Qwen3 text component: cosine similarity `0.999898`. - Real Qwen-Image server/API case: CLIP/SSIM `1.0`, infinite PSNR, zero pixel difference; `/v1/models` success and not-found paths passed. - Real MiniMax-H3 2-GPU video E2E: minimum CLIP `0.9953`, minimum SSIM `0.9687`, minimum PSNR `43.06`. - Existing Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL vision TP=1/TP=2, layerwise-offload, component-accuracy, and Qwen-Image-Edit E2E checks remain covered. ## Performance - Qwen2.5 split text MLP, real model size, H100: paired median ratio `0.9961` versus the previous MMGen implementation. - Qwen-Image E2E: `12697.67 ms` versus `12799.17 ms` baseline. - MiniMax-H3 2-GPU E2E: `47120.89 ms` versus `47538.57 ms` baseline. - Existing full vision-tower measurements remain 1.08x faster for Qwen2.5-VL and 1.19x faster for Qwen3-VL. These measurements show no observed regression; the E2E results are within or better than their checked-in baselines. ## Checklist - [x] Full pre-commit range passed. - [x] Focused unit and weight-transfer tests passed. - [x] Validate folded SRT collectives and TP-group restoration on two GPUs. - [x] Validate TP=1, TP=2, higher-rank residual RMSNorm, layerwise offload, component accuracy, and real server E2E. - [x] Validate Qwen-Image public image/model APIs. - [x] Public CLI and model compatibility are unchanged; no documentation update is required. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32027430394](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32027430394)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32027430176](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32027430176)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] Classify PIL decode-time failures as client errors (400)
signals.text: ## Motivation Image bytes that pass PIL's `open()`-time format sniffing can still fail during the eager `img.load()` in `_load_single_item`: - a PNG whose corruption sits **past the first IDAT chunk** raises `SyntaxError("broken PNG file")` — `Image.open` only parses up to the first IDAT, so sniffing succeeds; - a truncated file raises `OSError("image file is truncated")`. Neither type is in `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS` (`UnidentifiedImageError` only covers open-time sniffing failures), so these requests return **500** instead of **400**. This was observed in production as repeated 500 responses for the same corrupt screenshot payload. ## Modifications Catch `OSError` and `SyntaxError` only around PIL's eager `img.convert()` / `img.load()` step and translate them to `ValueError`. Keep `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS` narrow so the same broad built-in exceptions from non-PIL loaders or system work remain `RuntimeError` / 500. Tests in `test_base_processor_bad_input.py` cover: - zeroed later PNG chunk header → `SyntaxError` → `ValueError`; - truncated PNG → `OSError` → `ValueError`; - mocked non-PIL `OSError` → `RuntimeError`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32086532911](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32086532911)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32086532614](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32086532614)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(npu): split packed MTP HiCache transfers by pool
signals.text: > [!IMPORTANT] > For standalone Ascend HiCache validation, this PR branch bundles the complete > commit history of #32500 through `#32500@9acc6b733`. Users can fork this branch > and run it directly without fetching another PR. For upstream review and > merge, #32500 should still land first; GitHub will then remove the shared > commits from this PR's diff. #34560 is already merged into `main`. End-to-end > Qwen3.6 validation also uses the checkpoint semantic fix in #35086, but that > PR is not included in this branch. Recommended merge order: #32500, #35086, > then this PR. ## Motivation After #34560, the HiCache host K/V layer dimension includes both the target model layers and the NEXTN/MTP draft layers. #32500 adds the Ascend fused `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` path for `page_first_direct`, but that path invokes the operator once with the target device pool and the full packed host buffer. On Ascend, the target and draft K/V layers are separate device pools. A single invocation therefore pairs a target-only device buffer with a `target + draft` host-layer range, so the draft K/V layers are not transferred through the matching device pool. CUDA does not have this mismatch. Its existing path packs target and draft per-layer pointers into one pointer array, and the per-layer transfer kernels map each host layer to the corresponding device pointer. The Ascend fused operator accepts one contiguous device pool per invocation, so each pool must be transferred separately. ## Minimal reproduction Apply #32500 on top of a revision that contains #34560, then launch Qwen3.6-27B on Ascend with the following relevant options: ```text --tp-size 2 --attention-backend ascend --device npu --page-size 128 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-storage-backend mooncake --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` 1. Generate from a 3000-token prompt to populate HiCache. 2. For L2, generate a separate 6000-token filler to evict the original prefix from L1, then replay the original prompt. 3. For L3, wait for write-through completion, call `/flush_cache`, then replay the original prompt. 4. Request `return_cached_tokens_details` and inspect the target/draft transfer at the first `kernel_ascend` H2D or D2H operation. Without this change, the fused operation receives the full packed host layer range with only the target device pool. The draft pool is not transferred by a matching invocation. ## Changes - Skip CUDA-style packed device pointer arrays for the Ascend MTP path. - Iterate over the target pool and every draft pool on Ascend. - Slice the packed host K/V buffer to the layer range that belongs to each device pool. - Invoke `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` once per pool for both H2D and D2H. - Add focused tests for Ascend initialization and target/draft host-layer slicing. - Bundle all #32500 commits through `9acc6b733` so this fork branch is directly runnable for Ascend HiCache validation. Focused validation: - latest `upstream/main`: `2 passed` - exact branch head with `#32500@9acc6b733`: `3 passed, 17 deselected` - complete stacked focused tests with #35086: `8 passed` - pre-commit on both changed files: passed ## L2/L3 replay validation Validation stack: latest `main` with #34560, `#32500@9acc6b733`, #35086, and this fix. Model: Qwen3.6-27B BF16, TP2, Ascend NPU, NEXTN enabled, 4 prompts with 3000 input tokens and 512 output tokens. | Replay tier | Isolated cache details | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Host L2 | `host=2944, device=0, storage=0` for 4/4 prompts | passed | | Mooncake L3 | `storage=2944, device=0, host=0` for 4/4 prompts | passed | The L2 and L3 replay output IDs were identical for all four prompts: ```text sha256=a0349ca2a8cdf023da0ef7b86370fbc25eac55ba5d8a656665a845c4a1d969d9 ``` Their speculative statistics were also identical: - weighted accept rate: `62.8169%` - weighted accept length: `2.8845` - correct/proposed drafts: `1338/2130` Cold generation and cache replay were not token-identical. The first mismatch positions were `[217, 322, 293, 58]` for both L2 and L3. Since the L2 and L3 replays match each other exactly, Mooncake L3 does not introduce an additional divergence. #35086 fixes the packed Mamba checkpoint index; the remaining cold/replay divergence is the separate cold-prefill persistence-boundary issue described in #33515. ## Accuracy validation Ran the repository's `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` against the same NEXTN + Mooncake service using the first 200 examples from the official GSM8K test set: ```text num_questions=200 num_shots=5 parallel=4 temperature=0 max_new_tokens=512 chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false} ``` Result on the complete stack: `194/200` correct (`97.0%` accuracy), `0%` invalid responses, no request failures, and `218.519 s` latency. The earlier incomplete-stack result was `195/200`; only prompt 182 changed correctness, from the correct answer `23` to `24`. This run includes #35086 but does not include #33515's cold-prefill alignment change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32013404865](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013404865)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32013404713](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013404713)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Scheduler] Add configurable decode interval after prefill
signals.text: [by Codex] ## Motivation With DP attention, each rank schedules attention work locally while all ranks still participate in the same MoE collective. A rank with repeated chunked-prefill continuation work can therefore keep winning SGLang's prefill-first scheduling decision and starve decode work on peer ranks. In the AgentX workload this left requests waiting while the actual decode batch remained small. The DP-attention MLP-sync all-gather already exposes whether any rank selected an EXTEND batch. Use that globally synchronized signal to enforce a rank-consistent decode interval after prefill. ## Modifications - Add `--prefill-decode-interval N`, defaulting to `0` (disabled, so existing behavior is unchanged). - After an EXTEND batch, defer new prefill scheduling for the next `N` scheduler rounds so the running batch can decode. - Under DP attention, arm the interval from the existing globally synchronized `is_extend_in_batch` flag. Under non-DP scheduling, use the local forward mode. - Validate non-negative values and add focused scheduler/server-argument unit tests. No AIPerf source change is required. The benchmark prototype used the existing per-session routing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This changes batch selection cadence only; it does not change model math or sampling. - Added unit coverage for disabled, non-DP, globally synchronized DP, and decode/non-rearm behavior. - Added server-argument validation coverage. - `python -m py_compile` passed for all modified Python/test files. - The focused pytest command could not collect on the development VM because its base Python environment does not include `torch`/`numpy`; the new tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The equivalent scheduler prototype was evaluated with full 3,600-second DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 AgentX runs on 8x B200 using TP8/DP8/EP8, DP attention, MTP3, and an interval of 16: | Concurrency | Interactivity (tok/s/user) | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | Cache hit | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 56 | 30.75532 | 23,559.05865 | 95.945% | | 84 | 23.24221 | 26,110.24296 | 94.703% | The c84 run completed 7,096 profiled requests with zero request errors. These results validate the equivalent prototype on SGLang v0.5.17; this PR ports the behavior onto current `main` using the existing global DP EXTEND flag. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32090947690](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090947690)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32092092608](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32092092608)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: retire the multi-engine accommodation in the runtime context
signals.text: A process holds at most one live config: the bags always describe the engine running now. Re-publish stays last-publish-wins, which is what lets a process rebuild an engine after shutting the previous one down. Drop preserve_config() and its per-leaf bag snapshot/restore helpers. They existed for a nested build that publishes a private ServerArgs copy; the draft build stopped doing that when per-runner values became constructor arguments, and no production caller is left. Drop the launcher entry from ROLE_NAMESPACE_SETS: no process publishes under that role. The multi-item scoring tests held two engines alive at once. The reference engine now runs its scoring calls first and shuts down before the engine under test boots; engine boots per class are unchanged, so the CI harness still sees the same GPU demand. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32079649554](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079649554)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32079648227](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079648227)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: publish before a process reads configuration
signals.text: Five processes read config namespaces before they published. The launch path ran validation, port allocation and the subprocess launches ahead of its publish; the scheduler ran its process configuration first; the tokenizer manager read the parallel bag in a constructor that is the first publish in a tokenizer-worker process; the encode server's launch path read the DP size before the encoder it builds publishes; the detokenizer never published at all while reading resolution-written fields off the instance it was handed. Each publishes as early as its config is final -- for the launch path that is right after late resolution, which refuses a published instance. The two DSA seed predicates take no config argument: every caller was handing over the process config, and the fields they read are bag leaves. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32079715235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079715235)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32079715101](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079715101)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: spec: size the speculative buffers from the bags, not the startup record
signals.text: Adaptive speculative decoding switches the step config at runtime through get_context().override, which moves the spec bag leaves and leaves the ServerArgs record on its startup values. Six sizing paths read the record: - allocation_sizing: the per-decode KV reserve, recomputed every decode batch, kept reserving for the startup step count after a switch - spec_utils.resolve_num_tokens_per_req: draft-extend capture widths were sized for the startup draft-token count while a different candidate state was being captured - spec_info.create_dummy_verify_input: the autotune forward inside the capture window built its dummy verify input at the startup tree shape - eagle_disaggregation: the prebuilt-batch draft-input state count - managers.utils.compute_num_reserved_tokens: the token budget the rust ingress enforces All of them read the spec bag now, and so do the two DSA seed predicates the disagg path calls. The config parameter goes away where every caller was handing over the process config anyway, which drops the disagg draft-input hand-off chain down to what it uses; the tests that drove those paths with stand-in objects publish a config. The exposure pins shrink by 16 (axis 1) and 6 (axis 2) pairs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32079764161](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079764161)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32079764487](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079764487)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: the per-instance families read the bags
signals.text: The tokenizer manager, the detokenizer, the multimodal processors, the encode server and the HTTP entrypoint read resolved config off the instance they were handed. That was justified by several engines sharing one process; a process holds one live config, so they read the bags like every other consumer. The same goes for the launch paths, the sidecar and the Ray driver, and for the three single-reader decisions (the grammar-backend factory, the token-oracle install gate, the new-token ratio tracker). The parallel sizes are the exception that has to be spelled out: pp_size and its four siblings are read-through properties over the process groups, so a launch path -- which decides how many processes to spawn before joining any group -- must ask for the configured value. Functions lose the config parameter where every caller was handing over the process config: the EPD rejection guard, the hidden-state ceiling, the token-oracle gate. sarvam-moe stops caching the process config in a lazy slot and dispatches on the configured attention pair like the other dispatch sites. Two guards pin what only a server boot would otherwise catch: that no launch path reads a live-shadowed size, and that the bag accessors are never called as object members. The tests that drove these paths with stand-in objects publish a config instead. The reads that stay: the two gates deciding whether late resolution runs, the remote-instance seed check, and the NCCL environment setup. All three run before this process publishes, and each needs its own call on whether it is asking about raw input or about the effective value. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32079826723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079826723)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32079826653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079826653)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: one control-plane log for the process
signals.text: The tokenizer manager kept its own log of post-startup config changes with the same shape as the context's -- (source, fields) with provenance -- and read it back with a reverse scan on every output message. It records into the config bags now, so a process carries one log and one provenance format, and reading one field is an attribute read. config_leaf() is the read side of override(): callers holding a field name rather than a namespace no longer have to know which bag it lives in. model_path and served_model_name stay manager attributes. They answer the readback from there, and writing them to the bags would not reach the other processes that read them. The exposure census follows the wrapper: record_config_updates call sites are override sites now, and its resolver learned the loop-variable key shape the parser detection uses. Three parser pairs join the pinned surface -- the two launcher gates ask the record on purpose, and the grammar backend reads in a different process from the writer. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32079891933](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079891933)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32079891726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079891726)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [JIT Kernel] Migrate causal_conv1d_fwd and causal_conv1d_update from AOT to JIT
signals.text: ## Motivation Move `causal_conv1d_fwd` / `causal_conv1d_update` off the prebuilt `sgl_kernel` wheel and onto the JIT kernel infra, keeping the in-place contract, the exported ops, and bit-level numerics. Both sit on the prefill/decode path of every short-conv hybrid model — LFM2 / LFM2-MoE, Mamba2, GDN. ## Modifications - Device kernels move into `kernels/jit/csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cuh` unchanged; only the host launchers switch to the tvm-ffi `TensorView` API. Strides stay `uint32_t` elements, as in the AOT `ConvParamsBase`. - The JIT build matches the wheel's arch split — `-use_fast_math` on SM 9.0, precise math elsewhere, per `load_utils.py`'s `compute_capability == 90` — so the SiLU epilogue emits the same bits. Math mode is part of the build key. - CUDA serving goes through the JIT registry behind a `torch.compile`-compatible custom op; everything else keeps Triton. The AOT ops stay exported for external users and for the differential test. - Only a JIT/CUDA spec is registered, since the AOT kernel was CUDA-only anyway — `csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cu` sits in the CUDA CMakeLists and nowhere else, and `common_extension_rocm.cc` never defined the ops. ROCm and MUSA were already landing on Triton through the old `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.causal_conv1d_update` probe; now they get there directly via `_HAS_CONV1D_KERNEL = is_cuda()`. Nothing changes on any device. - The AOT `cudaFuncSetAttribute` branch goes away behind a `static_assert`: every instantiation sits near 4 KB of shared memory, nowhere near the 48 KB it existed to raise. - `width` outside 2..4 now raises in prefill, where the AOT `if`/`else if` chain had no `else` and quietly did nothing. - `has_initial_state` gets a dtype check. The kernel reads it as `const bool*`, and `kDLBool` has no C++ trait, so it lands as a `CHECK_HOST` on the dtype code rather than a matcher clause. - Tests and benchmarks move to the registered kernel layout, and the superseded AOT-only test is gone. ## Accuracy Tests `pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` | | H200 (SM90, fast-math) | GB300 (SM103, precise-math) | |---|---|---| | Total | 473 passed, 12 skipped | 473 passed, 12 skipped | | Bit-exact vs AOT (72 cases) | pass | pass | | Reference vs `F.conv1d` (393 cases) | pass | pass | Two machines because the kernel picks its math mode by arch, so each one compiles a different build. The 12 skips are the same deliberate guard on both: the circular-buffer reference can't arbitrate when `seqlen > state_len`, where `scatter_` hits duplicate indices. Behind those counts, the reference tests cover FP32/FP16/BF16 × widths 2–4 × seqlens 1–4096, varlen (per sequence) and non-varlen, both conv-state layouts, gathered slots. The differential is one config per dispatch path, narrowed from a ~900-config sweep that came back bit-identical to AOT throughout. On GB300 the SiLU epilogue — where a math-flag mismatch would show up — gives `max_abs_diff = 0.000e+00`. Also checked: `pad_slot_id` slots untouched, bad dtype / width / non-bool mask rejected, `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` bit-identical to eager, and `LiquidAI/LFM2-350M` serving end to end (GSM8K 200q = 0.325, H200). B200 is registered in `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/mamba/bench_causal_conv1d.py` — FP16/BF16, `dim` 2048–8192, prefill seqlens 128–8192 (4-sequence varlen batch), decode batch 1–256 with gathered slots. 24 configs each. | | prefill geomean | prefill range | prefill wins | decode geomean | decode range | decode wins | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | H200 (SM90) | **1.063x** | 1.022x – 1.122x | 24/24 | 1.001x | 0.995x – 1.015x | 14/24 | | GB300 (SM103) | **1.041x** | 1.015x – 1.062x | 24/24 | 1.000x | 0.987x – 1.013x | 10/24 (3 tied) | - Prefill wins every config on both machines. GB300 extremes: BF16 `(512, 2048)` 22.09 vs 22.41 us, BF16 `(2048, 8192)` 84.90 vs 90.16 us. - Decode is a wash, and those win counts are noise rather than a result: 23/24 configs on H200 and 20/24 on GB300 land within ±1% either way, three of them exact ties. The decode kernel is unchanged, so neither direction means anything. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing documentation change is required.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31951691285](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31951691285)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31951691178](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31951691178)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(disaggregation): route equal-TP fragmented KV transfer through staging
signals.text: ## Problem Equal-TP (MHA/GQA) PD-disaggregated KV transfer collapses bandwidth when the decode-side KV cache becomes fragmented: each `(group, layer)` slice becomes a separate transfer entry, and per-entry device-memory (D2H) copy overhead dominates the transfer. - engine-level: 1 entry → 4792 MB/s; 4096 entries → 15.5 MB/s - end-to-end (200 concurrent long shared-prefix requests): 1.41 → 1.76 req/s (+25%), TPOT 23.03 → 13.80 ms (−40%) This is the root cause behind the bandwidth collapse reported in #5450 (which was auto-closed without a confirmed fix; the "larger page-size" workaround avoids, but does not fix, fragmentation). ## Root cause 1. `alloc_extend` allocates across non-contiguous free segments under pool pressure (decode-side radix cache reuse) → fragmented dst indices. 2. The equal-TP direct path (`send_kvcache`) emits one transfer entry per (group × layer), so fragmentation blows up the entry count. 3. Per-entry fixed cost × thousands of entries → bandwidth collapse. ## Fix Route equal-TP fragmented chunks through the existing staging path (local gather → 1 bulk RDMA → decode scatter), collapsing G×2L entries into 1. Gated behind `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER` and a new `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_MIN_GROUPS` (default 8); `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_ALWAYS` opts into staging for every equal-TP chunk. - `mooncake/conn.py`: equal-TP fragmentation branch + `_fragmented_groups` + `_ensure_equal_tp_staging_req` (on-demand STAGING_REQ) + bounded spin - `decode.py`: register gate widened to non-MLA equal-TP, excluding fake-transfer requests (warmup/health-check) to avoid a warmup hang - `utils.py`: poll demote gate switched to `is_staging_room` - `environ.py`: `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_MIN_GROUPS` / `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_ALWAYS` All changes are env-gated and default-off: behavior is unchanged unless staging is explicitly enabled. ## Validation - Warmup passes with `STAGING_BUFFER=1`, and with staging + decode radix cache on both MHA and GQA. - Fragmented workload (200 rooms shared-prefix): 1.41 → 1.76 req/s (+25%), TPOT 23.03 → 13.80 ms (−40%), 90/90 staging transfers succeeded, 0 failures. - Healthy path no regression (1.47 → 1.49 req/s, within noise). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32033975111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32033975111)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32033974935](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32033974935)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
