signal.title: Skip inkling sheared bias under batch invariance
signal.text: ## Motivation The sheared-bias attention path is not batch invariant, so prefill-vs-decode logprobs cannot be bit-exact under `--enable-deterministic-inference`. Its bias tile geometry follows the query count, which means the same absolute (q, k) pair accumulates in a different order for a few-query decode step than for a many-query prefill. Dumping the per-call geometry gives the complete difference set between a speculative verify and a prefill — every other parameter (`tile_m`, `tile_n`, `group_tile_bias`, padded extent, varlen, causal, window) is identical: | field | verify | prefill | | --- | --- | --- | | `tile_bias` | 16 / 8 | 128 | | `max_m_blocks_leq_one` | True | False | | `bias_max_seqlen_q` | 3 | 3181..4205 | `tile_bias` rounds to the actual query count when it is below `tile_m`, which is where the query dependence enters. Pinning the two geometry knobs under `is_batch_invariant()` — separately, and both together so the verify geometry matches prefill field for field — still does not reach zero, so the ordering is decided inside the kernel rather than by these Python-side parameters. A forward-hook dump agrees: with a triggering sequence, q/k/v and the relative-bias input are bit-identical while one element out of 1024 of the attention output differs by 7.812e-03, about one ULP. A wrong bias entry would show a structured error, not a single-element ULP. Making the sheared path itself batch invariant means reorganizing the m-block accumulation in the cute kernel. Until then, deterministic mode takes the score_mod path, which is invariant. The flag keeps its default for normal serving, so this only changes behavior when deterministic inference is requested. Ref https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34899 ## Accuracy `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py`, with no environment override: ``` MTP (test_logprobs_match, test_decode_cache_hit) avg_kl_div=0.0 avg_kl_div=0.0 2 passed, 7 deselected, 15 warnings in 294.55s (0:04:54) ``` The non-speculative classes are the required regression here — they previously reached zero with the sheared path on, and the gate moves them to score_mod: ``` avg_kl_div=0.0 (x7) 7 passed, 2 deselected, 15 warnings in 569.13s (0:09:29) ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32091883626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091883626)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32091883504](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091883504)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CPU] Fix NUMA/core binding for DP ranks
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Before this PR, `ModelRunner.init_threads_binding` picked the NUMA node / core group for a worker using `tp_rank`. Under DP, DP rank 0 and DP rank 1 both resolve to tp_rank=0 and get bound to the same NUMA node/cores instead of being spread across the machine. This PR fixes this incorrect binding. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> `init_threads_binding` now takes `numa_index` (the worker's global device id) and `world_size = dp_size * tp_size * pp_size`, instead of `tp_rank` and `tp_size`, so every rank across every DP replica maps to a distinct NUMA node / core group. Removed the `world_size == len(threads_bind_list)` equality assert for the explicit `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` path, replacing it with only the per-rank bounds check. This permits the router-mode case (local `world_size=1`, multi-group bind string) while still catching a bind list that's too short. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [HiCache] Support DCP with DSpark
signal.text: ## Motivation DCP + HiCache + DSpark is currently rejected during server argument validation. Removing that guard exposed a draft HiCache sidecar sizing bug: draft indices inherit the target cache's DCP-wide logical index space, while the draft host pool was sized from only the target's physical per-rank rows. Once L1 eviction reached the uncovered range, the draft host transfer failed with `CUDA error: invalid argument`. ## Modifications - Allow DSPARK with HiCache when `--dcp-size > 1`, while retaining the guard for other speculative algorithms. - Size full draft HiCache sidecar pools from the target host pool's logical capacity. - Apply the same logical-capacity sizing to the legacy draft HiCache path. - Add a regression test for DCP-expanded draft sidecar sizing. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on RunPod node 5 with 8x NVIDIA B300 GPUs using a Kimi-K3 target and RadixArk Kimi-K3 DSpark draft model, TP8/DCP8, A2A, HiCache L2, and the normal CUDA graph path. - Eviction stress test: 64 requests x 16,384 input tokens, concurrency 48. - Result: 64/64 successful; 1,048,576 input tokens and 512 output tokens processed in 52.00 seconds. - Post-run `/health_generate`: HTTP 200. - No scheduler exceptions or CUDA errors after the fix. - `test_server_args.py`: 144 passed, 15 subtests passed. - `test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py`: 4 passed. [TODO] more advanced tests involving DeepSWE ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is a capacity/correctness fix rather than a kernel-path performance change. The eviction stress test above observed approximately 20,164 input tokens/s. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No documentation change needed; this enables an existing flag combination.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32085957613](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085957613)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32085957361](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085957361)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

For distributed OPs, use `torch.distributed.all_gather_into_tensor` and `torch.distributed.reduce_scatter_tensor` on CPU for now to fix the functionality. signal.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse compress+norm+rope, emit bpreshuffle scale natively, keep kv_score in bf16
signal.text: ## Motivation On DeepSeek-V4 decode a good part of each attention layer goes to kernels that only move or re-lay-out data rather than compute anything. Three of them run on every layer of every step: 1. On CSA layers (`compress_ratio` 4) compress, norm and rope are three separate launches. Each is 4-8 us, which is small enough that dispatch rather than the work sets the cost. 2. The fp8 quant path writes its scale tensor in one layout and then a second kernel transposes it into the layout the bpreshuffle GEMM actually wants — 152 extra launches per decode step. 3. The compressor takes fp32, so the bf16 `wkv_gate` output is widened by a separate elementwise copy before it can be consumed — 92 extra launches per decode step. None of these carry information the surrounding kernels don't already have, so each can be folded into its neighbour without changing the math. ## Modifications Three independent optimisations, each behind its own env gate. **`SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE`** — new `fused_compress4_norm_rope.cuh` folds compress, norm and rope into a single kernel for CSA layers. The fused kernel maps one token per 64-lane wavefront rather than two; that takes it from 85 to 47 VGPRs and lifts occupancy from 5 to 8 waves/SIMD, which is what makes the fused kernel actually cheaper than the three it replaces instead of merely equal to them. **`SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE`** — the quant kernel writes the scale tensor directly in the physical layout bpreshuffle wants (column-major in M), so the separate transpose pass is not needed. **`SGLANG_OPT_KV_SCORE_BF16`** — `c4_v2.cuh` and `c128_v2.cuh` gain a `SrcFloat` template parameter, kept separate from the compute dtype so `score_bias` stays fp32. The compressor then widens the `wkv_gate` output as it loads it and the fp32 copy in front of compress is never materialised. `compress_forward()` only widens on the XPU path, and `compressor.py` calls `linear_kv_score` where it previously called `linear_bf16_fp32`. **On the defaults.** All three gates default to on. They are separable on purpose — each can be turned off on its own with `=0` if it regresses a shape I did not measure — but the numbers below are all with the three together, which is the configuration the defaults select. Happy to ship any or all of them off by default instead if maintainers would rather see soak time first. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, on the environment below. | Run | Gates | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---|---| | Baseline | all off | 94.7% | 0.000 | | Patched, pass 1 | all on | 94.5% | 0.000 | | Patched, pass 2 | all on | 94.8% | 0.001 | Baseline and patched are the same build on the same image, gates flipped by env var only. The patched arm was run twice because temperature 0 is not bit-deterministic here — batching order moves with arrival timing — so a single number cannot separate a real accuracy change from run-to-run noise. The two patched passes differ from each other by 0.3 points and bracket the baseline, which is the most that can be claimed: no accuracy change is visible above run-to-run noise at this sample size. ```bash MODEL= FUSE=1 NATIVE_SCALE=1 KVBF16=1 \ NUM_QUESTIONS=1319 NUM_SHOTS=5 MAX_NEW_TOKENS=512 PARALLEL=1200 \ bash bench/gsm8k_item4_517.sh # FUSE=0 NATIVE_SCALE=0 KVBF16=0 for baseline ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) | | ROCm | 7.2.0 | | Image | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260812` | | Model | DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 61 layers | | Shape | 8k in / 1k out, `--random-range-ratio 1.0` | Server: ```bash sglang serve --model-path "$MODEL" --port "$PORT" \ --tensor-parallel-size $TP $DP_ARGS \ --trust-remote-code --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend dsv4 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs "$CONC" --max-running-requests "$CONC" \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --page-size 256 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --context-length 16384 \ --chunked-prefill-size $((ISL * TP)) \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion --watchdog-timeout 1800 # DP_ARGS for the conc-64 shape: # --dp $TP --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --enable-two-batch-overlap ``` Client: ```bash python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang-oai \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --model "$MODEL" \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" --max-concurrency "$CONC" ``` ### Throughput Each shape is measured A B B A and the pairs averaged, so drift over the sweep cancels instead of being charged to whichever arm happened to run second. | Shape | Baseline (tok/s) | Patched (tok/s) | Gain | |---|---|---|---| | conc 4, TP4 | 174.23, 174.85 -> 174.54 | 180.96, 179.99 -> 180.48 | **+3.40%** | | conc 8, TP4 | 302.63, 302.48 -> 302.56 | 314.70, 314.41 -> 314.56 | **+3.97%** | | conc 64, TP8 + DP8 | 1600.37, 1593.98 -> 1597.17 | 1645.41, 1643.07 -> 1644.24 | **+2.95%** | Within-arm spread is 0.05-0.40% on baseline and 0.09-0.54% on patched, comfortably under the gap between arms, so the gain is not sweep-order drift. ### Profile Decode window, 8k1k conc 64 TP8 + DP8, per layer on rank TP-0: | Per layer | Baseline | Patched | |---|---|---| | CSA kernels | 55 | **48** | | HCA kernels | 43 | **40** | | Elementwise, CSA / HCA | 8x / 6x | **3x / 3x** | | bf16->fp32 copy, CSA / HCA | 2x / 1x | **0x / 0x** | The widening copy that fed compress is gone from both layer types, and the 48 / 40 counts hold on all seven ranks that captured a full decode window. The compress kernels take bf16 directly — the fourth template argument is the source dtype: - CSA `flash_c4_decode_norm_rope<512l, float, float, __hip_bfloat16, float, 0, false, true>` - HCA `flash_c128_decode<512l, float, float, __hip_bfloat16, float, false>` The three elementwise launches left per layer are two same-dtype `direct_copy` (bf16->bf16, fp32->fp32) and one bf16 residual add. None is a dtype conversion and none sits in front of compress. One caveat worth stating: CSA layer time drops 6.1% while HCA is flat at -0.07% even though HCA also loses three kernels. A single five-step profiler window carries a few us of per-layer drift, which is the same order as the effect being measured, so the throughput sweep above rather than this table is the measurement of record. ### Unit tests ```bash python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py \ test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c128_v2.py -q # 110 passed ``` `test_c4_v2.py` and `test_c128_v2.py` are parametrised over a new bf16 source dtype: 55 of the 110 are those new cases. The `SrcFloat` path had no coverage before, and the bf16 arm was confirmed to actually reach the new specialisation (the dispatcher was observed compiling with `dtype_src=torch.bfloat16`) rather than being quietly widened somewhere above the kernel. All four compress specialisations (c4/c128 x fp32/bf16 source) were also checked to compile. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) — no user-facing surface changed; the three gates are internal env switches. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32091469394](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091469394) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32091469243](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091469243)

signal.title: [AMD] Enable heterogeneous AITER FHMoE for DeepSeek V4
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4-Pro stores its 384 routed experts as MXFP4/E8M0, but keeps the single shared expert in native FP8 E4M3 with 128x128 E8M0 scales. Converting that shared expert to MXFP4 introduces avoidable quantization error. This PR integrates AITER's heterogeneous fused shared-expert MoE (FHMoE), so routed experts remain MXFP4 while expert 384 remains native FP8 and both execute in one two-stage MoE schedule. ### AITER dependency This PR requires an AITER build containing both merged changes: - [ROCm/aiter#4269](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4269), merge commit [`00cbe979f20cf380548d7d1d9d73136aa359c276`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/00cbe979f20cf380548d7d1d9d73136aa359c276): FHMoE runtime/AOT implementation. - [ROCm/aiter#4314](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4314), merge commit [`334fd72ad6e69d16785efc97cb8b6b4aec3c2a92`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/334fd72ad6e69d16785efc97cb8b6b4aec3c2a92): C1/C2/C32/C64 decode tuning. All results below were validated with AITER [`868ac1f7aa0d403a77c03e941bc5ffa28c7766d5`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/868ac1f7aa0d403a77c03e941bc5ffa28c7766d5). The ROCm image/deployment must provide this revision or a compatible newer build before enabling the feature. ## Modifications - Add an AITER capability probe and forward native shared weights/scales plus `shared_expert_id` through the MoE runner. - Preserve native FP8 shared-expert checkpoint tensors instead of requantizing them into the MXFP4 routed tensor. - TP-shard shared tensors during loading, retain them for hot reloads, and serialize asynchronous weight/scale pairing. - Expand serialized 128x128 E8M0 scales to AITER's per-1x32 layout, pad the TP8 intermediate shard from logical 384 to physical 512, and apply the required shuffle. - Route six normal experts first, then append semantic expert 384 with weight 1 to form internal `E=385`, `top-k=7` geometry. - Support non-power-of-two routed top-k in the shared-expert append Triton kernel. - Add strict enablement guards and preserve the separate shared-MLP fallback for unsupported configurations. - Add focused tests for policy/fallback, top-k append, TP sharding, FP8/E8M0 layout, uint8 scales, asynchronous loading, hot reload, and argument forwarding. - Add a reproducible validation record under `benchmark/fhmoe/VALIDATION.md`. Enable with: ```bash --enforce-shared-experts-fusion --moe-runner-backend aiter ``` The optimized path is restricted to ROCm `gfx950`, TP=8, EP/A2A/EPLB/offload disabled, BF16 SiLU, 384 routed experts, routed top-k=6, one shared expert, MXFP4 routed weights, and serialized 128x128 block-FP8 shared weights. Unsupported configurations log the reason and use the existing unfused path. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, TP=8, EP disabled, temperature 0, concurrency 64, 20-shot GSM8K, all 1,319 questions: | Mode | Strict exact match | Flexible extract | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Unfused shared MLP | 1254/1319 (95.072%) | 1255/1319 (95.148%) | 0 | | AITER FHMoE | 1262/1319 (95.679%) | 1262/1319 (95.679%) | 0 | FHMoE improved strict accuracy by 0.607 percentage point. All requests completed successfully, with no E8M0-scale, worker, ROCm, or graph-replay errors. Focused SGLang tests: ```bash python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_shared_expert_fusion.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_fhmoe.py ``` Result: `10 passed`. AITER validation included the default and exact DSV4 `test_fhmoe.py` profiles, BM16 scale-boundary coverage, DSV4 AOT precompile, C1/C2/C32/C64 kernel selection, MXFP4 sorting, and HIP graph capture/replay. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Hardware/model: 8x MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, plain TP8, no EP/A2A/TBO. Workload: fixed 8192 input / 1024 output, `conc*2` warmups and `conc*8` measured requests. | Concurrency | Unfused total tok/s | FHMoE total tok/s | Gain | Unfused / FHMoE median TPOT | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 1,218 | 1,233 | +1.25% | 14.28 / 14.09 ms | | 4 | 2,294 | 2,329 | +1.52% | 14.73 / 14.48 ms | | 8 | 4,062 | 4,228 | +4.08% | 16.21 / 15.48 ms | | 16 | 6,803 | 6,917 | +1.67% | 18.55 / 18.18 ms | | 32 | 10,321 | 10,546 | +2.17% | 23.07 / 22.46 ms | FHMoE improved TP8 throughput at every tested concurrency and selected the expected tuned kernels, including the BM16 C32 path. ### Known DP-attention limitation At TP8 + DP8 attention, 8k/1k C256, FHMoE completed 2,048/2,048 requests without errors but regressed total throughput: - Unfused: 32,903 total tok/s, median TPOT 52.29 ms. - FHMoE: 29,330 total tok/s, median TPOT 59.05 ms. - Delta: -10.86% throughput, +12.93% median TPOT. FHMoE is therefore not recommended for DP C256 without additional optimization. Full methodology and results are recorded in `benchmark/fhmoe/VALIDATION.md`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (`isort`, `ruff`, `black-jupyter`). - [x] Add focused unit and GPU tests. - [x] Add reproducible validation documentation. - [x] Provide full accuracy and serving-speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Fix] Skip padded state slots in the chunked GDN kernel
signal.text: _forward_metadata poisons padded request rows with state index -1, and the decode kernel already skips them (fused_recurrent: `if idx >= 0`). The chunked extend kernel had no such guard, so -1 reached `initial_state + index * stride_init_state` for both the initial-state load and the in-place final-state store, addressing before the state pool. boundary_check does not help: it validates against the declared block shape, not the allocation. Under breakable-CUDA-graph prefill with DP attention an idle DP rank replays an extend with an all-padded batch, so every row carries -1 and the kernel faults with cudaErrorIllegalAddress. Reproduced on Qwen3-Next-80B and Qwen3.5-397B on pristine main; a single request against --dp 4 is enough. No per-commit suite covers a linear-attn hybrid with DP attention, which is why this went unseen. Add a regression test in the existing base-b (1-GPU, per-commit) kernel suite; it fails without the guard. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. signal.title: [multimodal] Bound tokenizer-side GPU memory in Kimi GPU image preprocessing
signal.text: ## Motivation `_gpu_preprocess_images` (Kimi K2.5/K3) keeps every image's fp32 patch tensor alive in a list and ends with a request-wide `torch.cat`. Peak GPU memory therefore grows with the request's total patch data because the accumulated outputs coexist with the final concatenation. On deployments running a high `--mem-fraction-static`, a large multi-image request can OOM device 0. The CUDA caching allocator may retain the resulting high-water reservation for reuse, reducing headroom for later requests. ## Modifications - `_gpu_preprocess_images`: process size-groups in sub-batches capped by `SGLANG_MM_GPU_PREPROCESS_CHUNK_BYTES` (default 512 MB); return per-image tensors instead of a request-wide concat; optionally hand each image to a `per_image_sink` as it is produced. - `MMFeatureStreamSink` (K2.5/K3): hash each image and wrap it into the CUDA-IPC pool (or move it to host for non-IPC transports) at production time, so preprocessing no longer retains every image's GPU output at once. - `get_new_expanded_mm_items`: split list-shaped bundled features by element and preserve production-time hashes (`PRECOMPUTED_FEATURE_HASHES_KEY`) instead of re-hashing wrapped features. - Kimi-K3's deferred model-side GPU preprocessing path materializes the per-image list before its grouped feature validation and splitting. `mimo_v2` has the same accumulate-and-concat pattern and can be ported in a follow-up. ## Validation Outputs are bit-exact with the previous pipeline and hashes are unchanged (same bytes and algorithm), so radix-cache keys remain stable. `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_kimi_mm_preprocess_bounded.py` checks parity across size groups, chunking, and K3 RGBA compositing. On H100, `test_peak_memory_bounded` measures an unchunked peak of at least 2× the total patch bytes and a bounded-path peak of at most 4× the configured chunk size for the test workload. Kernels are unchanged; chunking only splits batched launches. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) (no user-facing interface beyond the environment variable). - [x] Provide accuracy and memory validation results. - [ ] Provide a speed benchmark (kernel math is unchanged; out of scope for this memory-bound change). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32091205228](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091205228)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32091204861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091204861)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(kernels): generalize persistent CuTe JIT cache
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang already has a persistent CuTe JIT cache for FlashAttention, but it lives under the FlashAttention package and only supports TVM-FFI exports. Kimi-K3 KDA also uses explicit `cute.compile` calls, but its cache is process-local. ## Modifications - Move the existing cache to `sglang.kernels.jit.cute_aot_cache`. - Generalize it over consumer source roots and CuTe ABI while keeping per-key file locking. - Include the explicit `CUTE_DSL_ARCH` target, or the detected local CUDA architecture, in the source fingerprint. GPU probing remains lazy when persistence is disabled. - Publish compiled objects through a temporary path and `os.replace`, so readers never observe a partially written final object and failed exports leave no temporary artifact. - If an object fails to load, discard it while the per-key shared lock still excludes writers, then fall back to compilation. - Keep routine cache activity at debug level so enabling persistence does not add normal INFO-level server noise. - Keep FlashAttention as the TVM-FFI consumer. A small cache adapter preserves `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_*` behavior and gives `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` precedence when both configurations are present. - Add `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` as the shared opt-in cache root and document that it must be trusted. - Make Kimi-K3 KDA MTP the second consumer using the native CuTe ABI. - Normalize CUDA device ordinals only for disk keys so same-architecture ranks can share objects; KDA includes compute capability and indexing width in its compile key. The default remains process-local. This does not introduce rank authority, compiler monkeypatching, or kernel math changes. ## Reviewability Git detects the existing cache module as a 51%-similarity rename. The aggregate patch is 394 additions and 86 deletions across six files; 184 added lines are focused tests. The large add/delete presentation from the previous revision was caused by rename detection falling below GitHub's threshold and has been removed. ## Validation ### Focused unit and static validation - Eleven focused cache cases cover new/legacy FlashAttention environment precedence, quiet routine logging, disabled behavior, lazy architecture detection, factory/source/architecture namespacing, CUDA device ordinal normalization, both native and TVM-FFI export/load paths, atomic publication, failed-export cleanup, and invalid-object eviction. - SGLang's registered-test collector resolves the pytest file to `base-a-test-cpu`. - Black, Ruff, isort (for applicable paths), codespell, Python syntax compilation, `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, and `git diff --check` pass. ### Real GPU cache validation Validated commit `e48384b39c` on one NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103) with Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NVIDIA CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, and TVM-FFI 0.1.11. This was cache/kernel validation only; no model was loaded. - **KDA native ABI:** `TestKimiK3ComputeKernels.test_mtp_replayssm_ring` cold-compiled and exported two objects. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded both objects, passed the same output and recurrent-state checks, and left object hashes unchanged. - **FlashAttention TVM-FFI ABI:** a BF16 `[1, 64, 4, 64]` causal forward cold-compiled and exported one object. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded it and produced the identical output SHA-256 (`780881b74eb262e7831f1f2a710c53a5ec209f52f371ec4fe51c6b43b2ff9678`). Against an FP32 reference, relative L2 was `0.001861` and max absolute error was `0.007716`. - **Corruption recovery:** the FlashAttention object was replaced with invalid bytes. The next process detected and removed it, recompiled with the same output SHA-256, and published a repaired object. A final fresh process with `cute.compile` blocked loaded the repaired object successfully. [Validation run](https://modal.com/apps/modal-flash/main/ap-3PyR14z34YcGgsm8zGdHgO) - No object hashes changed and no `.tmp.o` artifacts remained after validation. ## Speed tests and profiling No end-to-end speed benchmark is included. A warm process can load an existing FlashAttention or KDA object instead of compiling it again. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the project configuration. - [x] Add focused unit tests. - [x] Document the new environment variable and trust boundary. - [x] Validate native and TVM-FFI cold-to-warm round trips on a real GPU. - [x] Validate invalid-object eviction, recompilation, and repaired warm loading. - [x] Keep the cache move visible as a rename for review. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. - [ ] Provide an end-to-end speed benchmark (out of scope for cache validation). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32091161530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091161530)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32091161307](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091161307)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Add AITER HIP backend for packed GDN decode on gfx950
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently uses the Triton GDN kernel for Qwen3.5 decode on ROCm. For the fixed packed BF16 contract on MI355X, the new AITER HIP kernel reduces decode latency by about 13–23% while keeping the existing one-launch packed data flow. This PR wires that kernel into SGLang as an explicit decode backend. Unsupported contracts continue to use Triton. ## Modifications - Add `--linear-attn-decode-backend hip` and `LinearAttnKernelBackend.HIP`; keep `hip` out of the shared/default and prefill backend choices, and reject it for non-GDN models during initialization. - Add `HipGDNKernel`, which calls AITER directly for the exact packed BF16 gfx950 contract. - Gate the AITER path with `is_gfx95_supported()` and fall back to Triton decode on other ROCm architectures. - Keep ReplaySSM and unsupported shapes, dtypes, strides, scales, or layouts on `TritonGDNKernel`. - Keep prefill/extend and verify paths on Triton. - Add unit tests for exact-contract dispatch, architecture and contract fallback, CLI scope, non-GDN rejection, ReplaySSM fallback, and prefill/verify dispatch. No QKV split/copy, state conversion, temporary tensor, or additional kernel launch is added to the supported decode path. The default backend is unchanged unless `hip` is selected. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, temperature 0, max new tokens 2048; Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X. Both servers used Triton prefill and BF16 Mamba state. | Backend | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Triton | 92.6459% | 1222/1319 | 8/1319 | | AITER HIP | 92.3427% | 1218/1319 | 6/1319 | This single deterministic pair differs by four correct answers (`-0.3033` percentage points). It is reported as a draft result rather than an accuracy-parity claim; prediction-level diffing and/or repeated evaluation is required before marking the PR ready. Normalized output throughput was `+0.819%`; total latency is not compared because the two runs generated different token counts. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Kernel (exact AITER PR commit) AITER `test_common.perftest`: two warmup iterations followed by 101 profiled decode calls, with default input rotation and device-time averaging. The table reports the median of five fresh-process `avg us/iter` results. | BS | Triton BF16 | AITER HIP | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 32 | 18.174 us | **13.965 us** | **23.16%** | | 64 | 31.746 us | **24.764 us** | **21.99%** | | 128 | 56.940 us | **49.603 us** | **12.89%** | ### End-to-end Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X; random ISL/OSL 8192/1024, range ratio 0.8, request rate `inf`, prompts = concurrency x 10. Each point used a fresh server and an identical full-workload warmup. Only the decode backend changed; prefill remained Triton. | Concurrency | Triton output tok/s | AITER HIP output tok/s | Throughput | Median TPOT (Triton -> HIP) | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 362.097 | 367.788 | **+1.572%** | 10.334 -> 10.181 ms | | 8 | 589.844 | 609.401 | **+3.316%** | 12.785 -> 12.541 ms | | 16 | 858.537 | 873.679 | **+1.764%** | 17.984 -> 17.663 ms | | 32 | 1140.530 | 1166.321 | **+2.261%** | 27.119 -> 26.482 ms | | 64 | 1461.569 | 1486.747 | **+1.723%** | 43.125 -> 42.335 ms | | 128 | 1823.527 | 1859.667 | **+1.982%** | 69.714 -> 68.288 ms | Across the six points, the non-weighted mean improvement was `+2.103%` output throughput and `+1.901%` median TPOT. Median TTFT, TPOT, ITL, and E2E latency improved at every point. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32091006451](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091006451)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32091006242](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091006242)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU]fix(dspark): preserve parity in folded NPU paths
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. --> This PR fixes numerical and graph-replay parity issues in DSpark's folded NPU paths, then optimizes the enabled paths so they preserve acceptance quality while outperforming the previous all-disabled fallback. ## Modifications - Replace folded sampling based on `softmax(logits / temperature) / Exp(1)` with the equivalent log-space exponential race: - stochastic: `argmax(logits - temperature * log(Exp(1)))` - greedy: direct `argmax(logits)` - Stage exponential noise immediately before graph replay only for stochastic requests. All-greedy requests avoid full-vocabulary RNG and corrected-logit stores. - Keep the dense Vanilla Markov W2 projection aligned with the target LM-head TP vocabulary shard: - compute only the local vocabulary slice; - reduce each local slice to one `(value, token_id)` candidate; - all-gather only the small candidate tensor and select the global top-1 with an NPU Triton kernel; - preserve the eager full-logit path for stochastic sampling. - Add contiguous KDA conv-snapshot and strided temporal-state commit kernels for Ascend, with the existing generic kernels retained as layout fallbacks. - Reshape flattened K tensors to `[tokens, heads, head_dim]` before the Ascend RoPE kernel and apply the same 3-D contract to stacked context KV. - Add NPU and NPUGraph regression tests for proposal parity, near ties, stochastic replay, TP-sharded top-1, production-size vocabulary reductions, and production KDA state layouts. The proposal changes are gated by `is_npu()` and the new state kernels live in the Ascend backend, so GPU execution paths are unchanged. ## Correctness | Check | Result | |---|---:| | Folded proposal vs. eager proposal with actual weights | Draft tokens exactly identical | | Corrected logits maximum absolute error | `0` | | Greedy near-tie case | Matches direct-logit `argmax` | | Mixed sampling with identical exponential noise | Token-by-token identical | | Stacked context K maximum absolute error | `<= 4.88e-4` | | Stacked context V maximum absolute error | `<= 2.44e-4` | | KDA conv/temporal state commits, ordinary + NPUGraph | Bitwise exact | The near-tie regression came from converting logits to softmax probabilities before greedy selection: distinct logits can round to equal probabilities and change tie-breaking. Direct-logit argmax preserves their ordering. ## Performance Tested on four Ascend nodes with Kimi K3 W4A8, TP64/DP4, exact 8,000 input / 1,000 output tokens, one request, four warm-up requests, and seeds 42-46. ### Group A reference: parent code, all four paths disabled ```text SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_STACKED_CTX_KV=0 SGLANG_DSPARK_EMBED_IN_GRAPH=0 ``` | Metric | Five-run mean | |---|---:| | TTFT | `7609.13 ms` | | TPoT | `15.6189 ms` | | ITL | `15.6189 ms` | | Acceptance length | `~7.392` | ### Final code: optimized paths enabled (`1111`) ```text SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=1 SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=1 # AUTO selects greedy folded sampling; stochastic requests stay eager SGLANG_DSPARK_STACKED_CTX_KV=1 SGLANG_DSPARK_EMBED_IN_GRAPH=1 ``` | Seed | TTFT (ms) | TPoT (ms) | Acceptance length | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 42 | 7731.116 | 15.806716 | 7.1667 | | 43 | 7767.762 | 14.556558 | 7.4667 | | 44 | 7758.790 | 15.001659 | 7.3667 | | 45 | 7789.845 | 15.106276 | 7.3500 | | 46 | 7533.141 | 14.453775 | 7.6633 | | **Mean** | **7716.131** | **14.984997** | **7.4027** | Compared with Group A, mean TPoT improves by `0.6339 ms/token` (`4.1%`) while mean acceptance length remains above 7.4 and mean TTFT remains below 7.8 seconds. ### State-commit microbenchmarks | NPU Event mean | Generic | Optimized | |---|---:|---:| | Conv snapshot, ordinary | 3.0991 ms | 0.0903 ms | | Conv snapshot, NPUGraph replay | 3.1370 ms | 0.0451 ms | | Temporal snapshot, ordinary | 0.6749 ms | 0.1334 ms | | Temporal snapshot, NPUGraph replay | 0.6800 ms | 0.0760 ms | ## Accuracy | Benchmark | Result | Notes | |---|---:|---| | GSM8K-200 | `96.5%` | Initial parity implementation; invalid `0.5%` | | GSM8K-1319 | `94.5%` | Final code; invalid `0.1%`; 1319/1319 complete; no request errors | | GPQA-Diamond | `92.42%` (`183/198`) | Final code; 198 predictions and reviews; no request errors | GPQA uses `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, and `reasoning_effort=max`. The final score is within the existing same-model run range observed on this machine (`91.41%` to `94.44%`). ## Validation - Full pre-commit suite: passed. - Python compileall: passed. - Final NPU/NPUGraph gate: `10 passed`. - Five random 8k/1k runs: 5/5 completed, exactly 1,000 output tokens, no errors. - GSM8K-1319 and GPQA-Diamond: complete, with no API, HTTP, or connection errors. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add NPU and NPUGraph unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (not required; no public API change). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with comments or contact authorized users to do so. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32091023196](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091023196)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32091022802](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091022802)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat: Add DeepSeek V4 SWA recompute
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 keeps a FULL cache containing compressed C4/C128 and indexer state, plus a sliding-window attention (SWA) cache backed by a smaller KV pool. When this pool evicts the trailing SWA pages while the FULL prefix survives, the prefix cannot be reused directly and may fall back to cold prefill. This PR retains the FULL hit and recomputes only the bounded trailing dependency window needed to rebuild SWA. The feature is disabled by default and enabled with `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_RECOMPUTE_WINDOW=1`. ## Changes ### Cache matching and scheduling - Compute a page-aligned recompute window from the sliding window `W`, number of layers `N`, and KV page size: `W_r = align_up(align_up(W, page_size) + (N - 1) * W, page_size)`. - Trigger recompute only when the trailing SWA data is missing from both GPU and host and the matched FULL prefix reaches a configurable threshold (`2 * W_r` by default). Otherwise, use normal cache matching or HiCache load-back. - Report the recompute length as `extra_compute_prefix_len` so the scheduler includes it in prefill admission, chunking, and SWA KV capacity checks. - Keep the matched prefix under a FULL-only lock and rebuild SWA in temporary private pages, leaving the global mapping unchanged during the forward. On success, publish and lock only the final SWA tail and free the remaining workspace. On abort, discard all private pages. ### DeepSeek V4 execution - Replay the selected trailing prefix together with new input tokens while preserving the original logical prefix boundary in DeepSeek V4 metadata. - Pass that boundary to Compressor V2 so replayed prefix positions skip duplicate FULL-side compression work while still producing the SWA state needed for recompute. - Route SWA reads and writes for replayed tokens through private pages in both prefill planner stages and in dense/sparse attention. Positions outside the replayed range keep the normal FULL-to-SWA mapping. ### HiCache - Allow eligible Mooncake L3 hits to omit trailing SWA pages. Fall back to cold prefill if the loaded state is insufficient for recompute. ### Current limitations and guards - The supported path is hybrid-SWA DeepSeek V4 on CUDA with `UnifiedRadixCache` and Compressor V2. - HIP, NPU, XPU, speculative decoding, online compression, decode context parallelism, and `unified_kv_triton` are rejected. - HiCache L3 supports Mooncake only. - Recompute requests do not support input embeddings, positional embedding overrides, or prompt/input logprobs. Output logprobs remain supported. - Prefill CUDA graphs and two-batch overlap are disabled for batches that contain recompute work. - `--chunked-prefill-size` must be at least `W_r + page_size`. ## Validation Registered tests cover window sizing, cache matching and fallback, private-page commit/abort, scheduler accounting, DeepSeek V4 prefill paths, Mooncake dispatch, and configuration guards. ## Performance Tested on `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8` using NVIDIA H200 GPUs. To isolate prefill cost, the benchmark uses fake-prefill transfer while keeping cache insertion enabled. SWA capacity is constrained with `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.005`. The test sends a 128K-token request with `seed=42`, uses `seed=43` to evict its SWA tail, and then repeats `seed=42`. <details> <summary>Benchmark command and cache sizes</summary> ```bash python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ --backend sglang \ --model sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 \ --num-prompts 1 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 128000 \ --random-output-len 1 \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --warmup-requests 0 \ --seed 42 ``` ```text DSV4 pool sizes: full=7065856, swa=35328, c4=1766464, c128=55202, c4_state=2208, c128_state=0 ``` </details> | Configuration | Request | Input throughput (tok/s) | TTFT (ms) | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | Recompute disabled | Cold | 44,622 | 2,856 | | Recompute disabled | Post-eviction | 45,140 | 2,824 | | Recompute enabled | Cold | 44,864 | 2,843 | | Recompute enabled | Post-eviction | 212,741 | 589 | Without recompute, the repeated request remains at cold-prefill performance. With recompute, it reuses 122,112 FULL tokens and prefills only `W_r + page_size = 5,888` tokens. Compared with the feature-disabled post-eviction request, throughput improves by `4.71x`, TTFT improves by `4.79x`, and physical prefill work drops by `95.4%`. ### Recompute length gate For `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8`, the physical recompute range is 5,888 tokens. Measurements around this size show that, for short prefixes, the saved prefill work does not outweigh the recompute overhead: | Input tokens | Cached FULL tokens | Cold TTFT (ms) | Recompute TTFT (ms) | TTFT change | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 6,144 (~1x) | 256 | 232 | 334 | 44.0% slower | | 8,960 (~1.5x) | 3,072 | 224 | 230 | 2.7% slower | | 11,776 (2x) | 5,888 | 280 | 243 | 13.2% faster | | 17,664 (3x) | 11,776 | 538 | 251 | 53.3% faster | The crossover is between approximately `1.5x` and `2x`, which motivates `2.0` as the default for `SGLANG_SWA_RECOMPUTE_GATE_MULTIPLIER`. The value remains configurable because the crossover depends on hardware, batch shape, and serving load. ### Accuracy #### Default-path regression check With recompute disabled, gsm8k was run on `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8` using NVIDIA H200 GPUs. ``` python3 gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1209 --parallel 32 --platinum Accuracy: 0.978 ``` #### BFCL multi-turn long-context Prompt/input logits are not exposed for internally recomputed tokens, so an exact logit comparison is unavailable. We use BFCL `multi_turn_long_context` as an end-to-end proxy because tool results repeatedly extend the same conversation prefix and produce frequent cache hits. SWA eviction depends on cache pressure and request timing, so a normal benchmark run cannot guarantee enough recompute events. We therefore collected 50 baseline measurements and 50 with `SGLANG_DEBUG_FORCE_SWA_RECOMPUTE=1`, which forces eligible cache hits through recompute: | Mode | Runs | Mean | Std | 95% bootstrap CI of mean | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline | 50 | 49.81 | 2.32 | [49.17, 50.45] | | Force recompute | 50 | 50.36 | 2.33 | [49.73, 51.01] | The mean difference is `+0.55` BFCL points, with a 95% bootstrap CI of `[-0.36, +1.45]`. Welch's t-test finds no statistically detectable difference (`p = 0.24`). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #29687292774](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29687292774)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #29687292668](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29687292668)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CPU] Support FP32 MoE Router Weights on AMX
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Some MoE models use FP32 router weights while receiving BF16 hidden states. On CPU AMX, this combination exposed two issues: The router logits could remain BF16, causing a dtype mismatch with the expected CUDA behavior of BF16 activations x FP32 router weights -> FP32 logits. FP32 router weights are not supported by the packed AMX weight path, so PackWeightMethod disables the AMX backend and the router falls back to an incompatible or inefficient path. This affects models and configurations using FP32 router weights, including LongCat, MiniMax-M2/M3, Hunyuan-V3, Grok, Ernie4.5-MoE-VL, Bailing/LLaDA2/Sarvam, and GLM4-MoE. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> * Ensure the CPU AMX MoE router path computes logits using FP32 inputs and FP32 router weights, preserving the expected FP32 logits behavior. * Keep FP32 router weights out of the unsupported packed AMX weight path and use the native FP32 linear implementation instead. * Add CPU-side conversion of router logits to FP32 before invoking the grouped top-k and biased grouped top-k AOT kernels. * Add explicit dtype validation in the CPU AOT top-k kernels so they require FP32 router logits and fail clearly for unsupported input dtypes. * Update the existing CPU top-k tests to cover: * Mixed BF16 hidden states and FP32 router logits. * Correctness and output dtypes for grouped top-k and biased grouped top-k. * Rejection of BF16 logits passed directly to the low-level CPU AOT operators. * Add a regression test verifying that the CPU AMX router path returns FP32 logits for both BF16 and FP32 router weights and does not invoke the unsupported packed AMX linear backend. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32090915330](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090915330)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32090915133](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090915133)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [HiCache][UnifiedTree] L3 SWA periodic checkpoint
signal.text: ## Motivation The current implementation stores a SWA cache for each page in the L3. This leads to high memory consumption in L3. The cache of 1kk tokens takes up ~18 GB in the L3 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash. At the same time, the compressed attention cache for a million tokens should occupy ~3.6 GB according to the [calculator](https://kvcache.ai/tools/kv-cache-calculator/). ## Modifications The DeepSeek-V4-Flash technical report suggests different strategies for saving the SWA cache to the L3 cache. This PR suggests adding the functionality of a periodic SWA checkpoint. It is important that, for simplicity, the first version does not recalculate only the SWA for the tail without a checkpoint. This PR essentially offers just a mechanism for hitting the cache with swa-checkpoint-interval size alignment. We also plan to add a mechanism for recalculating only SWA in the future PR. With this feature, the user gets the opportunity to balance between memory consumption in the L3 cache and TTFT with cache hits. It is also important to note that after adding the feature of recalculating only the SWA part, the gap in TTFT will decrease. * DeepSeek-V4-Flash * Hopper * CP4 * MoonCake Store * 1KK input | | L3 memory consumption | TTFT on hit (avg@5) | |---------------------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------| | Offload SWA every 256 tok. (default in main) | 18.25GB | 3039 ms | | Offload SWA every 2k tok. | 5.74GB (-68%) | 3536 ms (+16%) | | Offload SWA every 16k tok. | 4.03GB (-78%) | 4660 ms (+53%) | <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DCP] Drop the prefill index-selection syncs by taking each rank's rows by stride
signal.text: ## Motivation `prepare_decode_context_parallel_metadata` selects this rank's prefix KV rows with a boolean mask: ```python dcp_local_prefix_kv_indices = ( dcp_prefix_kv_indices[dcp_prefix_kv_indices % dcp_size == dcp_rank] // dcp_size ) ``` `dcp_prefix_kv_indices` is a CUDA tensor filled by a Triton kernel. The mask's output length depends on the data, so this lowers to `nonzero()`, which copies the surviving count back to the host — a device sync on every prefill forward, on the scheduler thread. ## Modifications Under DCP the allocator's page is widened by `dcp_size` (`kv_cache_builder.py`: *"When dcp enabled, kv_pool_allocator.page_size is page_size * dcp_size"*) and the radix tree pages at the same size. Every prefix length is therefore a multiple of `dcp_size`, each request's slice starts on a `dcp_size` boundary of the concatenated buffer, and a slot's residue tracks its token position. This rank's rows are then a plain stride: ```python dcp_local_prefix_kv_indices = ( dcp_prefix_kv_indices[parallel.dcp_rank :: parallel.dcp_size] // parallel.dcp_size ) ``` Same rows, length known from the slicing alone, so no `nonzero()` and no readback. It is also a strided view rather than a gather, so it is cheaper than the mask it replaces rather than trading the sync for other work. ## Accuracy Tests Checked against the masked select **on live indices**, by temporarily asserting equality inside `prepare_decode_context_parallel_metadata` and serving a DCP8 + TP8 DeepSeek-V3.1 workload on 8×H200 (chunked prefill, `--cache-hit-rate 0.9`, 16k input). Eight calls compared **1,843 real prefix rows** each, one per rank; **zero mismatches**, so the stride selected byte-identical rows to the mask on production data. A profile of the same configuration shows the `aten::nonzero` in that function going 1 → 0. Separately, the equivalence was checked offline across `dcp_size` 2/4/8 and every rank on generated slot indices: it holds exactly when prefix lengths are `dcp_size`-aligned, and diverges when they are not — which is why the guarantee above matters and is called out in the comment. ## Profile Before After ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests. - [x] Provide accuracy results. - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials if this PR changes the behavior of the code. - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32082580919](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32082580919) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32082580564](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32082580564)

signal.title: [NIXL] Fix O_DIRECT alignment and batch chunking for DSA indexer pool
signal.text: ## Summary The NIXL HiCache backend (`hicache_nixl.py`) has two bugs that cause silent data loss when used with DSA (Deepseek Sparse Attention) models such as GLM-5.2. The DSA indexer pool has a page size that is not a 4096 multiple, which triggers both bugs. This PR fixes O_DIRECT alignment failures and silent batch-size truncation. ## Background: DSA indexer pool GLM-5.2 uses DSA with a dual-buffer KV cache: - `kv_buffer` — MLA latent (fp8, per-layer) - `index_k_with_scale_buffer` — DSA indexer (uint8, per-layer) The indexer pool's page size is not a 4096 multiple. This is the root cause of both bugs below. ## Bug 1: O_DIRECT alignment failure (EINVAL) ### Root cause `_alloc_registered` allocates a bounce buffer of shape `(STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE, page_numel)`. Each slot's byte stride is `page_numel * elem_size`, which for the DSA indexer pool is **not** a 4096 multiple. O_DIRECT requires every I/O buffer address to be page-aligned. Slot 0 is aligned (the mmap base is page-aligned), but slots 1+ land at misaligned addresses, and every `aio_write` past the first slot fails with `EINVAL`. ### Fix Round the slot byte size up to an OS-page multiple: ```python page_bytes = page_numel * elem_size aligned_page_bytes = ((page_bytes + 4095) // 4096) * 4096 slot_numel = aligned_page_bytes // elem_size buf = alloc_mmap((STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE, slot_numel), dtype) ``` The bounce buffer is now `(STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE, slot_numel)` where `slot_numel >= page_numel`. All slot addresses are page-aligned. ### Follow-on fixes Because slots are now padded, every copy into / out of the bounce buffer must use only the first `page_numel` elements of each slot: - `_prepare_bounce_data`: `bounce[i].copy_(src)` → `bounce[i, :page_numel].copy_(src)` - `_batch_set` (non-zero-copy path): same fix - `_batch_get` (non-zero-copy path): `self._bounce_get[i]` → `self._bounce_get[i, :page_numel]` - `_get_v2` (non-zero-copy path): same fix ### Slot buffer descriptors `_get_bounce_slot_buffers` and `_bounce_slot_buffers` computed slot addresses as `base + i * page_bytes`. With padded slots, the actual stride is `slot_numel * elem_size`, not `page_bytes`. Both now use `buf.shape[1] * buf.element_size()` as the stride. ## Bug 2: Silent batch-size truncation ### Root cause The bounce buffer holds exactly `STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE` slots. Hybrid pools (e.g. the DSA indexer) routinely deliver 200+ pages per backup op. `batch_set_v2` / `batch_get_v2` passed the full transfer to NIXL, which only processes the first `STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE` pages and silently drops the rest. The indexer cache data for large requests was lost without any error. ### Fix Added `_chunked_v2_transfer`, which splits a `> STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE` transfer into sub-batches of `STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE` and runs each through the existing `batch_set_v2` / `batch_get_v2`. The `host_indices` tensor is sliced to match each chunk's page range. `_set_v2_chunked` and `_get_v2_chunked` are thin wrappers that pass the appropriate batch function. The two methods share the same chunking logic via `_chunked_v2_transfer` (DRY). `batch_set_v2` and `batch_get_v2` now check `len(keys) > STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE` up front and delegate to the chunked path. ## Bug 3: NIXL backend not on v2 path ### Root cause `HiCacheController._register_draft_pool` only routed `mooncake` to the multi-pool zero-copy v2 path. `nixl` was listed in the TODO unsupported list, even though `HiCacheNixl` implements `register_mem_host_pool_v2` / `batch_set_v2` / `batch_get_v2`. ### Fix - `if backend == "mooncake":` → `if backend in {"mooncake", "nixl"}:` - Removed `"nixl"` from the TODO unsupported list - Updated the `should_split_heads` warning to use `%s` formatting with `backend` ## Code quality fixes - `getattr(host_pool, "page_size", 1) or 1` → `host_pool.page_size` — `page_size` is a required `int` parameter in `HostKVCache.__init__`, always present. The `getattr` with default `1` violates the repo's `no-getattr-defensive` rule and masks a real `AttributeError` if the field is ever renamed. When `ctx` may be `None` (pool not in `_hybrid_pool_ctx`), the `None` check is on `ctx`, not on `page_size`. ## Testing - [x] Code compiles, no import errors - [ ] Regression: DSA indexer pool O_DIRECT writes succeed (no EINVAL) - [ ] Regression: > STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE transfers are chunked (no silent data loss) - [ ] Regression: same-prefix KV cache hit (L2 retrieve via NIXL) Testing will be conducted on 8×MI308X (gfx942) with GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8, NIXL backend. ## Related - LMCache DSA support: `sgl-project/sglang` PR #35230 - These bugs were discovered while testing DSA indexer support on the NIXL HiCache backend <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32090542626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090542626)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32090542436](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090542436)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [LMCache] Support MLA/DSA dual-buffer KV cache in LMCache connector
signal.text: ## Summary The LMCache connector (`LMCRadixCache`) hardcoded access to `k_buffer` / `v_buffer`, which only exists on MHA-style KV pools. MLA and DSA models use a fused `kv_buffer` instead, so LMCache could not be initialized for these architectures. This PR adds automatic KV buffer detection and DSA indexer support. ## Changes ### 1. KV buffer detection (MLA/DSA vs MHA) `__init__` now inspects the KV pool type and builds a flat `kv_caches` list: - **MLA / DSA** (`kv_buffer` present): fused single-buffer per layer, `use_mla=True`, `kv_cache_dim` inferred from the buffer shape. - **DSA indexer** (`index_k_with_scale_buffer` present): the indexer buffers are appended to `kv_caches` so both DSA layer groups are registered with LMCache. This mirrors the FlexKV connector pattern (`flexkv_connector.py:141-153`). - **MHA** (`k_buffer` / `v_buffer`): separate K and V buffers concatenated layer-first, `use_mla=False`. - **Unsupported types**: raises `AttributeError` with a clear message instead of a cryptic `AttributeError` deep in the connector. The old `k_pool` / `v_pool` connector kwargs are replaced by `kv_caches`, `use_mla`, `kv_cache_dim` — matching the `LMCacheMPConnector` / `LMCacheConnector` / `LMCacheLayerwiseConnector` signatures. ### 2. MP-mode `extra_config` resolution The MP connector now resolves `mq_timeout` and `heartbeat_interval` from `extra_config` (keys prefixed `lmcache.mp.`), mirroring the vLLM adapter (`vllm_multi_process_adapter.py`). Falls back to defaults (300 s / 10 s) when `extra_config` is absent — a no-op for existing configs that never set it. ### 3. MLA/DSA MP-mode requirement documented Added a NOTE explaining why MLA/DSA models must use MP mode: the layerwise (IP) path iterates per-layer with a single uniform shape and has no awareness of layer groups, making it incompatible with MLA's fused single-buffer layout and DSA's dual-buffer layout. ### 4. `cache_finished_req` hardening - Replaced `assert new_last_node is not None` with `raise ValueError(...)` including `req.rid` and context — a `None` device node after insert indicates an inconsistent radix tree state, which should fail loudly rather than silently. - Expanded the docstring to accurately describe the method's contract. ## Background: GLM-5.2 DSA KV layout GLM-5.2 uses Deepseek Sparse Attention (DSA) with a dual-buffer KV cache: - `kv_buffer` — MLA latent (fp8, per-layer) - `index_k_with_scale_buffer` — DSA indexer (uint8, per-layer) There are 39 layers per group and 2 groups = 78 layer tensors per group, 156 total. Both layer groups must be registered with LMCache for store/retrieve to work correctly. ## Testing - [x] Code compiles, no `TypeError` / `AttributeError` on import - [ ] Regression: short-sequence request completes without crash - [ ] Regression: long-sequence DSA dual-buffer store - [ ] Regression: same-prefix KV cache hit (L2 retrieve) - [ ] Performance: MP-mode TTFT/TPOT and L2 hit rate Testing will be conducted on 8×MI308X (gfx942) with GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8. ## Related - LMCache DSA indexer support: `LMCache` PR `feat/dsa-sglang-support-v2` (EngineKVFormat `NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS = 14`) - FlexKV connector already uses the same buffer detection pattern (`flexkv_connector.py:141-153`) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32090492632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090492632)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32090492257](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090492257)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation There has been extensive discussion around making HiCache work better for small host-memory setups: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28614, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20535, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16909, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14056. signal.title: [Bug] Anthropic /v1/messages drops PD bootstrap fields during AnthropicMessagesRequest → ChatCompletionRequest conversion
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug In PD disaggregation mode, external routers attach PD coordination metadata (`bootstrap_host`, `bootstrap_port`, `bootstrap_room`) to inference request bodies. The OpenAI path (`/v1/chat/completions`) accepts these fields via `ChatCompletionRequest` and PD works as expected. The Anthropic path (`/v1/messages`) does not preserve this metadata. Requests are parsed as `AnthropicMessagesRequest` (which has no PD routing fields), then converted to `ChatCompletionRequest` in `AnthropicServing._convert_to_chat_completion_request()` using only Anthropic-native fields. As a result, `bootstrap_room` (and related PD fields) are dropped before the request enters the existing PD disaggregation flow. On the decode worker, this surfaces as: `Invalid request: Disaggregated request received without bootstrap room id` The same request body with the same bootstrap fields succeeds on `/v1/chat/completions`. Note: `/v1/messages/count_tokens` is unaffected because it only tokenizes locally and does not enter the PD generation/KV-transfer path. This appears related to the fix proposed in #33076. ### Reproduction # Prefill python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /path/to/model \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ signal.title: [SM12x] Drop the 64-head TP pad on the DSv4 MLA prefill path
signal.text: ## Problem With `attn_tp_size=2`, `MQALayer` builds a **64-row** query tensor, writes only `[0:n_local_heads]` (= 32), runs attention on all 64 rows, and discards half the output via `o = o[:, tp_slice, :]`. ```python # FlashMLA's fp8 sparse decode kernel only specializes h_q for {64, 128}. padded_num_heads = 64 if self.n_local_heads <= 64 else self.n_heads ``` That comment is true of `sgl_kernel.flash_mla` — the `else` branch at `deepseek_v4_backend.py:1774`, which SM12x never takes. On SM12x the kernel is FlashInfer's, and the decode/prefill split happens **by row count** inside the FlashInfer entry (`B <= _DECODE_MAX_TOKENS`, `flash_mla_sm120.py:558`), **not by forward mode**. So a wide prefill chunk is dispatched to the paged/prefill kernel, which takes arbitrary `h_q`, and the pad buys it nothing. MLA is the one place where this is pure waste rather than a wash: 64 query heads share a **single** latent KV (`num_key_value_heads = 1`), so head-sharding saves compute without saving KV bandwidth. Prefill (many query rows, compute-bound) scales with head count; decode (few rows, KV-bandwidth-bound) does not. ## Fix Gate the pad off for wide prefill chunks only, behind `SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_UNPAD_PREFILL_MLA_HEADS` (default on, SM12x only). - **row term — this is the one that selects the kernel.** Strictly above `_DECODE_MAX_TOKENS`, read from FlashInfer rather than hardcoded, so the gate and the dispatch fork at `flash_mla_sm120.py:558` are provably the same number. If FlashInfer ever raised that cutoff, a hardcoded 64 here would unpad rows that still route to the decode kernel — a silent kernel-family swap, not a crash. That is what the import buys. - **mode terms — scope, not legality.** `is_extend_or_draft_extend_or_mixed()` (an allowlist, *not* `is_extend()`, which is also `True` for `TARGET_VERIFY`), plus `_original_forward_mode` because DP padding can rewrite a verify batch into `EXTEND`. To be explicit about what these do and do not do: FlashInfer's SM120 decode kernel is instantiated for `num_heads ∈ {8,16,32,64,128}` as well (`_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH`), so unpadding is *legal* on both sides of the row fork. The mode terms exist to keep `TARGET_VERIFY` and large-`bs` `DECODE` — both CUDA-graph-captured — on exactly the kernel instantiation they run today. I would rather change one path at a time here than two. - Because the gate reads `forward_mode`, which is not part of a captured graph's shape key, it bails under `is_in_breakable_cuda_graph()`. That is a consequence of the mode terms, not an independent requirement; a row-count-only gate would not need it (and would also work under `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill=breakable`, where this PR is a no-op). Supporting changes: - `sm120_flashmla_decode_max_tokens()` exposes the threshold instead of duplicating the constant. On an import failure it returns a value no batch can exceed, so the gate fails **closed** (everything keeps the pad). It returns `0` when the backend is not FlashInfer — there the triton and torch fallbacks read `h_q` off the query shape, so there is no floor to respect and the gate is free to fire. - `_local_attn_sink()` takes an optional `num_heads`. The narrowed sink is a **prefix view** of the cached padded tensor, not a second allocation, so a device pointer baked into a captured decode graph stays valid; and when `num_heads` is `None` or already equals the stored width, the *same object* is returned. `DSparkAttention` (`deepseek_v4_dspark.py:246`) calls it with no argument and is unchanged — the DSPARK draft block stays padded. ## Measurements 2× DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP=2 across two nodes. - **MLA prefill lane: −49.7%** - Kernel instantiation goes from `sparse_mla_prefill_mg_dual_kernel<(ModelType)1, (ComputeMode)1, 64, ...>` to `<..., 32, ...>`, verified from an in-server profile rather than inferred from the launch flags. That profile is also the evidence that the gate actually fired. - That matches the geometry the reference vLLM deployment of this model runs on the same box (`<..., 32, 128, ...>`, grid `[4072,1,1]` vs ours `[4096,1,1]`, block `[384,1,1]`). Decode, `TARGET_VERIFY`, and the DSPARK draft block are untouched and stay padded. ## Correctness — what is and is not established - GSM8K 500 questions: 0.944 → 0.948, `Invalid: 0.000`. **This is the wrong instrument and I am not claiming it as evidence of equivalence.** Attention is per-`(token, head)` independent and the dropped heads were fed `new_empty` garbage and then sliced away, so the surviving heads *should* be bit-identical and the score *should* have been unchanged. A 2-in-500 delta means either the two runs differed in more than this flag, or the `NUM_HEADS=32` and `NUM_HEADS=64` template instantiations are not bit-identical on the heads that survive. **A gate-ON/gate-OFF greedy text-exact comparison is owed and I will post it.** - Shape safety on the path this PR changes is enforced by FlashInfer, loudly: `TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(attn_sink.size(0), num_heads)` and a compiled `switch (num_heads)` whose `default:` returns false into `TVM_FFI_ICHECK`. Nothing on the prefill path fails silently. ## Known gaps - **No head-count legality guard.** The FlashInfer prefill dispatch is a closed `switch (num_heads) {8,16,32,64,128}`; and on the pinned `flashinfer==0.6.17` there is **no `case 8:`** (it was added after the tag). So at `attn_tp_size = 8` (`n_local_heads = 8`) the unpadded path would abort where the padded path worked. `attn_tp_size ≥ 16` is already non-functional for this model for an unrelated reason (`o_groups = 8` ⇒ `n_local_groups = 0`). A `n_local_heads in (16, 32, 64, 128)` term in the gate would close this; I have not added it yet and would like a view on whether the allowlist or a capability probe is preferred. - No test. The gate is a pure predicate over `(rows, forward_mode, _original_forward_mode, env, graph flag)` and is testable on CPU with `_is_sm120` and the threshold monkeypatched; happy to add it. - The pre-existing comment at `deepseek_v4.py:1362` attributes the `{64,128}` restriction to "FlashMLA's fp8 sparse decode kernel" without saying which kernel. It is correct for `sgl_kernel.flash_mla` and stale for the FlashInfer kernel SM12x calls. Say the word and I will amend it in this PR. ## Notes Only sm120/sm121 hardware was available; the gate is `is_sm120_supported()`-scoped and defaults off everywhere else. Note that `is_sm120_supported()` is `cc_major == 12`, so it also covers (12,0) parts I could not test — the row-threshold argument transfers because they take the same FlashInfer entry. CI: the red on `base-b-test-1-gpu-large (4)` is `test/registered/quant/test_awq.py::TestAWQMarlinBfloat16::test_mmlu` (`0.82421875 not greater than 0.83`), which is unrelated to this change and is currently flaky at its threshold on unrelated branches too — #34477 raised `num_examples` 64 → 256 without re-calibrating the bound. The CPU `build-test` and AMD failures reproduce on `main`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [HiSparse] Support hisparse multi-step swap io kernel
signal.text: ## Motivation The existing HiSparse swap path processes speculative decoding steps sequentially. For a four-step MTP request, this requires four independent cache lookups, swap passes, and cache-state updates. It also cannot naturally deduplicate misses shared by multiple speculative steps. This PR adds a standalone multi-step HiSparse swap kernel. It treats all MTP top-k tensors as one working set and resolves their device locations in one gather/commit launch pair. The scope of this PR is intentionally limited to the swap kernel, its JIT wrapper, correctness tests, and benchmark. It does not include IO prefetching or coordinator integration. ## Design The implementation uses two kernels: 1. A gather kernel flattens `[batch, steps, top_k]`, resolves extra-page and hot-cache hits, deduplicates host misses across speculative steps, and copies each unique miss into a scratch device location exactly once. 2. A per-request commit kernel updates the CLOCK cache, rotates scratch and hot locations, updates the token-to-slot hash tables, and resolves direct overflow misses. The two-kernel structure provides the grid-wide synchronization required before the cache commit can consume the final miss count and scratch hash table. Programmatic Dependent Launch is enabled on supported Hopper GPUs. Current-call device locations remain exact. If the union of unique hits and misses exceeds the hot-cache capacity, only the cache admission policy becomes approximate: the kernel favors the most recent speculative step for future cache residency. This does not change the data returned for the current attention call. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["top_k_tokens [batch, steps, top_k]"] --> B["Gather kernel"] B --> C["Extra-page lookup"] B --> D["Hot-cache hash lookup"] B --> E["Cross-step miss deduplication"] E --> F["Unique host-to-device copies"] C --> G["Resolved device locations"] D --> G F --> G B --> H["Commit kernel"] H --> I["CLOCK victim selection"] H --> J["Cache/hash update"] H --> K["Overflow resolution"] I --> L["Persistent state for next decode"] J --> L ``` ## Performance The benchmark uses CUDA Graphs with four speculative steps, top-k 2048, a 4096-entry hot cache, 576-byte MLA cache items, and 782 unique misses per request. On an NVIDIA H20, MTP reduces batch-64 latency from 794.42 us for four sequential LRU passes to 411.85 us, a 48.2% reduction. The gather block size is set to 64 threads. It preserves the cross-step warp mapping while reducing host-I/O bursts compared with larger CTAs. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4.
