signal.title: [Bug] Server stops responding after 2-3 requests — Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, TP=4 across 4x DGX Spark (GB10/SM121)
signal.text: ## Summary Reproducible scheduler/server hang: after 2–3 successful chat completions, all subsequent requests (including `/health`) time out indefinitely. Reproduced 3/3 attempts across 2 host boots. Generation quality and speed are normal until the hang. ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` @ `sha256:ceaf8b16e02d165143633ac228bbb994a05fe77d7e0526cf035ae4bbf4eacc36` (sglang 0.5.12.post1, torch 2.11.0+cu130) - Hardware: 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 128GB unified each), dual-rail 200G RoCE, NET/IB transport verified in NCCL logs (zero socket fallback) - Model: nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4, `--quantization modelopt_fp4` ## Launch ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --tp 4 --nnodes 4 --node-rank N --dist-init-addr <rank0>:29500 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8890 --attention-backend triton \ --context-length 4096 --max-running-requests 1 ``` (GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME/TP_SOCKET_IFNAME/NCCL_* set for the RoCE fabric; happy to paste full env) ## Repro 1. Serve; wait for "fired up and ready". 2. Send 2-3 sequential streaming chat completions (200 max_tokens, temp 0, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`). First 1-2 complete normally (observed 12.9-25.4 tok/s decode). 3. Next request hangs past 600s; `/health` also stops answering. No crash, no error in rank-0 log; container stays up. Run-to-run details vary slightly (sometimes 2 succeed, sometimes 3; one run wedged with thinking-mode requests that exceeded max_tokens via reasoning). The hang itself is 3/3. ## Observations (NOT a diagnosis — flagging for maintainers, unverified hypotheses) - At one hang we observed on rank 0: `resource_tracker: There appear to be 1 leaked semaphore objects to clean up at shutdown`. We have NOT established this as cause — could be shutdown noise. A shared-memory/IPC angle is our only (unverified) hypothesis; we'd value maintainer guidance on what to instrument. - Possibly relevant config quirks on our side: stock MoE kernel configs (no tuned configs for GB10), startup warning `DeepGemm is enabled but the scale_fmt of checkpoint is not ue8m0`, `--max-running-requests 1`. - Config deltas vs the known-good community run (ht12, sglang 0.5.10, same checkpoint, same 4x Spark shape, forum thread 366325): they ran `disable_deep_gemm=true` (we did not — and our build warns about DeepGemm scale_fmt), `max_running_requests=32` (ours 1 — maybe the single-slot admission path is implicated), raised `watchdog_timeout=3600`/`dist_timeout=1800`, fp8_e4m3 KV, explicit `fp4_gemm_backend=flashinfer_cutlass` with an SM121 cute/mma.py patch, sglang 0.5.10 vs our 0.5.12.post1. Happy to bisect any of these on request. - Community reports (ht12, NVIDIA forum) show this checkpoint serving fast and concurrent on Spark-class hardware via SGLang — so this may well be config-specific. We can run any diagnostic build/flags on the 4-node rig on request; full rank logs, env dumps, and probe streams preserved. - Related blocker we hit attempting to bisect on 0.5.10: this model cannot load at all on sglang ≤0.5.13 + transformers 5.x without out-of-tree patches (vision_config/text_config sub-config dicts not promoted; PR #22839 addresses it but has been unmerged since April 15) — which limits how much of the community-vs-stock delta anyone can bisect on stock builds. ## Evidence available rank-0 log tails at each hang (3 runs), full launch env, raw probe streams (timestamps per token), NCCL transport logs.

signal.title: Support Intern-S2-Mobius FP8
signal.text: ## Motivation `internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8` is now public, but it does not load on current SGLang. The serialized FP8 config lists `.linear_attn` parents as exact `modules_to_not_convert` entries, while SGLang treats ignored-layer names as prefixes and consequently skips quantized child projections. Strict loading then also needs to map the checkpoint's fused expert scale tensors and allow omitted KV-cache scales. The existing Intern-S2-Mobius cookbook only exposes the BF16 checkpoint. ## Modifications - Preserve FP8 quantization for Mobius linear-attention qkv/z and output projections while retaining the checkpoint's child exclusions. - Load `gate_up_proj_scale_inv` and `down_proj_scale_inv` into the fused expert scale parameters. - Treat Mobius `attn.k_scale` and `attn.v_scale` as optional while still loading them when present. - Add the FP8 checkpoint to the cookbook selector with verified 1xH200 TP=1 high-throughput and NEXTN recipes. B200 recipes remain explicitly unverified. - Separate the existing BF16 benchmark claims from the new FP8 launch verification. No unit test is added: this is a serialized-checkpoint integration path, and a mock loader test would only restate the configured parameter mappings. The real checkpoint path is covered by the end-to-end gate below. ## Accuracy Tests Verified commit `59c8810358` on 1xH200 with checkpoint revision `ea369586a687b1f31d29c8b10868acf2cb8e2889`: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \ --context-length 262144 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 sgl-eval run gsm8k \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \ --model internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius-FP8 \ --num-examples 1319 \ --num-threads 64 ``` | Examples | Accuracy | Stop rate | Truncated | Error | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1319 | **96.82%** | **100.00%** | 0.00% | 0.00% | All 1319 prediction records reported `finish_reason=stop`. The documented NEXTN recipe also passed live smoke tests: - Text: `15% of 240` returned `36`, `finish_reason=stop`. - Vision: the standard tiger image returned `tiger`, `finish_reason=stop`, with 70 image tokens. - A 292-token bounded generation stopped normally; telemetry reported accept length 4.00 and accept rate 1.00 with decode CUDA graphs enabled. Local validation passed: changed-file `pre-commit`, `py_compile`, cookbook config consistency, `git diff --check`, and `mint validate`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No FP8 speed benchmark is claimed in this PR. The cookbook explicitly keeps the existing speed tables scoped to BF16. For capacity context, the high-throughput server loaded 34.22 GB of FP8 model weights. The NEXTN target+draft process used about 94 GB on H200 with the documented settings. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signal.title: Add fmha_v2 attention backend for SM90/120
signal.text: ## Motivation Enables TRT-LLM's fmha_v2 prefill attention backend for SM90/120. This backend is more performant than the current default (FA3), and also enables skip-softmax feature, which can further boost performance for long-context / applications where attention output is sparse. ## Modifications Baseline enablement of trtllm's fmha_v2 prefill kernel for SM90/120. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32272 is needed for further perf improvement, and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32268 / https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32269 are used for the MTP accuracy reporting. ## Accuracy Tests ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /SGL/models/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking-FP8 \ --tp 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --disable-radix-cache --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --attention-backend trtllm_mha \ --trust-remote-code --port 30000 # --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ``` | Config | KV dtype | Score | Repeat range | |---|---|---|---| | FA3 | bf16 | 0.725 | 0.712-0.742 | | fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha) | bf16 | 0.723 | 0.702-0.753 | | FA3 + MTP | bf16 | 0.734 | 0.712-0.758 | | fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (fa3 verify) | bf16 | 0.721 | 0.707-0.732 | | FA3 | **fp8_e4m3** | 0.727 | 0.707-0.747 | | fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha) | **fp8_e4m3** | 0.724 | 0.682-0.753 | ### MTP Add to server launch: `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` | Config | Accept len | Accept rate | GPQA-20 score | |---|---|---|---| | FA3 + MTP (bf16) | 2.37 (2.35) | 0.46 (0.45) | 0.750 | | fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (bf16) | 2.45 (2.30) | 0.48 (0.43) | 0.700 | | pure trtllm_mha + MTP w/ XQA mask fix (bf16, 10q) | 2.20 | 0.40 | 0.70 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling The e2e performance is not improved with just this PR because it requires a large copy operation before the compute kernel to interleave KV. https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3575 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32272 address this issue. Unit Kernel Measurements show ~15% improvement over FA3 over a variety of problem sizes, reaching 20% at small problems. ### Skip-Softmax This feature can provide additional speedup, especially for long-context inference where the attention logits are sparse. We define the threshold factor `\lambda := a / L` where a is a hyperparameter, and L is the sequence length. To demonstrate the potential speedup, we keep a = 1000 here for simplicity. | ISL | Effective threshold (1000 / ISL) | bf16 gain | fp8 gain | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k | 0.122 | +1.8% | +0.2% | | 32k | 0.031 | +5.2% | +1.7% | | 128k | 0.008 | +12.9% | + 3.5% | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Fix] Record the WAR read-done event in-graph to cover replay-time metadata reads
signal.text: trtllm_mha's fused in-graph metadata kernel re-reads the live req_to_token / full->SWA mapping on every graph replay -- after the WAR fastpath's pre-replay read-done event was recorded -- so scheduler-side writes could overwrite them mid-replay. Record the read-done event as an external-event node inside the captured graph at the snapshot-completion point (for backends with a no-op in-graph hook the node sits at the graph head, preserving today's semantics), with a new backend capability falling back to post-replay recording where in-graph capture is unavailable. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #29707770973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29707770973)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #29707770880](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29707770880)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Chunk DSV4 indexer logits to bound transient memory
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35201. The DSV4 sparse indexer materializes a `[query_rows, max_c4_seq_len]` fp32 logits tensor per layer per forward pass — allocated inside DeepGEMM's `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (`csrc/apis/attention.hpp`, `torch::empty`) before the kernel launches. It grows linearly with accumulated context and **no part of sglang's memory budgeting accounts for it**, so long-context prefill OOMs deterministically, on every rank at once (the indexer is replicated, not TP-sharded). Repro on 4×H100 TP4, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.9`: a single 800K-token request dies with ``` indexer.py forward_c4_indexer → deep_gemm fp8_paged_mqa_logits → CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.42 GiB ``` which is exactly `4096 rows × align(ceil(372K/4/256)·64, 256) cols × 4 B` — the chunk covering ~372K of the 800K prompt. At the default `--chunked-prefill-size 8192` the non-paged path allocates ~2× that and walls proportionally earlier. Lowering `mem_fraction_static` only moves the wall, since the requirement grows without bound in context length. ## Modifications Slice logits + top-k over query rows under a free-memory budget — the same shape `dsa_indexer.py` already uses for its `fp8_mqa_logits` allocation: - `_mqa_logits_chunk_rows()` returns a slice size when `query_rows × aligned_row_bytes` exceeds the budget, else `None` (single-call path, unchanged behavior). - The paged branch loops slices: per-slice `q`/`weights`/`c4_seq_lens`/`page_table`, per-slice DeepGEMM schedule metadata, per-slice top-k written into the matching rows of `c4_sparse_page_indices`. `max_c4_seq_len` stays full-width — logits columns are absolute c4 positions. Peak transient memory becomes the budget instead of `chunk_tokens × context`. - `_get_nonpaged_indexer_plan()` declines prefills whose logits would exceed the same budget, so they fall through to the chunked paged path (that path materializes its logits in one call with no slicing available). - Knob: `SGLANG_DSV4_MQA_LOGITS_FREE_MEM_FRACTION` (default 0.2), capped at 0.3 × total, mirroring the DSA indexer. Top-k is row-independent, so slicing preserves results exactly. **One deliberate difference from the DSA precedent:** the budget is measured per call, not cached. The free remainder shrinks as the KV pool fills, and a cached budget sampled while the server was idle sizes slices that no longer fit — during development this reproduced as 1020 MiB slices against 831 MiB free, i.e. the same OOM one level down. A static pre-check (64 MiB) keeps normal batches off that path entirely, so steady-state serving pays no `mem_get_info` sync. Happy to align the DSA path the same way in a follow-up if maintainers agree it has the same latent issue. ## Accuracy Test Row-slicing equivalence is the correctness-relevant property, covered by `test/registered/attention/test_dsv4_indexer_row_slice.py` (CPU-only, no GPU needed): chunked vs unchunked top-k output is bit-identical across chunk sizes 1/7/16/36/37 on random logits, plus budget-arithmetic tests pinned to the observed 1.42 GiB case and the DeepGEMM 256-column row alignment. 4 passed. End-to-end on 4×H100 TP4 with `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (v0.5.17 image + this patch overlaid), greedy, cache flushed between probes: | prompt | before | after | |---|---|---| | 71,349 tok | OK | OK — **byte-identical output** | | 399,732 tok | OK (32.9 s) | OK (33.2 s) | | 799,550 tok | **OOM, all 4 ranks die** | **OK, 95.4 s**, 0 restarts, 0.76 GiB free | ## Benchmark and Profiling Result No steady-state throughput change is expected or observed: the static pre-check keeps sub-64 MiB allocations (all normal batches) on the original single-call path, byte-identical. The 71K and 400K probes above are within run-to-run noise of the unpatched server (4.8→4.9 s, 32.9→33.2 s). Chunking engages only where the alternative is a crash. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#running-unit-tests-adding-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#writing-documentations). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html). - [x] For reviewers: please read the [Reviewer Guidelines](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/developer_guide/reviewer_guidelines.md). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32081429908](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32081429908)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32081429719](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32081429719)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec] Reduce host-side overhead in ngram draft prep
signal.text: Three host-side trims in the ngram draft-prep path: - Build the accept-independent parts of the corpus query (req ids, prompt/output tails, base lengths) before the blocking `.cpu()` on `accept_tokens`/`accept_lens`, so that host work overlaps the in-flight forward. - Stop converting whole `origin_input_ids` to a list per request per iteration; only the last `max_trie_depth` tokens can enter the corpus query, so slice the tails first (same in `_update_ngram_corpus`). - Skip the accept D2H sync entirely when the spliced tokens are unused (non-overlap mode and grammar-sync batches), and hoist the `USE_FULL_MASK` ones-mask allocations (which only need `seq_lens_cpu`) above the sync. Verification: `test_spec_ngram.py` 18 tests OK. Single-batch fwd-occupancy probe: neutral on a short prompt; on a 9k-token prompt, fwd occupancy 88.8% -> 90.4% and decode throughput +1.9% with identical accept length. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32080874114](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32080874114)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32080874038](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32080874038)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [LoRA] Add the sgl_lora MoE execution engine with JSON config resolution
signal.text: ## Motivation MoE (expert-weight) LoRA serving in SGLang currently runs through the experimental TRT-LLM path (`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm` + virtual experts). That path has structural limits: - **Blackwell-only**: the trtllm-gen kernels require SM100/120, so there is no expert-LoRA path at all on Hopper (H200). - **Virtual-expert routing scales with `max_loras_per_batch × num_experts`**, so multi-adapter serving degrades sharply as slot capacity grows. - **No prefill CUDA graphs with LoRA**, and no support for shared-outer adapter factors (gate_up A / down B shared across experts, `expert_dim=1` — the native format of some recent MoE adapters). This PR adds `sgl_lora`: a self-contained MoE-LoRA execution engine selected with `--lora-execution-engine sgl_lora`, built from an exhaustive kernel/fusion/overlap sweep on GB300, B200, and H200 across three models (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B, Inkling-Small; per-expert and shared-outer adapters, ranks 8–64). ## Modifications - **Engine** (`python/sglang/srt/lora/sgl_lora/`): masked expert-major decode path and route-major serial prefill path; per-expert and shared-outer factor layouts; two base-GEMM providers (DeepGEMM, CuTeDSL); side-stream overlap windows for the shared-decode path; capacity-flat routing (cost scales with *active* adapters, not slot capacity). - **JSON config resolution** (`sgl_lora/configs/{gb300,h200,default}.json`): every kernel-family/fusion/overlap/tile decision is data, resolved per (layout, activation, phase, batch shape) through ordered first-match scenario rows with fail-closed validation — a malformed row, unknown plan field, or unknown predicate key aborts startup instead of serving a wrong plan. `SGLANG_SGL_LORA_CONFIG_DIR` points at an override config root (arch JSONs at top level, M-bucketed base-GEMM tile tables under `gemm/`). Every shipped row carries real-model sweep provenance; unknown architectures fall to a conservative serial fallback (`default.json`). - **Prefill CUDA graphs with MoE LoRA** (breakable backend), including graph-stable LoRA workspaces. - **Dense-module gate**: adapter targets are pruned to weight-backed modules at registration, and per-module effective ranks let mixed multi-adapter batches skip dense-LoRA work for adapters that carry no weights for a module (the shared dense kernels in `kernels/ops/gemm` stay byte-identical to upstream — the gate enters as a batch-info view). - **Onboarding tuner** (`benchmark/kernels/lora_moe/tune_lora_config.py`): `--check` (CI-gateable coverage report), `--emit-seed` (serve a new geometry immediately), `--sweep` (e2e-tunes the two geometry-sensitive axes; writes winners back into the seed). - Guards: expert LoRA + DP-attention / elastic-EP / EPLB fail closed at startup (the DP-attention token-axis limitation exists silently in the legacy path today). Scope: bf16 serving path. fp8/nvfp4 qlora support is planned as a follow-up in this PR (the tuner carries a `TODO(quant)` and the config resolver already fails closed on future `quant` predicate keys). Structure note: the first commit is the engine; subsequent commits are review-round changes and will be squashed before undrafting. Two orthogonal fixes found during this work ship separately: `fix/chunked-sgmv-cache-key` (csgmv compile-cache key omits codegen parameters) and `fix/swa-kvpool-v-head-dim` (SWAKVPool lacks `get_v_head_dim`, crashing hybrid-SWA models on the triton attention backend). ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/unit/lora/`: 248 passed / 6 skipped (H200), including config-resolution pins, kernel numerics vs an fp32 oracle, byte-identity pins for the decode kernel policy, and prefill graph-vs-eager bit-exactness. - Greedy-decode correctness on real adapters vs the legacy triton reference: per-token logprob deltas at the measured bf16 noise floor (per-expert and shared-outer, all three campaign models). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Protocol: `bench_one_batch_server`, input 4096 / output 1024, bs 1/8/16/32, `max_loras_per_batch=4` distinct adapters, medians after first-pass discard. Baseline = experimental TRT-LLM LoRA path at its best posture (incl. prefill graphs where it can use them). - **Qwen3.5-35B (GB300, TP4)**: prefill +15–19%, decode parity. - **Qwen3.5-397B (B200, TP8)**: prefill +23%, decode −1.2%…+4.5% across bs. - **Inkling-Small (GB300)**: decode +0.5%…+11.9% with the model's shared/routed-expert parallelism active on both engines; prefill +2–5%. - **H200 (fa4 posture)**: the TRT engine cannot run (SM100/120-only kernels); vs the only runnable incumbent (legacy virtual experts on triton fused_moe): decode +1.7%…+19.7%, prefill +1.0–1.5% at bs≥8 (−13% at bs1). - **Prefill CUDA graphs**: 2.5–3.0× prefill throughput vs eager at equal chunking (the incumbent disables prefill graphs under LoRA). - **Multi-adapter**: routing cost is capacity-flat; with 4 distinct adapters/ranks resident, +15–24% prefill and +2–17% decode vs the incumbent. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Constrained] Support MistralCommon tokenizers in the XGrammar backend
signal.text: Serving a Mistral model whose tokenizer resolves to `MistralCommonBackend` disables structured output entirely. XGrammar cannot build `TokenizerInfo` from it, so we log a warning, fall back to `grammar_backend="none"`, and every `json_schema` / `regex` / `ebnf` request is rejected with a 400. Neither alternate backend helps: outlines fails to compile any schema on this vocabulary, and llguidance refuses a non-fast tokenizer outright. The cause is that `MistralCommonBackend.get_vocab()` is keyed by decoded text, so byte-level pieces collide and most ids come back as 0 — 130044 usable entries for a 131072 vocabulary. The raw byte pieces are only reachable through the inner Tekkenizer, so `patch_mistral_common_tokenizer` now attaches the `init_xgrammar` hook that `xgrammar_backend.py` already looks for (the same escape hatch `tiktoken_tokenizer.py` uses) and builds the ordered vocabulary directly. mistral_common stays responsible for encoding and chat templating; only what the grammar backend sees changes. The second commit is related but separable: mistral_common validates conversation structure and rejects, for example, an assistant turn with empty content. That escaped as a 500 even though the Jinja path already mapped equivalent template errors to 400, so both paths now share one tuple of client-error types. Verified end to end on `Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B` (tp 4, `--tool-call-parser mistral --reasoning-parser mistral`): no fallback warning, `json_schema` returns 200 and is actually enforced (a prose-style prompt with a strict schema still yields conformant JSON), the empty-assistant request returns 400 instead of 500, and plain chat is unchanged. One caveat for reviewers: the hook reads `_vocab_size`, `_all_special_tokens` and `id_to_byte_piece` from mistral_common's Tekkenizer, two of which are private. If a future release changes them, `init_xgrammar` returns `(None, None)` and today's graceful fallback resumes rather than crashing. signal.title: config: the per-instance families read the bags
signal.text: The tokenizer manager, the detokenizer, the multimodal processors, the encode server and the HTTP entrypoint read resolved config off the instance they were handed. signal.title: [speculative] DSpark: support the mask-filling draft convention (verify width = gamma)
signal.text: ## Motivation DSpark currently assumes the autoregressive draft-block convention: a gamma-row block emits gamma drafts and the verify window is gamma + 1 rows. DFlash-style mask-filling draft heads use a different block layout — slot 0 carries the anchor token and slots 1..gamma-1 are the predictions — so a gamma-row block emits gamma-1 real drafts and the faithful verify width is gamma (= the config block_size). Serving such a head under the AR convention appends a junk token sampled from the clamped last slot and mis-sizes every width-derived buffer (CG capture widths, ragged verify layout, committed-token rail). ## Background: the two draft-block conventions Both conventions build the identical block input per request per round: a width-gamma row `[anchor, MASK, MASK, ..., MASK]` (anchor = last accepted token) plus the injected target-model features. They differ in how the head's outputs are read — the GPT-vs-BERT distinction applied to the draft block (gamma = 4): ``` input slots: [ t0(anchor) | MASK | MASK | MASK ] AR readout (existing convention; causal in-block, next-token loss): out@0->draft1 out@1->draft2 out@2->draft3 out@3->draft4 4 drafts from 4 slots; verify = 1+4 = 5 rows (num_draft_tokens = gamma+1) Mask-filling readout (this PR; bidirectional in-block, masked-token loss): out@0->(unused) out@1->draft1 out@2->draft2 out@3->draft3 3 drafts from 4 slots; verify = 4 rows (num_draft_tokens = gamma) ``` For readers more familiar with GPT-style models: a masked LM (BERT-style) replaces some input positions with a learned `[MASK]` embedding (content removed, position kept), attends bidirectionally, and reads the output at each masked position as a prediction for that same position — reconstruction in place rather than continuation. A mask-filling draft head is that objective specialized to speculation: "given the anchor token and the target model's features, predict the next gamma-1 positions jointly in one forward." Why heads are trained this way: 1. **Information flow**: every predicted slot attends the anchor directly and all sibling positions bidirectionally; under the AR readout, slot i sees only the anchor plus i content-free mask placeholders. 2. **Train/serve input match**: a mask-filling head trains on `[anchor, MASK, ...]` — byte-identical to the serving-time input — so there is no teacher-forcing/exposure gap on the block input. AR-readout block heads train on true tokens in the slots and serve on masks, a mismatch that compounds with slot depth. 3. The known weakness of in-place parallel prediction (slots are conditionally independent given the block context, so joint samples can be incoherent) is what DSpark's sequential Markov head compensates for — which is why this head family pairs naturally with the existing DSpark machinery. The two readouts are different functions of the same block (out@i means "token i+1" in one and "token i" in the other), so a mask-filling checkpoint cannot be served by re-indexing or padding under the AR convention — padding fabricates a draft the head never produced and wastes a verify row per request per round. The convention therefore has to be declared by the checkpoint and respected at every width-derived site, which is what this PR wires up. Note the bidirectional in-block attention is load-bearing at serve time (mask keys absorb a significant share of attention mass, acting as attention sinks); attention backends must reproduce the trained block geometry rather than approximate it causally. ## Modifications The convention is declared by the draft checkpoint config (`dspark_mask_filling: true`), parsed into `DSparkDraftConfig.mask_filling`. Builtin AR heads are unaffected: the flag defaults off and the verify width stays gamma + 1. A config declaring the convention names an out-of-tree head, so builtin head-name validation is skipped for it (the implementation is validated at draft-model build). Width choke points updated: - `dspark_config`: mask-filling heads hard-error on `speculative_num_draft_tokens != block_size`; `read_draft_checkpoint_is_mask_filling` helper. - `speculative_hook`: faithful verify width at the arg-validation site. - `spec_info.get_num_tokens_per_req_for_target_verify`: draft block rows == verify width at the CG/buffer sizing choke point; `set_dspark_mask_filling_convention` is called at server-args resolution AND at `DSparkWorkerV2` init (worker processes may not re-run arg hooks). - `dspark_planner`: `DSparkScheduleConfig` gains `verify_width`; the ragged layout must match the runtime verify width (one row wider makes the host committed-token stream read neighbor-row metadata as token ids at bs>1). - `dspark_verify`: `TargetVerifyExecutor` derives the drafts width as `verify_num_draft_tokens - 1` (identical for legacy AR heads). - `dspark_draft`: the folded sampler takes the gamma-1 draft view for mask-filling heads (duck-typed `markov_head.mask_filling`). - `dspark_worker_v2`: assert drafts+1 == verify width at the verify-ids joint. - `kernels/ops dspark_verify_window`: `compact_verify_ids` splits `block_w` (anchor stride over `draft_block_ids`) from `draft_w` (drafts stride); both shapes covered. - Extension seams for out-of-tree runner subclasses: a `_build_verify_executor` factory, an opt-in verify-forward-batch retention for post-accept state restoration, a `verify_skip_attn_backend_init` opt-out for runners whose eager prep re-pads the batch after `prepare_for_verify`, and an `_on_prefill_target_hidden` callback exposing the full prefill hiddens for draft-feature staging. ## Checklist - Default behavior for existing DSpark drafts is unchanged (flag off => gamma + 1 everywhere; drafts-width derivation is identity for AR heads). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32079572416](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079572416)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32079572224](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32079572224)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MoE] Fix flashinfer TRT-LLM BF16 expert weight reload on refit
signal.text: ## Motivation `process_weights_after_loading` rewrites BF16 MoE expert weights into the flashinfer TRT-LLM BlockMajorK layout whenever `use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe` is set, and that flag covers **both** `flashinfer_trtllm` and `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`. The inverse hook, however, was gated on `is_flashinfer_trtllm_routed()` alone. So with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm` the destination parameter stayed in block layout and the hot copy raised: ``` The size of tensor a (64) must match the size of tensor b (2048) at non-singleton dimension 2 ``` torch names the `copy_` destination first, so the 64 is ours: `block_k` is 128 bytes and the conversion runs on a `uint8` view, giving 128 / 2 bytes-per-bf16. Nobody opts into this — `flashinfer_trtllm` is auto-selected on sm100 for BF16 MoE models when `moe_runner_backend` is left at `"auto"`, so an RL weight refit on Blackwell hits it by default. Fixes #27787 ## Modifications 1. **Gate the inverse on the same flag that gates the transform** (`use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe`), so the two cannot drift apart again. 2. **The restore inverts the data, not just the shape.** RL callers batch weights, so one refit is many update RPCs; with a shape-only restore an earlier bucket's re-derive would block expert slots that a later bucket has not written yet a second time. 3. **New `repack_weights_after_hot_update` hook** to re-derive the layout once the copies are done. `update_weights_from_disk` and the checkpoint-engine IPC path already re-run `process_weights_after_loading`; `update_weights_from_tensor`, `update_weights_from_distributed` and the bucketed variants call `model.load_weights()` directly and do not. Widening the gate on its own would therefore only trade the loud copy failure for a parameter left in canonical layout while the kernel reads BlockMajorK. The re-derive is called from a `finally` on all four update paths, so a mid-update exception cannot leave parameters canonical while the kernel expects block layout. Files touched: `layers/quantization/unquant.py`, `layers/quantization/base_config.py` (no-op base hook), `model_executor/model_runner_components/weight_updater.py`, plus a new CPU unit test. Note on the rebase onto current main: the only conflict was add/add with #33905 (XPU MoE row-stride padding), which inserts helpers at the same module-level position. Both blocks are kept and there is no interaction — the XPU padding applies under an XPU default device, the BlockMajorK rewrite under flashinfer on sm100, and #33905 only touches `create_weights`, which this PR does not. ## Accuracy Tests Reproduced against the real code path on CPU with Qwen3-30B-A3B geometry (hidden 2048, moe_intermediate 768, tp=2 -> 384 per partition): ``` before: postprocess (4,32,768,64) -> restore no-op -> copy raises after: restore -> (4,768,2048) -> copy ok -> repack -> (4,32,768,64) ``` `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_flashinfer_trtllm_bf16_moe_reload.py` covers this end to end and is registered as a CPU test (11 cases): the block layout is applied on cold load and changes the shape; the restore runs for the non-routed backend and *inverts* the layout rather than reshaping it; a reload reproduces the cold-load layout exactly, including through the bucketed update path; the repack is a no-op when nothing was reverted and when the backend is inactive; non-bijective permutations and unexpected element counts are rejected; and the `finally` re-derive still runs when `load_weights` raises. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable to the forward path — this PR only changes the weight-update path. The re-derive runs once per update RPC, after the copies land; no kernel or forward-pass code is touched. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31643837888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31643837888)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31643837810](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31643837810)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Refactor: Deprecate Prefill CP V1
signal.text: ## Motivation Prefill context parallelism still carried both the v1 and v2 implementations behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2`. This duplicated server-argument compatibility handling, coupled model implementations to CP internals, and left legacy paths in attention backends and DSA. This PR makes the current v2 implementation the only prefill CP implementation and removes the version distinction. It is intentionally stacked on `clean-dsv4`. ## Modifications - Remove `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` and the legacy CP server-argument aliases and compatibility rewrites. - Delete the legacy `python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/cp_utils.py` implementation. - Remove prefill CP branches from model files, including DeepSeek and Qwen MoE implementations, so modeling code no longer owns CP data movement. - Remove CP v1 branches from CUDA, NPU, and MUSA attention backends and delete stale DSA v1 helpers. - Rename versioned APIs and fields, for example `is_cp_v2_active` to `is_cp_active`. - Delete v1-only and old parity tests while retaining the canonical CP test coverage. - Handle DSA CP warmup batches without speculative metadata and add regression coverage for that case. - Update documentation and examples to use `--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy ...`. ## Accuracy Tests Passed: - `test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py`: 26/26 tests. - `test/registered/cp/test_dsa_prefill_cp.py`: 1/1 test on H200; GSM8K score 0.946. - `test/registered/cp/test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4_cp.py`: 1/1 test on B200; GPQA score 0.6566 (threshold 0.58). - Two compatible configurations in `test_gqa_prefill_cp.py`: GSM8K score 0.98 each. signal.title: model: support encoder embedding models on Intel XPU (bge / NomicBERT / ModernBERT)
signal.text: Enables three encoder embedding models on the Intel XPU backend: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, and `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`, already supported by `bert.py`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact scored 0, output cosine vs HuggingFace 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang implementation, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings not auto-handled for NomicBertModel`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) also fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — the wrapper routed a bidirectional encoder through the paged decoder KV cache. ## Modifications - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` — the prefill path used `causal = not is_cross_attention` and ran encoder layers with a causal mask. Now matches every other backend. - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when auto-truncating over-length embedding inputs (CLS/mean pooling depends on it). Gated on `not is_generation`, so generation is unaffected. - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU MLP, post-norm blocks; mean pooling; in-model SDPA (no KV cache). - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, alternating local/global attention, GeGLU MLP; mean pooling; in-model SDPA. `bert.py` couldn't be reused for the two new models (it requires absolute, non-RoPE positions). The two model files are additive; the shared bge fixes are gated and leave decoder generation byte-for-byte unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60, tp-size 1), vs the HuggingFace reference; MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus): | Model | per-embedding cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 (short); long docs 0.997-0.9999 after SEP fix | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-embedding-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | All load with 0 skipped params. Residual gaps: bge — the scheduler's small reserved-token margin on the 8% of docs >512 tokens; nomic — the harness omits nomic's `search_query:`/`search_document:` retrieval prefixes; ModernBERT — bf16 execution-order noise. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. The bge causal fix flips a boolean for encoder layers only and the truncation guard runs once per over-length embedding request; the two new models are small encoders running attention in-model via SDPA (no paged attention / KV cache). Decoder generation is unaffected. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32078514647](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32078514647)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32078514463](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32078514463)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: model: InternVL fixes for concurrent multimodal on Intel XPU
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving InternVL3_5 MoE models (e.g. `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`) on Intel XPU fails in two ways: 1. **Weight loading crashes** with `AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`. The MoE expert mapping reads `config.num_experts`, but InternVL nests the LLM config — `num_experts` lives on `config.llm_config` (the Qwen3-MoE backbone, `num_experts=128`). 2. **The vision encoder hangs/crashes under concurrent multimodal at tp>1.** The XPU vision attention derives `max_seqlen` from GPU `cu_seqlens` in every block, and that device->host `.item()` deadlocks the Level Zero USM memcpy; separately, batching more than one request's ViT tiles into a single forward crashes Level Zero (DEVICE_LOST / OUT_OF_RESOURCES). (Baseline: P1 build #4722.) ## Modifications - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: let `VisionIntelXPUAttention.forward` accept and use `VisionAttentionMetadata` — it already exists upstream and is threaded into the vision encoder, but the XPU attention path still re-derived `max_seqlen` from GPU `cu_seqlens` every block. Reusing the host-side value skips that sync. - `models/internvl.py`: pass the host-side `max_seqlen` (uniform ViT tiles) into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata` so the value above is available. - `models/internvl.py` + `environ.py`: chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12) tiles on XPU; tiles are independent, so chunk-and-concat is bit-exact. All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`. ## Accuracy Test Verified on Intel XPU, tp-4 (4× Arc Pro B60, 61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads as `InternVLChatModel` with **0 skipped params**, MoE initialized (`UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`), KV cache allocated; multimodal smoke via `/v1/chat/completions` (red image + "What color is this image?" -> "Red"). P1 accuracy (lmms-eval, tp-4, build #4838): **mathvision_testmini 38.2**, **mmmu_val 27.4**. (Numbers are from the pre-rebase branch. After rebasing onto current main, an earlier `mm_schedule` mask-readback workaround was dropped as superseded — upstream now counts mm tokens from host offsets — and the vision fix was re-expressed on upstream's `VisionAttentionMetadata` path.) ## Speed Test and Profiling Not separately profiled. On XPU this removes a per-block device->host sync in the vision attention path and bounds the ViT forward size; non-XPU paths are unchanged (guarded by `is_xpu()`), so no regression is expected there. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32077622528](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32077622528)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32077622043](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32077622043)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Scheduler] Release all request-owned KV on no-insert cleanup
signal.text: ## Why `RadixCache.cache_finished_req(..., is_insert=False)` discards a request without inserting its KV into the radix cache. The old implementation derived the release range from committed token IDs rather than from `kv_len_to_handle`. Under overlap scheduling, a forward pass can commit a KV slot before its sampled output token is accepted, leaving the token-ID list one element shorter and leaking the final request-owned slot. ## Ownership contract - `[0, cache_protected_len)` is cache-owned and must be preserved. - `[cache_protected_len, kv_len_to_handle)` is request-owned committed KV and must be released on no-insert cleanup. - Overallocated KV after `kv_len_to_handle` is released by `release_kv_cache`. ## Change - Release the request-owned committed range directly from the request-to-token mapping with the existing `free_segment` allocator primitive. - Release the request's radix-node lock as before. - Leave the normal cache-insertion path unchanged. - Extend the existing matched-prefix failure test to cover a committed KV slot with no corresponding output token. ## Series This PR fixes the generic no-insert cleanup primitive. It is not sampling-mask-specific and applies to every `is_insert=False` cleanup path. 1. This PR fixes request-owned KV cleanup. 2. #35205 makes sampling-support capture producer-faithful and exact within runtime capacity. 3. #34037 adds explicit bounded mode and its public truncation signal. ## Validation - Focused registered unit test: 6 passed on one H200 using `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682`. - Repository pre-commit checks passed for both changed files, including the registered-test validator. - `git diff --check` passed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32076641901](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076641901)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32076641658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076641658)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: nanjiangwill

signal.title: [Sampling] Make sampling-support capture faithful and capacity-safe
signal.text: ## Why #27408 reconstructs a sampling mask after sampling. That is not a reliable description of the distribution that selected the token: PyTorch has already sorted and filtered its weights, while FlashInfer applies its own top-k/top-p threshold semantics and retains cutoff ties. #33593 also makes top-p-only requests valid, so finite `top_k` cannot serve as a general support or transport bound. This PR establishes the exact serving contract first: for the post-filter weights `w` that sampled token `y`, return the complete positive-weight support `S = {i | w[i] > 0}` and `log(w[y] / sum(w))`. If `|S|` exceeds `--sampling-mask-max-tokens`, abort before committing `y`. Sampling itself is unchanged. ## Design - Capture the producer's representation. PyTorch reuses its already-filtered weights and token permutation; FlashInfer uses SGLang's existing top-k/top-p renormalization primitives and min-p predicate; deterministic logprob and greedy sampling use their native representations. - Keep opted-in device row indices in `SamplingBatchInfo`, including filter and merge, so mixed batches restrict dense work and transfer to requests that asked for a mask. - Pack a fixed-width tensor result and use the existing `map_device_tensors` asynchronous D2H path. This avoids a host synchronization to discover a data-dependent support width. - Emit factual `OK`, `TRUNCATED`, or `INVALID` producer status and reach TP/CP consensus through the existing process groups. - Apply exact policy in the scheduler: `TRUNCATED` aborts before token commit, while missing or inconsistent capture is an internal error. - Preserve the exact contract through normal serving, pipeline parallelism, and prefill/decode disaggregation. This PR intentionally does not expose approximate output. The follow-up #34037 adds an explicit bounded mode and a public per-token truncation signal. ## PR chain - Depends on #35204, which fixes generic no-insert KV cleanup used by the exact-overflow abort path. - This is part 2 of 3. - #34037 is retained as part 3 and will contain only bounded-mode policy and truncation propagation after this PR lands. Until #35204 merges, GitHub's full PR diff also contains that prerequisite. The incremental core change is commit `fd6b752d23`. ## Performance - Feature-off requests add Python flag/tuple plumbing only: no new tensor operation, dense allocation, D2H copy, PP payload, or TP/CP collective. - Feature-on work is limited to `R` opted-in rows. With vocabulary size `V` and capacity `C`, support capture is `O(R * V)` using current sampling primitives and token-ID transfer is fixed at `4 * R * C` bytes plus three scalar fields per row. - No merged SGLang sampling primitive exposes realized FlashInfer support directly; this PR reuses current primitives rather than introducing a custom kernel or generic capture framework. ## Validation - The final combined implementation passed 295 focused tests with 2 skips and 75 subtests on one H200 using the SGLang nightly development image. - Its H200 operator matrix passed 4,927 checks against independent support and selected-logprob oracles, including cutoff ties and min-p input isolation. - Seven end-to-end serving contracts passed, including exact overflow abort, top-p-only policy, finite-support/logprob consistency, and deterministic sampling preservation. - One-node H200 TP2/4/8 status-consensus probes passed. - On this extracted branch, repository pre-commit checks passed for every changed file, including the registered-test validator; Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. The extracted branch keeps the already-validated producer and exact-policy code. GitHub CI will validate the dependency split itself. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32076644687](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076644687)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32076644511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076644511)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Sampling] Add explicit bounded sampling-mask mode
signal.text: ## Why #27408 added SGLang's native sampling-mask response, but reconstructed support after sampling and used finite `top_k` as its safety bound. #33593, now merged in `main`, made top-p-only requests valid and exposed sampling masks through the OpenAI chat extension. The remaining contract must therefore be general: top-p/min-p support is data-dependent, and SGLang's threshold primitives retain every token tied at the cutoff, so even finite top-k does not bound realized support. This PR makes the response describe the distribution that actually sampled the token, then bounds only its transport. This is a general serving contract, not an RL-only path. ## Contract For the post-filter weights `w` used to sample token `y`, let `S = {i | w[i] > 0}` and `C = --sampling-mask-max-tokens`: - sampling itself is unchanged; - if `|S| <= C`, the returned token IDs are the complete support `S`; - exact mode is the default, so `|S| > C` aborts before `y` is committed; - `sampling_mask_mode="bounded"` opts into at most `C` IDs and reports `output_token_sampling_mask_truncated=true`; - bounded mode keeps the highest-weight prefix and retains `y` by replacing its final entry when necessary; - the selected-token logprob is always `log(w[y] / sum(w))` over the full realized support, never over the truncated return; - missing or internally inconsistent producer output is an internal error, not truncation. The cap changes metadata only. It never changes the sampling distribution. ## Design - Capture the producer's representation. PyTorch reuses its filtered weights and token permutation; FlashInfer uses SGLang's existing top-k/top-p renormalization primitives and min-p predicate; deterministic logprob sampling and greedy sampling use their native representations. - Keep internal results tensor-backed. `SamplingMaskOutput` is a dataclass following the existing result-holder `map_device_tensors`/async-D2H path; `_SamplingMaskCapture` is a sampler-private `NamedTuple`. - Maintain opted-in device row indices in `SamplingBatchInfo`, including filter/merge, so mixed batches restrict dense work and transfer to requested rows. - Emit factual `OK`, `TRUNCATED`, or `INVALID` status in the sampler, reach TP/CP consensus through the existing process groups, and apply exact/bounded policy in the scheduler. - Propagate the per-token truncation bit through streaming, multi-tokenizer output, sessions, PP, and PD disaggregation. PD reuses its existing 64-byte padded metadata row; the first two slots carry returned length and truncation. - Reuse the OpenAI chat sampling-mask path merged in #33593 and forward its `sampling_mask_mode` into the existing native request field. - Abort exact overflow before committing the sampled token and release every request-owned KV slot, including overlap-allocated slots without a committed token ID. ## Internal API changes - Private `Sampler._sample_from_probs` now returns sampled IDs plus optional producer capture data. - `top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_probs_torch` keeps its existing token-only behavior by default; a keyword-only opt-in returns already-computed filtered data for capture. - Private `_attach_*` helpers became `_build_*` because they now return a tensor holder. The post-hoc `_compute_sampling_mask_from_probs` reconstruction was removed because it was not the producer's source of truth. - Request fields are placed so existing positional constructors and the tokenized Rust wire layout do not shift. - The PD field changed from `output_token_sampling_mask_len` to `output_token_sampling_mask_metadata` because the same padded row now carries length and truncation. No layout class, one-use global size constant, or additional RDMA buffer is introduced. - Existing PP `get_logprob_*` helper names remain unchanged; only their logits-output payload is widened. - Existing optional backend KV-release hooks are used at the release site; no new base-worker lifecycle interface is added. No public sampling function is removed or renamed. ## Performance - Feature-off requests add Python flag/tuple plumbing only: no new tensor operation, dense allocation, D2H copy, PP tensor, or TP/CP collective. - Opted-in rows require dense `O(R * V)` support work because current sampling primitives produce dense weights. Packing transfers `4 * R * C + 12 * R` bytes. A fixed cap avoids a GPU-to-CPU synchronization to discover a data-dependent width; finite top-k is not a valid bound because cutoff ties are retained. - On one H200 at `V=128256`, `C=4096`, measured opt-in operator overhead was approximately 0.28-0.72 ms across FlashInfer joint, min-p, and PyTorch paths. - Dense temporary storage scaled with opted-in rows: approximately 1.7 MB at `R=1`, 54 MB at `R=32`, and 107 MB at `R=64`. Bounded D2H payload p50 was approximately 53-55 us from `R=1` through `R=64` (16 KB to 1.05 MB). - Same-node TP2/4/8 status consensus measured approximately 20-42 us across 1-1024 rows. ## Validation - 295 focused tests passed, 2 skipped, with 75 subtests on one H200 using `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682` and the rebased PR source. - Seven end-to-end H200 serving contracts passed on the rebased tree: finite support/logprob consistency, exact overflow abort, bounded truncation signal, top-p-only policy, OpenAI chat bounded-mode propagation, invalid-mode rejection, and deterministic sampling preservation. - A 4,927-check H200 operator matrix passed against independent support and selected-logprob oracles, including uniform cutoff ties and min-p input isolation. - One-node H200 TP2/4/8 collective probes passed. - Repository-native `pre-commit run --all-files` passed on current `main`, including registered-test validation, lint-checker tests, Rust formatting, and workspace clippy. `git diff --check` passed. The existing CUDA/AMD end-to-end sampling-mask test remains registered in its current CI suites. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32076643369](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076643369)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32076642814](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076642814)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: model: fix Step3 (step3_vl) crash on configs without pad_token_id
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving `stepfun-ai/step3` (`Step3VLForConditionalGeneration`, a 321B MoE VLM) crashes at model init: ``` AttributeError: 'Step3TextConfig' object has no attribute 'pad_token_id' ``` `Step3TextModel.__init__` reads `config.pad_token_id`, but `Step3TextConfig` defines only `bos_token_id` / `eos_token_id`, so it fails before any weights load. (Baseline: P1 build #4780.) ## Modifications `models/step3_vl.py`: default the field to `None` — `self.padding_idx = getattr(config, "pad_token_id", None)`. `padding_idx` is only assigned in this class (never used, not passed to `embed_tokens`), so `None` is safe. This clears the reported `AttributeError`. ## Accuracy Test Not run. `stepfun-ai/step3` is 321B params (~642 GB in bf16) and does not fit the available hardware (8 × 24 GB = 192 GB), so it cannot be loaded here at any TP — load / generation / gsm8k were not executed. The change is a targeted fix for the exact reported config-init crash (static analysis); further issues may surface on a host large enough to hold the weights. The same code path (`models/step3_vl.py`) already serves the smaller sibling `stepfun-ai/Step3-VL-10B`. ## Speed Test and Profiling N/A — config-init crash fix; no change to the compute path. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32075838408](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32075838408)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32075838503](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32075838503)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

The test skipped the remote restore when a self-hosted runner already had `.pt` files under `/tmp/sglang_precision_baselines`. A stale baseline captured replicated layer-entry tensors after FlashInfer fusion failed to initialize, while the target contained TP-partial tensors. Treating both as partial produced the approximately 8x mismatch. The historical initialization failure is tracked by [FlashInfer #3676](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3676) and [SGLang #30875](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30875), and was mitigated by [SGLang #30580](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30580). 2. After a clean fused refresh, the comparator still observed rank-local BF16 buffers before fused all-reduce and residual RMSNorm. CPU-side reduction of those buffers is not the kernel's semantic output and drifted across runners. Current H200 runs initialize TRTLLM fusion on all eight ranks. This PR keeps fusion enabled and moves the comparison to `self_attn.inputs.hidden_states`, the replicated value consumed by attention after `prepare_attn()`. ## Fix - Always restore a signature-compatible remote baseline, atomically replace local tensors, and include the capture filters, TP size, and fusion backend in the signature. - Compare only the replicated post-fusion attention input. Keep layer-entry captures only as a per-layer/step/rank guard that rejects fusion fallback. - Make ordinary `/rerun-test` read-only. Add a maintainer-only, in-repo H200 refresh path: `/rerun-test --refresh-precision-baseline test/registered/debug_utils/test_nightly_precision_regression.py`. Serving runtime and all-reduce implementation code are unchanged. ## Verification - [Cross-runner Nightly comparator](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31862539092): passed all 33 post-fusion records with `max_rel_diff=0.0`. - [Cleanup-head baseline refresh](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893911079): fusion initialized on all eight ranks and the guarded refresh passed. - [Cleanup-head read-only comparator](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31894139007): restored the refreshed baseline, passed a non-empty comparison, and did not publish. - All 42 baseline-store unit tests and changed-file pre-commit checks passed. ## Accuracy Tests No model-forward changes. The registered 8-GPU H200 test exercises the actual fused path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; serving performance is unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32056494927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32056494927)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32056494453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32056494453)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] Prefill FLOPs estimate ignores `prefix_lens`, so `est. prefill TFLOPS/s` degenerates into 1/latency across chunked-prefill chunks
signal.text: ## Checklist - [x] I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help. - [x] The bug has not been fixed in the latest version (checked `main` @ `77c90e7e54`). - [x] Please use English, otherwise it will be closed. ## Describe the bug `SchedulerMetricsReporter._estimate_prefill_perf()` ignores the per-request prefix lengths and collapses all extend tokens in the batch into one fictitious sequence. It only reads `extend_lens` and never consults `batch.prefix_lens`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py#L456-L480 ```python tokens = max(0, int(sum(batch.extend_lens))) if tokens == 0: return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 # Causal prefill token-context product. context_product = tokens * (tokens + 1) / 2.0 flops = ( tokens * self._linear_flops_per_token + self._attn_dot_flops_coeff * context_product ) read_bytes = ( tokens * self._weight_read_bytes_per_token + tokens * self._qkv_act_bytes_per_token + tokens * self._prefill_attn_act_read_per_token ) ``` `extend_lens` is the length of the **current chunk only** — not the cumulative sequence length. See `prepare_for_extend`, where `prefix_lens` and `extend_lens` are built as two separate lists and the invariant is asserted explicitly: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L2364-L2365 ```python prefix_lens = [len(r.prefix_indices) for r in reqs] extend_lens = [r.extend_range.length for r in reqs] ... assert seq_len - pre_len == req.extend_range.length # line 2414 ``` So `batch.prefix_lens` is available on the same object and is simply not used by the estimator. There is a second error in the same formula: for a multi-request batch, applying one triangular number to `sum(extend_lens)` invents attention pairs between different requests. For example, two independent 100-token prefills have `2 × 100 × 101 / 2 = 10,100` causal pairs, while the current code estimates `200 × 201 / 2 = 20,100`. ### Consequence 1: with a fixed chunk size the numerator is a constant The reported value is `flops / gap_latency`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py#L592-L604 ```python flops, _, _ = self._estimate_prefill_perf(batch) tflops_per_s = flops / gap_latency / 1e12 msg += f", est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU): {tflops_per_s:.2f}" ``` Because `flops` depends only on `sum(extend_lens)`, every chunk of a long request under a fixed `--chunked-prefill-size` produces the **exact same numerator**. The log line therefore reduces to ``` est. prefill TFLOPS/s (chunk k) = C / gap_latency_k (C constant) ``` i.e. an inverse-latency plot wearing a TFLOPS label. Later chunks generally take longer as their prefix grows, so the number tends to decay even though the GPU is doing more useful work per chunk. Scheduler jitter, concurrency, and the use of an inter-log wall-clock interval mean strict monotonicity is not guaranteed; the deterministic problem is that the numerator remains constant and the metric is proportional only to `1 / gap_latency`. This is the opposite of the intended signal, and it breaks precisely the "trend analysis" use case the docs recommend the metric for: > These metrics are estimates intended for observability and trend analysis. > — `docs/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx` ### Consequence 2: the dense-attention undercount grows linearly with prefix length For a chunk of `c` tokens at prefix `P`, the true causal pair count is `c·P + c(c+1)/2`, while the code computes `c(c+1)/2`. The undercount factor is ``` 1 + 2P/(c+1) ``` With `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, the attention term is undercounted by ~33x at `P` = 128K, ~65x at 256K, and ~129x at 512K. These factors apply to the attention component, not necessarily to the estimator's total FLOPs, which also includes a prefix-independent linear term. The same defect applies to any prefill served from a prefix-cache hit, not just chunked prefill — a request with a 100K-token cache hit and a 200-token extend is scored as a 200-token prefill from scratch. ### Consequence 3: `read_bytes` omits the prefix KV cache read entirely Every term in the prefill `read_bytes` is `tokens * <per-token constant>`. There is no prefix-dependent KV-cache read term, so prefill contributes no KV-cache read traffic for the cached prefix at all. `sglang:estimated_read_bytes_per_gpu_total` and any MBU derived from it are therefore underestimated for chunked prefill and prefix-cache hits. The size of the error depends on the kernel's tiling and cache reuse, KV layout, cache dtype, and whether the intended metric represents logical traffic or actual HBM traffic. ### Consequence 4: the decode path already does this correctly `_estimate_decode_perf()` right below it uses the full context for both FLOPs and KV read bytes, which suggests the prefill path is an oversight rather than a deliberate simplification: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py#L482-L506 ```python total_context = float(_decode_total_seq_lens(batch)) flops = ( tokens * self._linear_flops_per_token + self._attn_dot_flops_coeff * total_context ) read_bytes = ( ... + total_context * self._kv_cache_bytes_per_token ) ``` Note also that this fallback branch is what essentially every deployment hits: `_prefill_sol_suffix()` is an unconditional `return ""` in the base class (line 507) and no subclass overrides it anywhere in the tree, so the `sol_suffix` short-circuit never fires. ## Observed impact Setup: GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), 8×B300 SXM, TP8, FP8 KV cache, `index_topk=2048`, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--enable-mfu-metrics`. Observed behaviour in this run: `est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU)` fell monotonically across the chunks of a single long request, which initially read as "prefill is becoming memory bound at long context". That interpretation is invalid: with a fixed chunk size the estimated numerator is frozen, so changes in the reported value reflect only changes in the inter-log interval. Other runs need not be strictly monotonic because that interval also contains scheduler and concurrency noise. Analytical/model-based decomposition of one 8192-token chunk (not measured per-kernel timings; absolute times depend on the model configuration and efficiency assumptions): | prefix `P` | chunk time | MoE+linear | sparse MLA attn | DSA indexer GEMM | logits + top-k | KV dequant | reported TFLOPS (rel.) | achieved TFLOPS (rel.) | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 0 | 56 ms | 15.6 ms | 36.6 ms | 2.3 ms | 0.9 ms | 0.0 ms | 1.00 | 1.00 | | 32K | 88 ms | 15.6 ms | 41.9 ms | 20.8 ms | 8.5 ms | 1.0 ms | 0.63 | 0.92 | | 128K | 168 ms | 15.6 ms | 41.9 ms | 76.2 ms | 31.0 ms | 3.3 ms | 0.33 | 0.91 | | 512K | 489 ms | 15.6 ms | 41.9 ms | 297.9 ms | 121.2 ms | 12.5 ms | 0.11 | 0.90 | In this model, the reported metric drops ~9x while the modeled achieved FLOP/s remains within 10%. The modeled growth is dominated by the DSA indexer, which the estimator does not account for. This table illustrates the mechanism; the source-level reproduction above does not depend on these modeled timings. ## Additional gaps in `_init_estimated_perf_constants` (same metric, separate root causes) These are independent of the `prefix_lens` bug but make the absolute magnitude unusable for MLA / MoE / sparse-attention models: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/77c90e7e54/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py#L372-L455 1. **MLA is charged using dense MHA/GQA shapes.** `attn_linear_flops` uses `2·hidden·head_dim·(n_q + 2·n_kv) + 2·hidden·head_dim·n_q`. For GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3-class MLA configs, `ModelConfig._derive_model_shapes` sets `head_dim = 256`, while `num_key_value_heads` defaults to `num_attention_heads` when the config does not provide it. This does not represent the actual MLA projection path through fields such as `kv_lora_rank`, `q_lora_rank`, and `qk_rope_head_dim`. For the configuration above it substantially misestimates the projection cost; the magnitude and even the net direction of the full linear-layer error are architecture- and implementation-dependent. 2. **MoE is charged as a dense FFN.** `mlp_flops = 6 · hidden · intermediate_size` uses `hf_text_config.intermediate_size` (the dense width) for all `num_hidden_layers`. The per-token MoE cost is `moe_intermediate_size × num_experts_per_tok` plus shared experts, and `first_k_dense_replace` layers differ from MoE layers. Neither is modeled, so the constant is off by a large factor in an unpredictable direction. 3. **Sparse attention is not modeled.** For DSA/NSA models the main attention is capped at `index_topk` keys per query, so `context_product` should saturate rather than grow — see `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.forward_extend`, which builds a `page_table` of `index_topk` entries per query token, and `SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` (default 2048) which gates the dense path. Conversely, the indexer's `fp8_mqa_logits` scan over the *whole* context is unaccounted for, and because the indexer submodules are `ReplicatedLinear`, that cost is not divided by TP size. At long context this term dominates per-chunk time. ## Reproduction ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <any model> \ --tp-size 8 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --enable-metrics --enable-mfu-metrics \ --context-length 262144 ``` Send one long request (e.g. 128K input tokens) and watch the `Prefill batch` log lines for that request: ``` Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 8192, ..., est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU): <A> Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 8192, ..., est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU): <B> Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 8192, ..., est. prefill TFLOPS/s (per GPU): <C> ... ``` In an otherwise idle single-request run, the values will typically trend downward while `#new-token` stays at 8192 on every line. Strict `A > B > C > ...` ordering is not required to reproduce the estimator bug because `gap_latency` is an asynchronous scheduler interval. Two checks that isolate the bug from any real hardware effect: 1. Multiplying each line's reported TFLOPS by that line's inter-log interval yields the same product, up to log rounding — confirming the numerator is constant across equal-sized chunks. 2. Send a request with a ~100% prefix-cache hit plus a short extend. The reported TFLOPS is computed purely from the extend length and ignores the cached prefix the attention kernels actually read. ## Suggested fix Minimal correctness fix — use the `prefix_lens` that is already on the batch, and add the missing KV read term: ```python def _estimate_prefill_perf(self, batch) -> Tuple[float, float, float]: if batch is None or batch.extend_lens is None: return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 extend_lens = batch.extend_lens prefix_lens = batch.prefix_lens or [0] * len(extend_lens) tokens = 0 context_product = 0.0 context_kv_tokens = 0.0 for c, p in zip(extend_lens, prefix_lens): if c <= 0: continue tokens += c # Causal pairs for this request: chunk-vs-prefix plus chunk-vs-chunk. context_product += c * p + c * (c + 1) / 2.0 # One possible logical-traffic convention: count one stream of the KV # context per chunk. This is not a measurement of actual HBM traffic. context_kv_tokens += p + c / 2.0 if tokens == 0: return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 flops = ( tokens * self._linear_flops_per_token + self._attn_dot_flops_coeff * context_product ) read_bytes = ( tokens * self._weight_read_bytes_per_token + tokens * self._qkv_act_bytes_per_token + tokens * self._prefill_attn_act_read_per_token + context_kv_tokens * self._kv_cache_bytes_per_token ) ... ``` `prefix_lens` is safe to zip against `extend_lens`: both are assigned together in `prepare_for_extend` and both are appended in parallel by `mix_with_running`, which pushes the running request's full context into `prefix_lens` alongside its `[1] * running_bs` extend entry. So the same patch also fixes mixed prefill+decode batches, where today the appended decode tokens contribute `1` to `context_product` and nothing to the KV read. The per-request attention pair-count above is exact for standard dense causal self-attention; it is not an exact whole-model FLOPs estimate and does not apply unchanged to sparse attention. The KV `read_bytes` term is only one possible logical-traffic convention, and maintainers should first define what the metric is intended to represent. `p + c/2` approximates one stream of the logical KV context per chunk, while using `context_product` models one KV-vector read per query/key pair, similar to the convention used by `_estimate_decode_perf`. Neither necessarily equals actual HBM traffic: real traffic depends on query tiling, on-chip and L2 reuse, fused paths, the model-specific KV layout, and cache dtype. Either convention at least accounts for the currently omitted prefix, but it should be documented explicitly. Two follow-ups worth considering, either here or as separate work: - Cap the per-query context at `index_topk` for sparse-attention models and add the indexer scan term, so DSA/NSA numbers stop being dominated by unmodeled work. `ModelConfig` already exposes `index_head_dim` / the DSA fields needed for this. - Make `_linear_flops_per_token` MoE- and MLA-aware (`moe_intermediate_size`, `num_experts_per_tok`, `n_shared_experts`, `first_k_dense_replace`, `kv_lora_rank`, `q_lora_rank`), or otherwise document that the absolute value is not meaningful for these architectures. Separately, dividing by `gap_latency` is documented in-code as a known mismatch (the comment at lines 592-597 notes it is "decoupled from this forward's execution"). Since `_prefill_sol_suffix` never returns content in-tree, that caveat applies to every deployment. Using the device-timer span when `ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER` is set would make the wall-clock branch meaningful too. ## Environment - SGLang: `main` @ `77c90e7e54` (also present in v0.5.17, v0.5.16, v0.5.15; introduced in #19395 "MFU metrics in Prometheus" and carried through the `SchedulerMetricsReporter` refactor) - Model: GLM-5.2 NVFP4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), 78 layers, 64 heads, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, `index_topk=2048` - Hardware: 8× B300 SXM, TP8 - The defect is architecture-independent and reviewable from the source alone; the GLM-5.2/DSA details only affect how large the discrepancy gets.
