signal.title: [Bug] DSPARK silently corrupts identifiers on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, making speculative decoding unsafe
signal.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug

Summary

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, SGLang’s DSPARK speculative decoding silently introduces single-character corruptions into identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt:

kimi-k3 → kimi-kw nova-x7 → nova-7 apollo-n9 → apollo-n11

The same server, weights, prompts, and launch configuration—with only speculative decoding disabled—produces zero such corruptions across thousands of grounded identifier tokens.

The corruption rate increases with the DSPARK verify-window width:

--speculative-dspark-block-size | speculative_num_draft_tokens | Temp 0 | Temp 1 -- | -- | -- | -- 6 | 7 | 1.03% | 0.82% 5 | 6 | 0.32% | 0.77% 1 | 2 | 0.00% | 0.00% Speculation disabled | — | 0.00% | 0.00%

Aggregated across both block_size=1 runs:

  • Temperature 0: 0 / 4561
  • Temperature 1: 0 / 3701

Using the rule of three, the corresponding approximate 95% upper bounds are:

  • Temperature 0: <0.066%
  • Temperature 1: <0.081%

This contrasts with the 1.03% observed rate at block_size=6, temperature 0.

Examples of corrupted identifiers

Malformed forms observed at block_size=6, temperature 0:

kimi-kw -> kimi-k3 (x5) kimi-k2 -> kimi-k3 (x3) kimi-k7 -> kimi-k3 (x2) apollo-n11 -> apollo-n9 (x2) nova-12 -> nova-x7 (x2) wq-7f2e -> wq-7f2b (x2) kimi-kw2 -> kimi-k3 kimi-v2 -> kimi-k3 kimi-k11 -> kimi-k3 apollo-n12 -> apollo-n9 nova-7 -> nova-x7 nova-v7 -> nova-x7 wq-7f2e2 -> wq-7f2b

These are not malformed responses or obvious decoding failures. They are plausible-looking, single-character-wrong identifiers embedded in otherwise normal output.

Expected behavior

At temperature 0, DSPARK should emit the same greedy token sequence as the target model without speculative decoding.

A draft token should only be committed if it matches the corresponding target prediction. On mismatch, DSPARK should emit the target prediction instead.

Therefore, enabling DSPARK should not change grounded identifiers from:

kimi-k3

to:

kimi-kw

when the non-speculative target forward selects the correct token.

Actual behavior

With multi-position DSPARK verification enabled:

  • Grounded identifiers are silently corrupted.
  • The issue reproduces at temperature 0.
  • The issue requires or is strongly amplified by heterogeneous concurrent batching.
  • The rate increases with verify-window width.
  • No request error or warning is produced.
  • The finish reason remains normal.
  • Disabling speculation eliminates the corruption.
  • Reducing DSPARK to block_size=1 eliminates the corruption.

Hypotheses investigated and ruled out

1. Lossy accept/verify rule

This does not appear to be the cause.

Both accept_greedy and accept_greedy_triton in:

sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/dspark/dspark_accept.py

delegate to compute_dflash_correct_drafts_and_bonus in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py

The relevant logic is:

matches = candidates[:, 1:] == target_predict[:, :-1] correct_len = matches.to(torch.int32).cumprod(dim=1).sum(dim=1) bonus = target_predict[torch.arange(bs, ...), correct_len]

Every committed token should therefore be either:

  1. An accepted draft token that compared equal to target_predict; or
  2. The bonus token, which is taken directly from target_predict.

A mismatching draft token should not be able to leak into the output.

This implies that the corrupted emitted tokens are likely themselves present in target_predict. In other words, the target verify forward appears to be producing incorrect logits or incorrect token alignment.

2. Ragged verify-window misalignment

accept_greedy performs:

torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( bs, verify_num_draft_tokens )

A dense reshape could misalign tokens if requests had different verify lengths.

However, SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE defaults to static. In static mode, resolve_ragged_verify_layout returns None, and verify lengths are uniform.

Therefore, the rectangular reshape is expected to be valid for this reproduction.

3. Numerical noise or batch-shape-dependent reductions

We tested three separate interventions. Each was verified to engage, and none removed the corruption.

FP32 LM head

Enabled:

--enable-fp32-lm-head

Engagement was confirmed empirically:

  • Before the change, 65.5% of recorded margins fell on the 0.25 BF16 grid.
  • After the change, 0% did.
  • There were zero exact ties across 34,420 records.

The typo rate did not improve.

Deterministic FP32 MoE reduction

We forced:

use_atomic_add = False

so the already-passed:

use_fp32_reduce = True

would engage.

In:

sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_wna16_marlin.py

the FP32 temporary buffer is allocated only under:

if use_fp32_reduce and not use_atomic_add:

This provides a structural confirmation that the path was active.

The observed rates remained approximately:

  • Temperature 0: 1.03%
  • Temperature 1: 0.82%

Tie epsilon on sampled accept path

Adding a tie epsilon to the sampled acceptance path had no effect.

More generally, an identifier repeated verbatim several times in the prompt should usually be a high-margin prediction. Low-order numerical noise would not be expected to repeatedly transform such identifiers into plausible alternatives.

The non-speculative control also varies in free-form prose between temperature-0 runs—likely due to prefix-cache or chunked-prefill effects—but it never corrupts a grounded identifier.

4. Draft/target gamma mismatch

The CLI can override the draft checkpoint’s declared gamma with only a warning:

DSpark gamma mismatch: using gamma=6 (from speculative_num_draft_tokens=7) but draft config block_size=5.

This occurs in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_config.py

The draft module itself obtains gamma from the checkpoint:

self.gamma = int(dspark_config.resolve_gamma(...))

in:

sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py

This means the draft module and worker may disagree about the verify-window width.

However, running with block_size=5:

  • Makes the configured values agree
  • Removes the warning
  • Still reproduces the bug

Observed rates at block_size=5 were:

  • Temperature 0: 0.32%
  • Temperature 1: 0.77%

Therefore, the gamma mismatch is not the root cause of this corruption, although the silent override may be worth hardening as a separate issue.

5. Draft-side kernels

SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL only gates the draft forward.

Under a correct speculative verification rule, draft quality may affect acceptance and performance, but it should not affect temperature-0 correctness. Incorrect draft tokens should be rejected in favor of the target prediction.

Therefore, a draft-only kernel failure does not explain committed token corruption unless there is also a target-verification or alignment bug.

Suspected fault area

The following is a hypothesis, not yet a verified root cause.

Given that:

  1. The accept rule appears to emit only target_predict;
  2. The corruption reproduces at temperature 0;
  3. The corruption disappears at a two-position verify window;
  4. The rate generally increases with verify-window width;
  5. Multiple numerical-determinism interventions had no effect; and
  6. The issue depends on concurrent heterogeneous batching,

the likely fault is in the target verify forward for multi-position DSPARK verification, especially for in-block positions t >= 1.

Potential areas include:

  • Intra-block causal masking
  • Position-ID construction or indexing
  • KV-cache placement for draft positions
  • Request-to-token mapping under heterogeneous batching
  • CUDA graph replay metadata for TARGET_VERIFY
  • Batch-slot reuse or stale per-request metadata
  • dsv4 attention behavior during multi-token verification

The current evidence suggests the target verification pass is computing incorrect logits or associating correct logits with the wrong request/position.

We have not yet isolated the specific kernel or metadata transition.

Suggested next diagnostics

A useful first datapoint would be:

--speculative-dspark-block-size 2

This would help distinguish between:

  • Failure beginning at the first genuinely multi-position verify step; and
  • Error probability accumulating with larger verify windows.

Other useful comparisons may include:

  1. DSPARK with CUDA graphs disabled.
  2. DSPARK with the hierarchical cache disabled.
  3. DSPARK with radix cache and chunked prefill disabled.
  4. An alternate attention backend, if DeepSeek-V4-Flash supports one.
  5. Capturing target_predict before acceptance and comparing it against independent one-token target forwards.
  6. Logging request IDs, verify positions, position IDs, and KV locations for the first divergent token.

Workaround

Both of the following avoid the observed corruption:

Option 1: Disable speculative decoding

This is the safest workaround.

Option 2: Use block_size=1

--speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1

This produced zero true typos across:

  • 4,561 grounded identifiers at temperature 0
  • 3,701 grounded identifiers at temperature 1

However, this sacrifices most of the speculative speedup, so it is a mitigation rather than a practical fix.

Until the multi-position verification issue is resolved, DSPARK should not be used with DeepSeek-V4-Flash for workloads where exact token reproduction matters.

Reproduction notes

DeepGEMM JIT warmup

Changing:

--speculative-dspark-block-size

changes num_tokens_per_req and invalidates the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache.

The first launch after changing this value may compile approximately 16,000 shapes and exceed a 3,600-second readiness budget. If the process is killed during warmup, it may look like an unrelated startup failure.

Please allow additional warmup time when changing the block size.

Log probabilities unavailable

DSPARK currently rejects:

"return_logprob": true

with:

DFLASH speculative decoding does not support return_logprob yet

Therefore, per-token target margins cannot currently be collected over HTTP on the affected speculative arm.

Severity

This is a silent data-corruption issue, not only a quality or performance regression.

The generated response is well-formed, and the corrupted identifier often looks plausible. Downstream systems therefore have no reliable way to distinguish the incorrect value from an intended value.

For DeepSeek-V4-Flash, this makes multi-position DSPARK speculative decoding unsafe for exact-identifier and tool-use workloads.

### Reproduction

Reproduction

The corruption usually requires concurrent, heterogeneous batching. A single request in isolation may not reproduce it. The script below sends four byte-identical target requests and four variable-length distractor requests per round.

1. Launch the affected DSPARK configuration

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \ --tp 4 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 6 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

2. Save the reproduction script

Save the following code as dspark_typo_repro.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Concurrency typo probe for one model and temperature.""" import collections import concurrent.futures import json import os import re import time import urllib.error import urllib.request MODEL = os.environ["TEST_MODEL"] TEMP = float(os.environ.get("TEST_TEMP", "0")) ROUNDS = int(os.environ.get("TEST_ROUNDS", "30")) BASE = os.environ.get("TEST_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:30000") URL = f"{BASE}/v1/chat/completions" IDS = [ "kimi-k3", "nova-x7", "atlas-j9", "wq-7f2b", "zeta-r1", "apollo-n9", ] CTX = " ".join( f"event{i}=ok latency={i % 37}ms owner=team{i % 9}" for i in range(350) ) PROMPT = ( f"Analyze this deployment history and write a 6-section operational report. " f"{CTX}\n" f"Canonical identifiers: {', '.join(IDS)}. " "Include a table and prose recap. " "Use every identifier at least four times, always verbatim; " "do not invent or normalize identifiers." ) RX = re.compile(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*-[a-z0-9]+", re.I) def lev(a, b): prev = list(range(len(b) + 1)) for i, x in enumerate(a, 1): cur = [i] for j, y in enumerate(b, 1): cur.append( min( cur[-1] + 1, prev[j] + 1, prev[j - 1] + (x != y), ) ) prev = cur return prev[-1] def ask(prompt=PROMPT, max_tokens=700, retries=5): body = json.dumps( { "model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": TEMP, "top_p": 1.0, } ).encode() for n in range(retries): request = urllib.request.Request( URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=300) as response: result = json.load(response) return result["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or "" except urllib.error.HTTPError as error: if error.code not in (429, 503) or n + 1 == retries: raise time.sleep(0.3 * (n + 1)) raise RuntimeError("retries exhausted") wrong = collections.Counter() truncations = collections.Counter() error_types = collections.Counter() exact = 0 grounded = 0 responses = 0 errors = 0 typo_responses = 0 started = time.time() with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool: for rnd in range(ROUNDS): futures = [pool.submit(ask) for _ in range(4)] # Variable-length distractors perturb server-side batch composition. for j in range(4): length = 50 + ((rnd * 67 + j * 97) % 500) distractor = "Summarize: " + " ".join( f"word{k}" for k in range(length) ) futures.append(pool.submit(ask, distractor, 128)) for future in futures[:4]: try: text = future.result() responses += 1 except Exception as error: errors += 1 error_types[type(error).__name__] += 1 continue response_has_typo = False for token in ( match.lower().rstrip(".,;:") for match in RX.findall(text) ): if token in IDS: exact += 1 grounded += 1 continue distance, target = min( (lev(token, identifier), identifier) for identifier in IDS ) if distance <= 2: grounded += 1 if any(identifier.startswith(token) for identifier in IDS): # Prefixes are output-limit truncations, not typos. truncations[(token, target, distance)] += 1 else: wrong[(token, target, distance)] += 1 response_has_typo = True typo_responses += response_has_typo for future in futures[4:]: try: future.result() except Exception: pass print( f"MODEL={MODEL} TEMP={TEMP} rounds={ROUNDS} " f"responses={responses} errors={errors} " f"errtypes={dict(error_types)} " f"elapsed={time.time() - started:.1f}s" ) print( f"grounded_ids={grounded} exact={exact} " f"true_typos={sum(wrong.values())} " f"typo_responses={typo_responses} " f"rate={(sum(wrong.values()) / grounded if grounded else 0):.4%} " f"truncations={sum(truncations.values())}" ) print("typo_forms:", dict(wrong.most_common(20)) or "NONE")

A true typo is a token with Levenshtein distance 1–2 from a canonical identifier that is not a prefix of one. Prefixes are counted separately as output-limit truncations.

3. Run the reproduction at temperature 0

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \ TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ TEST_TEMP=0 \ TEST_ROUNDS=30 \ python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

4. Repeat at temperature 1

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \ TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ TEST_TEMP=1 \ TEST_ROUNDS=30 \ python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

5. Run the non-speculative control

Relaunch the server with all --speculative-* flags removed while leaving every other launch argument unchanged. Repeat both commands above. This control produced zero true typos.

6. Test the block-size workaround

Relaunch DSPARK with a block size of 1: 

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \ --tp 4 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

Repeat the temperature-0 and temperature-1 tests. This configuration also produced zero true typos.

Expected result

At temperature 0, DSPARK should produce the same greedy token sequence as non-speculative decoding. All identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt should be emitted without modification.

Observed result

With --speculative-dspark-block-size 6, the output silently contains plausible single-character corruptions such as: 

kimi-k3 -> kimi-kw nova-x7 -> nova-7 apollo-n9 -> apollo-n11 wq-7f2b -> wq-7f2e

In one temperature-0 run, 23 of 2,224 grounded identifiers were corrupted (1.0342%), affecting 15 of 120 target responses. The same test produced zero corruptions with speculative decoding disabled and with DSPARK block size 1.

Reproduction note

Changing --speculative-dspark-block-size changes num_tokens_per_req and may invalidate the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache. The first launch after changing the block size can require a long recompilation warmup. Allow enough startup time to prevent the server from being killed before it becomes ready.

### Environment Run this **inside the same Python environment/container used to launch the affected SGLang server**: ```bash python3 -m sglang.check_env 2>&1 | tee sglang_check_env.txt ``` Then paste the **complete command output verbatim** into that field, preferably wrapped as: ```text ``` Do not substitute the manually listed environment details; the maintainers explicitly require the actual `check_env` output.

signal.title: Improve M3 performance on MI350
signal.text: ## Motivation Improve M3 performance on MI350. ## Modifications - Adds AITER FlyDSL MXFP8 MoE support, including pre-shuffled gate/up weights and E8M0 scales, OAI-SwiGLU activation handling, and fused shared-expert execution. - Adds selectable dense MXFP8 linear backends through `SGLANG_MXFP8_LINEAR_BACKEND`: - `auto`/`aiter`: native blockwise MXFP8 via `torch._scaled_mm` - `triton`: existing `dot_scaled` implementation - `bf16`: cached BF16 weight dequantization with hipBLASLt - Reduces decode overhead by: - Skipping redundant sparse KV-cache writes when fusion already populated the cache. - Avoiding unnecessary top-k ID sanitization when expert parallelism is disabled. - Fixes AITER top-k handling for fused shared experts and respects the configured gate/up layout. - Enables MiniMax-M3 shared-expert fusion on supported ROCm devices (gfx942 or newer), while preserving existing EP and DeepEP compatibility guards. - Allows the AITER MoE runner for MXFP8 on gfx950 and validates that `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is enabled when explicitly selected. - Applies the same ROCm shared-expert support to the MiniMax-M3-VL model. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend bf16 \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ## Accuracy Tests baseline ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 227.1s | 1485 tok/s | 337K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.61% truncated_rate = 10.39% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` this pr ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 151.2s | 2231 tok/s | 337K tokens * score = 88.63% stop_rate = 89.99% truncated_rate = 10.01% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - signal.title: [Spec] Relay ngram accept tokens through the FutureMap
signal.text: Under overlap, ngram carries `accept_tokens` / `accept_lens` across iterations on `batch.spec_info` to feed next iteration's CPU-side draft prep. These tensors are written by the forward stream at the end of verify, but when a request finishes, `NgramVerifyInput.filter_batch` gathers them on the schedule stream while that forward may still be in flight -- a cross-stream read of a shared buffer before it is written. The stale values reach the host at draft prep and crash the embedding gather one iteration later. Only the coarse WAR fence ordered this edge incidentally (the ngram special case in #35059). Fix: relay the state through the FutureMap, same as eagle's `future_indices` pattern -- verify stashes `accept_tokens` / `accept_lens` into pool-indexed bufs; `filter_batch` / `merge_batch` only slice `future_indices`; next iteration's resolve gathers the bufs on the forward stream, in-order after the stash. With the schedule stream no longer touching forward-produced buffers, the coarse-fence special case is removed and ngram runs on the fine-grained fence again. Verified: `test_spec_ngram.py` 18 tests OK, including a stall-amplified run that reproduced the race 100% before this change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32069637728](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32069637728)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32069637688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32069637688)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [GDN] Add MTP cache mode for final-state recompute, with FlashInfer kernel integration and overlapped CUDA-graph state recovery
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Summary This PR turns `--gdn-mtp-cache-mode none` into a production-viable, high-performance path for GDN (Gated DeltaNet) MTP speculative decoding. `none` mode `replaces the GDN` (Gated DeltaNet) speculative-decode target-verify path — which today writes a full [V, K] recurrent state to a post-verify state recompute. So only the per-token recurrence inputs (`post-conv k, v, and the α/β gates`) are stored during the target verify forward stage and uses them to recover the single accepted state h_K by replaying the recurrence from the committed h_0 after verify. The recompute, then, sits on the decode critical path. Here we make it effectively free on Blackwell by (1) an output-only WY verify kernel, (2) a FlashInfer state-pool recovery kernel that reads its inputs zero-copy, (3) overlapping the recovery on a side stream behind the next step's draft compute, and (4) capturing it into per-bucket CUDA graphs. A Triton recurrence path preserves none mode off the FlashInfer / state-pool hardware. ## Motivation GDN MTP target-verify must, for each accepted draft, advance the linear-attention recurrent state. In `full` mode (the prior default), the intermediate state S_t is cached at every draft position so the accepted state can be scattered out after verify. `none` mode drops the cache: verify emits output only, and the single accepted state h_K = S_{accept_len} is recomputed from the committed h_0 afterwards. This **recovers the memory but introduces a recurrence replay on the critical path** — done eagerly it costs latency and throughput, partially cancelling the win. This PR removes that cost, so none mode keeps the memory savings and outweights the full-mode throughput. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> This PR adds the none branch of `--gdn-mtp-cache-mode` and the following strategies that makes it fast: - **Mode plumbing**. `--gdn-mtp-cache-mode none` is threaded through server args and the GDN/Mamba token pool. In none mode the pool skips the per-draft intermediate_ssm allocation (the intermediate-state cache used by full) and keeps only conv-window rollback state. full stays the default, unchanged. - **Accepted-state recovery (replay the recurrence)**. After verify commits accept_len, `_no_cache_mtp_recompute` replays the gated delta-rule recurrence from the committed h_0 over the contiguous accepted prefix [0, accept_len), and writes only the final accepted state h_K back into the live SSM pool - **FlashInfer output-only verify kernel (SM100+)**. On the bf16 state pool, none-mode verify routes to FlashInfer's WY output-only kernel `gated_delta_rule_mtp_wy_output_only` ([flashinfer #3720](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3720)): a single launch over all T draft tokens via a chunked-prefill-style T×T GEMM + log-depth Neumann inverse on tensor cores, run with disable_state_update. - **FlashInfer recovery kernel (SM100+)**. Recovery uses `gated_delta_rule_mtp` in recovery mode ([flashinfer #3502](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3502)) to replay the accepted prefix into the state pool and scatter h_K per request. - **Zero-copy recovery inputs**. The verify conv writes its post-conv output straight into a persistent token-major buffer, and recovery reads k/v as strided views of that buffer. - **Side-stream overlap**. Recovery is issued on a dedicated CUDA stream so it overlaps the next step's draft compute - **Per-bucket CUDA-graph capture**. The FlashInfer recovery is captured into per-batch-size CUDA graphs at warmup and replayed on the side stream — bucket-padded to a captured size. - **Triton fallback (portability)**. Off the FlashInfer / state-pool path (SM90, or a non-FlashInfer decode kernel), recovery uses the Triton recurrence recover kernel with a flat k/v stash. ## Accuracy Tests Server start: ``` export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 export NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 export NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1 export SGL_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=false export SGLANG_ENABLE_FLASHINFER_GEMM=true export SGLANG_LOG_FORWARD_ITERS=1 export SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=/profiles export SGLANG_GDN_WY_NATIVE_T=1 export SGLANG_GDN_WY_NATIVE_AB=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --served-model-name nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \ --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 1 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend trtllm_mha \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --mamba-scheduler-strategy no_buffer --disable-radix-cache \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --max-prefill-tokens 32768 --cuda-graph-max-bs 512 \ --max-running-requests 512 --scheduler-recv-interval 30 \ --stream-interval 30 --watchdog-timeout 600 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --gdn-mtp-cache-mode none \ # or mode full --linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer \ # or mode triton --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ``` Test: ``` python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 1319 \ --num-threads 256 \ --max-tokens 16384 \ --num-shots 8 \ --temperature 0.6 \ --top-p 0.95 \ --top-k 20 ``` **GSM8K** (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4, TP4, bf16 SSM) | Metric | mode: none, recover: flashinfer | mode: none, recover: triton | mode: full, recover: triton (baseline) | |:---|---:|---:|---:| | Accuracy | 0.977 | 0.978 | 0.975 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Decode output throughput (tok/s)** — Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4, TP4 | Method | bs 64 | bs 128 | bs 256 | bs 512 | |:---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | mode: full, recover: triton (baseline) | 7312.98 | 11626.15 | 16385.06| 19879.96| | mode: none, recover: flashinfer | **7953.32** | **12834.41** | **18526.52** | **23407.08** | | mode: none, recover: triton | 7435.01 | 11608.98 | 16266.39 | 19816.06 | <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## signal.title: feat: add FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A16 mode
signal.text: ## Motivation @humansand Add an opt-in W4A16 compute mode for FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE: routed expert weights remain NVFP4 while MoE activations and outputs stay BF16. Registered tests cover online-quantized Nemotron accuracy and serialized ModelOpt Qwen3 disk-reload invariance. Dependency: - Merge gate: merge only after SGLang's pinned FlashInfer dependency and CI image use a stable release containing CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A16 support ([#4048](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4048)), SiTU support ([#4394](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4394)), and the invocation-workspace lifetime fix ([#4558](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4558)). This integration intentionally has no compatibility fallback for earlier FlashInfer APIs. - Upstream status on 2026-08-17: #4048 and #4394 are merged; #4558 is open at `c5ea45e4422e4c8be8059d79b27581971891132a`. The latest stable FlashInfer release is `v0.6.17`, so no eligible stable release exists yet. - Validation-only environment: FlashInfer [`nightly-v0.6.18-20260817`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/nightly-v0.6.18-20260817) at `e77a4a0d276367895c3b50a642fd8f326c03fb72` plus #4558 at `c5ea45e4422e`; `flashinfer-python==0.6.18.dev20260817`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.18.dev20260817`, and `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.7.0`. That nightly has no matching cu130 JIT-cache wheel, so the required kernels were compiled from source. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16` (default `false`). - Select `CuteDslMoEWrapper(quant_mode="w4a16")`, pass raw BF16 activations, and omit GEMM1/GEMM2 activation scales. - Reuse the existing packed NVFP4 weights and CuTe MMA-layout block scales, but construct weight-only decode alphas for both online-quantized and serialized ModelOpt weights. - Support the standard CuTe DSL v2 paths with no A2A or FlashInfer A2A on SM100-family GPUs (SM100/SM103). Keep FlashInfer A2A dispatch in BF16 by suppressing automatic NVFP4 dispatch and rejecting an explicit NVFP4-dispatch configuration; the existing DeepEP masked path remains W4A4-only. Both registered accuracy/reload tests exercise FlashInfer A2A, and the serving benchmark compares no A2A with FlashInfer A2A. - Preserve the configured finalize mode for ReLU2. For gated/SwiGLU W4A16, disable fused finalize and use FlashInfer's two-stage finalize path. - Register nightly `4-gpu-b200` end-to-end coverage for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8` with online NVFP4 expert-weight quantization. - Add a separate registered TP4/DP4/EP4 case with DP attention and FlashInfer A2A for serialized `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`: two same-checkpoint disk reloads across weight/CUDA-graph release and resume must preserve deterministic decode text and token IDs exactly, with token logprobs within `1e-4`. Requests are pinned to routed DP rank 0 for repeatable comparisons. This remains alongside the existing per-token NVFP4 CuTe DSL case. ## Accuracy Tests Environment: - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682` - Image digest: `sha256:fa8774dd128600a09fd6d46670b06fb69a55dac8a3881e50ccf0916a45eb39af` - Hardware: 4 of 8 NVIDIA B300 GPUs, compute capability SM103, TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention and FlashInfer A2A - Rebased SGLang base: `861eca8e2519e64a7d56ac1a947392e83873ee1c`; GPU-validated head: `d01db73b433ce975ee055fe21499d31d72571098`; historical serving benchmark: `508aef6135729ea66db55f3690f0036219145662` - The copied source files on the devbox were SHA-256 identical to the three files at `d01db73b43`; both registered tests below therefore exercised the final source content. - FlashInfer: `0.6.18.dev20260817` plus [#4558](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4558) at `c5ea45e4422e`, source-JIT for cu130 Commands: ```bash export PYTHONPATH=/hai-workspace/flashinfer-runtime-w4a16-fix:/hai-workspace/sglang/python export HF_HOME=/hai-workspace/hf-cache export SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/hai-workspace/sglang-cache-w4a16-a2a-20260817a export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 export SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=0 cd /hai-workspace/sglang/test python3 registered/backends/test_flashinfer_nvfp4_online_moe_backend.py \ TestFlashinferCuteDSLMoeBackendNvFp4OnlineW4A16.test_gsm8k -f python3 registered/rl/test_update_weights_from_disk_blackwell.py \ TestServerUpdateWeightsFromDiskNVFP4W4A16CuteDSL.test_parameterized_update_weights_from_disk -f ``` Results: ```text # Online FP8 checkpoint with online NVFP4 expert-weight quantization Flashinfer MoE A2A is enabled. Disable prefill CUDA graph because cuda_graph_config resolved prefill.backend='disabled'. Capture target verify CUDA graph end. elapsed=21.37 s Capture draft decode CUDA graph end. elapsed=7.97 s Capture draft extend CUDA graph end. elapsed=3.01 s Decode batch, ... cuda graph: True Total latency: 59.422 s Score: 0.965 Output throughput: 1330.554 token/s avg_spec_accept_length=3.112170753860127 Ran 1 test in 360.547s OK # Serialized ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint in deterministic W4A16 mode Flashinfer MoE A2A is enabled. [MnnvlMemory] creating address with stride=536870912 Decode batch, ... cuda graph: True # Both update variants passed: flush_cache=true and flush_cache=false. # Each variant released weights, then restored weights, KV cache, and CUDA graphs; # the post-reload text, token IDs, and token logprobs matched the baseline. Update weights end. # first reload Update weights end. # second reload Ran 1 test in 247.370s OK ``` The serialized Qwen3 test covers deterministic non-fused finalize, routed-DP-rank-0 decode, and two reload cycles through FlashInfer A2A. The Nemotron test covers model-quality accuracy, online weight quantization, EAGLE, and target/draft FlashInfer A2A. GPU-validation log SHA-256 values: Nemotron `ced2b8d4f8211bb8c8c59e4656a3420c1b4511bb093bdca1250d83ab4479263a`; Qwen3 reload `19384467f8aabe04752439bca6eefc55ef1b2561172b7c78f349d2ecda4cc19e`. Both tests use a 4,096-token FlashInfer dispatch capacity per rank, covering the inherited 16,384-token maximum prefill across EP4. The Nemotron DP-attention case follows SGLang's existing upstream exception and disables only target prefill CUDA graphs; target verify, draft decode, draft extend, and runtime decode graphs remain enabled. This does not claim support for Nemotron DP-attention breakable-prefill graphs. The test keeps its inherited `--mem-fraction-static 0.7` and does not use the earlier 2K diagnostic cap. This GPU validation used a fresh SGLang cache, so its wall times include source JIT compilation and autotuning and are not serving-performance measurements. Static validation: ```text git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD: PASS git rev-list --merges upstream/main..HEAD: 0 python3 -m py_compile (all changed Python files): PASS pre-commit run --files (all changed files): PASS python3 scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py: PASS ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Four-GPU serving comparison at historical head `508aef613`. signal.title: Expose selected worker ID in sglang model gateway responses
signal.text: ## Why is this change needed? Clients can provide a stable `x-smg-routing-key`, but today they cannot verify which backend worker served each response. This makes it difficult to diagnose whether multi-request agent sessions actually preserve worker affinity. The HTTP regular router now returns an opaque, deterministic `x-smg-worker-id` derived from the selected worker URL (including its data-parallel rank, when present). The identifier is added to both streaming and non-streaming responses after worker selection, including the final response after gateway retries, without exposing the worker IP or URL. For example, two requests routed to the same worker can now be correlated directly from their response headers: ```text request 1 -> x-smg-worker-id: 0f3a...c912 request 2 -> x-smg-worker-id: 0f3a...c912 ``` ## Test Plan - `cargo fmt --check` - `cargo test --lib test_insert_worker_id_is_stable_and_opaque` - `cargo test --test routing_tests test_worker_id_is_stable_for_streaming_and_non_streaming_responses` The integration test verifies that both streaming and non-streaming chat-completion responses expose the same worker ID when routed to the same backend. -Robot <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31902512993](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902512993)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31902512922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902512922)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Overlap spec-v2 lifetime: pin the draft-extend ForwardBatch, record_stream the mixed-gather indices
signal.text: ## Motivation Two cross-stream tensor-lifetime violations in the overlap scheduler (torch.Tensor.record_stream contract: a tensor allocated on stream A and consumed on stream B must stay alive until B finishes, or be record_stream'd; wait_stream orders execution but does not protect deallocation). Reachability is allocator-config-dependent, measured on B200-class hardware with the production stream ordering: default native allocator latent (0/40 corruptions: free-list eventing happens to order the reuse write after pending readers) expandable_segments:True corrupts 19/20 backend:cudaMallocAsync corrupts 19/20 Seam 1 (opt-in SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1): prepare_for_draft_extend runs inside the plan stream; its ForwardBatch owns plan-stream allocations that are NOT ScheduleBatch attributes (init_new's positions / extend_start_loc). When _draft_extend_for_decode returns, the ForwardBatch's only reference dies while forward-stream kernels still read those tensors. Fix (both the single-layer and multi-layer workers): append the draft-extend ForwardBatch to GenerationBatchResult.extra_keep_alive_refs beside verify_forward_batch, gated on the plan stream being active (the hazard exists only there; the default path keeps its prior no-retention behavior) -- the scheduler ring slot is the designed extension point ("a list (not tuple) so that workers can register additional refs") and already retains it for the 2-iteration window. Seam 2 (non-spec overlap + mixed chunked prefill): mix_with_running aliases the running batch's req_pool_indices into mix_running_indices. last_batch / the 2-slot record ring usually keep the running batch alive, but that ages out: intervening non-mixed prefills advance last_batch and overwrite both ring slots; a later mix leaves the staging field as the LAST owner, and resolve_forward_inputs clears it right after enqueueing the forward-stream gather. Fix: record_stream the indices on the gathering stream (CPU-device guarded). Corrections to the previous revision of this PR, from review (thanks): - The earlier seam-1 claim (verify input_ids / out_cache_loc unprotected) was wrong: production covers those via record_stream_each after eagle_prepare_for_verify plus the verify_forward_batch keepalive. The broad exit-time vars(batch) capture in the scheduler is removed: it covered only the batch-reachable subset and missed ForwardBatch-only tensors; the keepalive covers all of them, present and future. - The silent corruption that motivated this PR family came from the relay staging fence (#34077), not these seams; these are latent-by-accident on the default allocator and observable under the supported alternative allocator configs above. ## Modifications - `srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py` and `srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py`: append the draft-extend `ForwardBatch` to `GenerationBatchResult.extra_keep_alive_refs` beside `verify_forward_batch`, gated on the plan stream being active (the hazard exists only there; the default path keeps its prior no-retention behavior). - `srt/managers/overlap_utils.py`: `record_stream` the mixed-gather indices on the gathering stream (CPU-device guarded). - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py`: rewritten suite preserving the production ownership graph (see Test below). ## Test Tests (test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py, rewritten to preserve the production ownership graph): the seam-1 arms drive the REAL prepare_for_draft_extend -> ForwardBatch.init_new -> compute_position chain under a real plan stream with production ordering (wait_stream) and natural reference death (function scope; scheduler ring mirrored verbatim); the seam-2 arms walk the real aging-out sequence (real mix alias, real 2-slot ring, real resolve_forward_inputs) and prove last-owner death with a weakref. Only kernel latency (torch.cuda._sleep) and next-round allocation pressure are compressed for determinism. Corruption arms run in a subprocess pinned to PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True so red/green is deterministic regardless of the CI host's allocator default. Red/green on the base commit (test file alone on pristine 2b4381956): test_gather_survives_aging_out FAILS -- the recycled indices fire a device-side IndexKernel out-of-bounds assert (the loud variant; in-range recycled values corrupt silently); the seam-1 ring/keepalive pair shows CORRUPTED vs CLEAN on the same real producer chain. With the fix: 6/6 pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No kernel or scheduling change. Cost per overlap iteration under the opt-in plan stream: one list append into the existing ring slot (freed on the same 2-iteration cadence). The default path adds nothing. `record_stream` on mixed prefill+decode batches is O(1) host-side. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32068311405](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32068311405)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32068310608](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32068310608)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix MoE MORI Accuracy Issue
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes a bug where MoE models served with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` produce garbage output (0/10 on known-answer accuracy), while the exact same model/config with `--moe-a2a-backend none` is correct (10/10). This reproduces on: - Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8) - Hy3-preview / Hunyuan (`HYV3ForCausalLM`, 192 experts, top-8, with shared experts) It reproduces at single node (where MoRI runs its IntraNode kernel) and at multi-node (InterNode/RDMA kernel), so it is not tied to a specific transport. ### Root Cause After the experts run, `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock` / `HYV3MoEFused` apply a post-experts all-reduce (`moe_expert_parallel_all_reduce` / `moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`), gated by `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(...)`. That all-reduce is correct for backends whose experts return a partial result per rank. But MoRI's `combine` already all-to-all-reduces each token's expert outputs back to the source rank — the routed output is already complete and replicated across the group, exactly like the `flashinfer` and `pplx` dispatchers, which are already excluded from the post-experts all-reduce. Because `mori` was not in the skip list, the extra all-reduce re-reduces an already-complete result, summing it `ep_size`/`tp_size`× and destroying the output. We confirmed this directly by dumping per-rank MoE tensors on the failing server: the routed MoE output is identical across all ranks (already reduced by MoRI combine), and the post-experts `final_out` equals `Σ_ranks(routed)` (i.e. `ep_size × routed`), the fingerprint of the erroneous re-reduce. A reference-trajectory comparison against a correct HuggingFace forward on the same prompt showed layer-0 attention matching (cosine ≈ 1.0) but the trajectory diverging starting at the first MoE layer's output — isolating the defect to the post-experts reduce, not to MoRI's dispatch/GEMM/combine (which produce numerically correct values). ### Specific to Hunyuan 3 `HYV3MoEFused` adds a shared expert (`shared_mlp`, built with `reduce_results=False`) to the routed output before the all-reduce. Under MoRI, the routed output is already full/replicated (must not be reduced again), but the shared output is still a TP/EP partial (still needs reducing). So simply skipping the blanket all-reduce fixes the routed part but leaves `shared` at a fraction (`1/group_size`), which still corrupts the sum. The fix reduces only the shared partial over the same group(s) the blanket reduce would have used, then adds it to the already-full routed output. Qwen3 has no shared experts, so it needs only the skip. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/utils.py` — `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce(...)`: add an `is_mori()` skip alongside the existing `is_flashinfer()` / `is_pplx()` skips (same "combine already reduces to source rank" rationale). This alone fully fixes models without shared experts (e.g. Qwen3). - `python/sglang/srt/models/hunyuan_v3.py` — in both `_forward_single_stream` and `_forward_dual_stream`, for the MoRI path only, reduce the shared-expert partial over the EP/TP group before adding it to the already-full routed output; plus the `get_moe_a2a_backend` import. Required for Hunyuan/Hy3 and any MoRI model with shared experts. Both changes are gated on `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()`, so `none`, `flashinfer`, `deepep`, and `pplx` behavior is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Accuracy = greedy known-answer probe (10 factual prompts, temperature 0). Baseline `mori` is the unpatched image; `none` is the reference-correct control. ### Probe Test | Model | Nodes | Geometry | Backend | Before Fix | After Fix | |-------|:-----:|----------|---------|:--------:|:--------:| | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 | TP/EP=8 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 2 | TP/EP=16 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | TP/EP=32 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 1 | TP/EP=8 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 2 | TP/EP=16 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | | Hy3-preview | 4 | TP/EP=32 | mori | 0/10 | 10/10 PASS | - Qwen3: clean PASS at 1/2/4 nodes (0/10 degenerate). - Hy3: all answers correct at 1/2/4 nodes. At multi-node the probe's separate degenerate-tail heuristic flags 3–4/10 (the base model repeats after answering), but the correct `none` reference shows the same 2–4/10 — i.e. it's a base-model/prompt artifact, not a regression from this fix. - Controls: `--moe-a2a-backend none` remains 10/10 (unchanged), confirming the fix is scoped to MoRI. Both single-node (MoRI IntraNode) and multi-node (MoRI InterNode/RDMA) paths verified. ### GSM8K (exact-match, 40 problems, 5-shot) | Model | Nodes | Geometry | none (control) | mori (before fix) | mori (after fix) | |-------|:-----:|----------|:--------------:|:-----------------:|:----------------:| | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1 | TP/EP=8 | 87.5% (35/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 90.0% (36/40) | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 2 | TP/EP=16 | 90.0% (36/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 90.0% (36/40) | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | 4 | TP/EP=32 | 85.0% (34/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 92.5% (37/40) | | Hy3-preview | 1 | TP/EP=8 | 77.5% (31/40) | 2.5% (1/40) | 77.5% (31/40) | | Hy3-preview | 2 | TP/EP=16 | 80.0% (32/40) | 2.5% (1/40) | 77.5% (31/40) | | Hy3-preview | 4 | TP/EP=32 | 80.0% (32/40) | 0.0% (0/40) | 80.0% (32/40) | - Before the fix, mori is broken at every scale (Qwen3 0%, Hy3 0–2.5%), consistent with the garbage output on the known-answer probe. - After the fix, mori tracks the none reference at every scale: Qwen3 lands at or slightly above none (within noise at N=40), and Hy3 matches the reference closely (exactly equal at 1 and 4 nodes: 31/40 and 32/40). - The absolute score reflects each base model's own capability (Hy3-preview is a preview model, so its ceiling is lower); the fix restores reference-equivalent accuracy on the MoRI path rather than changing model quality. - Single-node exercises MoRI's IntraNode kernel; 2-node and 4-node exercise MoRI's InterNode (RDMA) kernel. Scored offline against the staged GSM8K test split via final-integer exact-match. ### Test Environment - Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm700-mi30x-20260728` (SGLang upstream `main` @ `84cdfde`, version `0.5.16.dev20260728`), 8× MI300 per node, pure TP (`tp==ep`), `--disable-custom-all-reduce`. - Hy3 runs also apply an orthogonal, environment-specific workaround for AITER's `biased_grouped_topk` on ROCm (falls back to the reference impl when `apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output=True`); this is unrelated to the all-reduce fix. ## Follow Up - Other MoRI models with shared experts (beyond Hunyuan) would need the same shared-expert handling in their model file; consider factoring the "reduce shared partial only" step into a shared helper. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32048833857](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32048833857)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32048833336](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32048833336)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kernel] Enable Helion backend for Kimi Delta-Attention
signal.text: ## Motivation Add an opt-in Helion backend (e.g. used for Inkling [silu_mul fusion](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/inkling_moe.py)) for Kimi Delta Attention packed decode and prefill while preserving the existing default backends, public contracts, state mutations, and fallback behavior. The decode kernel delivers a **1.1x speedup** over Triton default. The prefill kernel delivers a **1.6x speedup** over Triton default. For Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (TP=2, 2xGB200), we observe geomean **5.04%-5.27%** improvement in tok/s with **4.06%-5.22%** reduction in TTFT compared to default kernels. This enables helion==1.4.0 as an optional dependency that is required only for the helion backend, matching what is done for some of the other KDA backends. ## Modifications - Add Helion implementations for packed recurrent decode and fixed/packed-varlen prefill. - Support FP32, BF16, and FP16 recurrent states, padded cache indices, bounded gates, intermediate states, and an opt-in Newton-Schulz research path. - Register helion for KDA decode and prefill selection: ```bash sglang serve MODEL_PATH --linear-attn-backend helion ``` Phases can also be selected independently: ```bash sglang serve MODEL_PATH \ --linear-attn-decode-backend helion \ --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton ``` - Keep generic decode, speculative verification, and ReplaySSM on the existing Triton fallback. - Add registered CUDA kernel tests, CPU dispatcher tests, benchmark coverage, and backend documentation. - Use fixed Helion configurations and static shapes, with no runtime autotuning on the model hot path. ## Accuracy Tests - Decode comparisons against packed Triton: - FP32 state: maximum output difference: 7.63e-6; maximum state difference: 2.24e-8. - BF16 state: maximum output difference: 7.63e-6; maximum state difference: 1.22e-4. - Prefill comparisons against recurrent Triton: - Maximum output difference: 7.32e-4. - Maximum state difference: 4.90e-3. - Covered fixed and packed-varlen prefill, FP32/BF16/FP16 state, padded `-1` cache indices, partial chunks, safe gates with `lower_bound=-5.0`, and stable sub-chunk normalization. - End-to-end Kimi-Linear GSM8K smoke test with Helion decode passed with score 0.915. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on NVIDIA 2xGB200 GPUs. End-to-End benchmarks: - Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct - TP=2 - input length 8192, batches 1/4/16, and output lengths 64/256. - Geomeans cover all six shapes for each state dtype. - We compare against default prefill/decode for KDA. | State dtype | Activation dtype | Overall throughput gain | TTFT reduction | TPOT reduction | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | FP32 | BF16 | 5.04% | 5.22% | 4.83% | | BF16 | BF16 | 5.27% | 4.06% | 5.68% | Microbenchmark summary: | Benchmark | State dtype | Activation dtype | Baseline | Geomean speedup | |---|---|---|---|---:| | Decode | FP32 | FP32 | Packed Triton | 1.134x | | Decode | BF16 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.067x | | Decode | FP32 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.118x | | Decode | BF16 | BF16 | FlashInfer | 1.393x | | Prefill | FP32 | BF16 | Triton | 1.603x | | Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton | 1.595x | H = 12, lower_bound=-5.0 | Benchmark | State dtype | Activation dtype | Baseline | Geomean speedup | |---|---|---|---|---:| | Decode | FP32 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.552x | | Decode | FP32 | BF16 | CUDA decode | 0.721x | | Decode | BF16 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.130x | | Prefill | FP32 | BF16 | Triton | 1.385x | | Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton | 1.390x | | Prefill| FP32 | BF16 | Triton ReplaySSM | 1.707x | | Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton ReplaySSM | 1.225x | Currently Helion decode under performs the custom cuda KDA decode kernel, as the CUDA kernel fuses convolution, recurrence, and RMSNorm. A follow up PR will evaluate Helion under the same fusions. Note that the`bench_kda_prefill_cutedsl.py` script precomputes CuTe metadata and scratch buffers outside the timed region and bypasses the production adapters, so this is not a super faithful representation of performance (helion has a 0.86x speedup compared to cute on this benchmark). signal.title: feat(unified-memory): three sub-pools for mamba + hybrid-SWA models
signal.text: > **Stacked PR.** This builds on #35154 and #35158 and should be reviewed after > them. Its own change is the last 13 commits, 7 source + 6 test files, +4359/−179. > The rest of the diff shown here is those two PRs. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Unified memory currently supports exactly two sub-pools, so it cannot serve a model whose KV state comes in three kinds — full-attention KV, sliding-window KV, and recurrent (mamba/conv) state. Inkling is the first such model in tree. Under static pools those three get fixed walls sized once at boot, so idle capacity in one cannot relieve pressure in another: a workload that exhausts sliding-window pages retracts requests while full-attention bytes sit unused. Whether that split was right depends on the request mix, which is not known at boot. This PR generalizes the unified pool from two sub-pools to N, adds a sub-pool that *floats* between its neighbours instead of being anchored to one end of the buffer, and routes mamba + hybrid-SWA models onto the resulting three-pool composite. All three kinds then share one buffer with boundaries that move at runtime. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> Three layers change, from the buffer outward. **The pool** accepts any number of sub-pools instead of exactly two: one growing up from the low end, one growing down from the high end, and any number floating in between. A factory builds the three-sub-pool arrangement. **The allocators** become a chain rather than a pair. Each knows its low and high neighbour and walks the chain for frontier math, skipping members that currently hold nothing. A new floating allocator type lives between its neighbours and relocates on demand instead of anchoring to one end. All shortfall handling collapses into a single ladder — flush, re-check, ask the float to slide, re-check — driven by a per-band demand vector, so one band running out of pages and a composite missing a coupled multi-band allocation take the same path. Capacity views are memoized on a mutation epoch, since a chain makes them costlier to compute than a pair. **The wiring** routes mamba + hybrid-SWA models to the new arrangement, which previously fell into the mamba-only branch and crashed at boot. Admission reserves shared-gap bytes per new recurrent-state slot, and the scheduler's pool stats and invariant checks read slot-conserving capacity views, since byte-derived totals now move as boundaries float. One change reaches existing models: the per-step sliding-window free receives the freed range's start position and derives page representatives arithmetically, removing a host sync. That applies to the current two-pool SWA composite as well. Otherwise two-pool layouts and boot signatures are unchanged. Tests cover the widened pool (pinning that two sub-pools stay byte-identical), the floating allocator and the ladder, capacity-memo coherence, the composite and its factory, and an end-to-end Inkling run with an optional static-vs-unified parity lane. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> GSM8K, 200 questions per cell, unified vs static pools comparisons Delta in percentage points, unified minus static: | Model | Sub-pools | Median Δ | Range | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen3.5-9B | 2 (full + state) | +0.00 | −0.5 .. +1.5 | | Kimi-Linear-48B | 2 (MLA + state) | +0.00 | −2.0 .. +1.0 | | Falcon-H1-7B | 2 (full + state) | +0.50 | −4.0 .. +3.5 | | gpt-oss-20b | 2 (full + SWA) | −0.75 | −11.0 .. +7.5 | | **Inkling-Small (tp8)** | **3 (full + SWA + state)** | +0.75 | −6.5 .. +7.5 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> Serving benchmark, unified vs static pools at matched attention backends, over two workloads (steady-state decode and a retract/compaction lane) and both schedulers. Median inter-token latency, negative = unified faster: | Model | Sub-pools | Backends | Median ITL | Range | |---|---|---|---|---| | Falcon-H1-7B | 2 (full + state) | triton | **−0.81%** | −1.40 .. +1.50% | | Inkling-Small (tp8) | **3 (full + SWA + state)** | triton | +0.85% | −2.30 .. +1.61% | | Qwen3.5-9B | 2 (full + state) | triton | +0.90% | +0.05 .. +2.83% | | Kimi-Linear-48B (tp2) | 2 (MLA + state) | fa3, flashinfer, triton | +1.21% | +0.82 .. +2.39% | | gpt-oss-20b | 2 (full + SWA) | triton | +1.32% | −2.85 .. +2.98% | ## Checklist - [ ✅ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ✅ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ✅ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ✅ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Diffusion][Refactor] Refactor and extract complex RoPE implementation to layers/rotary_embedding for MOVA DiT
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang has a dedicated directory (`layers/rotary_embedding`) designed to house unified, high-performance Rotary Positional Embedding implementations. Was observed that a complex-valued RoPE representation is highly efficient for the `neox_style=False` and `interleaved=True` configurations. However, implementing this complex multiplication logic directly within model-specific code leads to duplication and limits its reusability. Since this optimized complex RoPE path is generic, mathematically clean, and performant, it is logical to extract the implementation out of the model code and move it into the shared `layers/rotary_embedding/utils.py` utility module. This enables other models within SGLang using interleaved RoPE to easily inherit and reuse this optimization. ## Modifications Were modified 4 key files to implement this refactoring and optimization: ### 1. `sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/utils.py` - Added the `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` function: - **Inputs:** - `x` of shape `[batch, num_tokens, num_heads, head_size]`. - `freqs` of shape `[num_tokens, 1, head_size // 2]`. - **Outputs:** Evaluated tensor of the same shape and dtype as `x`. - **Optimization Details:** It utilizes `view()` transformations to group activation dimensions and cast to `float32`. It then performs a single vectorized complex multiplication kernel. Calling `torch.view_as_real()` on the result natively lays out the real and imaginary elements sequentially in memory, producing the interleaved layout. This excludes the need for `torch.stack()` and `.contiguous()` allocations. ### 2. `sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/__init__.py` - Registered the new `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` utility in the package exports: imported the function from `.utils.py` and added it to the `__all__` list to expose it cleanly to the rest of the codebase. ### 3. `sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/mova_video_dit.py` and `mova_audio_dit.py` Cleaned up the attention blocks and models: - Removed custom inline complex RoPE functions. - In `SelfAttention.forward`, reshape `q`, `k`, and `v` to `[B, S, H, D]` format using `view()` operations, and apply the `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` directly. This eliminates `rearrange` and `flatten` steps inside the attention loop. ## Accuracy Tests https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9239f012-ea90-496d-8823-01fe6d95584e ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### 1. SGLang Server Launch Command ```bash sglang serve --model-path $(pwd)/mova_video_360p --pipeline-class-name MOVAPipeline --num-gpus 4 --ring-degree 1 --ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode memory --dit-layerwise-offload --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0.1 --text-encoder-cpu-offload true --vae-cpu-offload true --enable-torch-compile --warmup-mode server --vae-tiling --vae-sp ``` ### 2. Video Generation Request ```bash curl -X POST "http://localhost:30000/v1/videos" -F "prompt=A curious raccoon" -F "input_reference=@/.../images/raccoon.png" -F "size=640x352" -F "num_frames=49" -F "fps=24" -F "num_inference_steps=25" -F "guidance_scale=5.0" -o create_video.json ``` ### 3. Offline Profiling Command ```bash SGLANG_DIFFUSION_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR="/home/s60128115/profile_complex" sglang generate --model-path /home/s60128115/models/mova_video_360p --pipeline-class-name MOVAPipeline --prompt "A curious raccoon" --image-path /home/s60128115/images/raccoon.png --width 640 --height 352 --num-frames 49 --fps 24 --num-inference-steps 25 --guidance-scale 5.0 --profile --num-profiled-timesteps 10 --num-gpus 4 --ulysses-degree 4 --enable-torch-compile --warmup-mode request --dit-layerwise-offload --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0.1 ``` ### 4. signal.title: [AMD] Enable Fast Triton Sparse MLA backend
signal.text: # Fast Triton Sparse MLA Kernels for DSA (Prefill + Decode) ## Summary This adds `triton` as an explicit DSA prefill/decode backend: ```bash --dsa-prefill-backend triton --dsa-decode-backend triton ``` The new backend provides pure Triton sparse MLA kernels for the fp8 DSA path on ROCm, validated on MI355X (gfx950) and MI300X (gfx942). It replaces the previous Triton prefill env-var gate, SGLANG_DSA_TRITON_PREFILL, with a faster kernel exposed through the normal backend option and adds a fast Triton kernel for the decode path. ## What Changed - Adds `triton` to `DSA_CHOICES` for `--dsa-prefill-backend` and `--dsa-decode-backend`. - Adds startup validation in both server-args paths so Triton DSA is only used with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. - Adds standalone Triton prefill and decode dispatch branches in `dsa_backend.py`. - Ensures HIP Triton DSA uses the raw MLA KV layout (`512 nope + 64 rope`) instead of the scaled fp8 layout used by other non ROCm backends. - Extends the gfx950 fused-rope skip path to include Triton, matching the TileLang/AITER raw-layout flow. ## Kernel Notes - Prefill uses a split-dim 4x128 implementation for the 512-wide nope dimension, plus the 64-wide rope tail. - Prefill can split topk work across CTAs and reduce partial online-softmax state in Triton. - Decode uses an adaptive split-K path with a fused single-pass fast path when `kv_splits == 1`. - Kernels use `exp2` with `sm_scale * LOG2E` prescaling. The kernels consume raw fp8 MLA KV cache layout on HIP. They are not intended for NVIDIA's scaled fp8 KV layout. ## Validation - GSM8K 400-question validated: TileLang and Triton both produced 95.5% accuracy with 0% invalid answers. Accuracy also verified on gfx942 - Isolated prefill microbench on MI355X/GLM-5.2 shape (`H=16`, `D_V=512`, `D_TAIL=64`, `topk=2048`) showed about 10% speedup for the split-dim prefill kernel versus the earlier 512-wide-dot Triton env gated kernel, with cosine similarity 1.00000. - End-to-end GLM-5.1-MXFP4 serving on TP4 MI355X (`ISL=8192`, `OSL=1024`) showed Triton improving throughput by roughly 3-5% versus TileLang in the measured concurrency range. - Performance improvement is seen across all concurrencies, TPs, and for short and long context. ## Performance End-to-end GLM-5.1-MXFP4 serving on TP4 MI355X, concurrency 2: | Backend | Total tok/s | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | TileLang | 1,005 | 112 | 834 | 17.1 | | Triton | 1,044 | 116 | 701 | 16.6 | | Improvement | +3.9% | +3.6% | -16.0% | -2.9% | ## Changed Files - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/triton_sparse_mla.py`: updates the Triton prefill implementation with split-dim and split-K paths. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/triton_sparse_mla_decode.py`: adds the Triton decode implementation. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py`: adds Triton prefill/decode dispatch and removes the old env-var-gated prefill path. - `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`: exposes `triton` as a DSA backend choice. - `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py`: validates Triton DSA override combinations against fp8 KV cache requirements. - `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py`: selects raw HIP MLA KV layout for Triton DSA. - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py`: includes Triton in the gfx950 fused-rope skip check. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32058283003](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32058283003)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32058282865](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32058282865)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix NIXL cleaner grouping for hybrid cache keys
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #32702. The NIXL FILE L3 cleaner must evict every physical shard of a logical cache entry atomically. `_parse_group_key()` removed only a trailing `_k`/`_v` and then a trailing TP-rank suffix, but hybrid names append their pool component after the rank (for example, `page-a_model_0_8_swa_k`), so the anchored rank match failed and one entry was split into independently evicted groups. ## Modifications - Build the hybrid pool-name pattern from `PoolName`, ordered longest-first for overlapping names such as `swa` and `draft_swa`. - Strip the generated hybrid component shapes (`_{pool}`, K/V, indexed, Mamba temporal, and Mamba convolution suffixes) before applying the existing K/V and TP-rank parsing. - Add CPU regression coverage for every component shape and for `_tick()` deleting legacy K/V files, hybrid components, and TP ranks as one logical group. For example, `page-a_model_0_8_swa_k` previously grouped as `page-a_model_0_8_swa`; it now groups as `page-a_model`, together with the entry's other ranks and components. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: this changes only background disk-eviction grouping and does not modify cache contents, transfer logic, or model computation. signal.title: [SM120] flash_mla: allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode
signal.text: ## Purpose `_split_kv_pages_to_64` keeps two lazily allocated persistent buffers in the same `buffers` dict, with the same lifetime: allocated once on first use, reused across autotune, CUDA graph capture and steady-state serving. On current main only one of them is protected: ```python buf = buffers.get(key) # page-split destination if buf is None or buf.shape[0] < num_dst_pages: buf = torch.empty(...) # <- no guard buffers[key] = buf ... mbuf = buffers.get(mkey) # dirty mask if mbuf is None or mbuf.shape[0] < N: # The first allocation can happen under inference mode (autotune), # but the buffer is zeroed again later during CUDA graph capture # outside inference mode -- an inference tensor cannot be mutated # there, so force a normal tensor. with torch.inference_mode(False): # <- guarded mbuf = torch.empty(N, dtype=torch.int8, device=dev) buffers[mkey] = mbuf ``` The reasoning in that comment applies verbatim to `buf`: it is written during CUDA graph capture too. This PR closes the asymmetry. The `mbuf` guard was added after @moxcat reported the failure while running DSV4 on SM120; the fix at the time covered *both* lazy buffers in this function, and the `buf` half was lost somewhere between that backport and main. The same pattern, with the same justification, also exists in `sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py`. When it does fire, the symptom is: ``` RuntimeError: Inplace update to inference tensor outside InferenceMode is not allowed ``` ## What I could and could not verify I could not construct a configuration on 4x RTX 6000D (SM120) where the unguarded allocation actually lands under inference mode. Instrumenting the allocation site: | config | autotune ran | mode at allocation | result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` | no (0 invocations) | `inference_mode=False` | boots, no error | | `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | yes (4 invocations) | `inference_mode=False` | boots, no error | In both, `buf` is first allocated during `Capturing batches`, so the ordering never arises. So I am not attaching a before/after reproducer — the case for this change is the asymmetry with `mbuf`, not a failure I can demonstrate on demand. @moxcat — if you still have the configuration that hit this originally, it would turn the table above into a real before/after. ## Context Split out of #29927 at @Fridge003's request, since it is not SM120 enablement work. #29927 now depends on it. ## Scope One allocation site. Buffer contents, shape, caching key and lifetime are unchanged; only the mode it is allocated under. No-op wherever the allocation already happens outside inference mode.

signal.title: [AMD][CI] Surface AMD ROCm 7.2 state in the PR CI-states block
signal.text: ## Motivation `pr-states.yml` maintains the **CI States** block at the bottom of every PR body, but it only queries `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml`. A merge oncall reading the PR description therefore sees the CUDA result and nothing else, even though `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` is a full PR gate that most PRs dispatch. ## Modifications **`.github/workflows/pr-states.yml`** - New row `Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2)` with its own `<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720 -->` markers, reusing the existing `runIcon` / `runLink` rendering. - `"PR Test ROCm 7.2 (AMD)"` added to the `workflow_run` subscription, so the block refreshes when the AMD run is requested and when it completes. This is also the path that covers fork PRs, whose `pull_request` token is read-only. - One AMD-specific state: unlike `pr-test`, the AMD gate has an `on.pull_request.paths` filter, so "no run for this SHA" legitimately means *nothing ROCm-relevant changed* rather than a missed dispatch. It renders as `:heavy_minus_sign: **Not triggered for this commit**` instead of the stale-push warning the Extra row uses, and its lookup skips the retry budget for the same reason — retrying cannot conjure a run that was never dispatched, and a later dispatch refreshes the block through its own `workflow_run` event. - Two adjustments keep the added row from degrading the existing ones. The three lookups are independent, so they now run concurrently and the extra query costs no wall-clock time. The per-workflow query also asks for more than one run and skips `skipped` records, because `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml` subscribe to `labeled` events and a label-only dispatch can leave a deliberately skipped run ahead of the substantive attempt for the same SHA. **`.github/workflows/pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** - A `notify-pr-states` job mirroring the one already in `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml`. `workflow_run.completed` fires only once per run record, and rerunning (`/tag-and-rerun-ci`) is how a PR recovers a gate-blocked AMD run, so without this the row would go stale precisely when it starts carrying real results. The workflow already declares `actions: write`, and fork PRs are excluded for the same read-only-token reason documented on the existing jobs. Example rendering with `run-ci` present, CUDA green, and a PR that touches no ROCm-relevant paths: ``` ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): ✅ [Run #1](…) Latest PR Test (Extra): ⚠️ **Not enabled** -- add `run-ci-extra` label to opt in. Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): ➖ **Not triggered for this commit**. ``` ## Verification The rendering is tested offline, because it structurally cannot be tested by a PR: `pull_request_target` always runs the **base branch** version of the workflow, so this branch's copy never executes on its own PR. The inline `actions/github-script` body was extracted from the YAML and run under Node against a mocked Actions API, covering: no `run-ci` label; a path-filtered AMD gate; in-progress and failed AMD runs; a skipped record not masking the real run; and re-patching an already-patched body without duplicating the block or drifting between passes. `scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py`, `check-yaml`, `codespell`, and the whitespace hooks pass on both files, as does `actionlint` (excluding warnings this workflow already carries on `main` for the empty dropdown option and the self-hosted runner labels). ## Known limitation A red AMD row is still ambiguous between "`pr-gate` blocked it" and "tests actually failed" — the same ambiguity the existing rows have, noted in the file's own comment above `runIcon`. Distinguishing them needs a per-run jobs lookup; worth doing, but kept out of this PR to hold the diff to one reviewable concern. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CI reporting only, no runtime code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — no change to runner allocation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — n/a, no unit-test harness exists for the inline workflow scripts; tested as described above. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — n/a. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1.
