signal.title: [Skill] Document AMD nightly workflow conventions in ci-workflow-guide
signal.text: ## Motivation `ci-workflow-guide` documents `pr-test.yml` in detail — stages, gating, fast-fail, partitioning — but says nothing about the AMD nightly workflows. Anyone adding or editing an AMD nightly job has to infer the conventions from neighbouring jobs, and the two that matter most are invisible until they break something CI does not catch: - A test step must **clear `github_summary.md` first**. Tests append to that file and the step then copies it into `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. A job with a single test step gets away without the clear — until someone adds a second step, at which point the second step republishes the first step's block and the rendered summary silently shows it twice. - A test step must **capture `run_suite.py`'s exit code** (`|| TEST_EXIT_CODE=$?` … `exit ${TEST_EXIT_CODE:-0}`). Steps run under `bash -e`, so a bare failing command aborts before the line that publishes the summary — losing the results on exactly the failing run where they are most needed. Both are already followed by the large majority of existing steps (64 and 60 of 67 in the ROCm 7.2 workflow), so they are real conventions; they were just never written down. ## Modifications Add an **AMD nightly workflows** section to `.claude/skills/ci-workflow-guide/SKILL.md` covering: - the two near-duplicate workflow files (ROCm 7.2 with 48 jobs, ROCm 7.0 with 44, job names differing only by the `-rocm720` suffix, 7.0 having no unique jobs) and that a change to one usually belongs in both - that none of `pr-test.yml`'s machinery — stages, `wait-for-*`, partitioning, `check-pr-test-health` — applies here - the test-step contract, as a copyable block, with the reasoning for each half - the three places a job must be registered: definition, `job_select` options, `check-all-jobs.needs` - that AMD nightlies never pass `--enable-retry`, so a flaky assertion fails on first occurrence and thresholds need real headroom - how to validate a change before merge by dispatching the workflow against a branch with `job_filter` - the MI30x setup cost (~49 min median, 59% of MI30x GPU-hours) that argues for adding a step to a job already serving the model rather than creating a new job Also extend the Key Files table with both workflow files and add three AMD rows to the debug table (duplicated summary block, empty summary on a red job, registered test that no workflow runs). Every figure quoted was measured against `main` rather than recalled: job counts and the 7.0/7.2 job-set difference from parsing both workflows, the 64/67 and 60/67 convention counts from scanning their test steps, and the absence of `--enable-retry` by grep. ## Accuracy Tests Documentation only — no code, test, or workflow changes. Verified: headings and the new intra-document anchor resolve, code fences balance, and codespell passes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; no runtime or CI behaviour changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Avoid deadlock when shared-memory node probe fails
signal.text: Fixes #34800 ## Summary - Keep every rank in `in_the_same_node_as()` on the same broadcast when the source shared-memory probe fails. - Add a two-rank Gloo regression that forces source shared-memory creation to raise `OSError`. ## Root cause `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` previously covered both local shared-memory operations and `broadcast_object_list()`. If source-rank creation failed, it skipped the broadcast while peers waited forever. ## Fix Limit the `OSError` suppression to local shared-memory creation/opening. The source broadcasts `None` on creation failure, reports itself as colocated, and peers report that they are not on the source node. Downstream readers therefore fall back to the remote path without a negative local-reader count. The macOS shared-memory name-length error is one trigger. The regression injects the same `OSError` and is registered in the Linux CPU CI lane to validate the platform-independent collective-safety invariant. Shared-memory name generation is intentionally unchanged. ## Validation - `PYTHONPATH=python python/.venv/bin/python -m pytest test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py::test_shm_creation_failure_keeps_all_ranks_in_the_collective -q` - `SKIP=no-commit-to-branch uvx pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py --show-diff-on-failure` - GitHub Lint: [Run #31923509772](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31923509772) - `git diff --check` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31893507153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893507153)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31893507005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893507005)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Disagg: enqueue middle prefill KV transfer after launch
signal.text: ## Summary - enqueue PDD middle-chunk KV transfer immediately after the producer batch launch - pass the producer `copy_done` event to Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori workers so they wait off the scheduler thread - keep final-chunk handling and the existing one-step overlap window unchanged ## Why The overlap scheduler currently waits until the previous prefill result is processed before submitting its KV chunk. That puts CPU result processing and KV submission back on the scheduler critical path and weakens zero-overhead scheduling. ## Validation - unit tests: 4 passed in the official SGLang ROCm image - GLM-5.2 dummy-weight PDD on one MI350X8: P TP4 + D TP4, 25,001-token cache-miss prompt split into 4 chunks - TP0 profile: 390 matched Mooncake HIP copies, 2.506 GB, with 390 API-to-GPU arrows - physical XGMI counters rose on matching P/D GPU pairs during the request This PR intentionally does not add multi-inflight or multi-step-ahead scheduling. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32013667094](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013667094)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32013666617](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013666617)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Sampler: add missing TP=1 short-circuit in _sync_token_ids_across_tp
signal.text: ## Motivation Sampler._sync_token_ids_across_tp directly calls torch.distributed.all_reduce and misses the world_size == 1 short-circuit that the wrapped tp_group.all_reduce provides at parallel_state.py:667. Sampler.__init__ cached self.tp_sync_group but not the corresponding world_size, so the sync function had no way to skip the no-op all_reduce on TP=1. This is the only direct torch.distributed.* call in the LLM forward/sampling hot path missing this guard. Every other site already handles the TP=1 case — see references in Modifications. As a result, on TP=1 the sync path still invokes the NCCL backend for a semantically no-op all_reduce, even though no cross-rank communication is needed. ## Modifications python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py (9 lines added, 0 removed): 1. Sampler.__init__: cache self.tp_sync_group_size = <group>.world_size, covering both the default branch (get_tp_group()) and the is_dp_attention_enabled() branch (get_parallel().attn_tp_group). 2. Sampler._sync_token_ids_across_tp: add if self.tp_sync_group_size == 1: return at the top, before if SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP or sampling_info.grammars:. Aligns with the existing convention already applied elsewhere: - parallel_state.py:667 — if self.world_size == 1: return (canonical pattern used by wrapped tp_group.all_reduce) - constrained/grammar_manager.py:242 — if self.grammar_sync_size == 1: ... (same semantic) - mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py, unified_radix_cache.py, managers/hisparse_coordinator.py, mem_cache/embedding_cache_controller.py, layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py, mem_cache/pool_host/base.py, mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py — all guard direct collectives with world_size > 1. TP>1 behavior is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model forward / sampling logic. On TP>1 the new guard never fires (byte-for-byte identical path). On TP=1 the all_reduce is a no-op semantically, so skipping it changes no output. Verified a grammar-constrained request (POST /v1/chat/completions with response_format.type = "json_schema") on TP=1: - Before patch: need NCCL all_reduce. - After patch: 200 OK with output matching the schema; server stays up. - Plain chat request: unaffected on both before/after builds. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. On TP=1 the patch removes a no-op torch.distributed.all_reduce call and its NCCL backend round-trip, which is a minor speedup, not a regression. On TP>1 the execution path is unchanged. ## Checklist - Format your code according to the https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit. - Add unit tests according to the https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests. - Update documentation according to https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations. signal.title: [Kernel] Fuse W4A8 DeepEP quantization with permutation
signal.text: ## Motivation The W4A8 DeepEP-normal path currently permutes BF16 activations into an expert-ordered temporary, then launches a second kernel to quantize that entire temporary to FP8. This reads and writes the reordered activations twice, keeps a full BF16 buffer live, and adds one launch on the latency-sensitive MoE path. ## Modifications - Make `deepep_permute_triton_kernel` optionally apply the static reciprocal input scale, clamp to the FP8 E4M3 range, and cast while scattering tokens into expert order. - Allocate the final FP8 `gateup_input` directly in `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal`, removing the BF16 reordered temporary and standalone input quantization launch. - Preserve the existing unscaled behavior when the scale pointer is `None`, as used by the generic `moe_permute` path. - Add a CUDA regression test covering random reorder mappings, invalid assignments, top-k variants, token counts, and hidden sizes, plus a CPU call-contract assertion for the DeepEP-normal path. ## Accuracy Tests Tested on 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB (CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.11.0). The fused output is bitwise identical to the previous `permute -> static per-tensor FP8 quant` sequence for all 27 combinations of: - `num_tokens`: 1, 7, 33 - `hidden_size`: 128, 512, 7168 - `topk`: 1, 2, 8 - random destination permutations and `-1` invalid assignments ```text 28 passed, 15 warnings in 8.46s ``` This includes 27 CUDA kernel cases and one CPU host-side call-contract test. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H100 80GB microbenchmark, CUDA events, 50 warmups, median of 5 runs with 500 iterations per run. Output buffers were preallocated for both paths. | Tokens | Hidden | Top-k | Old (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup | BF16 temporary removed | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 7168 | 1 | 19.835 | 10.374 | 1.912x | 0.014 MiB | | 8 | 7168 | 2 | 19.566 | 10.206 | 1.917x | 0.219 MiB | | 32 | 7168 | 8 | 19.436 | 10.337 | 1.880x | 3.500 MiB | | 128 | 7168 | 8 | 19.237 | 10.307 | 1.866x | 14.000 MiB | The input preparation changes from two kernel launches to one. The removed temporary is `num_routed_assignments * hidden_size * sizeof(bfloat16)` bytes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: fix(npu): split packed MTP HiCache transfers by pool
signal.text: > [!IMPORTANT] > For standalone Ascend HiCache validation, this PR branch bundles the complete > commit history of #32500 through `#32500@9acc6b733`. Users can fork this branch > and run it directly without fetching another PR. For upstream review and > merge, #32500 should still land first; GitHub will then remove the shared > commits from this PR's diff. #34560 is already merged into `main`. End-to-end > Qwen3.6 validation also uses the checkpoint semantic fix in #35086, but that > PR is not included in this branch. Recommended merge order: #32500, #35086, > then this PR. ## Motivation After #34560, the HiCache host K/V layer dimension includes both the target model layers and the NEXTN/MTP draft layers. #32500 adds the Ascend fused `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` path for `page_first_direct`, but that path invokes the operator once with the target device pool and the full packed host buffer. On Ascend, the target and draft K/V layers are separate device pools. A single invocation therefore pairs a target-only device buffer with a `target + draft` host-layer range, so the draft K/V layers are not transferred through the matching device pool. CUDA does not have this mismatch. Its existing path packs target and draft per-layer pointers into one pointer array, and the per-layer transfer kernels map each host layer to the corresponding device pointer. The Ascend fused operator accepts one contiguous device pool per invocation, so each pool must be transferred separately. ## Minimal reproduction Apply #32500 on top of a revision that contains #34560, then launch Qwen3.6-27B on Ascend with the following relevant options: ```text --tp-size 2 --attention-backend ascend --device npu --page-size 128 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-storage-backend mooncake --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` 1. Generate from a 3000-token prompt to populate HiCache. 2. For L2, generate a separate 6000-token filler to evict the original prefix from L1, then replay the original prompt. 3. For L3, wait for write-through completion, call `/flush_cache`, then replay the original prompt. 4. Request `return_cached_tokens_details` and inspect the target/draft transfer at the first `kernel_ascend` H2D or D2H operation. Without this change, the fused operation receives the full packed host layer range with only the target device pool. The draft pool is not transferred by a matching invocation. ## Changes - Skip CUDA-style packed device pointer arrays for the Ascend MTP path. - Iterate over the target pool and every draft pool on Ascend. - Slice the packed host K/V buffer to the layer range that belongs to each device pool. - Invoke `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` once per pool for both H2D and D2H. - Add focused tests for Ascend initialization and target/draft host-layer slicing. - Bundle all #32500 commits through `9acc6b733` so this fork branch is directly runnable for Ascend HiCache validation. Focused validation: - latest `upstream/main`: `2 passed` - exact branch head with `#32500@9acc6b733`: `3 passed, 17 deselected` - complete stacked focused tests with #35086: `8 passed` - pre-commit on both changed files: passed ## L2/L3 replay validation Validation stack: latest `main` with #34560, `#32500@9acc6b733`, #35086, and this fix. Model: Qwen3.6-27B BF16, TP2, Ascend NPU, NEXTN enabled, 4 prompts with 3000 input tokens and 512 output tokens. | Replay tier | Isolated cache details | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Host L2 | `host=2944, device=0, storage=0` for 4/4 prompts | passed | | Mooncake L3 | `storage=2944, device=0, host=0` for 4/4 prompts | passed | The L2 and L3 replay output IDs were identical for all four prompts: ```text sha256=a0349ca2a8cdf023da0ef7b86370fbc25eac55ba5d8a656665a845c4a1d969d9 ``` Their speculative statistics were also identical: - weighted accept rate: `62.8169%` - weighted accept length: `2.8845` - correct/proposed drafts: `1338/2130` Cold generation and cache replay were not token-identical. The first mismatch positions were `[217, 322, 293, 58]` for both L2 and L3. Since the L2 and L3 replays match each other exactly, Mooncake L3 does not introduce an additional divergence. #35086 fixes the packed Mamba checkpoint index; the remaining cold/replay divergence is the separate cold-prefill persistence-boundary issue described in #33515. ## Accuracy validation Ran the repository's `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` against the same NEXTN + Mooncake service using the first 200 examples from the official GSM8K test set: ```text num_questions=200 num_shots=5 parallel=4 temperature=0 max_new_tokens=512 chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false} ``` Result on the complete stack: `194/200` correct (`97.0%` accuracy), `0%` invalid responses, no request failures, and `218.519 s` latency. The earlier incomplete-stack result was `195/200`; only prompt 182 changed correctness, from the correct answer `23` to `24`. This run includes #35086 but does not include #33515's cold-prefill alignment change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32013404865](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013404865)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32013404713](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013404713)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [3/3] [EAGLE] perf: Remove redundant draft capture input staging
signal.text: ## Motivation Multi-step EAGLE/MTP CUDA graph capture routes per-step draft forwards through the eager runner. Staging fields that already alias graph-stable draft buffers records redundant copy nodes into the captured graph. This is part 3 of 3 extracted from #30388. ## Changes - Add `ForwardBatch.skip_eager_input_staging` to explicitly identify batches backed by persistent graph buffers. - Set the flag for EAGLE draft and frozen-KV MTP draft CUDA graph capture batches. - Keep generic capture staging unchanged unless the explicit batch flag or global `SGLANG_EAGER_INPUT_NO_COPY` override is set. - Add `SGLANG_EAGER_INPUT_NO_COPY_IN_DRAFT_CAPTURE` as the draft-capture kill switch. - Add focused `EagerRunner.load_batch` unit coverage. These 3 memcopies are removed from each DRAFT loop: ## Safety The marked capture batches contain views into each draft graph runner's persistent input buffers. Replay refreshes those buffers in place, so their tensor addresses remain stable. Generic capture mode alone does not establish that aliasing contract and continues to stage inputs. ## Accuracy and Speedup Accuracy and speedup were measured on the unified three-part stack. See the full results in #30388. ## Validation - `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_eager_runner_load_batch.py -q`: 5 passed. - `python -m py_compile` on all changed source and test files. - `git diff --check`. - This commit is an unchanged component extraction from #30388; the three-part aggregate is verified separately against the original PR tree. ## Series - [1/3: Fuse topk=1 draft postprocess](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30947) - [2/3: Fuse TP vocab-parallel embedding](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30948) - [3/3: Remove redundant draft capture input staging](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30949) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32013382888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013382888) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32013382661](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013382661)

signal.title: [Bug] DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool (SWA/HiSparse) has no get_cpu_copy() → decode-mode retract crashes with NotImplementedError (offload is unconditional, not gated on --disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On a **disaggregated (PD) decode** node serving **DeepSeek-V4** (which uses the SWA / HiSparse KV pool `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool`), whenever the KV pool fills up and the scheduler has to **retract** a running request, the process crashes with `NotImplementedError` from `KVCache.get_cpu_copy()`. Root cause: on the decode server, `release_req()` **unconditionally** offloads the retracted request's KV cache to CPU. This offload path is gated only on `disaggregation_mode == "decode"` — it is **not** gated on `--disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache` (which defaults to `False`). The offload calls `token_to_kv_pool_allocator.get_cpu_copy(...)`, but `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool` (a `BaseSWAKVPool` subclass) does **not** implement `get_cpu_copy()`, so it inherits the base `KVCache.get_cpu_copy()` that raises `NotImplementedError`. `MHATokenToKVPool`, `MLATokenToKVPool` and `DSATokenToKVPool` all implement it; the SWA pool does not. Net effect: for DeepSeek-V4 in PD decode mode, **any** KV-full retract crashes the scheduler, even though the user never enabled KV offloading. The only known workaround is to keep KV utilization below the retract threshold (e.g. raise `--mem-fraction-static` to ~0.95 to leave headroom), which merely *avoids* the crash path rather than fixing it. ### Crash chain (file:line on v0.5.14, commit 49e384c) ``` retract_decode() → release_req(req, ..., server_args, ...) python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1606 if server_args.disaggregation_mode == "decode": python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1619 # UNCONDITIONAL: not gated on offload flag req.offload_kv_cache(req_to_token_pool, token_to_kv_pool_allocator) :1620 → Req.offload_kv_cache() python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1485 self.kv_cache_cpu = token_to_kv_pool_allocator.get_cpu_copy(...) :1490 → SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.get_cpu_copy() python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py:381 return self._kvcache.get_cpu_copy(indices, mamba_indices=...) :382 → DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool (class BaseSWAKVPool) python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:438 # NO get_cpu_copy override → BaseSWAKVPool(KVCache) python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_swa_memory_pool.py # NO get_cpu_copy override → KVCache.get_cpu_copy() python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:1058 raise NotImplementedError() :1059 ``` Traceback (representative): ``` File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", ... in event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", ... in update_running_batch File ".../sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", ... in retract_decode File ".../sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 1620, in release_req req.offload_kv_cache(req_to_token_pool, token_to_kv_pool_allocator) File ".../sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 1490, in offload_kv_cache self.kv_cache_cpu = token_to_kv_pool_allocator.get_cpu_copy(...) File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/swa.py", line 382, in get_cpu_copy return self._kvcache.get_cpu_copy(indices, mamba_indices=mamba_indices) File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 1059, in get_cpu_copy raise NotImplementedError() NotImplementedError ``` ### Reproduction Environment: - Model: DeepSeek-V4 (SWA / HiSparse KV pool), tp8 / dp8, `--enable-dp-attention`. - PD disaggregation, decode server: `--disaggregation-mode decode`. - Natural MTP4 speculative decoding (EAGLE, `--speculative-num-steps 3`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`). - `--disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache` **left at its default `False`** (never set). Trigger: 1. Drive the decode server with a long-input / long-output closed-loop load (e.g. input ~60000, output 1000, `ignore_eos`, high concurrency) so that the KV pool reaches ~100% utilization. 2. When the running decode batch pushes KV usage to the full line, the scheduler calls `retract_decode()` to free space. 3. `retract_decode → release_req → req.offload_kv_cache → allocator.get_cpu_copy → NotImplementedError` → scheduler process dies. Observed: `#running-req` at the CUDA-graph max (e.g. 144), `full token usage == 1.00`, then the crash. It is a race near the KV-full line, not deterministic per seed; higher concurrency / higher accept-length loads hit it sooner. ### Environment - SGLang: v0.5.14 (commit `49e384c`). - Model: DeepSeek-V4 (SWA / HiSparse KV pool, `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool`). - Parallelism: tp8, dp8, `--enable-dp-attention`. - Mode: PD disaggregation, decode server (`--disaggregation-mode decode`), `--disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache` = default `False`. - Speculative decoding: EAGLE / MTP, `--speculative-num-steps 3`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`.

signal.title: [sglang-miles] Extract Anthropic conversion into standalone utils
signal.text: ## Motivation External OpenAI-compatible frontends that must interpret Anthropic Messages exactly as this server does (e.g. the Miles session server's token-in-token-out `/v1/messages` route) previously had to vendor `protocol.py`/`serving.py` and maintain a derived codec, plus a sync ledger to keep the copies honest. This gives the server and external callers one conversion implementation, maintained here. ## Modifications - New `srt/entrypoints/anthropic/utils.py`; `serving.py` and `protocol.py` are untouched. - `to_openai_request` / `to_anthropic_response` delegate to the original `AnthropicServing` methods through a runtime-detached instance (the conversion paths only read `_merge_inline_system`; the reasoning paths that need `OpenAIServingChat` are rejected up front). - `AnthropicRequestContext` feature gates let a frontend that has verified only a subset of typed features fail closed with a 400 instead of the server's accept-and-log policy; thinking is always rejected. - `to_anthropic_error` returns the envelope DTO against a composite map: `serving.py`'s `ERROR_TYPE_MAP` plus the 413/422 entries the HTTP layer maps in `http_server.py`'s `/v1/messages` exception handler. - `to_anthropic_fake_sse_events` eagerly synthesizes the Anthropic SSE event sequence from one complete `ChatCompletionResponse`, for callers that proxy a finished non-streaming response. - New `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_utils.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`): a delegation-equivalence matrix against a normally constructed `AnthropicServing` (16 request cases x 2 inline-system policies, 6 response cases, 10 statuses x 5 error bodies, failure-message equality), absolute goldens for the conversion semantics, a depth-2 gate canary, an AST cross-check of the 413/422 policy against `http_server.py`, fake-SSE sequences, and an import-hygiene subprocess test (no serving_chat / tokenizer manager / engine). ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Tests: `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/` passes (90 tests + 100 subtests, including the pre-existing `test_serving.py`). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32012531501](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32012531501)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32012531447](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32012531447)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: perf: fix overlap scheduling and all-reduce fusion for NVIDIA Confidential Computing(CC) on Blackwell
signal.text: ## Motivation Two fixes so SGLang runs efficiently under **NVIDIA Confidential Computing (CC)**, where the GPU operates behind a bounce buffer: 1. **Per-step D2H result readback stalls the scheduler.** Under CC, `cudaMemcpyAsync` (D2H) is forced synchronous — it blocks at issue — so the per-step readback of `next_token_ids` / logprobs serializes onto the scheduler's critical path and kills decode overlap. 2. **FlashInfer AR+RMSNorm fusion disables itself.** `create_allreduce_fusion_workspace` allocates a symmetric-memory (cuMulticast) workspace whose preflight fails under CC, so the fusion silently falls back off — even though the fusion kernels themselves are multicast-free. Both paths are gated on `is_confidential_compute()` (NVML, overridable via `SGLANG_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE`); **off-CC behavior is unchanged.** ## Modifications **`cc: async device->host result-readback worker`** - New `python/sglang/srt/managers/async_d2h_copy_worker.py` (`AsyncD2HCopyWorker`): runs the per-step D2H copy on a dedicated thread with its own CUDA stream, off the scheduler's critical path, so overlap is preserved. Wired into `scheduler.py` / `managers/utils.py`; only routed through the worker when CC is detected. - Adds `is_confidential_compute()` to `srt/utils/common.py`. **`cc(fix): enable FlashInfer AR+RMSNorm fusion under Confidential Computing`** (`layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`) - FlashInfer now auto-selects a multicast-free IPC workspace under CC, so SGLang reuses the normal off-CC fusion path: `_resolve_backend` forces the `trtllm` backend under CC (SM100 "auto" defaults to `mnnvl`, which needs NVLink multicast), the symmetric-memory preflight is skipped, and the workspace stays a normal `AllReduceFusionWorkspace`. signal.title: fix: Allow remote-loaded instances to serve as TransferEngine weight seeds
signal.text: ## Motivation **Fix:** After syncing weights from another instance via the transfer engine, it cannot serve as a seed to provide weights for other instances. When an instance loads model weights from another SGLang instance through TransferEngine, its destination memory regions are registered before the transfer and `weight_info` is already populated. Previously, `RemoteInstanceWeightTransporter` registered and published weight metadata only when `weight_info` was `None`. As a result, a destination instance could receive weights successfully but would not publish its existing TransferEngine session and weight metadata, preventing it from serving as a seed for downstream instances. ## Modifications - Decouple TransferEngine memory registration from seed metadata publication. - Reuse existing `weight_info` when the destination buffers were registered by the remote-instance loader. - Register model memory only when `weight_info` is missing. - Publish registered weight metadata when the instance is configured to start a TransferEngine seed service. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change only affects weight-transfer metadata registration and publication. It does not modify model weights, kernels, or model forward logic. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This change does not affect the inference execution path.It also avoids unnecessary duplicate memory registration. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [PD] Avoid unused PREBUILT prompt tensor transfer
signal.text: ## Motivation Decode-side PREBUILT batches never enter a model forward. However, `prepare_for_prebuilt` still flattened every transferred prompt and copied the result to a CUDA `input_ids` tensor. The first decode step later reconstructs its input from the relay metadata, so this prompt transfer is unused and can be expensive for long-context disaggregated requests. ## Modifications - Derive `extend_num_tokens` from the existing extend ranges. - Leave `input_ids` unset for PREBUILT batches instead of reading, flattening, and copying the complete prompt. - Preserve cache locations, sequence lengths, request-pool indices, sampling metadata, and relay behavior. - Add one regression case to the existing disaggregation wire test. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 requests, 5-shot chat evaluation: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Accuracy | **0.990** | | Mean speculative acceptance length | 4.528467 | | Acceptance rate | 0.705827 | | CUDA graph request fraction | 1.0 | | Retractions | 0 | | Error markers | 0 | The evaluation used natural model output; no simulated-accuracy path was enabled. ## Speed Tests and Profiling AgentX 393-trace workload, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, 24 GB300 GPUs, 4P+1D, concurrency 896. The production A/B uses each arm's independently aligned formal `180-900 s` window. | Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Exact-shape output TPS/User | 71.75528 | 84.65411 | **+17.97615%** | | Strict decode TPS/GPU | 3890.433 | 4385.898 | **+12.73548%** | | Matched mean context | — | — | -0.08271% | | Matched acceptance length | — | — | -0.03042% | A targeted replay of the 44 observed PREBUILT prompt shapes reduced the unused transfer from `1.690525` to `0.001745 ms/target-step` on the GPU-visible timeline (`1.688780 ms` saved); CPU wall saving was `1.688699 ms/target-step`. Targeted production-container unit coverage passed before the production A/B. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: [Feature][DSpark] Support Speculators-format checkpoints and ragged multimodal CUDA graphs
signal.text: <!-- Suggested title: [Feature][DSpark] Support native Speculators checkpoints and ragged multimodal CUDA graphs --> > **Status:** implementation, public-checkpoint compatibility, and paired > fixed-output performance tests are complete. Greedy target-output equivalence > remains unresolved, so this PR does not claim lossless output. ## Motivation This PR extends SGLang's DSpark path to run native Speculators checkpoints end to end in eager mode, CUDA Graph replay, and ragged multimodal verification. It covers the checkpoint config and weight formats, both DSpark anchor layouts, independent draft vocabularies, and the runtime paths needed to verify them. Native Speculators checkpoints are not limited to the shared-vocabulary layout that DSpark originally supported in SGLang. They may contain an independent reduced-vocabulary LM head plus a draft-to-target (`d2t`) mapping. For example, the public [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark) checkpoint has: - target vocabulary: 248,320 tokens; - draft `lm_head`: 32,000 tokens; - `markov_w1`: target-vocabulary input; - `markov_w2`: draft-vocabulary output; - `d2t`: a 32,000-entry mapping from sampled draft IDs to target IDs. Treating these tensors as a shared-vocabulary model either fails during loading or feeds/scatters IDs in the wrong vocabulary space. Speculators checkpoints can also use either DSpark draft-block layout: - `sample_from_anchor=false`: the anchor is only a conditioning token. The draft forward has `gamma + 1` slots, and slot 0 is excluded from sampling and verification. - `sample_from_anchor=true`: the anchor is a trained prediction. The draft forward has `gamma` slots. Using the wrong width does not always crash; it can shift real draft positions and reduce the acceptance length toward 1. After checkpoint loading and draft geometry were working, mixed image/text validation exposed separate problems in ragged mRoPE and linear attention. The ragged-path changes make multimodal verification work under CUDA Graphs. During the same validation, I found a pre-existing interaction between `/flush_cache` and DSpark draft CUDA Graphs: emptying the allocator cache can invalidate addresses retained by a captured graph. This is included as a separate DSpark graph-lifecycle fix. ## Modifications - Normalize the native Speculators DSpark config format, whose backbone lives under `transformer_layer_config`, without importing checkpoint-side remote config code. This path is gated on `speculators_model_type=dspark` and reuses the existing config-dictionary fetch. - Load an independent tensor-parallel `ParallelLMHead` when `draft_vocab_size != target_vocab_size`; preserve the original shared-head path for full-vocabulary DSpark checkpoints. - Support the asymmetric Markov geometry: `markov_w1` consumes target IDs while `markov_w2` and the draft LM head produce draft-vocabulary logits. - Map sampled draft IDs through `d2t` before storing tokens or feeding the next Markov step. For probabilistic acceptance, scatter draft probabilities into target-vocabulary columns and leave unmapped target tokens at `-inf`. - Validate mapping shape/range and fail early for unsupported reduced-vocabulary checkpoints without `d2t`. Load `t2d` as checkpoint metadata without using it in the decode path. - Read authoritative `gamma` and `sample_from_anchor` metadata, reject inconsistent checkpoint geometry at startup, and propagate the same draft width through eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. - Keep verification, KV commit, and acceptance accounting at `gamma` real draft tokens. Only the draft forward width changes. - Build speculative mRoPE positions from each request's actual verify length; CUDA Graph padding uses zero-delta ghost positions. - Add packed-to-dense scatter/gather support for ragged linear attention and declare ragged CUDA Graph support per attention backend. - Preserve captured DSpark draft graph allocations across `/flush_cache` while still clearing logical request, KV, radix, grammar, and metrics state. - Use an 8-token SPS `M` bin for compact scheduling and recompute the simulated bonus token at the acceptance boundary. - Add regression coverage for full/reduced vocabularies, configuration normalization, tensor-parallel LM heads, Markov shapes, `d2t` mapping, corrected-logit scatter, both checkpoint layouts, CUDA Graphs, ragged mRoPE, linear attention, cache flushing, and SPS fitting. ## Status - [x] Bonus-anchor and dense anchor-first checkpoint layouts - [x] Full-vocabulary DSpark checkpoint regression - [x] Independent reduced-vocabulary LM head - [x] Draft-to-target vocabulary mapping and probabilistic corrected logits - [x] Eager and CUDA Graph draft-width propagation - [x] TP=1 and TP=2 public RedHat checkpoint inference - [x] Greedy and non-greedy sampling - [x] Ragged multimodal mRoPE and linear-attention layouts - [x] DSpark CUDA Graph behavior after `/flush_cache` - [ ] Greedy token-level equivalence with target-only decoding - [x] Same-GPU paired performance benchmark at concurrency 1 and 8 ## Correctness Tests On the PR branch rebased onto upstream `main` on 2026-08-13, the focused suite reports `212 passed, 54 subtests passed`; the reduced-vocabulary file reports `26 passed, 2 subtests passed`. Python compilation, formatting, focused Ruff checks, and `git diff --check` also pass. The public-checkpoint validation uses [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4) as the target and [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark) as the draft. The environment has PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, and FlashInfer 0.6.17. The official workloads are MT-Bench (80 two-turn conversations, 160 requests) and the MMSpec test split (600 conversations, 723 turns). Correctness runs compare target-only autoregressive (AR) decoding with DSpark under greedy decoding at concurrency 1. | Workload | AR repeat | DSpark completed | Exact first-turn AR/DSpark token sequences | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 160/160 | 160/160 | 8/80 | | MMSpec | 723/723 | 723/723 | 18/600 | The AR repeat is exact on both workloads, confirming a deterministic baseline. DSpark completes every request, but target-output equivalence is not established. A separate 20-prompt eager probe also mismatches on all 20 prompts, so disabling decode CUDA Graph does not remove the divergence; its cause remains unresolved. Acceptance is aggregated from raw server counters. The acceptance length below includes the target bonus token. | Workload | Draft acceptance rate | Acceptance length including bonus | | --- | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 32.863% | 3.6257 | | MMSpec | 24.956% | 2.9925 | Separate focused lanes also pass TP=1 and TP=2 inference, greedy and non-greedy sampling, ragged multimodal CUDA Graph replay, and a post-`/flush_cache` request. ## Fixed-output Performance The formal fixed-output benchmark consists of three same-GPU paired repeats with service restart and unmeasured warm-up before each mode: - MT-Bench first turns with exactly 256 output tokens per request; - a deterministic 20-per-topic MMSpec subset with exactly 128 output tokens per request; - closed-loop concurrency 1 and 8; - pair order `target -> DSpark`, `DSpark -> target`, `target -> DSpark`. All 2,400 measured requests completed with the required output length. Values below are medians across the three runs; the interval is the range of the three paired throughput ratios. The raw service logs and result manifests bind these runs to the reported source commit and execution-environment freeze; strict reanalyzing after the provenance audit produced an identical summary. | Workload | C | Target tok/s | DSpark tok/s | Paired throughput | p50 E2E target -> DSpark | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | MT-Bench | 1 | 151.64 | 262.32 | 1.730x [1.726, 1.741] | 1.687s -> 1.008s | | MT-Bench | 8 | 715.30 | 942.30 | 1.317x [1.300, 1.327] | 2.853s -> 2.076s | | MMSpec | 1 | 132.89 | 178.49 | 1.343x [1.343, 1.346] | 0.937s -> 0.715s | | MMSpec | 8 | 467.98 | 519.74 | 1.111x [1.110, 1.124] | 2.086s -> 1.754s | The gain is not uniform across the latency distribution. MT-Bench C=8 p99 E2E regresses in all three repeats (paired target/DSpark ratios 0.906-0.920). MMSpec C=8 has about 9% higher p50 TPOT and mixed p99 E2E results (paired ratios 0.938-1.092, median 0.961). This supports a stable fixed-output throughput and p50 E2E improvement under the reported configuration, not a universal tail-latency improvement. SSE chunk gaps are not reported as token-level ITL because one speculative event can expose multiple tokens. TPOT is client-observed and amortized from the first to last token-bearing event. ## Known limitation Greedy token-level equivalence with target-only decoding has not been established for the tested public checkpoint. The reported results demonstrate checkpoint compatibility, request completion, online acceptance, and fixed-output performance, but do not support a lossless-output claim. ## Related work - Original SGLang DSpark implementation: [#30261](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30261) - Bonus-anchor checkpoint layout: [#30982](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30982) - vLLM Speculators checkpoint support: [vLLM #47093](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47093) Thanks to the authors and reviewers of these changes for the checkpoint-layout analysis and reference behavior. ## Contributors Engine Architecture Group 5, Engine Infrastructure Department, Xiaohongshu (RedNote): Su Zhan, Fei Ziyu, Hong Chenchen, Luo Zhaokai, Jin Huayi. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32011377578](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32011377578)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32011377305](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32011377305)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec] Resolve shared-read ends from the backend declaration alone
signal.text: The decode runner gated the shared-read-ends resolution on the forward mode before asking the backend. Both halves of that gate are now redundant: - `elif not forward_mode.is_decode()` -- the modes that reach this runner are `DECODE` / `TARGET_VERIFY` / `IDLE` / `DLLM_EXTEND` (plus `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2`, since the multi-layer eagle draft-extend runner subclasses it), and the base `shared_read_ends` already returns `UNKNOWN` for everything but decode and target verify. No in-tree override deviates on those modes. - the `is_last_shared_read_phase` check -- which runner owns the publish is already answered by `last_shared_read_runner`. For every algorithm whose last reading phase is not verify, the target runner is not the runner the scheduler reads, so its verify record is simply never picked up. `is_last_shared_read_phase` had no other caller, so it is deleted from both `SpeculativeAlgorithm` and `CustomSpecAlgo`. A plugin whose last reading phase is not the target verify should point `last_shared_read_runner` at the runner that does run it, or drop the record the way NGRAM does below. NGRAM is the one algorithm the gate was load-bearing for: its scheduler-read runner *is* the target runner, so dropping the gate hands the barrier a fine-grained record for the verify. That record is not sound -- NGRAM's verify keeps reading scheduler-shared state past the runner's in-graph marker, and the fine-grained fence reproduces device-side index asserts (`indexSelectSmallIndex: srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize`) in `test_spec_ngram.py`. `NGRAMWorker` now clears the record after verify, so the scheduler keeps the coarse whole-forward fence it had before this PR. Also refreshes two stale comments that enumerated which phase publishes the event; the owner is `last_shared_read_runner`, not a fixed list. Stacks on #35057, which is what makes the verify record harmless for multi-layer eagle. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32003256628](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32003256628)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32003256417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32003256417)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix inflated row pitch when a CP round-robin shard has a single row
signal.text: ## Motivation `dsa_cp_round_robin_split_data` can hand downstream kernels a shard whose row pitch is `cp_size` times too large, which on DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism causes a GPU memory fault. The last line of the function is ```python return input_.view(-1, cp_size, *input_.shape[1:])[:, cp_rank].contiguous() ``` When a prefill chunk holds exactly `cp_size` tokens, every rank's shard has a **single row**. A size-1 outer dimension imposes no contiguity constraint, so `is_contiguous()` returns `True` regardless of `stride(0)` — and `.contiguous()` becomes a no-op. The shard keeps the `cp_size`-inflated row pitch, `cp_size * row_numel` instead of `row_numel`. Any kernel that takes its row pitch from `stride(0)` then treats the shard as `cp_size` times larger than it is. On DeepSeek-V4 (`hc_mult=4`, `hidden_size=7168`, `cp_size=8`) the pitch is `229376` instead of `28672`; aiter's `mhc_pre` sizes its buffer descriptors from it and addresses past the tensor: ``` Memory access fault by GPU node-N on address 0x... (8 GPUs, 8 distinct addresses) Fatal Python error: Aborted deepseek_v4.py:1541 hc_pre -> aiter/ops/mhc.py:372 mhc_pre ``` ### Reproducer (deterministic, no GPU fault needed) ```python import torch HC, HID, CP = 4, 7168, 8 for tokens in (8, 16, 24): x = torch.randn(tokens, HC, HID, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") # contiguous out = x.view(-1, CP, *x.shape[1:])[:, 7].contiguous() # the current line print(f"tokens={tokens:3d} m={out.shape[0]} stride0={out.stride(0):7d} " f"expected={HC*HID} is_contiguous={out.is_contiguous()}") ``` ``` tokens= 8 m=1 stride0= 229376 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True <-- no-op, pitch is 8x tokens= 16 m=2 stride0= 28672 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True tokens= 24 m=3 stride0= 28672 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True ``` ## Modifications Compare the shard's row pitch against the parent's and copy with `clone(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)` only when they differ, plus a comment explaining why `.contiguous()` cannot be used here. Copy behaviour versus the current code (`row_numel = prod(shape[1:])`): | `cp_size` | shard rows | current | this PR | note | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | any | no copy | **no copy** | shard is genuinely contiguous | | >1 | 1 | **no copy** (pitch stays `cp_size * row_numel`) | copy | this is the bug being fixed | | >1 | >=2 | copy | copy | unchanged | So the only added copy is the one that is required for correctness, and it copies a single row. An unconditional `clone()` would also have copied for `cp_size == 1`, where `.contiguous()` correctly does nothing, so the pitch comparison is used instead. Values are unchanged in every case. Verified alternatives that also work: `torch.empty(shape).copy_(shard)`, `shard.reshape(-1, *shard.shape[1:])`. Does **not** work: `.contiguous()`, and `input_[cp_rank::cp_size].contiguous()`. ## Accuracy Tests Values are bit-identical to the current code in all cases (the change only affects the layout of a shard whose contents are already correct): ``` tokens= 8 rank=0: m=1 old_stride0=2272 new_stride0=284 torch.equal(old, new) = True tokens= 8 rank=7: m=1 old_stride0=2272 new_stride0=284 torch.equal(old, new) = True tokens= 16 rank=0: m=2 old_stride0= 284 new_stride0=284 torch.equal(old, new) = True tokens= 24 rank=7: m=3 old_stride0= 284 new_stride0=284 torch.equal(old, new) = True ``` Separately, feeding a strided shard to the affected kernel produces wrong results, which is what this fix prevents downstream (same logical values via a strided view vs a compacted copy, DeepSeek-V4 dims): ``` m=2 cp=8 max|diff| in y = 7.42 m=4 cp=8 max|diff| in y = 10.31 ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling The copy runs only for single-row shards. Measured on MI355X, `(1, 4, 7168)` bf16 = 56 KB: ``` clone(memory_format=contiguous_format) on (1, 4, 7168) bf16 = 56 KB : 0.1 us per call observed frequency: 8 calls per ~5,200 mhc_pre calls in a 3600 s run => ~1 us added per hour-long run ``` The `m >= 2` path is unchanged — `.contiguous()` already copied there — and `cp_size == 1` still copies nothing. ### End-to-end validation 1P1D DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 on MI355X, prefill TP8/EP8/**CP8** (`interleave`), decode TP8/EP8/DP8, agentic trace replay. Instrumented runs logging every `mhc_pre` shard's strides, before the fix: | runs | mhc_pre calls | shards with the inflated pitch | GPU memory faults | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 7 runs | ~45,000 | 0 | 0 | | 1 run | 5,240 | **8** (one per CP rank) | **8** | The condition is rare by default because a request's tail chunk is `extend_len % chunked_prefill_size`, so at 8192 a chunk small enough to leave a rank with one token occurs for roughly 1 request in 1000. Forcing it with `chunked-prefill-size 256` raises the rate to ~3%: | run | forced | fix | single-row shards | inflated pitch | faults | outcome | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---| | A | yes | no | yes | **8** | **8** | crash after ~15 min | | B | yes | **yes** | **8** | **0** | **0** | no fault | Same trigger and the same number of single-row shards; the fix removes the inflated pitch and the faults. ## Related observation (not changed here) `python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/cp_utils.py:194` has the same pattern: ```python input_ids = input_ids[cp_rank::cp_size].contiguous() ``` I verified this `.contiguous()` is also a no-op for a single-element shard (it leaves `stride(0) == cp_size`). It is not known to cause a failure today — `input_ids` is consumed by ops that honour strides — so I left it alone to keep this PR focused, but it may be worth the same treatment. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. — the function calls `get_parallel()` and needs a distributed context, so the reproducer above is given instead; happy to add a test if you can point me at the right harness. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. — not applicable. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32010474564](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32010474564)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32010474245](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32010474245)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [SM120] DeepSeek-V4: DeepGEMM paged-MQA indexer +FP4 MoE+ page-split
signal.text: **Motivation:** a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) box can hold DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but on current main the only configuration that starts there is the slow torch fallback — this PR makes the DeepGEMM and FlashInfer paths work on SM120, cutting decode latency up to 3.4x. It routes the sparse-MLA indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel, enables batched sparse-MLA prefill through FlashInfer, and unblocks the DeepGEMM FP4 MoE backend. ## Split out of this PR Following @Fridge003's review, the changes here that were not SM120 enablement now have their own PRs: - #35116 — allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode (correctness fix) - #35118 — fuse the hc-prenorm combine into a Triton kernel (arch-independent) **This PR now depends on #35116**: without it the page-split buffer is allocated under inference mode during autotune and CUDA graph capture cannot write to it. Will rebase once it lands. The E2E tables below were measured with #35118 still in this tree. Measured separately on the same box with only that kernel toggled (ISL 8K, BS1, TP4, deep_gemm MoE), it accounts for **3.2% of the TPOT gain** (12.81 -> 12.40 ms, two repeats each, run-to-run spread 0.01 ms) and roughly 2% of TTFT. Discount the tables by that much, or land #35118 first to reproduce them as written. ## What is in it 1. **Sparse-MLA indexer on DeepGEMM** — route the indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel instead of the eager-torch fallback that scales with batch x context and dominates decode. Opt in with `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. 2. **Batched sparse-MLA prefill** — prefill (q_len > 64) goes through FlashInfer's `_sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention`; indexer metadata is chunked at M=4096 (the DeepGEMM row cap is SKU-dependent) and built once per batch instead of per layer. 3. **Page-split dirty mask** — `_split_kv_pages_to_64` re-laid out the whole SWA KV pool (~105 MB/layer) every decode step; now only the pages this step's top-k references are split (CUDA-graph safe, bit-identical). 4. **DeepGEMM FP4 MoE on SM120** — probe the block-scale entry point (DeepGEMM#324) instead of hard-disabling DeepGEMM at `sm==120`, plus the contiguous grouped-GEMM prefill path, the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant fix, and the swiglu-clamp fallback for TP>=2 shapes. 5. **SM120 kernel fixes** — u64 page-split copy, sparse-prefill head pad removal, TileLang `mhc_pre` compile fix, and the paged-MQA metadata kernel now sizes its shared-memory request from the device budget instead of a fixed 128 KB. Non-SM120 architectures are unchanged: every behavioural change is either gated on `is_sm120_supported()` or is a fix that only engages where the previous code was wrong (the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant and the shared-memory cap). ## E2E benefit "main" is marlin MoE + the torch paged-MQA fallback, because that is the only SM120 path on `14bd315d` that starts: the default (`flashinfer_mxfp4` + TileLang indexer) dies in the TileLang JIT for `sm_120a` (TileLang ships nvcc 13.3, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` has CUDA 13.0 headers), and `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` raises `AttributeError: module 'sglang.srt.layers.deep_gemm_wrapper' has no attribute 'get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor'` (SM120 disables `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM` while the runner stays selectable). Both sides then run identical server args, only the tree differs: TP4, marlin MoE, CUTLASS FP8, chunked prefill 8192, `--disable-radix-cache`, and no speculative decoding except where the tables say otherwise. 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, OSL 256, `--warmup-requests 0` so every measured request is a real prefill. TTFT is a median. **Single request (BS=1)** — 3 sequential requests, median. TTFT: | ISL | main | this PR | | |---|---|---|---| | 8K | 1124 ms | 899 ms | −20% | | 32K | 4540 ms | 3585 ms | −21% | | 128K | 20107 ms | 15481 ms | −23% | TPOT, without and with MTP-2 (EAGLE, 2 steps / 3 draft tokens) on both sides: | ISL | main | this PR | | main + MTP-2 | this PR + MTP-2 | | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8K | 36.1 ms | 10.5 ms | **3.4x** | 13.6 ms | 6.0 ms | 2.3x | | 32K | 35.8 ms | 10.7 ms | **3.3x** | 12.6 ms | 5.7 ms | 2.2x | | 128K | 36.1 ms | 11.9 ms | **3.0x** | 13.4 ms | 6.8 ms | 2.0x | Accepted length is within 0.2 of each other on the two sides at every context length, so the MTP gain comes from the decode path itself, not from better speculation. **Concurrent (ISL 8K)** — `--num-prompts BS --max-concurrency BS`: | BS | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | | output tok/s main | output tok/s this PR | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 3574 ms | 2826 ms | −21% | 42.9 ms | 16.8 ms | 2.6x | 71 | 147 | | 8 | 5660 ms | 4530 ms | −20% | 51.9 ms | 24.3 ms | 2.1x | 108 | 191 | | 16 | 10482 ms | 8365 ms | −20% | 71.6 ms | 40.9 ms | 1.8x | 143 | 219 | TTFT holds at −20% across batch sizes; the decode multiple decays with batch (3.4x at BS1, 1.8x at BS16) because what this PR removes is per-step fixed cost, which amortises as the batch grows. Speculative decoding amortises it the same way. GSM8K (50 questions) is 0.980 on main and 0.960 on this PR at 8K — one question apart. All tables are without prefill context parallelism, which is upstream code this PR does not touch. <details> <summary>Recipes</summary> Common to both: `--fp8-gemm-backend cutlass --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32`, plus `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. **Prefill-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1`. **Decode-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend marlin --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1`. </details> ## Dependencies - FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (SM120 sparse-MLA kernels) and sglang-kernel 0.4.5 — both are what `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` currently ships. - DeepGEMM at or after deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#324 for the FP4 MoE backend. The `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` indexer path additionally needs DeepGEMM's attention host-gates to accept SM120 (a 3-line arch gate, not yet upstream in sgl-project/DeepGEMM); without it, keep the TileLang indexer default. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant.py` (9 cases, registered for CI) covers the fused swiglu-clamp + silu_mul + fp8-quant kernel against a reference. GSM8K numbers are from `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`. Reviewed and validated with @ormandj (conflict resolution) and @moxcat (inference-mode buffer fix, now #35116) on 2x and 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. Re-validated after the split on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (the pinned version), this tree plus #35116: GSM8K-50 1.000 with `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, 0.960 with MTP-2; ISL 8K BS1 TTFT 116/88 ms, TPOT 12.8/7.3 ms. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #30265 / #29781 (supersedes #30379). #30265 merged with two gaps flagged in its own review: 1. The GLM-5.2 Quark-MXFP4 MTP path has **no PR-CI coverage** — the only AMD GLM-MXFP4 test is `nightly=True` and does not enable MTP; the GLM MTP e2e test is CUDA-only + FP8, not Quark MXFP4. 2. `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN._resolve_nextn_quant_config` remaps `layer_quant_config` keys by **mutating the shared `quant_config` in place**, which can corrupt the main model's per-layer scheme selection (gemini-code-assist review on #30265). The fix and the CPU test here originate from #30379 (@fanxingran, co-authored). ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py`: `_resolve_nextn_quant_config` `copy.copy`s `quant_config` (and its nested dict) **before** any remap, and only copies when a remap/exclude is actually needed — no shared-state mutation. - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_nextn.py`: docstring on the base `_resolve_nextn_quant_config` documenting the subclass override contract. - `test/registered/unit/models/test_nextn_quark_exclude.py` (new, CPU CI `base-a-test-cpu`): base `DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN` passthrough (non-quark / `None`), GLM-5.2 MTP `exclude_layers` + `layer_quant_config` remap, coarse fused-expert prefix, and the no-mutation guarantee. - `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_glm52_mxfp4_mtp_eval_mi35x.py` (new, nightly `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-glm52-mxfp4-mtp`): 8-GPU GLM-5.2-MXFP4 EAGLE-MTP GSM8K eval — GPU coverage that the bf16 nextn layer loads under Quark MXFP4 and MTP accepts drafts. Wired into `nightly-test-amd.yml` and `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`. ## Accuracy Tests CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/models/test_nextn_quark_exclude.py` on this branch: ``` 6 passed, 5 warnings in 10.64s ``` `test_layer_quant_config_keys_remapped_without_mutation` fails on current `main` (exercises the #30265 in-place mutation); green after this change. `pre-commit run` passes all hooks (isort/ruff/black/yaml/duplicate-job-name/registry validation). Nightly GPU eval thresholds are the reported `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` MI355x numbers: GSM8K accuracy floor **0.935** (#29781 measured 0.950 at EAGLE 5/1/6, the fixture's config) and accept-length floor **5.0** (#30265 measured 5.94). ## Speed Benchmarks N/A — quant-config resolution runs once at model construction; no inference-path change. ## Checklist - [x] CPU unit test added and registered (`base-a-test-cpu`) - [x] Nightly GPU test added and wired into the AMD nightly workflows - [x] Co-authored with the original author (#30379) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32010423443](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32010423443)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32010423453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32010423453)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(moe): fold padded-topk_ids fill into fused shared-experts append+remap
signal.text: ## Summary On the aiter **per-rank shared-slot** path (MoRI / DeepEP-class EP, EPLB off), the padded-`topk_ids` region was zero-filled by a **separate `_fill_padded_rows` Triton launch** immediately before the fused shared-experts **append + per-rank-shared-slot remap** kernel ran. This PR **folds that padded fill into the append+remap kernel**: rows `>= num_token_non_padded` get `pad_fill_id` in every routed slot, computed on the rows already loaded into registers. With `pad_fill_id=0` the result is **bit-identical** to the old `fill(topk_ids=0) -> remap(0)=0`, and it removes **one launch-bound kernel per MoE layer per step**. The win shows up in decode TPOT and is largest at low concurrency (launch/latency-bound), tapering at higher concurrency. The fold is gated so it only triggers when the fused append+remap kernel will actually run (`num_fused_shared_experts > 0 and _use_aiter and use_per_rank_shared_slots and not EPLB remap`); otherwise the separate fill is kept (unchanged behavior). ## What changed - `kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`: `_fused_append_remap_shared_experts_deepep_kernel` gains `num_token_non_padded_ptr` / `pad_fill_id` / `HAS_PADDING`; the wrapper takes optional `num_token_non_padded=None, pad_fill_id=0`. - `srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: on the HIP/aiter path, skip the separate `_fill_padded_rows` launch when the fold will run, and pass `num_token_non_padded` into the fused append+remap call. - `test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_remap_per_rank_shared_slots.py`: adds `test_pad_fold_matches_separate_fill` guarding fold == separate-fill. ## Profiling Before After ## Validation **Environment:** `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260715` (MI355X / gfx950) **Model:** `DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4` **Config:** TP8 / EP8 / DP-attention, MoRI-EP, shared-experts fusion, `SGLANG_MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE=fp8` Server: ```bash export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_MOE=1 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 export SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=1 export SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM=1 TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1 export SGLANG_AITER_AR=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=512 export TRITON_ENABLE_PRELOAD_KERNELS=0 TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT=1 PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True export SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_MLA_CONCAT_CACHE=1 SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_KVB_SPLIT_CAT=1 export MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=16G SGLANG_MORI_LEC_IN_GRAPH=0 export SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=auto SGLANG_MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE=fp8 export SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096 SGLANG_MORI_NO_PAD_MASK=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /data/inference/models/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 signal.title: MXFP4 (E2M1+E8M0) KV cache for Ampere sm86: quantization + fused decode kernels [WIP]
signal.text: ## Summary Experimental MXFP4 KV cache for GPUs without native MXFP4 tensor-core support (targeting Ampere sm86, e.g. RTX 3090). Research/WIP — **not ready for review yet**; opened as a draft to track ongoing kernel work. Components: - **Quantization kernels** (JIT, `python/sglang/srt/layers/jit_kernels/`): packed E2M1 values + E8M0 block scales (block32), round-to-nearest-even, bit-exact against a torch reference. - **Fused decode attention kernel**: reads packed FP4 K/V directly from the pool and dequantizes in registers (no bf16 workspace round-trip), flashinfer-style CUDA-cores pipeline with online softmax. - **Integration**: `--kv-cache-dtype fp4_mx_block32` (server_args → memory pool layout with separate data/scale buffers → model_runner capacity accounting → flashinfer backend prefill path). Vendored flashinfer 0.3.1 decode headers patched for CUDA 12.6. ## Current status (Qwen3-4B, single RTX 3090, production defaults: CUDA graph + radix + overlap on) | | BF16 | MXFP4 | |---|---|---| | GSM8K (200) | 94.0% | ~89% | | KV capacity | 1x | ~3.7x | | TPOT | 1x | +26% | The TPOT gap is measured to be entirely in the decode kernel (FP4 fused 0.855ms vs fp16 tensor-core 0.475ms at batch=100/seq=1024; dequant ALU is the dominant cost). Ongoing work: closing that kernel-level gap. ## Status Draft on purpose — this is early-stage exploration (part of a research thesis). Will mark ready-for-review and ping maintainers once the kernel work settles.
