signal.title: [AMD] Strict bit-exact SWA HiCache for DeepSeek-V4 with unified_kv: SWA-window + c4/indexer state riding across L1/L2/L3
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> DeepSeek-V4's `unified_kv` backend on ROCm packs three KV families in one pool: the content-addressed compressed KV (C4/C128), the per-request **SWA ring** (addressed by `req_pool_idx * window + pos % window`), and the compressor's **c4 / indexer overlap state**. Only the compressed KV is content-stable; the SWA ring and the c4/indexer overlap state are not, and are never written into the radix tree. Two prior PRs made reuse of such prefixes *safe* but only **approximately correct**: - **#29417** enabled unified_kv HiCache, but it offloads **only** the compressed KV (C4/C128). The SWA ring is not preserved, so on a hierarchical hit the trailing sliding window is **re-prefilled** (`swa_reprefill_tail_tokens()`) rather than restored. - **#30339** applied the same **re-prefill** idea to the radix-only path: cap the match by the trailing window and recompute it into the request's own ring, so decode never reads a stale ring. Re-prefill recomputes the trailing window (and, implicitly, the c4/indexer overlap state for that region) instead of reproducing the exact values the original prefill wrote. That is enough to prevent gross stale-ring errors and to keep GSM8K-level accuracy within noise — but it is **not bit-exact**: a partial re-prefill cannot reconstruct the original SWA window and c4/indexer overlap state byte-for-byte, so the reused output can differ from a full fresh compute at the bit level. This PR closes that gap. Instead of re-prefilling an approximation, it **captures and offloads the true values** of the SWA window and the c4/indexer overlap state across L1→L2→L3, and **restores them exactly** on a hierarchical hit — making unified_kv SWA prefix reuse **strict and bit-exact**. A hard reuse gate re-prefills only when the truth is unavailable (never a stale/approximate read). This is an **opt-in** gated by `SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE` (default **off**), and it engages only when **all** of the following hold at once: - running **DeepSeek-V4** on **ROCm/HIP**; - the **`unified_kv_triton`** attention backend is chosen (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`); - **HiCache is enabled** (`--enable-hierarchical-cache`). In every other case, the feature is a strict no-op, no pool is allocated, no capture, no restore; behavior is byte-identical to `main`. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> Organized as three layers: **1. Substrate (Commit 1–5):** - `SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE` flag + `--hicache-swa-offload-page-stride` arg (`environ.py`, `server_args.py`). - Dedicated pinned-host SWA-window offload pool with capture-done handshake + upstream deferred release (`memory_pool_host.py`). - Two independent, tile-start-addressed L3 pools for c4 state and indexer state, packing (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`). - Version-namespaced L3 keys (`hicache_storage.py`, `storage/nixl/hicache_nixl.py`). - Startup fail-fast guard (`hybrid_pool_assembler.py`): with the strict flag on, raise a clear `ValueError` unless `--hicache-write-policy write_through`, before any host pool is pinned. **2. Capture (Commit 6–8):** - Capture the SWA ring window at each completed prefill/decode page with EAGLE-safe geometry (`deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py`, `model_runner.py`, `deepseek_v4.py`). - Snapshot c4/indexer overlap state for the same window into the independent state pools (`compress_hip.py`, `compressor_v2.py`). **3. Reuse/restore + strict gate (Commit 9–10):** - Ride the captured window + state back to device at the correct `buf_lo` offset on a hierarchical hit; **strict reuse gate** caps the match and re-prefills any tail that isn't provably bit-exact, never a stale read; commit-coupling guard keeps window+state+full-KV committed atomically (`swa_component.py`, `unified_radix_cache.py`, `base_prefix_cache.py`, `schedule_batch.py`, `schedule_policy.py`). ## Note to reviewers This PR can be split into three cumulative sub-PRs on request — substrate / capture / reuse (boundaries C1–5 / C6–8 / C9–10) — each gated by the same flag and a strict no-op by default. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> Two detectors (like #30339): a byte-exact harness is the real detector; GSM8K is only a no-regression guard. ### 1. Unit Tests (5 test files, 163 UTs total) **How:** `cd test && python3 -m pytest -q srt/mem_cache/test_swa_*.py` **Expected:** `163 passed` — byte-exact swa+c4_state/c4_indexer_state capture/restore across L1→L2→L3, strict-gate reject, commit-coupling guard, dirty-read protection, L3-only restore. ### 2. E2E (DeepSeek-V4 unified_kv on ROCm, HiCache + strict flag) **How:** launch with the gates on and `SGLANG_SWA_DBG_CHECKSUM=1` (emits a per-window checksum vs a fresh device re-read), trigger prefix reuse, grep the log. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE=1 # dev; set 0 for the "off" baseline export SGLANG_SWA_DBG_CHECKSUM=1 # + standard dsv4 env as in #30339 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --enable-cache-report --port 30001 \ --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through \ --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout layer_first \ --tp 4 --dp 4 --enable-dp-attention 2>&1 | tee server.log # decode + EAGLE spec path (tp8/dp8): add --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 # L3-only variant: add --hicache-storage-backend file --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete # + SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR=/ssd/dir, populate, kill, restart same dir, resend prefix ``` **Trigger reuse** — send the same long prompt N rounds; `cached_tokens` climbs 0 → large: ```bash python3 - <<'PY' import json, urllib.request P = "This is a long shared prefix sentence. " * 4000 # >> page_size (256) tokens for r in range(6): # 6 for prefill; 20 for decode dp8 (every rank must hit) b = json.dumps({"model": "x", "prompt": P, "max_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0}).encode() u = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request( "http://127.0.0.1:30001/v1/completions", data=b, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})).read())["usage"] print("round", r, "cached_tokens", (u.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens", 0)) PY ``` **Expected** (grep `server.log`): | check | grep | expect | | --- | --- | --- | | byte-exact SWA + c4/indexer | `[C4-STATE-DBG]` state ride bit-exact / `[LB-DEV]` device landing byte-exact / `[SWA-DBG]` restore verified | **L1/L2 same-process reuse**: all three **> 0**. **L3-only cross-restart**: `[LB-DEV]` + `[C4-STATE-DBG]` **> 0** (`[SWA-DBG]` is **0** on this path — the prefill checksum is not persisted across a process restart, so the window's byte-exact verification is carried by `[LB-DEV]` device-landing). | | no failure / no dirty read | `MISMATCH\|reuse_reject\|BIND-MISS\|AssertionError\|Traceback` | **0** | | L3-only source | `prefetch .*matched=[0-9]+ loaded=[0-9]+` | `matched=0 loaded>0` | **L3-only restore validated** (cold restart, empty L1/L2): `prefetch matched=0 loaded=2304`, the first request immediately reports `cached_tokens=2304`, `[LB-DEV]` + `[C4-STATE-DBG]` byte-exact all pass, zero `MISMATCH`. **gsm8k eval**: Two arms, each run once per server profile — off (SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE=0) and dev (=1) — with the cache flushed (/flush_cache) before each pass and temperature=0, so the only variable is the strict flag. GSM8K is a no-regression guard (the byte-exact harness above is the real correctness detector); the acceptance criterion is that dev is not below off and invalid ≈ 0. - non-thinking ``` python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30001 --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1319 --parallel 256 ``` For off (SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE=0) and dev (=1) , all above tests we got acc ~0.94(invalid ≈ 0). - thinking ``` python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --eval-name gsm8k --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30001 \ --num-threads 256 --temperature 0.0 --repeat 1 --num-shots 8 --max-tokens 8192 ``` For off, we got 0.933, and for dev, we got 0.942(invalid 0). ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> Both arms HiCache on, `DBG=0`, `--hicache-ratio 1.0` (single variable = strict flag); customer clients. Just take some of the configs as example. | scenario | metric | off | dev | note | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Prefill (dp4, 50k ISL, prefix-cache0.6) | tokens/s | ≈ 32.7k | ≈ 30.8k | dev ≈ −5.8%| | Prefill (dp4, 50k ISL, prefix-cache0.8) | tokens/s | ≈ 31.4k | ≈ 29.1k | dev ≈ −7.3%| | Decode TPOT (dp8, EAGLE, batch 32/48/64) | ms/token | ≈ 70.6 / 82.4 / 96.8 | ≈ 70.8 / 83.8 / 98.4 | dev slightly slower, no regression | The prefill cost is the deterministic price of strict correctness (positional H2D of the SWA window + c4/indexer state on reuse, not a content-addressed page copy), applied only with the flag on. **Optional in-repo reproduction.** The table above comes from the customer perf clients. For a self-contained check that needs no external scripts, the stock bench_serving client reproduces the strict overhead directly in-repo (it is a different, smaller workload, so absolute numbers differ). Launch the same server twice with DBG=0 — once SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE=1 (dev), once =0 (off) — then run against each: ```bash python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 50000 --random-output-len 200 --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 42 --port 30001 ``` Compare peak output token throughput: dev trails off by a small, consistent margin (measured off ≈ 1536 tok/s vs dev ≈ 1472 tok/s, ≈ −4%), the same direction as the customer-client table. Note that at this concurrency/input length the Median/P99 TTFT is dominated by request queueing (~50–100 s) and is not a reliable reuse detector — prefix-reuse correctness is verified separately by the byte-exact harness and the climbing cached_tokens above, not by this client's TTFT. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [NPU] Add sparsity-driven KV offload for DeepSeek DSA on Ascend
signal.text: # [NPU] Add sparsity-driven KV offload for DeepSeek DSA on Ascend USTC: Yinhe Chen, Chengru Yang, Chengjie Tang(SXU, intern at USTC-IAI), Youhui Bai, Cheng Li Ascend NPU Network Lab\*\*: Ning Zhao, Heyuan Li, Biao Wang, Pengcheng Wang, Chen Sun ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in sparsity-driven KV offload path for DeepSeek DSA models using the Ascend MLA attention backend. When enabled, the runtime: - keeps the DSA index KV cache on the NPU; - stores the full MLA latent KV cache in NPU-registered host shared memory; - maintains a per-request, 2,048-token selected-KV cache on the NPU; - resolves top-k cache hits through a device slot map; - fetches cache hits from device memory and misses from registered host memory; and - runs sparse flash attention over the compact selected-KV buffer. The feature is disabled by default. Without the environment variable, the existing Ascend MLA KV-cache and attention paths remain unchanged. Related to sgl-project/sglang#31779 (including motivation, accuracy tests, speed test profiling, etc.) Kernel dependency: sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#636. ## Accuracy Tests Accuracy tests based on GSM8K. ## Design ```text DSA top-k indices | v device slot-map lookup |-----------------------------| | hit | miss v v selected-KV device cache registered host KV | | |-------------+---------------| v compact selected-KV buffer | v NPU sparse flash attention | v selected-KV cache refill ``` ### Feature gating The path is enabled with: ```bash export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPARSITY_DRIVEN_KV_OFFLOAD=1 ``` The configuration is accepted only when all of the following are true: - the runtime device is NPU; - `--attention-backend ascend` is selected; - the model uses the MLA backend; - the model is recognized as a DeepSeek DSA model(DeepSeek V3.2); and - `--max-running-requests` is set explicitly. Invalid combinations fail early with a configuration error. The explicit request limit bounds the per-process host and device allocations, both of which scale with request capacity. ### KV storage and pool sizing With offload disabled, `NPUMLATokenToKVPool` allocates the native latent K/V buffers and the DSA index buffer as before. With offload enabled: - native NPU latent K/V buffers are not allocated; - the DSA index buffer remains device-resident; - the KV-token cell size is calculated from `index_head_dim * num_layers * element_size`; and - attempts to use native K/V accessors fail explicitly instead of dereferencing an absent buffer. The small hook in `model_executor/pool_configurator.py` is required so the scheduler's token capacity matches the physical index-only device pool. It delegates to the NPU-specific configuration only when this feature is enabled and otherwise preserves the existing calculation. ### Host storage and request lifecycle `SparseKVCacheManager` allocates per-layer host shared-memory tensors and registers them with the current NPU. The registered device-visible address is used by the custom indexed-copy operator for D2H/H2D movement. The manager also: - resets per-request slot-map state whenever a request slot is newly allocated; - includes the request-pool padding row when sizing sparse buffers; - reserves sentinel rows and columns for padded or invalid graph entries; and - validates request IDs, sequence lengths, tensor ranks, and index shapes before copying. ### Prefill and decode For prefill/extend, newly produced latent KV rows are copied to host storage. The sparse attention path can gather the request KV into a compact TND buffer and invoke NPU sparse flash attention with normalized DSA sparse-index shapes. For decode: 1. the DSA top-k indices are checked against the per-layer slot map; 2. device-cache hits and host-cache misses are copied on separate NPU streams; 3. stream events join both copies before the selected-KV cache is refilled; 4. the compact selected K/V tensors are passed to NPU sparse flash attention in BSND layout; and 5. the slot map is updated for the next decode step. ACL report processing is registered for graph streams so host callbacks can be serviced when graph execution is used. ## Code changes | File or module | Change | | --- | --- | | `hardware_backend/npu/sparsity_driven_kv_offload/config.py` | Adds the environment switch, platform/model validation, and index-only cell-size calculation. | | `hardware_backend/npu/sparsity_driven_kv_offload/manager.py` | Adds registered host KV storage, request lifecycle handling, slot-map maintenance, multi-stream prefetch, and cache refill. | | `hardware_backend/npu/sparsity_driven_kv_offload/attention.py` | Adds the dedicated prefill/decode sparse-attention path and DSA index-shape normalization. | | `hardware_backend/npu/sparsity_driven_kv_offload/host_callback.py` | Adds ACL report-thread and stream-subscription support. | | `hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py` | Makes native latent K/V allocation conditional and retains the device index cache. | | `hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py` | Initializes the manager and dispatches DSA sparse attention to the offload path only when enabled. | | `model_executor/pool_configurator.py` | Uses the NPU index-only cell size when offload is enabled. | ## Benchmark results Model: GLM-5.1 Accuracy: no-loss compared to baseline (AIME-26) Throughput (Decode): 39.42 TPS (baseline) -> 63.06 TPS **(1.6x faster)** Settings: TP16, colocation deployment with graph optimization enabled, details included in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31779 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #31602307140](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31602307140) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31602306885](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31602306885)

signal.title: [JIT Kernel] Migrate causal_conv1d_fwd and causal_conv1d_update from AOT to JIT
signal.text: ## Motivation Move `causal_conv1d_fwd` / `causal_conv1d_update` off the prebuilt `sgl_kernel` wheel and onto the JIT kernel infra, keeping the in-place contract, the exported ops, and bit-level numerics. Both sit on the prefill/decode path of every short-conv hybrid model — LFM2 / LFM2-MoE, Mamba2, GDN. ## Modifications - Device kernels move into `kernels/jit/csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cuh` unchanged; only the host launchers switch to the tvm-ffi `TensorView` API. Strides stay `uint32_t` elements, as in the AOT `ConvParamsBase`. - The JIT build matches the wheel's arch split — `-use_fast_math` on SM 9.0, precise math elsewhere, per `load_utils.py`'s `compute_capability == 90` — so the SiLU epilogue emits the same bits. Math mode is part of the build key. - CUDA serving goes through the JIT registry behind a `torch.compile`-compatible custom op; everything else keeps Triton. The AOT ops stay exported for external users and for the differential test. - Only a JIT/CUDA spec is registered, since the AOT kernel was CUDA-only anyway — `csrc/mamba/causal_conv1d.cu` sits in the CUDA CMakeLists and nowhere else, and `common_extension_rocm.cc` never defined the ops. ROCm and MUSA were already landing on Triton through the old `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.causal_conv1d_update` probe; now they get there directly via `_HAS_CONV1D_KERNEL = is_cuda()`. Nothing changes on any device. - The AOT `cudaFuncSetAttribute` branch goes away behind a `static_assert`: every instantiation sits near 4 KB of shared memory, nowhere near the 48 KB it existed to raise. - `width` outside 2..4 now raises in prefill, where the AOT `if`/`else if` chain had no `else` and quietly did nothing. - `has_initial_state` gets a dtype check. The kernel reads it as `const bool*`, and `kDLBool` has no C++ trait, so it lands as a `CHECK_HOST` on the dtype code rather than a matcher clause. - Tests and benchmarks move to the registered kernel layout, and the superseded AOT-only test is gone. ## Accuracy Tests `pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` | | H200 (SM90, fast-math) | GB300 (SM103, precise-math) | |---|---|---| | Total | 473 passed, 12 skipped | 473 passed, 12 skipped | | Bit-exact vs AOT (72 cases) | pass | pass | | Reference vs `F.conv1d` (393 cases) | pass | pass | Two machines because the kernel picks its math mode by arch, so each one compiles a different build. The 12 skips are the same deliberate guard on both: the circular-buffer reference can't arbitrate when `seqlen > state_len`, where `scatter_` hits duplicate indices. Behind those counts, the reference tests cover FP32/FP16/BF16 × widths 2–4 × seqlens 1–4096, varlen (per sequence) and non-varlen, both conv-state layouts, gathered slots. The differential is one config per dispatch path, narrowed from a ~900-config sweep that came back bit-identical to AOT throughout. On GB300 the SiLU epilogue — where a math-flag mismatch would show up — gives `max_abs_diff = 0.000e+00`. Also checked: `pad_slot_id` slots untouched, bad dtype / width / non-bool mask rejected, `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` bit-identical to eager, and `LiquidAI/LFM2-350M` serving end to end (GSM8K 200q = 0.325, H200). B200 is registered in `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/mamba/bench_causal_conv1d.py` — FP16/BF16, `dim` 2048–8192, prefill seqlens 128–8192 (4-sequence varlen batch), decode batch 1–256 with gathered slots. 24 configs each. | | prefill geomean | prefill range | prefill wins | decode geomean | decode range | decode wins | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | H200 (SM90) | **1.063x** | 1.022x – 1.122x | 24/24 | 1.001x | 0.995x – 1.015x | 14/24 | | GB300 (SM103) | **1.041x** | 1.015x – 1.062x | 24/24 | 1.000x | 0.987x – 1.013x | 10/24 (3 tied) | - Prefill wins every config on both machines. GB300 extremes: BF16 `(512, 2048)` 22.09 vs 22.41 us, BF16 `(2048, 8192)` 84.90 vs 90.16 us. - Decode is a wash, and those win counts are noise rather than a result: 23/24 configs on H200 and 20/24 on GB300 land within ±1% either way, three of them exact ties. The decode kernel is unchanged, so neither direction means anything. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: Suppress expected FlashInfer TRT-LLM workspace warnings
signal.text: ## Summary FlashInfer TRT-LLM warns on every oversized all-reduce during prefill CUDA graph capture, even though SGLang safely falls back. One startup produced **28,032 repeated warnings / 56,064 warning lines** like this: ```text Workspace is insufficient for problem size. Workspace validation failed: - token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2880) exceeds workspace max_token_num (2048) * hidden_dim (2880). This may cause Illegal Memory Access. ``` This skips the noisy TRT-LLM validator only when cached workspace metadata already proves the request cannot fit. It preserves valid total-capacity reuse and FP32 Lamport compatibility, while leaving MNNVL's validator untouched. Added focused regression coverage and confirmed on 4x H100 with TP4: full prefill graph capture through 8192 tokens completed without the warnings, while TRT-LLM fusion stayed enabled. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31873437993](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31873437993)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31873437892](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31873437892)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [SM12x] Add b12x MoE runner backend for DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 experts on GB10
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4's MXFP4 experts (`fp4_e8m0_k32`) have no fused MoE path on the SM12x family (GB10 / DGX Spark, RTX PRO 6000 class). This PR adds an opt-in `--moe-runner-backend b12x` that maps them onto NVIDIA b12x W4A16 fused MoE kernels, making DeepSeek-V4-Flash practical to serve on 2x DGX Spark. ## Modifications - **`mxfp4_b12x_moe.py`** (new): `Mxfp4B12xMoEMethod` — weight prep hands the checkpoint tensors to b12x (E8M0 scales consumed natively, Parameters released after prepare), plus a frozen scratch plan shared per shape across all expert layers. - **Warmup ladder**: b12x refuses to compile kernels during CUDA graph capture and falls back to a pinned tile config that does not fit every block size, so every token count a captured graph can present is compiled eagerly first (decode `bs x spec_window` plus a power-of-two ladder for chunked prefill, sized by `SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS`). - **`moe_runner/b12x.py`** (new): fused-path runner registration. - **Version pinning escape hatch**: `SGLANG_B12X_PATH` selects an alternate b12x checkout. Rationale: 1.2.2 passes weights as raw pointers and rebuilds layouts at runtime, measuring 875.6 us/call vs 707.9 us/call for 0.15.3's static-stride `cute.Tensor` path on DSv4-Flash decode (bit-identical output). Both are supported; the env lets deployments keep the faster one. - **`mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py`**: register the new method in the `routed_scaling_factor` whitelist (it is silently dropped otherwise, compressing the whole MoE block by the scaling factor). - Env knobs registered in `environ.py` per conventions (`SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS`, `SGLANG_B12X_RELAX_BLOCKS_PER_SM`, `SGLANG_B12X_PATH`). ## Validation 2x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=2 cross-node, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with DSPARK speculative decoding (`gamma=5`), chunked prefill 4096: | Metric | Result | |---|---| | GSM8K 1319q (few-shot, parallel 8) | accuracy **0.945**, invalid 0 | | decode (8k ctx, bs=1) | 73-77 ms/step, accept-length 5.4-5.9 | | prefill 30k input | ~1.9k tok/s input throughput | Also boots and passes GSM8K (200q sampled: 0.960) on current main. Related: #34018 (FP8 wo_a GEMM on sm12x) is complementary and kept separate on purpose. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32004868000](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32004868000)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32004867794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32004867794)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DFLASH] Remove FlashInfer and MRoPE host syncs
signal.text: ## Motivation DFlash speculative decoding with overlap scheduling still performs blocking CPU/GPU synchronization in four places: 1. FlashInfer planning for the draft worker's attention wrappers. 2. Calling `paged_kernel_lens.sum().item()` while preparing the draft worker's sliding-window attention metadata. 3. Uploading multimodal MRoPE deltas during target verification. 4. FlashInfer planning for the target worker's full-attention wrapper. These synchronizations force the CPU to wait for queued GPU work, preventing the CPU scheduler from staying ahead and introducing gaps before draft and target-verify execution. ## Modifications This PR addresses the synchronization points in three corresponding areas. The optimization is guarded by: ```bash export SGLANG_DFLASH_SYNC_FREE_DECODE=1 ``` The flag defaults to `False`. ### 1. Remove host synchronization from draft-worker FlashInfer planning The draft worker may use either a sliding-window wrapper together with a full-attention wrapper, or a single full-attention wrapper. Both layouts now use SGLang's sync-free FlashInfer prefill planning path during CUDA graph replay. During graph capture, the original FlashInfer `plan()` is still called once to initialize the wrapper's cached module. During replay, SGLang constructs the planning metadata from CPU-side request bookkeeping and calls `fast_prefill_plan()` instead of invoking the original blocking planning path. For sliding-window attention, the previous implementation also evaluated: ```python paged_kernel_lens.sum().item() ``` Because `paged_kernel_lens` is a CUDA tensor, `.item()` copies the scalar result to the host and waits for preceding GPU work. The optimized path computes the equivalent planning length from the existing CPU-side sequence-length metadata, removing this additional synchronization. This follows the approach introduced in [PR #32218](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32218). The CPU lengths are conservative planning bounds used only to select and partition the FlashInfer workload. The GPU `indptr` and `indices` remain the authoritative layout used for actual KV-cache access, so the attention computation is unchanged. Supported draft-worker layouts: | Attention layout | Optimization | | --- | --- | | Sliding-window + full attention | Both wrappers use sync-free planning | | Full attention only | The full-attention wrapper uses sync-free planning | | Unsupported layout | Falls back to the original FlashInfer planning path | ### 2. Avoid repeated MRoPE delta uploads during target verification For multimodal requests, the MRoPE delta is request-level metadata and remains unchanged across decode steps for the same request. Previously, target verification repeatedly stacked CPU tensors and copied the result to the GPU, introducing host-to-device transfer and synchronization overhead on every step. The optimized path creates a GPU-side MRoPE delta cache during prefill and reuses the cached tensor during subsequent DFlash target-verification steps. Cache entries are validated against the request metadata and device before reuse, and are recreated when the corresponding request state changes. This also supports batched requests: each request has its own cached delta, and the per-request tensors are stacked in the current batch order before use. ### 3. Remove host synchronization from target-worker FlashInfer planning The target worker's full-attention wrapper previously entered the original FlashInfer planning path during target verification. This PR applies the same sync-free planning mechanism used by the draft worker. The target wrapper uses CPU-side sequence-length metadata to construct the host planning inputs while retaining the exact GPU KV-cache layout for execution. Unsupported configurations, non-DFlash execution, and runs without `SGLANG_DFLASH_SYNC_FREE_DECODE=1` continue to use the existing implementation. ## Correctness The optimization changes only how FlashInfer planning metadata is constructed and when MRoPE deltas are transferred. It does not change attention computation or KV-cache addressing. The implementation preserves the following invariants: - CUDA graph capture initializes FlashInfer's cached module with the original `plan()` implementation. - CUDA graph replay uses CPU-side planning metadata without GPU-to-CPU scalar reads. - Host planning lengths are never smaller than the exact GPU KV lengths. - GPU `indptr` and `indices` remain authoritative for actual KV-cache access. - Unsupported layouts automatically fall back to the original code path. - The original behavior is preserved when the feature switch is disabled. ## Accuracy Tests Tested with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B and its DFlash draft model on 8x NVIDIA A800 GPUs (`TP=8`, `EP=8`, draft tokens `4`, DFlash block size `4`). Each multimodal request contained approximately 14k input tokens and three images: - Multimodal requests: **60/60 passed**. - Concurrent requests with `bs=2/4/8`: **14/14 passed**. - No plan metadata, host-bound, reconstructed indptr, or MRoPE value mismatch during development validation. - No scheduler exception, traceback, or CUDA error in the final service logs. Benchmark results before and after enabling the synchronization optimization: | Configuration | Math500 | GSM8K | MMBench_dev_en | MMStar | RealWorldQA | gRefCOCO | CountBench strict | MMLU-Redux | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Before sync optimization | 95.8 | 95.8 | 79.6 | 76.7 | 78.7 | 70.4 | 93.3 | 84.1 | | After sync optimization | 97.2 | 96.1 | 79.7 | 77.5 | 79.2 | 70.5 | 93.3 | 84.2 | No benchmark showed an accuracy regression. The optimization only changes how FlashInfer planning metadata is constructed and when MRoPE deltas are transferred; it does not change the attention computation. Unit tests on the latest `upstream/main`: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python3 \ test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_overlap_hostsync.py ``` Result: **10/10 passed** on an A800. ## Speed Tests and Profiling For the multimodal workload, TPOT decreased from **5.2 ms/token** to **4.5 ms/token**. | Metric | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | TPOT | 5.2 ms/token | 4.5 ms/token | MRoPE profiling: | Metric | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | MRoPE `cudaStreamSynchronize` calls | 13 | 0 | | MRoPE stream wait | 1200.4 us/step | 0 | | `forward_batch_init` | 1618.1 us/step | 555.5 us/step | With all three paths enabled, 39 speculative FlashInfer plans used the fast path (26 draft and 13 target). The remaining blocking plan was initialization or outside the speculative hot path. signal.title: [BUG] Fix fallback tensor aliasing in DP MLP sync all_gather
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation This PR fixes a PyTorch overlapping-memory runtime error in `MLPSyncBatchInfo.all_gather`. `fallback_tensor.expand(...).contiguous()` can still alias `fallback_tensor` when every expanded dimension is size 1. In that case, the gathered output tensor and the fallback tensor share storage. Later, when inactive ranks are overwritten with the fallback value, PyTorch rejects the in-place assignment: `unsupported operation: some elements of the input tensor and the written-to tensor refer to a single memory location` The fix changes the initialization to `expand(...).clone()` so the global gather buffer always owns independent storage. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications - Replace `expand(...).contiguous()` with `expand(...).clone()` in DP MLP sync. - Add a comment explaining why `clone()` is required. - Add a CPU unit test for the single-slot inactive-rank fallback path. <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests This issue would be encountered before this PR, causing the sglang service to fail to start: ``` bash [2026-08-17 03:44:24 PP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4947, in run_scheduler_process scheduler.run_event_loop() File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1662, in run_event_loop dispatch_event_loop(self) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4800, in dispatch_event_loop scheduler.event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill() File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 124, in decorate_context return func(*args, **kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py", line 262, in event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill batch = self.dp_attn_adapter.maybe_prepare_mlp_sync_batch(batch) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py", line 431, in maybe_prepare_mlp_sync_batch batch = self.prepare_mlp_sync_batch(batch) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py", line 402, in prepare_mlp_sync_batch return prepare_mlp_sync_batch_raw( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py", line 339, in prepare_mlp_sync_batch_raw mlp_sync_info.all_gather( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py", line 180, in all_gather tp_info[tp_active_ranks[:num_ranks_in_tp_info] == 0] = fallback_tensor ~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ RuntimeError: unsupported operation: some elements of the input tensor and the written-to tensor refer to a single memory location. signal.title: [diffusion] Fix width/height silently dropped on multipart /v1/videos requests
signal.text: ## Summary - `create_video()` declares explicit `Form(...)` parameters for `seconds`, `size`, `fps`, `num_frames`, `seed`, etc., but not for `width`/`height`. Because those two names are already declared fields on `VideoGenerationsRequest`, the generic "extra form field" fallback explicitly excludes already-declared fields, so a multipart request's `width`/`height` are never read — the pipeline's `SamplingParams` subclass default silently wins instead. - Fix: add `width`/`height` as explicit `Form(None)` parameters, threaded through the same `form_value()` precedence already used for `fps`/`num_frames`. - Not model-specific: any multipart `/v1/videos` request with explicit `width`/`height` hits this, for any model (surfaced here while building an image-to-video client against LTX-2.5, #35107). The JSON body path was already unaffected. ## Test plan - [x] Before: multipart request for `width=704&height=512` produced a `960x544` video (LTX25SamplingParams' hardcoded default), confirmed via `ffprobe` on the actual output. - [x] After: same request produces `704x512` output, confirmed via `ffprobe`. - [x] JSON body path re-verified unaffected (worked before and after). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32004190886](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32004190886)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32004190724](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32004190724)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec] Fix Dspark and Dflash state divergence across TP rank
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Related to: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33289 To fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33289 bug, upgrade NCCL to the newest version (2.30.7). When TP > 1, Dspark makes serveral sampling decisions on reach rank: 1. The draft Markov chain samples proposal tokens step by step (with in-graph philox noise introduced since https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33298) 2. Target verify derives `correct_len` / `bonus` / `cap_trim_lens` 3. Prefill samples `next_token_ids` In order to maintain the speedup, SGLang skips cross-rank sync of sampled tokens by default (I found the comment here: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py#L496). So nothing forces these values to agree. Once one rank commits a different token or accept length, sequence lengths and KV state drift apart and a later collective deadlocks (demonstrated by fault injection in the Accuracy Tests section below). ## Modifications Broadcast rank 0's sampling decisions before they affect state. The idea follows the existing `verify_lens` handling in `dspark_planner.py` and the EAGLE proposals in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29003 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31478: 1. Broadcast every Markov proposal token in **both** eager and graph-folded sampling. Sync only at the end of a draft block is too late because each step depends on the previous token. 2. Broadcast `correct_len`, `bonus`, and `cap_trim_lens` in the eager verify path and the captured verify epilogue, before finalization, token output, or KV commit. Separate `all_reduce(MIN)` calls could combine fields from different ranks. 3. Broadcast prefill `next_token_ids` before entering the draft path. `DsparkTpSync` in `dspark_tp.py` (newly added file) uses the TP group's PyNCCL communicator. Process-group collectives cannot be captured in CUDA graphs, and using the model's existing TP communicator preserves collective ordering across eager and captured execution. With DP attention, it uses `attn_tp_group`, matching `verify_lens_broadcast_group` in original `dspark_planner.py`. TP=1 is a no-op. The reason why I don't match RNG seeds is because ranks can still diverge if they consume different numbers of random values, and it does not cover non-RNG differences. In addition, for TP > 1, this add `gamma + 3` broadcasts of a `[bs]` tensor per decode step, all within the captured graphs. ## Accuracy Tests All tests below on following configs: - 2 DGX Sparks - TP=2 - DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with 131k context - Decode CUDA graphs and folded sampling enabled - Add https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33407 code. It fixes an unrelated bug for SM12x sparse-MLA topk dispatch crash at boot. Dspark + DeepSeek V4 Flash cannot start on DGX Sparks without it. - **NCCL 2.30.7** for SGLang's PyNCCL communicator via `SGLANG_NCCL_SO_PATH` (torch's bundled 2.28.9 wedges this workload's graph/eager mix with or without this patch; a separate problem from this fix) For accuracy test, we run`python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200` (temp=0): accuracy 0.965, invalid 0.000. This is expected since there's no mathematical changes. To demonstrate the failure mode this patch addresses, we fault-injected a rank-local accept divergence into both builds: rank 1 lowers every accept length by one (`correct_len = torch.clamp(correct_len - 1, min=0)`, NCCL 2.30.7 in both _runs). **_Note: the fault reproduction code has been removed before submitting PR._** Without the fix, the server deadlocks before finishing startup warmup. With the fix, the same injection is harmless: rank 0's broadcast overwrites the divergent values, the server boots, and a temp=0 request returns the expected output. As a stability check on the fix itself (its broadcasts run inside the captured decode graphs), I sent 42 sequential chat requests with `ignore_eos=true` and `max_tokens=512` (30 at temp=1, then 12 at temp=0) and probed `/health_generate` after every request with a 180s client timeout, so a stuck collective surfaces as a failed request instead of a silent hang. As the result, all 42 returned HTTP 200 with `finish_reason=length`. 21504 tokens generated in total and mean acc_len during the temp=1 run was 2.86 (block_size=4). Same for temp=0, neither of them occur any error. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test on 24 natural prompts, 256 output tokens, concurrency=1, temp=1, same setup as above: | Requests | Output throughput | TTFT mean/median/P90 (ms) | TPOT mean/median/P90 (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | 24 | 31.9 tok/s | 157.6 / 153.7 / 178.6 | 30.8 / 31.7 / 35.5 | Comparing with pre-fix TP baseline is impossible because it cannot survive under such load. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Test] Add unit tests for mem_cache/multimodal_cache
signal.text: ## Motivation Part of #20865. `MultiModalStaticCache` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/multimodal_cache.py`) is the byte-budgeted LRU cache used to reuse precomputed VLM image/video embeddings across requests (consumed by `managers/mm_schedule.py` and `disaggregation/encode_server.py`). It currently has no dedicated unit tests, so its capacity accounting, LRU eviction order, oversized-item rejection, and the two `set`/`get` (combined-hash, multi-item) vs `set`/`get_single` (raw-hash, single-item) retrieval contracts are all uncovered. ## Modifications - Added CPU-only unit tests for `MultiModalStaticCache`, `EmbeddingResult`, `combine_hashes`, and the `_get_tensor_size` helper. - Covered: - byte-level capacity-accounting invariant (`current_size` == sum of stored tensor byte sizes) across arbitrary `set`/`get`/`free`/`clear` sequences, including dtype-dependent accounting (float32 / float16 / int64); - LRU eviction order tracking access recency (insertion order, `get`/`get_single` promotion, and repeated-`set` refresh); - oversized-item rejection leaving the cache empty and accounting-consistent, plus single/multi-eviction and exact-fit / one-byte-over boundary cases; - the multi-item combined-hash path (`set(combine_hashes(...))` + `get(item_hashes)`) and the single-item raw-hash path (`set(h)` + `get_single(h)`), matching the two production call sites; - failure paths: misses, freeing an absent key, and the `EmbeddingResult` type assertion. No server is launched and no model weights are loaded; tensors stay on CPU. Production code is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — test-only change, does not affect model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — test-only change, does not impact inference speed. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Test Plan ```bash pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multimodal_cache.py -v ``` ``` 32 passed ``` Local coverage on the target module: 100% (77 statements, 0 missed). signal.title: [Fix] Restore fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor on biased_grouped_topk_cpu
signal.text: ## Motivation `select_experts()` passes `fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor` to `biased_grouped_topk()` unconditionally, but `biased_grouped_topk` is rebound to `biased_grouped_topk_cpu` at import time when the CPU engine runs on an AMX-capable host, and the CPU variant does not accept that keyword: ``` TypeError: biased_grouped_topk_cpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor' ``` This is raised while binding arguments, so it fires before the function body runs and even when the value is `None`. Any model on the `use_grouped_topk` + `correction_bias` path crashes at its first MoE forward, during warmup. ## Modifications Accept `fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor` in `biased_grouped_topk_cpu` and reject a requested scale, so the argument is validated rather than silently ignored. The CPU kernel enforces `num_fused_shared_experts == 0`, so no shared expert is appended on this path and there is no weight a scale could apply to: ```cpp TORCH_CHECK( num_fused_shared_experts == 0, "num_fused_shared_experts must be 0 default value, got: ", num_fused_shared_experts); ``` Whether a scale is needed is the caller's decision, so the CPU path only states that it cannot apply one and leaves the value itself alone. A call site that has no scale to request should leave the field unset; one that passes an explicit value now gets an error naming the parameter, instead of the unrelated `num_fused_shared_experts` message or the `TypeError` above. The guard follows the shape already used for `routed_scaling_factor` in the same kernel: ```cpp TORCH_CHECK( !routed_scaling_factor.has_value() || routed_scaling_factor.value() == 1.0f, "routed_scaling_factor must be None or 1.0f default value, got: ", routed_scaling_factor.value()); ``` `raise ValueError` rather than `assert`, matching `fused_topk_cpu`, which rejects its four unsupported arguments the same way: asserts are stripped under `python -O`. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical change on any platform. The GPU path is untouched, and on CPU the accepted value is the existing default, under which no shared expert is appended. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32003680107](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32003680107)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32003679991](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32003679991)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: Jacob0226

signal.title: [DeepEP] Use static FP8 communication for W4AFP8 normal dispatch
signal.text: ## Motivation For W4AFP8 MoE on the DeepEP normal-dispatch path, the dispatcher previously sent BF16 hidden states over the all-to-all and re-quantized them on the receiving side using the checkpoint's static activation scale. This doubles the communication volume (BF16 instead of FP8) and re-does a quantization that the weights were already calibrated against. Since W4AFP8 carries a single static `w13_input_scale` from the checkpoint, we can quantize hidden states to FP8 *before* dispatch and communicate the FP8 payload directly, removing the BF16 transport and the redundant re-quantization. ## Changes - **`token_dispatcher/deepep.py`**: `dispatch()` of the normal dispatcher now accepts an optional `static_scale`. When provided, hidden states are per-tensor quantized to FP8 (`float8_e4m3fn`) with that scale before the all-to-all, so the dispatch payload is FP8 instead of BF16. The low-latency path is left unchanged (it already consumes DeepEP's per-token-group scales). - **`ep_moe/layer.py`**: `DeepEPMoE` computes and forwards the static `w13_input_scale` to `dispatch()` when running a W4AFP8 model on DeepEP. - **`cutlass_w4a8_moe.py`**: `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal` now accepts an already-FP8 `gateup_input_pre_reorder` and skips the redundant per-tensor FP8 quantization in that case. - **`quantization/w4afp8.py`**: `W4AFp8MoEMethod` configures the dispatcher's `normal_dispatcher_output_dtype` to `fp8` (instead of `bf16`) for the DeepEP backend, and `postprocess_dispatch` validates that a static FP8 payload (no per-token-group scale) was produced. - **`batch_overlap/two_batch_overlap.py`**: thread `static_scale` through the TBO dispatcher wrapper so the overlap path benefits from the same FP8 dispatch. - **Tests**: extend `test_w4afp8_deepep_dtype.py` and `test_w4afp8_deepep_post_reorder.py` to cover the static-FP8 normal-dispatch path (dtype assertions + post-reorder correctness). ## How it works ``` Before: hidden_states(BF16) --a2a--> per_tensor_quant_fp8 --> W4A8 GEMM After: hidden_states --quant(static_scale)--> FP8 --a2a--> W4A8 GEMM ``` The all-to-all now transmits FP8 (half the bytes of BF16), and the receiver no longer re-quantizes — the static scale used for dispatch is the same one the weights were calibrated with. ## Checklist - [x] Code follows the project style (ruff/black conventions in place). - [x] Existing W4AFP8 + DeepEP unit tests extended for the new path. - [ ] CI (will rely on the project CI run on this PR). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31676535100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31676535100)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31676534754](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31676534754)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PP&Sepc] enanble dspark under pipeline parallelism (deepseek-v4 & kimi-k3)
signal.text: ## Motivation roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/11857, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30344, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607 Our previous PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31139) enabled PP + EAGLE support. Testing showed DSpark speculation performs far better than EAGLE, so this PR builds on it to add DSpark + PP compatibility. This PR depends on the previous one and should be merged afterwards. DSpark's verify path is structurally different from EAGLE's (per-layer aux hidden capture, linear block verify, confidence-driven budget), so it could not reuse the EAGLE PP machinery verbatim. This PR lifts that ban and makes DSpark run under PP, targeting DeepSeek-V4-Flash + the bundled DSpark draft checkpoint. ## Modifications The core idea mirrors the EAGLE PP design — the draft model lives only on the last PP rank, every rank runs its own target verify forward, and the draft proposal is relayed across stages so each rank rebuilds an identical verify context. The DSpark-specific work is making the per-layer aux-hidden capture and the linear block verify cross the PP boundary correctly. 1. **Per-rank draft proposal carrier (`DSparkPPVerifyInputRaw`).** A new spec input type carries the last rank's draft / confidence / accounting fields (bonus tokens, draft tokens, new seq lens, confidence, accept/cap-trim/verify lens) across the PP ring. Every rank rebuilds an identical verify layout from the same source each iteration, so all PP ranks produce byte-identical verify windows. It mixes in the shared `DFlashDecodePrepareMixin` so the non-last rank's verify forward (which reads `verify_cache_loc` from `req_to_token`) pre-allocates KV headroom exactly like the last rank. Linear verify reuses the formal `req_to_token` slots, so `accept_index` is always `None` and the token-move step in `batch_result_processor` is skipped automatically. 2. **Per-layer aux hidden capture across PP stages (`deepseek_v4.py`).** DSpark's draft needs per-layer aux hidden states (`dspark_aux_hidden_states`), but each PP rank only executes layers in its own `[start_layer, end_layer)` range. The aux list is now stacked as `[L, num_tokens, hidden]`, relayed downstream under the `"dspark_aux"` key in `PPProxyTensors`, and rebuilt in global layer order on the last rank (upstream layers first, then local captures). `set_dspark_layers_to_capture` no longer early-returns on non-last ranks, so every rank registers its own capture range. 3. **PP-aware verify forward.** `pp_proxy_tensors` is threaded through `TargetVerifyExecutor.run` / `run_non_compact` so the target verify forward relay hidden states along the PP ring on every rank. `TargetVerifyResult` carries `pp_hidden_states_proxy_tensors` back to the scheduler. Logits adjustments (penalizer / vocab mask / logit bias) are now gated on `result.logits_output is not None`, since non-last ranks never sample and their logits output is `None`. 4. **Embed / weight loading split (`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`).** The DSpark draft used to borrow `embed_tokens` from the target. Under PP the last rank builds its own `VocabParallelEmbedding` and only `lm_head` is shared from the target; `attach_shared_modules` now takes `embed_tokens: Optional` so the PP path passes `None` and the draft keeps its locally-built embedding. Weight-name remapping keeps `embed_tokens.weight` on the last PP rank. 5. **PP proxy buffer sizing (`base_runner.py`).** The static `pp_proxy_tensors` buffers are allocated by max token count, not batch size, so the dummy / capture buffer fits the verify-token-expanded shape `[num_tokens, *hidden]` produced under speculative decoding. 6. **Planner / draft fixes for the relayed layout.** `alloc_verify_window` and `DraftBlockProposer` derive `prefix_lens` from the verify window's anchor position instead of `batch.seq_lens`, because the last rank's re-propose pass builds the next window from post-iter seq lens while `batch.seq_lens` is still the pre-iter value. The planner forces `RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=STATIC` and non-compact (eager) verify under PP, since the confidence-driven ragged scheduler and the cuda-graph compact path only run on the last rank and cannot keep cross-rank layout identity. Supporting changes: `draft_worker_common.build_draft_tp_worker` accepts a `pp_global_random_seed` so the draft sampler on the last rank is seeded consistently with the target; `speculative_hook` replaces the blanket `pp_size != 1` ban with a narrower "PP + DP-attention unsupported" check (DP-attention partitions the batch, which conflicts with the PP requirement that every rank see an identical batch). ### Limitations asserted now - **PP + DP-attention** is rejected. Only `--dp-size 1` is permitted under PP. - **PP supports greedy-commit only.** - **PP forces static verify and eager (non-cuda-graph) verify** ## Accuracy Tests Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 GSM8K accuracy (200 examples, 5-shot, temperature=0): | Configuration | GSM8K Accuracy (%) | |---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 98.00 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 98.50 | ## Speed Tests Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, single 8*H20 node; three PP2+TP4 configs: - **PP2-TP4** — PP2+TP4, no spec (baseline) - **PP2-TP4-MTP314** — PP2+TP4 + EAGLE (`speculative-num-steps=3`, `speculative-eagle-topk=1`, `speculative-num-draft-tokens=4`) - **PP2-TP4-DSpark** — PP2+TP4 + DSpark (this PR) bench_serving: `--dataset-name random` with local ShareGPT path (`--dataset-path /datasets/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json`), `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts 5`, `--max-concurrency 1`, `--random-output-len 1024`, `--seed 42`; 3 rounds per point, reporting the min. **TPOT (ms)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 11.11 | 11.14 | 11.13 | | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 5.39 | 5.43 | 5.65 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 2.30 | 2.34 | 2.38 | **Average accepted length (tokens / iter)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 2.75 | 2.90 | 2.83 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 4.91 | 4.85 | 4.87 | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to the [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix rope config compatibility and VL/transformers-fallback weight loading
signal.text: ## Summary Five independent, small fixes uncovered while enabling additional models. - **`utils/hf_transformers/common.py`**: `get_rope_config()` raised `KeyError: 'rope_theta'` whenever a model's `rope_parameters` dict existed but didn't contain a `rope_theta` key (e.g. `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-VL-28B-A3B-PT`, `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct`). Now falls back to `config.rope_theta` (default `10000`) in that case. - **`models/ernie45_moe_vl.py`**, **`models/olmo2.py`**: switched from indexing `config.rope_parameters["rope_theta"]` directly to `get_rope_config(config)`, so they benefit from the fallback above. - **`models/qwen.py`**: `load_weights` now skips checkpoint keys absent from `params_dict` (e.g. `transformer.visual.*` on `Qwen/Qwen-VL-Chat`), since this implementation only covers the text backbone and previously crashed with `KeyError` on VL checkpoints sharing the `QWenLMHeadModel` architecture name. - **`models/transformers.py`**: two fixes for the generic `transformers` fallback path — (1) remap legacy `vision_tower.vision_model.*` checkpoint keys when the live model lacks that sub-module (transformers v5 flattened SigLIP/CLIP), and (2) pad 5D `pixel_values` features to the batch-wide max patch count instead of flattening, so anyres-style models with varying per-image tile counts concatenate correctly instead of crashing/misaligning. - **`managers/mm_schedule.py`**: `_get_chunked_prefill_embedding` batches image cache-misses from *all* concurrent per-image requests into one cross-request ViT call (`_batch_encode_per_image_misses`) for throughput, which assumes every item's feature tensor has the same non-batch shape. Phi-4-multimodal-instruct's dynamic-HD preprocessing gives each image its own crop count based on that image's resolution/aspect ratio, so two images from different concurrent requests can carry different crop counts — when such items land in the same batched ViT call, `phi4mm.get_image_feature`'s `torch.cat` crashes (`Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 0. Expected size 7 but got size 11...`). This same class of bug was already worked around for ROCm/NPU by routing `is_hip`/`is_npu` through the per-request-only `_get_chunked_embedding_by_item` path; XPU had never been added to that list and inherited CUDA's batched path. Adds `is_xpu` to the same condition, so XPU now takes the same safe, already-production-proven per-request path as ROCm/NPU. ## Validation Each fix was validated end-to-end on real hardware (4x Intel Arc Pro B60, XPU backend) via differential baseline-vs-patched testing against the exact checkpoints that originally hit each bug: - `get_rope_config` + `olmo2.py` — `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct`: baseline reproduces `KeyError: rope_theta`; patched loads, serves, and passes gsm8k (0.75 exact_match/8 examples). - `get_rope_config` + `ernie45_moe_vl.py` — `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-VL-28B-A3B-PT` (TP=4): baseline (common.py excluded from overlay) reproduces the identical `KeyError`; patched loads weights cleanly across all 4 TP ranks. - `qwen.py` — `Qwen/Qwen-VL-Chat`: baseline reproduces `KeyError: 'transformer.visual.positional_embedding'`; patched loads and serves successfully. - `transformers.py` — `llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf`: loads, serves, mmmu_val (10 examples) gives 30% accuracy, consistent with the documented 32.2% full-run. - `mm_schedle.py` — `microsoft/Phi-4-multimodal-instruct` (XPU): confirmed on hardware that the unpatched routing takes the batched cross-request path (`_is_xpu` absent → falls through to CUDA-style batching) while the patched routing takes the safe per-request path (`_is_xpu=True`). A direct unit-level repro reproduced the exact error text (`Expected size 7 but got size 11`) from concatenating two mismatched-shape items, confirming the mechanism; `_get_chunked_embedding_by_item` is scoped to one request's own items only, so the fix structurally rules out cross-request shape collisions rather than just reducing their probability. ## Test plan - [x] Differential (baseline vs. patched) smoke test per fix on real checkpoints, as above - [ ] CI <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31997517342](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31997517342)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31997517065](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31997517065)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(lora): build the MoE LoRA align JIT kernel on ROCm
signal.text: ## Problem `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/lora/moe_lora_align_kernel.cu` does not compile on ROCm, so MoE LoRA cannot run there: ``` moe_lora_align_kernel.cu:9:10: fatal error: 'cub/cub.cuh' file not found ``` and once that include is resolved, `cudaFuncSetAttribute`, `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` and `cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin` are undeclared as well. The AOT build hipifies its sources, so they can spell CUDA names directly; the JIT path hands the `.cu` to `hipcc` with `-DUSE_ROCM` and no rewrite, so this file has to provide the names itself. ## Fix - Include `hipcub` under `USE_ROCM` the way `sgl-kernel/csrc/moe/moe_topk_softmax_kernels.cu` does, plus a `namespace cub = hipcub` alias, because on the JIT path there is no hipify to rewrite `cub::` for us. The alias sits inside `namespace moe`, where the single `cub::BlockScan` use lives. - Add the three missing names to the ROCm alias block in `jit_kernel/include/sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`, which this file already includes. - Pass the kernel through `std::bit_cast<const void*>` as `csrc/deepseek_v4/paged_mqa_metadata.cuh` does: HIP's `hipFuncSetAttribute` takes `const void*` where CUDA has a templated overload. These three aliases are what this kernel needs. Other `jit_kernel` files that spell `cudaFuncSetAttribute` still fail on other CUDA-isms, so this does not make them ROCm-clean — it also cannot regress them, since anything referencing these names under ROCm already failed to compile. ## Test Registers the kernel's existing unit test for AMD so this cannot regress unnoticed. Verified on MI350X / ROCm 7.2: the kernel JIT-compiles from a cold cache and `test/registered/jit/test_moe_lora_align_block_size.py` passes 32/32, two of which exercise the `std::bit_cast` branch. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31995488415](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995488415)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31995488235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995488235)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(moe): follow the built runner's expert-ID namespace, not the configured backend
signal.text: ## Problem `StandardDispatcher` decides whether to remap `topk_ids` into the rank-local expert range from `get_moe_runner_backend()`. Only the AITER runner keeps global expert IDs, which its comment states correctly — but the *configured* backend is not necessarily the backend of the runner this layer got. On ROCm, compressed-tensors W4A16 selects `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE`, which builds a Triton runner: ```python # compressed_tensors_wNa16_moe.py:540 self.runner = MoeRunner(MoeRunnerBackend.TRITON, moe_runner_config) ``` With the configured backend at `auto` and `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (which the ROCm images set), the dispatcher concludes "AITER runner, keep global IDs" and skips the `local_expert_mapping` remap in `StandardDispatcher.dispatch`. The Triton path then sizes its buffers from the rank-local expert count — `moe_align_block_size` allocates `cumsum_buffer` with `num_local_experts + 2` int32 — while `topk_ids` still holds global IDs, so `sgl-kernel/csrc/moe/moe_align_kernel.cu:40` does `atomicAdd(&cumsum_buffer[topk_ids[i] + 1], 1)` with an index up to 384 on a 98-entry buffer. Every rank dies during warmup: ``` Memory access fault by GPU node-N (Agent handle: 0x...) on address 0x7f... Reason: Unknown. ``` one per rank, reasons varying between `Unknown` and `Write access to a read-only page`. It reproduces with plain `sglang.launch_server`, no LoRA and no training framework: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <Kimi-K2.5> \ --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend triton --trust-remote-code ``` and `--moe-runner-backend triton` avoids it, which is the clue. On CUDA the same code is safe: `_use_aiter` requires HIP, and CUDA + `auto` selects the Marlin scheme instead. Any EP>1 MoE on ROCm whose quant method builds a non-AITER runner under `--moe-a2a-backend none` reaches this — W8A8-FP8 with `CHANNEL` strategy builds an AITER runner and was never affected. ## Fix `MoeRunner` already receives the same `MoeRunnerConfig` object the dispatcher is built from a line later (`fused_moe_triton/layer.py:357-358`). Record the backend on the config at runner construction, and let the dispatcher use it to **override the inference only when the built runner is not AITER**. Narrowing only, deliberately: `new = old and (recorded is None or recorded.is_aiter())`, so the set of layers that keep global IDs can only shrink. Several quant methods promote `auto` to AITER without consulting `_use_aiter` — `mxfp4.py:1436`, `fp8.py:2115` under `SGLANG_INT4_WEIGHT`, `quark_int4fp8_moe.py` and `quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` among them — so on a ROCm box without `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` they build an AITER runner while the old inference returns False. That is the mirror-image mismatch; it may well be a real bug, but it needs hardware testing for those schemes, and narrowing-only keeps it exactly as it is today. Every backend reachable here on ROCm (Triton, DeepGEMM, Humming) sizes its kernels from `num_local_experts`, so the override is only ever correcting the direction that writes out of bounds. `skip_local_expert_mapping` in the same constructor still reads the configured backend, unchanged and commented as deliberate. ## Test `test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py` execs `StandardDispatcher.__init__` against a hand-built config, so it gains the new field plus a case over all four configured/recorded combinations, and one asserting `MoeRunner.__init__` writes the field on the shared config in the first place. Verified on MI350X / ROCm 7.2 at `--tp 4 --ep-size 4`: | probe | before | after | |---|---|---| | Kimi-K2.5 W4A16, default backend | memory access fault on all 4 ranks | serves | | same with `--moe-runner-backend triton` | serves | serves | Paths where the built runner is AITER, including unquantized BF16 MoE, are untouched by construction: the override cannot set the flag True. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31995985292](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995985292)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31995985010](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31995985010)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
